title: State the M365 source-document controller boundary in the customer DPA
description:
## Action

Add wording to the customer **DPA** stating the M365 source-document controller boundary.

## Why

From KS-234 §5.3: Secuura's m365 integration holds only an **org-scoped OAuth connection** (`svc_m365_connections`), not a per-user copy of source documents. The source documents live in the **customer's own M365 / SharePoint tenant**, where the **customer is the data controller**. On a Secuura erasure, the customer's M365 source is therefore the **customer's** erasure responsibility, not Secuura's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Customer DPA explicitly states the customer is controller of their own M365 source documents and is responsible for erasing them in their own tenant.

Refs: KS-234 §5.3. (Belongs in the DPA legal doc, not the platform repo.)

title: Phase 2 — JWT RS256 → hybrid (RS256 + ML-DSA-65)
description:
> **⚠ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 (session 19) — the shim blocker below is DEAD, and the real blocker is different. Kam's ruling needed on a design change; see the pinned comment for the measurements.**
>
> `jose` 6.2.8 signs and verifies ML-DSA JWTs on Node 24 today — **no liboqs, no WASM shim**. Measured: RS256 435 B / ML-DSA-44 3326 B / **ML-DSA-65 4511 B** / ML-DSA-87 6269 B, and ML-DSA **verifies faster than RS256** (0.3 ms vs 0.5 ms), so performance is not the constraint.
>
> **The real blocker is token size against the refresh-token COOKIE.** `generateRefreshToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts`) returns a *signed JWT* which `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:367,534,613` sets as the `refresh_token` cookie; browsers cap one cookie at **4096 bytes**. ML-DSA-65 measured 4511 B on a *three-field* payload — the real refresh payload is larger. It does not fit. That forces a design change (opaque refresh token + server-side session lookup — the pattern already exists at `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:133`, cookie chunking, or access-token-only migration) — **Kam's ruling, not an implementation detail.**
>
> Residual risk from the original refusal, still real: Node reports `ExperimentalWarning: The ML-DSA-65 Web Crypto API algorithm is an experimental feature and might change at any time`. Available ≠ production-hardened.
>
> Also: auth signs with `jsonwebtoken` 9.0.2, which has no ML-DSA support — any rollout starts by moving auth's signing path to `jose`.

Migrate JWT signing to hybrid via the Phase-0 registry.

- [X] `~~jsonwebtoken~~`~~ / ~~`~~jose~~`~~ don't yet ship ML-DSA — add a COSE/JOSE PQC shim (liboqs-node or a vetted WASM ML-DSA lib) behind the crypto abstraction.~~ **OBSOLETE 2026-08-12:** `jose` **6.2.8 ships ML-DSA; no shim required. Replaced by: migrate auth's signing from** `jsonwebtoken` **to** `jose`**.**
- [ ] Roll out **verifier-first** (api-gateway, originate accept both), then signer (auth), then drop classical.
- [ ] Entra ID / CIAM (RS256) is **Microsoft-owned** — only ensure `obeden-ssd` doesn't hard-fail on their token-alg rotation; track their PQC timeline.

Blocked by Phase 0. Ref: plan §5 Phase 2.

nodes.body:
## Catalogue pass — the description's bounce is **STALE**; this is actionable, and blocked elsewhere

The description leads with *"Kam's ruling needed on a design change"*. **That ruling landed** — 2026-09-02, the opaque refresh token plus server-side session lookup — and the comment of 12:43 records the split into **KS-756**, related as blocking this ticket.

So the correct reading is: **not a bounce, not waiting on a human, blocked on KS-756.** The design is settled and the build sits on this desk.

Not started tonight — it is a phase-2 crypto change that wants a full session, and its blocker is not cleared. Recorded so the next pass does not re-bounce it.

Split filed as **KS-756** — *Wire up the opaque refresh token that `createSession` already mints* (P2, project *Auth, Tenancy & Access Control*), related as blocking this ticket. It carries the scope, the transition decision and the 1–2 day sizing from the design note above. KS-329 stays the algorithm swap, which gets smaller once the refresh path carries no signature.

## DESIGN NOTE — ruling (a) implemented against measured numbers, not the banner's

**BLUF — the ruling is right, and it is cheaper than it looks in one place and dearer in another. The mechanism it names is already half-built in-tree and *already dead*: `createSession` has minted an opaque refresh token since day one, and nothing has ever read it. The banner's size numbers are also optimistic in the platform's favour and pessimistic in ML-DSA-44's: the real cap on a cookie's *value* is 3976 B, not 4096, and the real refresh payload signs to 5018–5147 B under ML-DSA-65 — over by 1042–1171 B, roughly double the banner's implied margin.**

**Recommendation: split this ticket.** The opaque-refresh-token migration is a prerequisite that stands entirely on its own merits — it is *not* PQC work, it closes a piece of half-wired security machinery, and it can ship without committing to ML-DSA at all. Do that first as its own ticket; leave KS-329 to be the algorithm swap, which becomes small once the refresh path no longer carries a signature. Sizing for both below.

---

### 1. The ruling's mechanism exists in-tree and is dead code — measured

`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:143`, inside `createSession`:

```
refreshToken: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex'),
```

That is exactly the opaque handle ruling (a) calls for, minted on every session since the session service was written. **It has one write site and zero read sites.**

- Write sites: `session.ts:289` (`session.refreshToken = newRefreshToken`, inside `rotateSessionRefreshToken`).
- Read/compare sites across all of `services/`: **none**. The only other occurrence of the identifier anywhere is a *comment* at `routes/auth.ts:635`.
- **Control** — the same grep against `session.isActive`, a field that genuinely is compared, returns **6** read sites (`session.ts:265, 304, 346, 357, 363` + `oauth.ts:391`). So the search can find comparisons; the zero is real.

`session.token` — also minted as `randomBytes(32)` at `session.ts:142` — has **zero** read sites too.

And the code says so itself. `routes/auth.ts:634-635`:

> `// The session-record rotation alone is not enough — nothing in the`
> `// /refresh path compared the incoming JWT against session.refreshToken.`

**The second half of the ruling is already live.** `POST /api/auth/refresh` (`routes/auth.ts:606-607`) already does a server-side session lookup:

```
const payload = verifyRefreshToken(refreshTokenValue);
const session  = await getSession(payload.sessionId);
```

So both halves of "opaque refresh token + server-side session lookup" are present. What is missing is the wire between them: the cookie carries the JWT, the lookup keys off a claim *inside* that JWT, and the opaque handle sits in Redis unread. The work is finishing a mechanism somebody started, not adopting a new one.

### 2. The size numbers, re-measured — the banner is optimistic by 120 bytes and by a whole payload

Signed with the tree's own `jose` on the tree's own Node, using the **exact field set** from `generateRefreshToken` (`jwt.ts:186-200`) and a `kid` header, because `signToken` sets one (`jwt.ts:152`). Role names and `tenant_slug` lengths taken from the local database; e-mail values are synthetic at realistic lengths, because the column is PII-encrypted at rest and I did not decrypt it.

| profile | claims JSON | RS256 (today) | ML-DSA-44 | ML-DSA-65 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| null tenant_slug (139 users) | 400 B | 942 B | 3833 B | **5018 B** |
| typical — `issuer_admin` / `oxford-university` | 474 B | 1040 B | 3931 B | **5116 B** |
| widest real — `issuer_approver` / `greenfield-university` | 488 B | 1059 B | 3950 B | **5135 B** |
| `owner` (the only role `getDefaultScopesForRole` gives a scope) | 497 B | 1071 B | 3962 B | **5147 B** |
| *the banner's own 3-field baseline, reproduced* | 114 B | 560 B | 3451 B | *4636 B* |

**The cap is 3976 bytes, not 4096.** RFC 6265 §6.1 measures the 4096-byte limit as *name + value + attributes*. Serialising with the exact options at `routes/auth.ts:644-650` — `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite: 'strict'`, `maxAge` 7 d, `path: '/api/auth'` — costs **120 bytes** before a single byte of token:

```
refresh_token=X; Max-Age=604800; Path=/api/auth; Expires=Wed, 09 Sep 2026 …; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict
```

So:

- **ML-DSA-65 is over by 1042–1171 B** on real payloads (not the ~415 B the banner's 4511-vs-4096 implies). The banner's conclusion was right; its margin was out by more than 2×.
- **ML-DSA-44 fits — by 14 bytes** on the widest real profile (3962 against 3976 available). The banner called it *"marginal at best"*; that is the number behind the word. One added claim, one longer tenant slug, one more scope and it breaks silently in a browser, on one tenant, in production. It is not a design, it is a coincidence.
- RS256 today sits at 942–1071 B — 2.9 KB of headroom. Nothing is under pressure now.

**Under ruling (a) the size question disappears from the refresh path entirely.** An opaque handle is 64 hex characters regardless of signing algorithm: 64 B against 3976 B available, **3912 B spare**, permanently, for any future algorithm.

### 3. The access token is not a blocker — measured, with the buffer checked rather than assumed

The banner flagged nginx `large_client_header_buffers` as a second constraint worth pricing. Priced:

- ML-DSA-65 **access** token (same payload minus `jti`): **5074 B** → `Authorization: Bearer …` = **5096 B**.
- `large_client_header_buffers` is **not set anywhere** in the gateway config — confirmed by `nginx -T` inside `secuura-nginx-gateway`, so nginx's default `4 8k` applies (control: the same file has 16 `proxy_pass` directives, so the grep reads the file).
- 5096 B against an 8192 B buffer: **fits, 3096 B spare.** No tuning needed at the gateway.

**Unverified and worth one check before any rollout:** Caddy in front of the VM demo. I have not measured its header limits, and this note should not be read as clearing it.

### 4. One honest security observation — and it is *not* a live hole

Because nothing compares the incoming token against `session.refreshToken`, the rotation at `routes/auth.ts:636` is decorative; reuse detection rests entirely on the `jti` Redis denylist (`services/refreshDenylist.ts`). I checked whether that is a gap and **it is not**: `denylistRefreshJti` throws when Redis is unavailable rather than skipping (`refreshDenylist.ts:30-35`), `getSession` also requires Redis, and the denylist TTL is set to the token's own remaining lifetime — so the window closes exactly when the token would have expired anyway. The A-05 control is sound as built.

The point is narrower: an opaque handle compared against the session record would give the same guarantee *by construction*, with no denylist, no `jti`, and no TTL arithmetic. That is a simplification the migration earns for free, not a defect it repairs.

### 5. What the migration actually touches

1. A Redis reverse index `refresh:<handle> → sessionId` (sessions are keyed `sess:<id>` and `user_sessions:<userId>` today — there is no way to find a session *by* refresh token).
2. `POST /api/auth/refresh` — look up by handle, compare against `session.refreshToken`, rotate; drop `verifyRefreshToken` from the path.
3. The three cookie-set sites — `routes/auth.ts:394` (register), `:565` (login), `:644` (refresh) — carry the handle instead of the JWT.
4. `routes/oauth.ts:242, 289` emit `refresh_token` in the body, and `:254-271` runs its **own** refresh path with its own `verifyRefreshToken` + denylist check. It has to move in the same change or it becomes the bypass.
5. `shouldEmitRefreshTokenInBody` (`auth.ts:100-102`) — native/api clients get the token in the body and are not cookie-capped, but they should carry the handle too or there are two token formats to verify forever.
6. **Transition.** Live cookies hold JWTs. Either accept both formats for one refresh lifetime (7 days) and then drop the JWT branch, or accept a single forced re-login. That choice is worth making explicitly rather than discovering.
7. `generateRefreshToken` / `verifyRefreshToken` / `generateTokenPair` shrink or go.

### 6. Sizing — honest, and split

- **Opaque-refresh-token migration (the prerequisite, not PQC): 1–2 days**, dominated by item 6 (the transition) and item 4 (oauth's parallel path), not by the handle itself. Failing-test-first; the reverse index and the both-formats window each want their own test with a negative control.
- **The ML-DSA swap on top (this ticket proper): smaller than it currently reads** once refresh carries no signature — auth's signing path moves from `jsonwebtoken` to `jose`, the verifier side accepts both algorithms first, then the signer flips. I am not putting a number on it until the prerequisite lands, because the verifier-first rollout across every service is the part I have not measured.
- **Still true and unchanged:** Node reports `ExperimentalWarning: The ML-DSA-65 Web Crypto API algorithm is an experimental feature and might change at any time`. Available is not production-hardened, and nothing on the roadmap dates this.

### 7. Two corrections to this ticket's own record

- The description says `jose` **6.2.8** was what shipped ML-DSA. The tree hoists **6.2.3**, and it signs and verifies ML-DSA-44/65/87 on Node v24.7.0 today — `kty: AKP`, verified before measuring. The capability arrived earlier than the record says.
- The description and the pinned comment both say auth signs with `jsonwebtoken` **9.0.2**. The tree has **9.0.3**. Immaterial to the argument; corrected so the next reader does not re-derive it.

---

*Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) on develop `8c9559cfd`. No code changed; no PR. Everything above is a read of the working tree at that SHA plus local signing runs — no platform writes, no chain writes, no deploy.*

## RULED — option A, "Opaque refresh token + server-side session lookup"

**Kam, dashboard decision card, 2026-09-02 19:35 AEST** (card `secuura-ks329-refresh-token-size`), relayed with provenance by the coordinator.

**The design question this ticket was blocked on is now answered.** The banner said the ML-DSA-65 refresh token measures **4511 B** against a browser's **4096 B** single-cookie cap, that it therefore does not fit, and that choosing between an opaque refresh token, cookie chunking, and an access-token-only migration was *"Kam's ruling, not an implementation detail."*

It is ruled: **opaque refresh token + server-side session lookup**. Cookie chunking and access-token-only are not taken.

**This ticket moves from category 2 to category 1** — it no longer waits on anyone. Worth noting the shape is already half-present: `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:133` carries the server-side session pattern the ruling points at, so this is adopting an existing mechanism for the refresh path rather than inventing one.

**Still true and unchanged by the ruling:** auth signs with `jsonwebtoken` 9.0.2, which has no ML-DSA support, so any rollout starts by moving auth's signing path to `jose`; and Node still reports `ExperimentalWarning` for the ML-DSA-65 Web Crypto algorithm — available is not production-hardened.

Not started in this session — sized honestly against the remaining window and handed to the next one as a design note plus PR.

**BLUF — CORRECTION to the record. The previous session's note that sizing had to be REFUSED ("no production-grade ML-DSA for our JOSE stack, blocked on a PQC shim") is now out of date. `jose` 6.2.8 signs and verifies ML-DSA JWTs today on Node 24 with no liboqs and no WASM shim — I tested it. The blocker has moved, and this ticket is sizeable. The real constraint turns out to be token SIZE, and it is a hard one.**

**Recommendation:** re-scope this ticket around the two findings below and put it to Kam as a decision, not a build. The Phase-0 crypto registry work stands; the "add a COSE/JOSE PQC shim" checklist item should be deleted as obsolete.

**Detail**

**1. ML-DSA works today — measured, not assumed.** In `node:24-alpine` with `jose@6.2.8`, sign + verify round-trips for all three parameter sets:

| alg | token | sign | verify | public JWK |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RS256 (today) | **435 B** | 2.0 ms | 0.5 ms | `kty: RSA` |
| ML-DSA-44 | 3326 B | 0.6 ms | 0.3 ms | `kty: AKP` |
| **ML-DSA-65** | **4511 B** | 2.1 ms | 0.3 ms | `kty: AKP` |
| ML-DSA-87 | 6269 B | 0.5 ms | 0.3 ms | `kty: AKP` |

Performance is a non-issue — ML-DSA **verifies faster than RS256** (0.3 ms vs 0.5 ms), which matters because verification is the hot path across every service. Node does emit `ExperimentalWarning: The ML-DSA-65 Web Crypto API algorithm is an experimental feature and might change at any time`, so "available" is not yet "production-hardened" — that is the honest residue of the original refusal, and it is a risk to accept or wait out, not a missing capability.

**2. The blocker is the refresh-token COOKIE, and it is hard.** `generateRefreshToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts`) returns a **signed JWT** — payload carries userId, email, role, organizationId, verificationLevel, sessionId, type, tenantId, tenantSlug, scopes and jti — and `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:367,534,613` sets it as the `refresh_token` **cookie**. Browsers cap a single cookie at **4096 bytes**. An ML-DSA-65 JWT measured **4511 B on a three-field payload**; the real refresh payload is considerably larger. **The refresh token would not fit in its cookie.** ML-DSA-44 (3326 B minimal) would be marginal at best against the real payload.

That is a design change, not a parameter tweak — options are an opaque refresh token with server-side session lookup (the session service already mints `crypto.randomBytes(32)` opaque tokens at `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:133`, so the pattern exists in-tree), cookie chunking, or keeping refresh on RS256 while moving only the access token.

**3. Second constraint worth pricing before committing:** a ~4.5 KB bearer token travels on every request. nginx's default `large_client_header_buffers` is `4 8k`, so a 4.5 KB Authorization header plus cookies gets close enough to warrant explicit tuning at the gateway and on the VM's Caddy front.

**4. What does not change:** auth signs with `jsonwebtoken` 9.0.2, which has no ML-DSA support, so any hybrid rollout starts by moving auth's signing path to `jose`. Entra ID / CIAM stays RS256 and Microsoft-owned, as the ticket already notes.

**BLUF — not startable, and the blocker is upstream of us: no production-grade ML-DSA implementation exists for the JOSE/JWT stack we use. Sizing it now would be guessing.**

**Recommendation:** leave in Backlog and re-check when either `jose` ships ML-DSA natively or Node ships it in `crypto`. This is a watch item, not a queued piece of work.

**Detail**

1. **Phase 0 is done** — the crypto registry (KS-326) and runtime KMS key loading (KS-346) landed, so the abstraction this ticket plugs into exists. That part of "blocked by Phase 0" is cleared.
2. **The remaining blocker is the ticket's own first checkbox and it is external:** `jsonwebtoken` and `jose` do not ship ML-DSA. The options are a liboqs-node binding (native build, adds a compiled dependency to every service image — meaningful supply-chain and build-time cost for a platform that currently ships pure-JS crypto) or a WASM ML-DSA library (needs vetting we are not positioned to do). Neither is a decision to take casually to get ahead of a standard.
3. **The one genuinely actionable sub-item is small and independent:** confirming `obeden-ssd` does not hard-fail if Microsoft rotates Entra's token algorithm. That is a robustness check on someone else's timeline, not PQC migration, and it could be split out if you want any movement here.
4. **No deadline pressure identified:** nothing on the roadmap dates this, and RS256 remains current best practice for our threat model today. Harvest-now-decrypt-later matters for long-lived confidential data, not for short-lived signing keys on JWTs measured in minutes.

**Sizing: refuse to give one.** Any number would be dominated by the choice of an ML-DSA implementation that does not yet have an obvious answer — an estimate now would be a guess wearing a number.

title: Grant Phil + Steve extranet access (evolve toward company source of truth)
description:
Decision (2026-06-26 Stuart meeting): grant **Phil + Steve** extranet access so the extranet can evolve into a centralised, company-wide source of truth (beyond the dev team).

* Add per-person passcodes (`PASSCODE_PHIL`, `PASSCODE_STEVE` SWA app settings) + brief them.
* Could be a sub-task of **KS-146** (team onboarding) rather than fully standalone — link/consolidate as appropriate.

nodes.body:
## Sweep note — **the ticket says config-only; it is not. It needs a code change first.**

Not closing. Verified against the extranet **source** (`Secuura/secuura-extranet`), not its README.

## What the ticket assumes

> Add per-person passcodes (`PASSCODE_PHIL`, `PASSCODE_STEVE` SWA app settings) + brief them.

That reads as a configuration task — set two app settings, done.

## What the code actually does

`api/src/shared/auth.ts`:

```ts
/** The three people who can log in with a personal access code. */
export type Person = 'kam' | 'stuart' | 'peter';

export function personFromPasscode(code: string): Person | null {
  const map: Array<[Person, string | undefined]> = [
    ['kam',    process.env.PASSCODE_KAM],
    ['stuart', process.env.PASSCODE_STUART],
    ['peter',  process.env.PASSCODE_PETER],
  ];
  …
}
```

**The person list is hard-coded in three places** — the `Person` union type, the lookup map, and (downstream) every place that narrows on it. Setting `PASSCODE_PHIL` in the SWA config would do **nothing**: no code reads it, and `personFromPasscode` would return `null`, so Phil's code authenticates nobody.

## Revised shape of the work

1. **Code** — extend `Person` and the map (extranet repo, small PR + deploy; it auto-deploys on push to `main`).
2. **Config** — then set `PASSCODE_PHIL` / `PASSCODE_STEVE` as SWA app settings.
3. **Brief them** — as the ticket already says.

Also worth deciding as part of this, since the ticket's stated goal is *"evolve toward company source of truth"*: whether Phil and Steve get the **same** view as the dev team, or a read-mostly one. Today `Person` carries no role, so everyone who can log in can do everything. Adding people without answering that quietly widens write access to the board.

## Separate small defect found while checking

The extranet **README is stale and contradicts the code**: it states *"Humans — a single **shared passcode** … validates it against the `PORTAL_PASSCODE` app setting"*, and lists `PORTAL_PASSCODE` in its config table. The code has used **per-person** codes for some time. Anyone provisioning access from the README would set the wrong variable and conclude the portal is broken. Worth a one-line README fix alongside step 1.

*Backlog sweep 2026-08-14. Extranet is the declared coupled sibling of Platform K, so this was in scope to read.*

title: CI: require all systemTest (all tools) PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)
description:
## Goal

Make **every** systemTest PR suite **and** the pre-merge tests actually **block a merge on failure**. The workflow YAML already runs each suite to completion and then hard-fails its check (complete-then-block); what's missing is the **settings half** — a red check only prevents merge when branch protection marks it **Required**, and a check is matched by its **check-run display name**, not its job id. The pre-merge gate specifically must be a **manual human approval** (not an auto-pass).

## Background (already in place, code side)

`.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` (build-once → isolated per-suite stacks) runs each suite `continue-on-error` then an Enforce step fails the required check on any failure:

* **Schemathesis** — blocking spec-auth ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)) + pytest ([KS-126](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-126/schemathesis-pytest-suite-runs-only-ad-hoc-locally-wire-it-into-ci-dev)) + offline quality/unit gate; [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) auth sweep stays informational by design.
* **Playwright** — blocking `quality:check` + `npm run ci`.
* **Performance** — quality/unit gate + k6 smoke, complete-then-block.
* **Akto** — quality/unit gate + PR-gate scan, complete-then-block via step-outcome (emits Allure, not JUnit).

## Tasks (settings — cannot be code)

1. **Branch protection ruleset — mark these check-run display names Required** (match by display name, not job id):
   * `build`
   * `Schemathesis suite`
   * `Playwright suite`
   * `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`
   * `Akto suite (PR-gate subset)`
     Require `build` too — in the build-once topology a `build` failure **skips** the suite jobs, so confirm a required-but-skipped check does not wedge the PR (skipped ≠ stuck).
2. **Pre-merge must be a MANUAL human-approval gate — no auto-pass.** The comprehensive `run.py pre-merge` sweep (`pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`) must require a designated human to **manually click Approve** before the PR can merge; it must never pass on its own.
   * Implement via the GitHub `pre-merge-signoff` **Environment** with **required reviewers** (an Environment reviewer *is* a manual Approve/Reject gate): pin the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` job to that Environment so the run **pauses and waits** for a human decision, and no merge proceeds until a reviewer manually approves. GitHub → Settings → Environments → `pre-merge-signoff` → add required reviewers (start with @peter).
   * Mark the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` check **Required** in the branch-protection ruleset so the manual approval is enforced, not advisory.
   * Per CLAUDE.md, "PR checks green" is **not** the pre-merge sign-off — a human must have run/confirmed the comprehensive pre-merge sweep and then manually approved.

## Notes / carve-outs

* Two deliberate non-blocking exceptions stay as-is: the rate-limited [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) Schemathesis auth sweep (429 back-off would flap the gate) and **all nightly** runs (report-only soak).
* This ticket is GitHub **settings** work; no systemTest code change is required (the YAML is already complete-then-block, and the sign-off job already targets the `pre-merge-signoff` Environment — it just needs reviewers + to be Required). Verify on a draft PR: all five suite checks Required and red-on-failure blocks merge, and the merge stays blocked until a human manually approves the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate.

---

## Precondition: the pre-merge ack checkboxes have no not-applicable path (added 2026-09-09)

**Close this before** `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` **is set to** `true`**, or turning enforcement on will require a false attestation on any PR that legitimately needs neither suite.**

`.github/pull_request_template.md` seeds two boxes under the heading **"Pre-merge acknowledgment (author)"**, instructing: *"Tick each box **only after** you have run that suite's pre-merge tier and it passed"*. `.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml` ([KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling)) matches **only**:

```
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:schemathesis-->
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:akto-->
```

A tick, or nothing. No N/A marker, no label escape, no "suite not applicable" branch. So for an offline shell gate, a docs change or a workflow tweak, the only ways to satisfy the check are to tick a box asserting a sweep that did not happen, or to leave a box that reads as an omission.

**The exemption pattern already exists in that workflow** — drafts pass green unconditionally (`if [ "${DRAFT}" = "true" ]`). And the template models the right affordance one section down, in the PII block: *"Not applicable? Say so explicitly rather than leaving the boxes blank — a blank box reads as 'not checked', which is the state this section exists to make visible."* The ack section has no equivalent.

**How it surfaced.** PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) ([KS-778](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-778/preflight-leg-10s-pin-label-parser-is-blind-to-a-quoted-uses-and-an)) changes exactly one file — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/action-pins-labelled.sh`, an offline shell gate that reads `.github/` with `git grep` and prints to stdout. Measured: **0 of 1** changed files fall under `services/`, `frontend/`, `packages/`, `migrations/`, `contracts/`, `systemTest/`, any compose file or any `.env`, so neither pre-merge suite exercises anything in it. Both boxes were left unticked with the reason stated inline, following the PII section's pattern — a workaround, not a fix; the workflow still counts it as un-acknowledged.

**Not urgent today:** enforcement is soft by default (the repository Variable `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` is unset ⇒ warn + pass), and the workflow has not executed since 2026-08-17. It becomes live the moment task 2 above is actioned.

### Fix — one of these, not all

1. **An N/A marker** the workflow recognises, e.g. `<!--ack:schemathesis:na-->`, requiring a stated reason on the same line. Smallest, keeps the human in the loop, and mirrors the PII section so the template gains one convention rather than two. The assertion becomes "I considered this suite and it does not apply" — a true statement, still auditable.
2. **A label escape**, e.g. a `no-premerge-suites` PR label that passes both ack checks, reviewable in itself.
3. **A path-based skip** — passes when the diff touches nothing the suites cover. Most automatic, but duplicates suite-scope knowledge into the workflow and will drift.

### Done means

* A PR that legitimately needs neither suite passes both ack checks **without** anyone ticking a box that asserts an unrun sweep.
* The escape requires a stated reason — an acknowledgment, not a bypass. A blank body still fails.
* Red→green with `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK=true`: a PR using the new form passes; the same PR with the reason removed fails. Proven both ways.
* Template instruction text updated to describe the not-applicable path, in the shape the PII block already uses.
* Ticking a box still means what it says today — this must not weaken the positive assertion.

*Provenance: template and workflow read at* `dbe7ba6b3` *(PR* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) *head), 2026-09-09; last workflow execution 2026-08-17 via* `gh run list --workflow=pr-premerge-ack.yml`*; surfaced at [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/921#issuecomment-5602690418](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/921#issuecomment-5602690418>)*

## ⚠ STOPGAP WARNING — do not dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` yet: its job cap was not raised with its timeout

@stuart.jamieson @peter — **this is a relay of Peter's own finding, placed here rather than left on [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441), because this is the ticket whose execution actually triggers that workflow.** Task 2 of this ticket ends with *"Verify on a draft PR … the merge stays blocked until a human manually approves the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate."* **Whoever does that is the first person to dispatch pre-merge — and they will hit this.**

**Flagging it as a stopgap, deliberately. This comment is not the fix and should not be mistaken for one later.**

### The trap
`PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` was raised 1260 s → **3600 s** (`systemTest/akto/src/core/constants.ts:108`), but `Akto pre-merge (full)` still carries **`timeout-minutes: 30`** (`.github/workflows/pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:190`). Only the *PR* job's cap was raised (30 → 45).

**The arithmetic:**
- poll budget = 90% of 3600 s = **54 min**
- job cap = **30 min**
- → **the runner kills the job 24 minutes before the harness can report.**

And the constant's own comment extrapolates the pre-merge tier at **~2260 s ≈ 37.7 min**, which is **already over the 30-min cap** on its own. The pre-merge tier has **never run in CI**, so nothing has surfaced this.

### What it looks like when it bites
**A killed job at 30 minutes with no report and no artifact — which reads as a failure of the thing being tested, not as a cap that was never raised.** That is the expensive part: the first person to see it will reasonably start debugging the platform.

### What to do
**Either** raise the pre-merge Akto job to `timeout-minutes: 65` (54 min poll budget + stack boot + teardown) **in the same sitting** as your first dispatch, **or** don't dispatch until someone has. Peter's recorded fix is the 65 with the arithmetic written beside it.

### One more thing, because it will mislead you before you get here
**The docs still describe the old ceiling**, so reading them will actively confirm the wrong picture:

| File | Still says |
| -- | -- |
| `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1761` | `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 1260s`, *"while staying inside each Akto job's 30-min `timeout-minutes`"* |
| `systemTest/akto/docs/how_to_test_with_akto.md:211, 218` | `1260 s (21 min)` |
| `systemTest/akto/docs/how_to_test_with_akto.md:222` | *"keeping each Akto CI job inside its 30-minute `timeout-minutes` cap"* |
| `systemTest/akto/src/core/constants.ts:77, 86, 94, 100` | *"21 min ceiling"*, *"stays inside its 30-minute cap"* |

**All eight of those are now false**, verified against `origin/develop` @ `5f3cc8fef` on 2026-08-15. The value is 3600 s and it does **not** fit the cap. Peter has the full list on KS-441 and it is his to correct — **I have not touched any of it.**

### Provenance
Peter's post-merge review of PR #698, [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441) comment 2026-08-14T13:31Z, marked *"RECORDED, NOT ACTIONED"* — **items 1 and 2 are live on `develop` and no branch is open for them.** His words on this one: *"Do not dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` until this is fixed, or raise the cap in the same sitting."* I re-verified both line citations myself against `5f3cc8fef` rather than relaying them unchecked.

**The durable fix — making the workflow refuse or announce the mismatch when dispatched, instead of relying on people remembering this comment — is recorded as a separate decision and is not mine to make.**

**KS-413 merged to `develop`** (PR [#458](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/458), squash `7cffe434`). So everything in the "current state" section above is now **live on develop**: the renamed `Akto suite (PR)` check, the new `Akto pre-merge (full)` job, the `pr-premerge-ack.yml` checks (soft/green), the PR template checkboxes, and the `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` toggle.

This ticket's remaining scope is unchanged — the **"fully-enforced state" (section B)** is still to do: set `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK=true`, mark the three ack/Linear checks Required in ruleset 18499832 (develop+main), and bump required approving reviews 0 → 1.

## Full state — current vs. fully-enforced (2026-07-08)

Expands the previous comment. Everything is on PR [#458](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/458) (KS-413 branch, draft, not merged). The `require-pr-gates` ruleset (id **18499832**) targets **both `develop` and `main`**, so all ruleset changes below apply to both at once.

---

### A. CURRENT STATE (built; mostly OFF)

**Ruleset `require-pr-gates` — Required checks now (develop + main):**
- `build / Build + push platform images (fresh)`
- `Code Security Gates`
- `Standalone locks pass clean-room npm ci`
- `Schemathesis suite`
- `Playwright suite`
- `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`
- **`Akto suite (PR)`** ← renamed from `Akto suite (PR-gate subset)` (KS-413); repoint **done** on both branches
- Required approving reviews: **0**

**Built but NOT enforcing yet:**
- **Pre-merge tier checks** — `Schemathesis pre-merge sweep`, **`Akto pre-merge (full)`** — run only via `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`, which is **`workflow_dispatch`-disabled** (not per-PR). Not in the ruleset.
- **PR acknowledgment checks** (`.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml`, run on every PR): `Pre-merge acknowledged — Schemathesis`, `Pre-merge acknowledged — Akto`, `Linear ticket present`.
  - **SOFT** — repo Variable `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` is **unset**, so a missing checkbox / Linear ticket only **warns and passes green** (no red). **Drafts exempt.** Not in the ruleset.
- **PR template** (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) seeds the two acknowledgment checkboxes + a Linear line + a "run pre-merge" reminder.
- The Environment-based `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` jobs from this ticket's Task 2 were **removed** (replaced by the checkbox model).

**Net today:** a PR merges when the suite checks + Code Security Gates + lockfiles are green. **No** acknowledgment, **no** review, and **no** pre-merge run are required. (Same gating as before KS-413, plus the Akto check rename.)

---

### B. FULLY-ENFORCED STATE (target) — what to flip

1. **Turn the ack checks hard:** `gh variable set ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK --body true` → the three ack/Linear checks now **fail** on a missing box/ticket instead of warning.
2. **Mark them Required** in ruleset 18499832 (develop + main): `Pre-merge acknowledged — Schemathesis`, `Pre-merge acknowledged — Akto`, `Linear ticket present`.
3. **Require a review:** set the ruleset's `pull_request` rule `required_approving_review_count` **0 → 1** (any writer; CODEOWNERS deferred).

The pre-merge run is represented by the **author's acknowledgment checkbox** + the required review.

**Resulting merge requirements (enforced) — a PR into develop/main merges only when ALL of:**
- `build` + `Code Security Gates` + `Standalone locks…` green
- `Schemathesis suite`, `Playwright suite`, `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`, `Akto suite (PR)` green
- both pre-merge acknowledgment boxes ticked **and** a Linear ticket present (ack checks green)
- **≥ 1 approving review**
- (draft PRs can't merge; ack checks are exempt while draft)

**Model change vs. this ticket's original Task 2:** the "manual human confirmation that the pre-merge suites were run" is now split into **(a)** the author ticking the two acknowledgment checkboxes (confirms they ran Schemathesis + Akto pre-merge) and **(b)** a required reviewer approval — instead of a GitHub Environment reviewer on a `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` job. Acknowledgment is honor-system (verifies the box is ticked, not that the suite truly ran); accepted as convenience for now, can tighten later.

## Update — KS-413 supersedes parts of this ticket (2026-07-08)

Two things changed in [KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413) that make the tasks below partly stale. PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/458

### Task 1 — required check-run names (updated)
- **`Akto suite (PR-gate subset)` was renamed → `Akto suite (PR)`** (KS-413). The `require-pr-gates` ruleset on **develop** has **already been repointed** to `Akto suite (PR)` (old name removed) — done.
- A **new** blocking Akto check now exists at the pre-merge tier: **`Akto pre-merge (full)`** (`pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` → akto job, `npm run test:pre-merge`).
- So the required-check list should read: `build`, `Schemathesis suite`, `Playwright suite`, `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`, **`Akto suite (PR)`** (+ `Akto pre-merge (full)` where the pre-merge tier is required).

### Task 2 — pre-merge sign-off mechanism CHANGED (Environment reviewer → PR-description checkboxes)
The Environment-based `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` approach in this ticket was **removed** and replaced with an **author-acknowledgment-in-the-PR-description** model:
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` seeds two acknowledgment checkboxes (**Schemathesis**, **Akto**) + a Linear line + a pre-merge reminder.
- `.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml` enforces three checks: **`Pre-merge acknowledged — Schemathesis`**, **`Pre-merge acknowledged — Akto`**, **`Linear ticket present`** (fail until each box is ticked / a real Linear ticket is present; **drafts exempt**).
- The human "manual approval" half is now a **required PR review = 1 (any writer)** rather than an Environment reviewer. (CODEOWNERS deferred — anyone with write for now.)
- The two `pre-merge-signoff-*` Environment jobs and the interim YES/NO dropdown were reverted/removed.

Rationale: the checkbox is honor-system (verifies the box is ticked, not that the suite truly ran, and a description checkbox isn't author-attributed) — accepted as convenience for now; may tighten to a comment-based/author-attributed gate later.

### Still to do (settings only — the "enable" half)
Built but **non-blocking today** (Option A). To enforce, on the **develop AND main** rulesets:
1. Mark Required: `Pre-merge acknowledged — Schemathesis`, `Pre-merge acknowledged — Akto`, `Linear ticket present`, and `Akto pre-merge (full)`.
2. Turn on **required approving reviews = 1**.
(`Akto suite (PR)` on develop is already Required.)

**Scope addition — add an Akto _pre-merge_ blocking gate.**

The Akto PR scan is now **informational / non-blocking** (KS-413) because it's endpoint-bound and times out. That leaves Security Misconfiguration + the full OWASP set covered **only nightly (report-only)** — no blocking tier.

So the pre-merge gate this ticket enforces should also include **Akto**: a new blocking `akto` job in `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` (alongside the existing Schemathesis pre-merge sweep) that boots the platform + Akto stack and runs the full OWASP scan (`npm run test:security`) or an SM-focused subset. That gives SM/full-OWASP a **blocking** gate at pre-merge without slowing every PR.

- **Implementation** is tracked in **KS-413** (the new Akto pre-merge job, modelled on the Schemathesis pre-merge action).
- **This ticket (KS-412)** covers the enforcement half: once that job exists, its check-run must be **required** in branch protection for pre-merge (the same way this ticket already requires the four PR suites + the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate).

Updated pre-merge expectation: Schemathesis `pre-merge` sweep **+ Akto full/SM scan**, both blocking, behind the manual `pre-merge-signoff` approval.

title: systemTest (all tools): enable nightly platform test suites after full AWS migration
description:
## Reminder: re-enable the nightly system-test suites once we have fully migrated to AWS

The nightly platform test suites (Schemathesis, Playwright, Performance, Akto) are currently **disabled** — the workflow only runs on manual `workflow_dispatch`. They were prepared to run on a daily schedule but the `schedule:` cron is commented out pending the AWS migration.

### What to do when AWS migration is complete

1. In `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml`, **uncomment the** `schedule:` **block** to re-enable the daily trigger:

   ```yaml
   schedule:
     - cron: '0 14 * * *'   # 14:00 UTC — ~midnight Sydney, 22:00 Singapore
   ```
2. Re-point any `--env`/base-URL config from the local isolated stacks to the AWS targets if the nightly is meant to hit AWS rather than a fresh ghcr build.
3. Flip the STATUS header comment in the workflow back to **LIVE**.
4. Confirm the four suite check-runs appear and the shared `build` → fan-out topology still holds.

### Context

* Start time chosen: **14:00 UTC** (≈ midnight Sydney AEST/AEDT year-round, 22:00 Singapore SGT).
* All four suites already start **simultaneously** off the single schedule (each `needs: [prep, build]`), so enabling the one cron enables all four together.
* The Performance job runs a single isolated stack with all scenarios **serial**: smoke → auth-spike → (15m 429 cooldown) → smoke → spike → (15m) → smoke → stress → (15m) → smoke → scalability → (15m) → smoke → nightly soak (~4h4m). ⚠ ~5.9–6.1h total — near GitHub's 6h/job cap; re-check headroom on the AWS runners.
* Everything stays **report-only** (`continue-on-error`); no merge gating.
* Prepared on branch `feature/nightly-schedule-perf-sequence`.

## Review of PR #891 — the nightly-schedule wording, and this ticket's premise

Kam raised [PR #891](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/891) to correct the published claim that the nightly `schedule:` was *"DISABLED pending full AWS migration (KS-418)"*. Posting the review evidence here since it bears directly on this ticket.

**KS-418 itself is untouched by that PR** — deliberately so. Kam kept the ticket id out of the branch name (`docs/nightly-schedule-true-reason`) precisely so the Linear integration would not auto-transition it. That was a thoughtful call and it worked.

### What the PR corrects

Four sites said the schedule was waiting on an AWS migration, and that `workflow_dispatch` was the working fallback. Both halves turn out not to hold:

- **There is no Platform K AWS migration to wait on.** No AWS deployment target exists in the repo (`deployment/` holds `azure/`, `caddy/`, `cardano/`), and the demo runs on the Azure VM. Platform S did migrate to AWS — the citation appears to have travelled between the two platforms.
- **`workflow_dispatch` is not a fallback.** GitHub Actions is retired for this repo per Kam's 2026-08-27 ruling that the billing will not be fixed.

### Test evidence

| Workflow still parses | `yaml.safe_load` | PASS — keys `name`, `on`, `permissions`, `concurrency`, `jobs` |
| Behaviour unchanged | trigger set inspected | PASS — exactly `{workflow_dispatch}`; `schedule:` still commented out |
| Jobs intact | parsed job list | PASS — `prep`, `build`, `schemathesis-soak`, `playwright-nightly`, `performance-nightly`, `akto-security`, `integration` |
| Actions genuinely retired | `gh run list --limit 20`, run 2026-09-09 | PASS — 20/20 `startup_failure`, latest 2026-09-09 07:58Z |

**Not run, and why:** no unit suite, no platform suite, no build, no Docker stack, no `.env` work. Documentation and comments only — there is no runtime behaviour to sweep, so the live-stack requirement does not apply. **Migrations / config:** none.

### Addition pushed

I added one commit (`57a695de6`) carrying the same correction into the two platform-k HTML reference docs, which held the claim in three further places — the performance card, the k6 `<pre>` block and the pipeline-tier row in the cheat sheet, plus the Mermaid `FULL` node in the flow diagram. They had escaped the original `grep` because it searched for *"pending **full** AWS migration"* and these omit the word "full".

### What this means for KS-418 — for discussion, nothing changed yet

This ticket's title and description still carry the premise the PR corrects: *"enable nightly platform test suites after full AWS migration"*, with step 2 asking to re-point config at the AWS targets. On the evidence above there is no such migration pending, and the real blocker is that Actions is retired.

I have **not** rewritten anything here. Two sensible options when there is a moment:

1. **Re-frame** the ticket around *"re-enable the nightly suites if GitHub Actions is ever restored"*, keeping the cron and topology steps and dropping the AWS re-pointing step.
2. **Park it** as blocked-on-Actions, given the manual local-run process has replaced it.

Happy either way — flagging it so the ticket does not quietly keep asserting something the docs no longer do.

### Also left open

The cheat sheet still shows `✅ Live` badges against the PR gate in places. If Actions is retired repo-wide those read a little oddly for the same reason, but that is a broader question about how the PR tier is described rather than this PR's defect, so it was left alone.

## PR #891 is on origin at a new head — `3c07157a2` -> `721e5b773`

**BLUF: #891 was `dirty`; it is now `clean`. Landed by merging `develop` IN, not by rebasing — zero force pushes.**

- **Old head** `3c07157a2` -> **new head** `721e5b773`, a true fast-forward (`..`, not `+`)
- `mergeable_state` **dirty -> clean**
- **PREFLIGHT PASSED 13/13**
- The branch's own diff is unchanged: 4 files, 35 insertions, 16 deletions

### Why it read `dirty` — it was never a real conflict
`develop` **renamed** two of the files this PR touches (`how_to_test_secuura.md` -> `how-to-test-secuura.md`, `quick_start.md` -> `quick-start.md`). Git followed the renames and the merge applied with **no conflict at all**; the content is preserved byte-for-byte.

### One consequence, recorded because it is a fact about the PR, not a request
Peter's approval of 2026-09-08 sits at commit `3c07157a2`. The new head is `721e5b773`, so:

- the approval is **still recorded** and was **not dismissed**
- the approved commit `3c07157a2` **remains a reachable ancestor** — a force push would have orphaned it, which is one reason the merge route was chosen over rebasing
- but `commit_id != head.sha`, so by this repo's own standard it is **no longer at-head**

**Whether to seek a re-confirm is Kam's call.** Recording the state here so the ticket carries it; **nothing is being asked of anyone on this ticket.** Tracked with the wider at-head / withdrawn-approval problem on **KS-1035**.

## PR #891 reviewed and **approved** — the premise of this ticket has changed, and the docs now say so

[PR #891](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/891) (Kam) corrects four published passages that told a reader the nightly `schedule:` was *"DISABLED pending full AWS migration (KS-418)"* and that the workflow *"runs only on manual `workflow_dispatch`"*. Both halves were wrong, and the second was the costly one — it invited someone to press a button that cannot work.

I re-measured the claims independently rather than taking the PR body at its word. They hold.

### Test evidence — re-measured in a clean worktree, 2026-09-08

| Claim | Result | How it was checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No AWS deployment target in this repo | ✅ confirmed | `git ls-tree origin/develop Blockchain/Dev/deployment/` → `azure/`, `caddy/`, `cardano/`. No AWS path. |
| Kam ruled 2026-08-27 that Actions is retired | ✅ confirmed | `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` v3 footer, 27 August 2026 — records the ruling and replaces the earlier "suspended, not retired" framing. |
| 20 most recent runs are 100% `startup_failure` | ✅ confirmed | `gh run list --limit 20` re-run today: 20 of 20, still. |
| `DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents is a real destination | ✅ confirmed | Present at line 77, with the per-job local command map. |
| Behaviour unchanged | ✅ confirmed | On the merged tree the `schedule:` block is still commented out and the trigger set is still exactly `{workflow_dispatch}`. |
| Retirement corroborated beyond that PR | ✅ confirmed | KS-789, KS-910, KS-926, KS-1012 all rest on the same finding. |

**Merge check.** GitHub shows `CONFLICTING`, but that looks like a rename-detection artefact rather than a real clash — merging `origin/develop` into the branch locally returns exit 0, auto-merging all four files, with the edits landing correctly on the two docs `develop` renamed to kebab-case in the meantime. A plain `git merge develop` and push should clear it.

**Not run, and correctly so** — documentation and comments only, so no unit suite, no platform suite, no build and no Docker stack applies.

### What this means for this ticket

**The condition this ticket waits on does not exist.** There is no Platform K AWS migration to complete — Platform S migrated to AWS, this repo did not, and the demo runs on the Azure VM. The nightly is off because **GitHub Actions is retired for this repository**, which is a different situation with a different exit: the suites run locally now, per `DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents.

So the trigger for re-enabling the cron is no longer *"AWS migration complete"* — it is *"Actions restored"*, if that ever happens. The title and description here still carry the old framing and are mine to bring into line with the corrected docs.

### One small note for the record

The PR deliberately kept `ks-418` out of the branch name to avoid auto-transitioning this ticket, which was thoughtful. The `(KS-418)` in the PR **title** did it anyway — the integration moved this ticket `Todo → In Progress` at 04:18:00 on 7 September, three seconds after the PR opened. Worth knowing for next time: the branch-name precaution alone is not sufficient. I will set the state back myself.

Nothing here reflects on the change, which is accurate, carefully evidenced and carries no runtime risk.

title: Security review — plan, methodology & handover (Platform K)
description:
> **This issue is the coordination hub and living plan for the Platform K security review.** It holds the scope, threat model, methodology, the index of review work-streams, the evidence-cited findings register, remediation sequencing, and full handover context so anyone can pick this up cold. Modelled on the Platform S plan [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175).
>
> **v1 — grounded 2026-07-21 against** `develop` **@** `fcf2d878c` (161 commits since 2026-07-01). Register built from a 6-stream parallel recon (A–F); each finding cites `file:line` under `Blockchain/Dev/` on develop.

## 1. Target & threat context

* **System:** platform-k = the Secuura Cardano/blockchain anchoring platform. Node.js microservices monorepo (28 backend services: api-gateway, auth, originate, anchoring, timestamping, kyc, billing, analytics, m365-integration, tenant-provisioning, wallet-connector, nft-certificate, vc-issuer, security, governance, guardian, etc.), PostgreSQL/Prisma + RLS, Redis, Aiken smart contracts on Cardano, three React frontends (Issuer/Verifier/Admin) + Outlook/Gmail add-ins.
* **Code:** `Distributed_Secuura`, remote `github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git`, branch `develop`. Platform under `Blockchain/Dev/`.
* **Live env (2026-07-08,** [KS-414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-414/demo-env-cost-pivot-replace-container-apps-with-a-single-vm-running)): single Azure VM — Caddy auto-TLS → compose nginx gateway (`nginx-demo.conf`) at `https://demo-pk.secuura.net`. The Container Apps template + hardened `nginx-production.conf` are **decommissioned/unused**. **⚠ v1 claimed** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING=true` **in the demo. That is FALSE (corrected 2026-08-13).** The demo does **real** Cardano `preview`-testnet anchoring: `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is unset, `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` is set, anchoring boots `cardanoMode: REAL (Blockfrost)`, and a funded **platform wallet mnemonic is present on the VM**. Treat the anchoring path on the live target as a live chain-submission path with key material, not a simulation — see the re-grounding comment (2026-08-13) and KS-535 / KS-607.
* **Integrations:** platform-s (SSD document platform, the S↔K channel — K is the server), Stripe (billing), Microsoft 365 / Entra Verified-ID (KYC/IDV), M365 Graph (Outlook/Gmail add-ins), Cardano (Blockfrost).
* **Protects:** legally-significant artefacts (on-chain anchors, timestamps, VCs/NFTs, document hashes), PII, org/tenant data, payment flows, per-tenant connector credentials.
* **Threat assumptions:** millions of users, high public profile, under continuous attack. Treat availability, tenant isolation, and **anchor/signature integrity** as first-order.

## 2. Objectives

1. Evidence-cited findings register (`file:line`, severity) across the whole attack surface — kept current with develop.
2. Prioritised, **sequenced** remediation issues with owners and acceptance criteria (see §5).
3. Strategic hardening for scale — WAF, bot/anti-automation, edge rate-limits/body-caps, secret manager at runtime, DDoS protection, observability/alerting.
4. Repeatable security gates (make the report-only CI scans blocking; keep the [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) audit-gate + lockfile clean-room green) so posture doesn't regress.
5. A **security regression test** for every confirmed finding, in the right harness (systemTest — schemathesis / Akto / cross-tenant-isolation / Playwright).

## 3. Scope & review work-streams

Recon streams A–F are **complete** (this v1 pass). Work-stream owners: **Kamil** for A–F + H; **Peter** for G (systemTest).

> **Table amended 2026-08-13** — the v1 table showed six streams all reading "Recon done", which had drifted from the board in both directions and **omitted Review H entirely** (created by comment on 2026-07-21, closed 2026-08-02). A wrong index costs every future reader. `Status` below is the live Linear state; `Recon` records whether the v1 recon pass covered it.

| \# | Work-stream | Issue | Owner | Recon | Status (live 2026-08-13) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A | AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR | [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| B | Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto | [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| C | S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations (M365 / KYC / wallet / email) | [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| D | Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity | [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| E | Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain | [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| F | Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation | [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491) | Kamil | done | **Todo — IN PROGRESS 2026-08-13** (untouched 07-21 → 08-13) |
| **G** | **systemTest security regression coverage** | [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492) | **Peter** | n/a | Standing (Todo) |
| **H** | **Dependency currency & known-vuln package upgrades** | [KS-493](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-493) | Kamil | done (pass-2) | ✅ **Done 2026-08-02** |

**Deferred as its own sequenced pass:** re-recon of streams A–F against the 168 commits / 202 changed files landed since v1's baseline `fcf2d878c`. Tracked as [KS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-612) (child of this issue) — this re-grounding refreshed the *plan*, not the findings.

## 4. Methodology

Recon → findings register (severity-rated, evidence-cited, mapped loosely to OWASP ASVS / Top 10) → triage (severity × exploitability × blast-radius-at-scale) → sequenced remediation issues with acceptance criteria → verification (reproduce pre-fix, confirm blocked post-fix, add a systemTest regression). **Re-ground the register against develop whenever the branch has materially moved** (the [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s) v2 pass is the template).

## 5. Findings register + remediation sequencing

**Legend:** Sev = severity as found on develop @ `fcf2d878c`. All rows cite `Blockchain/Dev/…`. Full evidence + GREEN notes live on each work-stream issue.

### A — AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242-272` | `POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body, no self/admin check → spoofed `security`/`system` notifications w/ `actionUrl` to anyone (in-app phishing / BOLA). |
| Med | `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:173-205`; transfer `routes/documents.ts:1318` | Documents scoped by `tenant_id` only, never `owner_user_id` — any user in a tenant can read/mutate/transfer another user's doc. Confirm intended tenant==org boundary. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/index.ts:220-227`; `routes/documents.ts:131-133` | Tenant scope derived from inbound `x-tenant-id`; originate JWT has no `tenantId` to cross-check → pure header trust. Safe only via gateway strip + RLS; header-forwarding/SSRF re-opens [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug)-class cross-tenant read. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/routes/mfa.ts:225-236` | `mfa/verify` validates TOTP with no proof factor-1 passed (standalone TOTP oracle; issues no tokens). |
| Low | gateway `middleware/auth.ts:106-150` vs auth `middleware/authenticate.ts:19-65` | `test_token_*` backdoor guarded asymmetrically — one mis-set env = role/tenant spoof. |

### B — Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto — [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:1072,1202` | Teams `webhookUrl` validated only by `z.string().url()` — no SSRF guard; `fetch()` to `169.254.169.254`/RFC1918/localhost. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:153-205,455-490` | `validateWebhookUrl` blocks only IP literals (no DNS resolution → DNS-rebind) and only at registration, not send time. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1769-1773` (+`:36`) | `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` mints ORG_ADMIN/OWNER w/ hardcoded `admin123`; no `NODE_ENV`/`ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` gate. |
| Med | `services/kyc/src/index.ts:251` | ID images stored from caller-supplied `mimeType`, no magic-byte verification. |
| Low | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/taskpane/index.tsx:60` | `el.innerHTML` interpolates `${e.message}` — unescaped sink (error path). |

### C — S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations — [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts:201` | Callback authed by static `api-key` w/ hardcoded default `'secuura-kyc-callback'` → forge Entra Verified-ID results. |
| High | `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts:246-259` | `POST /api/wallets/verify` is a stub — always `verified:true`. Wallet-ownership proof fully bypassable. |
| Med | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:138-161,235-243` | Graph access+refresh tokens persisted to Postgres in plaintext. |
| Med | `services/billing/src/routes/webhooks.ts:34-37` | `isEventProcessed` fails **open** on DB-unavailable → redelivered Stripe event re-adds credits. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/services/email.ts:40-45,148-149` | No CRLF sanitisation on `documentTitle`→`subject`; no recipient-domain allow-list. |
| Low | `frontend/gmail-addon/Code.gs:17-18` | Hardcoded to decommissioned Container Apps URLs (stale). |

### D — Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity — [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:582-593` | On anchoring-POST failure with `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` unset (**default**), fabricates `tx_sim_…` + `status:'anchored'` — outage → fake anchored doc. No `NODE_ENV` guard. |
| Med | `services/timestamping/src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:305-325` | TSA error/timeout → `success:true` self-generated `mock:true` token for eIDAS/UETA artefacts. |
| Med | `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts:38-50` | First non-null Blockfrost `getTransaction` → `confirmed:true`; no finality threshold. |
| Med | `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:982-1041` | `verify` derives `verified:true` from local DB row only; single anchors get no chain re-fetch/hash compare. |

### E — Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain — [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:61` (repeated) | 32-char `APP_DB_PASSWORD` literal committed as `:-default` across **51** conn strings — `grep -c 'APP_DB_PASSWORD:-' Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` at the grounding SHA `fcf2d878c` **and** at develop `87384a8ba` (2026-09-06); the original "\~20" was wrong when written, not drifted. See comment `ef553d29`. |
| High | `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml:99,112,134,138,272,298` | Trivy/Gitleaks/Semgrep/Checkov all `continue-on-error` → report-only, can't block a merge. |
| Med | `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:365-366,369,377` | KV secrets → `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` unmasked + inlined into `DATABASE_URL`. |
| Med | `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:64,119` | Postgres (`:6432`) + Redis (`:6379`) publish to host by default. |
| Med | root `package-lock.json` axios 1.16.1; kyc 1.15.2; mobile 1.13.2 | Stale-lock axios drift vs 1.18.1 (other advisories already patched — axios is the only live drift). [KS-420](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-420/dependency-and-tooling-version-hygiene-audit-from-clean-rebuild) #6. |
| Low | all `services/*/Dockerfile`, `frontend/*` | Base images tag- not digest-pinned; `auth/Dockerfile:46` ships build tooling in runtime layer. |

### F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation — [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere (Cloudflare DNS-only). Product owner wants WAF — greenfield. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` | Live gateway has no `limit_req`/`client_max_body_size`; hardened `nginx-production.conf` is decommissioned-path only. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | Real TLS edge (Caddy on VM) not version-controlled. |
| High | repo-wide absent | No CAPTCHA/Turnstile on signup/login/verify. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on Redis error ([KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |

### Remediation sequencing (amplifier-first)

* **Wave 1 — active exposure + one-liners:** ungated `seed-demo-users` (B), KYC callback default-secret (C), wallet-verify stub (C), committed `APP_DB_PASSWORD` + lock pg/redis to internal (E/F), make CI scan gates blocking (E).
* **Wave 2 — integrity criticals (K's crown jewels):** anchor-fabrication-on-outage + `NODE_ENV` guard (D), qualified-TSA mock fallback (D), verify-against-chain not DB (D), finality threshold (D), m365 SSRF + originate webhook DNS-rebind/send-time revalidation (B).
* **Wave 3 — authz/tenancy hardening:** notification BOLA (A), document owner-scoping decision + fix (A), close header-trust tenancy path / add JWT `tenantId` cross-check (A), M365 token encryption at rest (C), billing idempotency fail-closed (C).
* **Wave 4 — edge & strategic (scale):** WAF at the edge (F), bot/anti-automation (F), version-control the Caddy edge + port `nginx-production.conf` rate-limits/body-caps/headers to the live conf (F/E), runtime secret manager on the VM (E), observability/alerting (F).
* **Wave 5 — hygiene backlog:** axios lockfile regen (E, [KS-420](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-420/dependency-and-tooling-version-hygiene-audit-from-clean-rebuild) #6), digest-pin base images + drop build tooling from auth runtime (E), MFA-verify factor-1 binding + test-token env symmetry (A), email CRLF/allow-list + gmail-addon dead URLs (C).

## 6. Handover / continuity

* **Grounded against** `develop` @ `fcf2d878c` (2026-07-21). All findings cite `file:line` under `Blockchain/Dev/`.
* **Owners:** Kamil (A–F remediation); Peter (G / all systemTest security work — per project convention).
* **Live env reality:** the demo runs on a single VM (Caddy → `nginx-demo.conf`), **not** the Container Apps template — treat `nginx-production.conf` as an unused hardening template, not today's edge. See `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`.

@peter

**What shipped**

- **Rollback tags:** `pre-20261029k9` (kintsugi) and `pre-20261029d9` (demo), 33 images each.

**Security-relevant changes**

1. **Role folding (KS-1591):** `isPlatformRole` and the security service's `requireKeyAdmin` now fold a role with an ASCII-only upper-case and refuse a role that is not a string. A dotless i, a long s or a role array no longer reads as an admin role.
2. **Error classes (KS-1467):** `AppError` subclasses now keep their own prototype, in `packages/shared` and in auth, so `instanceof` on a subclass works. A weak-password 422 now carries `details`.
3. **Timeouts (KS-1240):** every hand-built api-gateway fetch, the 12 auth social-provider fetches, the nft-certificate IPFS fetches and tenant creation's two outbound calls are now bounded. An API key the gateway cannot verify answers 503, not a cached 401.
4. **OAuth authorize (KS-1219):** a non-string `scope` answers 400, not 500.
5. **Hostile throws (KS-1780):** the system-errors list and `extractPgCode` no longer hang a request when the thrown value cannot be inspected.
6. **m365 redirect (KS-1670, site 1):** the success redirect now encodes the connection id.
7. **Behaviour-preserving:** issuerCerts' admin-role test is one helper (KS-1536); an adminConfig lint fix (KS-1779).

**Not observed live:** none of the above was exercised on the boxes; that needs sign-ins, writes or a failing dependency, and none was done. Each change is checked in the running images by its own strings, rollback image against new image, on both boxes.

**No migration ran:** the tracker reads 56 rows, max `055`, on both boxes, and there is no `.sql` in the delta. **No secret or config change:** the `.env` hash is identical before and after on both boxes. `secuura-demo-service` is stopped on both boxes, per Kam's 2026-09-05 ruling.

**Not swept:** authenticated paths.

No action needed. Pull `develop` when it suits you.

Until this deploy, the gateway's own `POST /api/documents` from a caller in a non-default tenant was filed under the default tenant. `GET /api/signatories` and `GET /api/third-party-verifiers` read the default tenant's rows for such a caller. **The one worth knowing about (#1651, KS-1682).** `exchangeAuthCode` was taking the **first** refresh token out of a token cache that is shared by the whole process. Once two organisations had connected within one process lifetime, the second organisation's connection stored the **first** organisation's refresh token, and from its first refresh onward read the first organisation's Microsoft 365 as its own. **No attacker and no leaked id was needed — two organisations connecting normally was enough.** The connection's first *access* token was its own, so the swap only showed about an hour later, which is why a demo would never reveal it.

It now selects on the signing-in account and **stores nothing** when that cannot be determined, rather than guessing. A connection with no stored refresh token answers `400 "No refresh token available"` and needs a fresh sign-in — visible and recoverable, which another organisation's credential is not.

> | Path | CSP served? | Distinguishing directive |
> | -- | -- | -- |
> | `/` (issuer) | **yes** | `script-src … 'unsafe-eval'` — issuer only |
> | `/admin/` | **yes** | `connect-src … wss://*.secuura.io` — admin only |
> | `/verify/` | **yes** | `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.secuura.io https://secuura.io` |
>
> **They differ from one another, and that difference is the discriminator.** A single `add_header` at the gateway would make all three byte-identical. Control: `/api/health` returns a **fourth, different** CSP from the API service — so a CSP on this host is not a gateway-wide artefact.
>
> Source side agrees: **8** `Content-Security-Policy` occurrences across `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin,outlook-addin}/nginx.conf`, and the gateway does **not** `proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy`, so downstream policies pass through untouched. It *does* hide-and-re-add `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and HSTS — which is why those five are gateway-owned and CSP is not. The file is internally consistent.
>
> ### 2. The gateway's abstention is a decision, and it is NEWER than this row
>
> `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf:240-245`, immediately above the live header block:
>
> > *"CSP is DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE. It is app-specific — issuer, admin and verifier each ship their own — and a single generic policy at the gateway would either be too loose to be worth having or would break a portal. Owning it here would also silently override a tighter downstream policy. That stays with the apps; tracked as its own decision, not smuggled in."*
>
> `git log -S"DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE"` attributes it to exactly one commit — `045c658ec`**, 2026-08-13, "KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge…" (#678)** — the same hardening pass that fixed F-2, F-6 and F-7. Sentinel control returns empty. **The missing gateway CSP is not an oversight this review caught; it is a decision the F-remediation took afterwards, in writing.**
>
> ### 3. Why "just add one" is actively harmful, not merely redundant
>
> Two `Content-Security-Policy` headers are **not merged**. Each policy is enforced independently, so a resource must satisfy **both** — the effective policy is the **intersection**. Intersecting the commented-out `:595` policy against what admin actually serves:
>
> | directive | `:595` policy | admin's live policy | effective | consequence |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `connect-src` | `'self' https://*.blockfrost.io` | `'self' http://localhost:* https://*.secuura.io wss://*.secuura.io` | `'self'` | **admin's XHR/WebSocket blocked** |
> | `script-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` | `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` | `'self'` | **wasm blocked, all three portals** |
> | `img-src` | `'self' data: https:` | `'self' data: https: blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob images blocked** |
> | `worker-src` | absent → falls back to `script-src` | `'self' blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob workers blocked** |
>
> That is the portal-breaking outcome the in-file comment predicts, arrived at independently.
>
> ### 4. Recorded so it is not re-derived
>
> Two things stated explicitly because a later reader will otherwise repeat the work:
>
> * `frame-ancestors` **is NOT part of the breakage.** It does not fall back to `default-src`, so an unspecified `frame-ancestors` in a gateway policy leaves each portal's own value governing. An earlier note of mine claimed otherwise; it was wrong and the four rows above stand without it.
> * `outlook-addin` **is not routed through this gateway** (0 matches for `outlook` in `nginx-demo.conf`), so its policy is unaffected either way.
>

> The policies exist and are well-formed, but two directives are weak: `'unsafe-eval'` **on the issuer alone** (the other two manage on `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) and `'unsafe-inline'` **styles on all three**. That is an app-level quality question, exactly as the in-file comment says — filed as [KS-648](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-648), Low, in the Security Review project. **Not** part of F-9.

## Small finding for this register: the gateway sends `Server: nginx` on every route (LOW)

Recording it here as the edge/WAF work-stream's home. It came up in the Akto OWASP scan during KS-1286 (Akto 2.35.6, slot 2, 2026-09-28, template `UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS`) — the only finding in a 50,162-result full run.

>>> Scope, why config alone can't remove it, and options

**Scope:** information disclosure (product fingerprinting). Akto flagged one endpoint, but the gateway sets the header, so it's every route. On slot 2:

| route | response |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` | `401`, `Server: nginx` |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | `Server: nginx` |
| `GET /health/deep` | `Server: nginx` |
| `GET /` | `Server: nginx` |

**What's already in place:** all three gateway configs set `server_tokens off` (`nginx-demo.conf:196`, `nginx-production.conf:288`, `nginx.conf:24`), which hides the version — the part that maps to CVEs. Removing the product name as well needs the `headers-more` module (`more_clear_headers Server;`), which the base image doesn't include: `Dockerfile:1` is `FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine`, `nginx -V` shows no `headers-more`, and none of the three confs uses `more_*`.

So it isn't a false positive, and there isn't a one-line config fix.

**Options, for whoever takes it**

1. An nginx build with `headers-more`, then `more_clear_headers Server;` (a non-stock base image).
2. Strip it one layer up — Caddy on the VM demo, or the ingress on the Container Apps template.
3. Accept and record it — a fingerprinting nuisance rather than an exploitable weakness.

**Effect on the scan gate:** while it stands, the full-OWASP tier FAILs by design (any severity counts), so `test:security` is red on an otherwise clean run. Worth knowing before reading that red as a regression. Cross-referenced on KS-1286.
