**Net:** F's four code-fixable findings are fixed on develop (KS-613/614/615/616); F-7/F-8 addressed; F-1 + F-5 stay Kam-gated. The whole non-F-3 set is Kintsugi-gated for the live demo.

**RE-VERIFICATION + REMEDIATION FILING — 2026-08-13, `develop` @ `b3042a5eb`. Recon was done 2026-07-21 @ `fcf2d878c`; this stream had been untouched for 23 days and had zero remediation issues filed, which is why nothing had moved.**

## BLUF

All eight v1 findings **re-verified against the current tree and the live VM**. Every one still stands. Two changed materially: **F-4 is worse than v1 recorded**, and **F-6 is half-fixed in a way that reads as fully fixed**. Five remediation issues filed — this stream's acceptance asked for them and they did not exist.

## Verification table

| # | v1 finding | Sev | Verified 2026-08-13 | Tracked |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| F-1 | No WAF anywhere | Crit (strategic) | **CONFIRMED** — repo-wide search still finds no ModSecurity/CRS/Front Door WAF | **needs Kam** (product + spend) |
| F-2 | Live gateway conf has no rate-limit / body cap | High | **CONFIRMED** — measured `nginx-demo.conf`: `limit_req` **0**, `limit_conn` **0**, `client_max_body_size` **0** | **[KS-613](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-613)** |
| F-3 | Caddyfile not version-controlled | High | **CONFIRMED** — still absent (the 2 repo hits are Akto test-library fixtures, not our config) | **[KS-615](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-615)** |
| F-4 | pg/redis published to `0.0.0.0` | High | **CONFIRMED and UPGRADED** — see below | **[KS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-614)** |
| F-5 | No CAPTCHA on signup/login/verify | High | **CONFIRMED** — no recaptcha/hcaptcha/turnstile anywhere in services or frontends | **needs Kam** (product) |
| F-6 | Limiter fails open; per-replica counters | Med | **HALF-FIXED — see below** | **[KS-616](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-616)** |
| F-7 | No Slowloris / slow-request protection | Med | **CONFIRMED** — no `client_body_timeout` / `client_header_timeout` on the live conf | folded into KS-613 |
| F-8 | Gateway emits no security headers | Low | **CONFIRMED, with a nuance that matters** — see below | folded into KS-613 |

## F-4 — worse than "relies on an external firewall"

v1 hedged that the NSG/ufw might cover it. Measured on the VM today:

- `ss -lntp` → `LISTEN 0.0.0.0:6432` and `LISTEN 0.0.0.0:6379` (plus `[::]`), via docker-proxy.
- `ufw status` → **inactive**.
- `iptables -S DOCKER-USER` → **`-N DOCKER-USER` only — zero rules**.
- So **there is no host firewall of any kind**. The sole control is NSG `secuura02-demo-vmNSG`: three inbound allows (22 / 80 / 443) plus Azure's implicit `DenyAllInBound`.

Confirmed from outside: 6432 / 6379 / 5432 / 6882 filtered; 443 and 22 answer. So **nothing is exposed right now** — but it rests on one Azure rule that is not in version control, and Docker's published ports are specifically the thing that bypasses a host firewall, so anyone later "hardening the box" with ufw would get a false sense of safety.

## F-6 — the half that survived its own ticket

v1 cited [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170) for this finding, and **KS-170 is Done** — so F-6 reads as resolved. It is not. KS-170 fixed the per-replica counters; the **fail-open** half is still in `rateLimitEnforce.ts`:

```js
} catch (err) {
  // Rate limit check failed — allow the request (fail open)
  next();
}
```

An error in the limiter allows the request with **no limiting at all**, silently, precisely under the load that makes Redis wobble. Split out as KS-616 — otherwise it disappears with its closed parent.

## F-8 — do not close this on a live `curl`

`https://demo-pk.secuura.net/` **does** serve a full header set today: CSP, HSTS `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, nosniff, referrer-policy, permissions-policy. Anyone spot-checking would call F-8 fixed.

It is not: those come from **downstream** frontend nginx/helmet. In `nginx-demo.conf` all six security `add_header` lines are **commented out** (lines 413–420); the only live one is an `Allow` header on an internal 405 block. So the guarantee holds today and is one forgotten helmet away from not holding — exactly what v1 said.

## Also worth recording

`nginx-production.conf` — the hardened conf with the 10r/s limits and `client_max_body_size 10m` — was written for the **Container Apps** path, which was deleted 2026-07-31. **It has never run in production and runs nowhere today.** A hardened config that applies to nothing reads, at a glance, as protection that exists. KS-613 includes deciding its fate: fold in or delete.

## What is NOT done

- **F-1 (WAF)** and **F-5 (CAPTCHA)** are product/spend decisions, not engineering defects — flagged for Kam rather than filed with an owner and an invented deadline.
- No changes made to any config. This pass verified and filed; the fixes are in the child issues.
- Re-recon of the 168 commits since v1 remains **[KS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-612)**.

All checks read-only — repo greps, `ss`/`ufw`/`iptables` reads over SSH, outbound port probes, and `az network nsg rule list`. Nothing written to the VM; Kintsugi hold intact. Azure tenant verified as Founders Hub `efc17e5f-…` before any `az` call.

## ⚠ New gap found 2026-08-14 — anti-automation has ZERO coverage

Found during the [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441/akto-ci-scan-throughput-21-s-local-vs-10-min-in-the-isolated-pr-akto) Akto throughput investigation (**report attached above**, §7). Two independent measurements, both pointing the same way:

* The **login brute-force limiter is disabled in CI *and* on the VM**, so nothing exercises it.
* Akto's rate-limiting family produces **969 results, 100% not-applicable, zero executed** — which renders in the report as "0 vulnerable", indistinguishable from a pass.

**A regression removing brute-force protection would ship green today.** This is exactly the MUST #13 rule-6 shape: a check whose input is missing scoring as clean rather than red.

A regression test has been added and **proven red** (`tests/test_login_rate_limit.py` + the pure helper `tests/support/login_rate_limit.py`, offline-unit-tested). **Green is blocked** by a harness gap, not a platform one: `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` never passes `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT` through to the gateway, so the limiter cannot be turned on for the test. Fixing that passthrough is the next step and is the only thing standing between this row and ✅.

Also relevant to how this register should be read: **Akto verdicts are non-deterministic** (same template/endpoint/session returned clean, clean, HIGH, clean, HIGH; three scans with identical 1,615-result coverage returned `vulnerable` 1, 0, 0). Treat Akto as discovery, not acceptance — a green Akto row is not evidence a finding is fixed.

## ✅ Landed

**Cross-tenant / cross-owner document isolation — the A (BUG-ISOLATION-001-class) case (**[KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions), PR **#590, merged to** `develop`**)** — extended the `@pytest.mark.isolation` suite beyond the read-only vector to: cross-tenant **mutate** (revoke → 404) + **transfer-custody** (404) under a foreign `X-Tenant-Override`; **forged** `x-tenant-id` header stripped by the gateway (context unchanged); **api-key** list/revoke isolation (folds `repro-api-keys.sh`); and **cross-owner** read (404)/revoke (403) within one tenant. Pure predicates in `tests/support/tenant_isolation.py` unit-tested offline; split into siblings (`test_tenant_isolation_writes.py`, `test_cross_owner_isolation.py`) under the file-size cap. All **pass** (no `xfail`) — each targets an already owner-/tenant-scoped route. QA docs synced. **Only systemTest tests were added — backend owner-scoping/header-trust remediation stays in Review A /** [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor)\*\*, Kamil.\*\*

**Six schemathesis A/B/C regressions (PR #585, merged to** `develop`**)** — all **report-only** (`xfail(strict=False)`/`skip`) in the pre-merge/nightly integration suite: notification BOLA, webhook-SSRF (existing-guard + DNS-rebind), seed-demo, wallet-verify, KYC-callback (passing guard), billing idempotency. QA docs synced. The spec-auth conformance sweep already lives in preflight ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)).

Anchoring-integrity Integration mode — the D cases ([KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489/review-d-blockchain-anchoring-smart-contract-integrity)-D, PR #588) — landed in the anchoring-integrity suite co-located in `systemTest/schemathesis` (run via `run.py integration`, also inside pre-merge/nightly): `test_anchoring_fail_closed.py` + `test_tsa_mock_fallback.py` (fail-closed asserts **pass**; an `xfail` for the missing qualified-vs-mock signal) and `test_anchor_verify_no_fabrication.py` (chain-verify-never-fabricates **passes**; an `xfail` for the honest-labelling gap). **Only systemTest tests were added — the backend tests are Kamil's and were not touched.**

## ✅ Child tickets closed (systemTest test-writing complete)

* [KS-502](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-502/systemtest-schemathesis-skipped-security-regressions-needing-a-proper) **Done** — the skipped schemathesis regressions (billing idempotency, seed-demo prod-gate, webhook-SSRF send-time + m365 sink) are documented with exactly what harness/env each needs; the DNS-rebind portion landed as `xfail`. Green-flip is backend/env-driven and spins out as a separate PR.
* [KS-507](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-507/systemtest-de-flake-the-3-timingrate-limit-skipped-schemathesis-pytest) **Done** — the 3 timing/rate-limit `skip` sites (undeclared-method 429, anchor/export polling) tracked for de-flaking.
* [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) **Done** — cross-tenant/cross-owner document isolation regressions (PR #590). The "Document owner-scoping + header-trust (A)" coverage row is now ✅.

## ⬜ Still to fix (open work — systemTest only)

1. **Flip the report-only tests green** — each `xfail`/`skip` (notification BOLA, wallet verify, webhook DNS-rebind, KYC code-residual, seed-demo, billing idempotency, + the two anchor `xfail`s: missing qualified-vs-mock signal, honest-labelling of simulated anchors) becomes a hard pass only when its **A–F platform remediation / prod-like env** ships. That is **backend work owned by Kamil** under the Platform K review work-streams — tracked in his tickets, not here; the flip lands as a separate backend PR, at which point G un-marks the `xfail`/`skip`.
2. **Fix the** `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT` **passthrough in** `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` so the new anti-automation regression can run green. The test exists and is red; only the harness wiring is missing. (2026-08-14, PR #698.)
3. ~~**Document owner-scoping + header-trust (A)**~~ — ✅ **Done** ([KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions), PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#590](https://linear.app/secuura/review/testsystemtest-ks-513-cross-tenantcross-owner-document-isolation-0fabfbd1cef6) merged). Cross-tenant mutate/transfer-custody, cross-owner read/revoke within a tenant, forged `x-tenant-id`, and api-key isolation all landed as passing regressions. (Backend owner-scoping/header-trust remediation is Review A — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor), Kamil — not tracked here.)
4. **Other harnesses under G** — Akto OWASP re-baseline ([KS-395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-395/validate-weekend-platform-fixes-akto-owasp-security-scan) pattern) and Playwright UI-level auth/admin-gating/XSS: **not started**.
5. **S↔K connector-identity regressions (**[KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks)**)** — the only rows of the [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) data-loss register that land in G: #16 provenance never on-chain and #17 erasure pseudonymises. [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) was closed 2026-09-14 with every row dispositioned (K-side residue [KS-532](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532/sk-dr-k-side-key-store-restore-path-joint-restore-point-coverage-demo) / [KS-581](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-581/register-connector-volume-alerting-rate-limit-and-correlation-of), Kam); these two are Peter's and are **blocked on** [KS-516](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516/schemathesis-systemtest-seed-a-real-sk-api-key-documentswrite-so-the) seeding two real `sk_` keys (provisioning + operational). Not started.

## Method

For each confirmed finding: (1) write a test that **reproduces** it pre-fix (red), (2) land it alongside the remediation so it goes green, (3) keep it in the pre-merge tier so regressions fail fast. Follow `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` standards; **local commits only — no GitHub push/PR/issue interaction for any systemTest change** unless explicitly instructed, and use `KS-###` / `akto#NNNN` text refs, never GitHub issue URLs.

## The exact case to add

The drift this must catch is **an attribution regression that is invisible at the HTTP layer** — every request below returns a normal 2xx whether or not the provenance row is written, which is precisely why it went unnoticed for the whole life of KS-566. The assertion has to be on the **row**, not the response.

Against a connector (`sk_`) key:

| # | request | must assert |
| - | - | - |
| 1 | `POST /documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` **without** `onBehalfOf` | **201**, and exactly **one** new `action_provenance` row: `action = 'lifecycle:<verb>'`, `connector_id` set, and `email_enc` / `display_name_enc` / `email_hash` / `external_ref` / `resolved_user_id` **all NULL** |
| 2 | same **with** `onBehalfOf` | **201, not 400** — the field is ignored, not rejected (S is live sending it, PS-616) — and the row is the **same connector-only shape** |
| 3 | `POST /api/anchors` (flat) **without** `onBehalfOf` | **202**, exactly **one** new row, `action = 'anchor'`, same connector-only shape |
| 4 | `POST /api/anchors` **with** `onBehalfOf` | **202**, field stripped, same single connector-only row |
| 5 | `POST /documents/{id}/revoke` **with** `onBehalfOf` as a connector | one `revoke` row **with** the PII columns populated (the onBehalfOf pattern) — see the caveat below |
| 6 | **negative control** — a JWT human sending `onBehalfOf` on revoke | **400 `onBehalfOf is connector-only`** |

**The regression this actually guards:** if someone later re-gates the provenance write on `data.onBehalfOf` instead of the caller's role, cases 1 and 3 silently write **zero** rows and every HTTP assertion still passes. A count assertion is the only thing that catches it.

**Case 5 caveat, so you do not write a test that cannot pass:** a connector currently gets **403 "Only the owner can revoke this document"** — the ownership gate compares `document.owner?.id` to `user.id`, and a connector principal is never an owner UUID. Measured live, with controls (owning human → 200; human sending `onBehalfOf` → 400). So case 5 asserts the row **and** the 403 until that gate is decided; it is flagged on KS-566 §3 as needing a call from you, Stuart and Kam.

## One extra case worth having, from something #742 found by measuring

Making the flat-anchor provenance role-gated instead of field-gated made K's own `originate → anchoring` hops record a **second** row — one lifecycle call produced both a `lifecycle:rename` **and** an `anchor` row, which on demo's corpus would have roughly doubled the table. #742 suppresses it with `x-emitter-internal`, made non-spoofable by adding `emitter` to the gateway's existing `TRUST_HEADER_PATTERN` strip.

That deserves a harness case, because it is a **security-shaped** assertion and it belongs in yours rather than a unit test:

| # | request | must assert |
| - | - | - |
| 7 | flat anchor from an external client that **sets `x-emitter-internal` itself** | the row is **still written** (delta 1) — the gateway strips the header, so a caller cannot suppress its own provenance |

Case 7 is the one I would most want in KS-492: it is an attribution-**evasion** check, and if the gateway's strip list ever regresses, nothing else in the suite would notice.

## Coverage update from KS-519 (merged `b3042a5eb`, 2026-08-12)

Posted because this ticket's own rule requires it — *"when you add or change such a test, keep KS-492 updated (which finding it covers, which harness) and cross-reference the source work-stream"*. Two changes below alter Review G's coverage; a third is a finding about the gate itself.

### 1. A revoked document does NOT verify — KS-489-D's open question, answered

`tests/integration/test_verify_local_override.py::test_revoked_document_does_not_verify` **passed against demo** (39.80 s, real preview-testnet anchor → revoke → verify).

Coverage significance: this vector had **13 recorded occurrences and had not executed since 2026-07-30**. It did not skip — it hard-failed on its flake guard, so the suite carried a red that verified nothing. It is now excluded on a mock-anchoring target and exercised on a real one.

Worth recording for this work-stream specifically: the platform fix it proves (KS-521, Kam's `59ab35d8d`) is otherwise covered **only** by two jest tests that mock prisma and assert the *shape* of the emitted SQL — they never execute it against a database and never touch the verifier. Between 2026-07-30 and today, the sole end-to-end evidence for the revocation contract was unavailable. That is the KS-564 shape Kam described: *"they pin the token check, and the token check was never the problem."*

### 2. API-key document creation is now exercised — skips 4 → 3

`test_document_creation_with_api_key` executed for the first time (`setup.py` now mints a real `sk_*` `documents:write` key). The live integration suite reports **334/345 exercised, 3 skipped**, down from 333/345 with 4.

The three remaining are KS-502's — billing idempotency, seed-demo prod gate, SSRF send-time/M365. Commented there separately: **KS-502's blocking premise has partly expired**, because the "future `systemTest/integration` harness (service-down / prod-like config + fault injection)" it waits on **was built** by KS-489-D. §1's fault injection and §2's prod-like boot are now reachable; §3a (controllable DNS) and §3b (real M365 tenant) are not.

### 3. A gate finding — the fifth outcome, and why it is not a loosening

Review G's suites now carry `OUT OF SCOPE` alongside PASS / FAIL / SKIP / KNOWN FAILURE. Flagging it here because it *looks* like a relaxation of the "a skip is not a pass" rule and is not:

* it is recognised **only** by a single shared constant, so an ordinary `pytest.skip("…")` still reds;
* a run that exercised **nothing** fails with `NOTHING EXERCISED` — rule 6 applied to the exclusion itself;
* the gate line and the report both **name** the exclusion rather than claiming a clean sweep.

## 2. The blocking gate can report PASS having executed NOTHING

After a platform rebuild wiped the Akto mongo volume, `yaml_templates` fell from 199 to 9 (built-ins only). The pre-merge scan then ran 322 endpoints against zero matching templates, produced **0 test results**, and the tier **reported PASS with "0 vulnerable"** — on a stack where a HIGH-severity bypass was provably live at that moment. The HTML report showed a clean result.

The runner did emit `WARN … this run is inconclusive rather than a pass`, but `assertNoVulnerabilities` (`systemTest/akto/tests/fixtures.ts`) counts findings, so **"nothing ran" and "nothing found" are indistinguishable to the gate**.

Per `fixtures.ts` treating an empty run as inconclusive-rather-than-failed is deliberate, so this is a design question rather than an outright bug — but the current behaviour means a blocking security gate can go green because its environment silently degraded. Options worth weighing:

- fail (or hard-warn) when a scan returns 0 results across a non-empty endpoint set;
- assert a floor on executed results for the tier;
- assert template count at scan start (`yaml_templates` ≥ threshold) as a precondition, which is cheap and catches exactly the observed cause.

Any of these would also protect CI, where a volume/cache reset is likelier than locally and nobody is watching the WARN line.

**Review-G schemathesis slice — added and merged to `develop` (PR #585).** Six security regressions for the findings that fold into the schemathesis harness, all report-only (`xfail(strict=False)`/`skip`) so they document the live vuln without red-ing the pre-merge gate and auto-flip when the platform fix lands. They run in the pre-merge/nightly integration suite (`_run_pytest_integration` → `tests/`):

- **A (KS-486)** — `test_notification_bola.py`: a non-admin creating a notification for another `userId` must 403; handler returns **201** today (no self/admin check) → `xfail` (verified it reproduces).
- **B (KS-487)** — `test_webhook_ssrf.py`: (a) passing guard pinning originate's existing `validateWebhookUrl` protection on `POST /api/webhooks` (plaintext http, loopback, 169.254/16, RFC1918, `.internal`); (b) a **DNS-rebind** `xfail` — a hostname resolving to an internal IP (redis/postgres docker svc, `169.254.169.254.nip.io`) is accepted at registration since no DNS resolution is done; (c) a `skip` for send-time re-validation + the 503-gated m365 sink. `test_seed_demo_gate.py`: `skip` (prod-only gate, absent from the spec).
- **C (KS-488)** — `test_wallet_verify_stub.py`: `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature → `xfail` until CIP-8. `test_kyc_callback_auth.py`: passing guard that the callback rejects a non-secret/known-default `secuura-kyc-callback` api-key (local sets `KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY`, so the code's default fallback is a documented prod residual). `test_billing_idempotency.py`: `skip` (needs the Stripe signing secret + DB-unavailable simulation).

Not-locally-reproducible pieces are honest `skip`s, not false greens. `run.py quality` gate green; QA docs synced per the systemTest MUST (`systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, the QA cheat-sheet, and the architecture flow-diagrams Schemathesis node all list the six).

**Kept open** — this is the standing Review-G tracker. The cross-tenant-isolation / playwright / preflight harnesses and the **D** anchor findings aren't covered yet, and each xfail flips to a hard pass only when its A–F remediation ships. Skips that need a new `systemTest/integration` harness (Stripe signing + DB control) or prod-like/M365 envs are split out to **KS-502**.

**Table note (the E/A row):** *"CI scan gates blocking + spec-auth → preflight"* bundles two things. The **spec-auth conformance** sweep (`scripts/preflight/spec-auth-conformance.mjs`, KS-380) is a genuine G verification check (its file lives in the platform tree but it's functionally a test/gate — keep it in G; it mirrors the schemathesis `public_operation_auth_conformance`, KS-425). **"Make the scan gates blocking"** (flipping `security-scan.yml`'s Trivy/Gitleaks/Semgrep/Checkov off `continue-on-error`) is **not a test** — it's a CI remediation owned by **E (KS-490)**. Suggest splitting the row so G lists only verification.

### What needs doing, in order

1. **Decide D1, D2 and D3** (R9, R10).
2. **Phase 0** — the checklist below, minus the CI items (R4), with the oxlint rule (R7) and always-on masking (R12).
3. **Phase 0b** — recount against the current spec and re-home all 346 operations into the flow catalogue (R1). Raise `COVERAGE_FLOOR` towards the new total.
4. **Spine** (F3 → F4 → F5), then the **F10 pilot**, reviewed before the remaining plans are written.
5. **The 22 remaining child plans** and their implementation.
6. **Triage** the `no-documented-flow` residuals.

---

## Summary

`systemTest/playwright/` covers **8 of 310** published API operations (2.6 %) and issues **no writes at all** — so no complete business flow exists anywhere in the suite. This ticket takes Playwright to full coverage of the published contract, driven by the documented product flows, reusing the personas the platform already seeds.

## Current state (measured 2026-07-24 — see R1–R3 for today)

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Published contract | `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — 278 paths / **310 operations** / 42 tags |
| Playwright today | 3 clients, 3 spec files, 11 tests, **8 operations** |
| Writes today | **zero** — read-only plus two unauthenticated 401/403 checks |
| Zero-coverage domains | Billing 21, M365 22, Governance 18, NFT 18, KYC 16, GDPR 15, Analytics 12, Staking 12, VC/VP/StatusList/DID 24, Webhooks 7, Tenants 6, Timestamps 6, API Keys 4, Sessions 2 |

Covered today: `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `GET /users/me`, `GET /documents`, `GET /documents/{id}`, `POST /verification/verify`, plus unauth-only checks on `POST /documents/{id}/verify` and `POST /notifications`.

> **Design verified against the Playwright docs for the pinned** `@playwright/test` **1.61.1** (2026-07-24). *Pin is now 1.64.1 — re-check per R6.* Every design decision cites its source in **Playwright references** at the end.

## Implementation principle — use Playwright's own primitives

**Never implement something ourselves if Playwright already provides it.** Anything the framework ships — polling, stepping, retries, parallelism, artifact attachment, context isolation — is used as-is. Our code exists only to express *Secuura's* domain (personas, flows, coverage classes) or to fill a capability the framework genuinely does not have. A hand-rolled equivalent of a framework feature is a review rejection.

| Need | Mechanism | Ours or Playwright's? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Wait for an async outcome | `expect.poll` (`{ timeout, intervals, message }`) | **Playwright's.** `helpers/settle.ts` is a thin wrapper supplying the project deadlines **\[ref 8\]** |
| Ordered, named stages in a flow | `test.step()` | **Playwright's** |
| Per-persona session isolation | `playwright.request.newContext()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 2\]** |
| Persist an artifact + surface it in the report | `testInfo.outputPath()` + `testInfo.attach({ path })` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 6\]** |
| Parallelism, retries, sharding, reporters, tagging | runner config | **Playwright's** |
| Setup/teardown lifecycle | fixtures with `use()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 7\]** |
| **Capturing API exchanges as a durable artefact** | `helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` | **Ours — the framework has no equivalent** (upstream request closed unimplemented, **\[ref 5\]**). Built *on* `testInfo.attach`/`outputPath` |
| CSRF double-submit echo | `helpers/csrf.ts` | **Ours** — application-protocol concern |
| Coverage classification vs the OpenAPI spec | `coverage/*` | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |
| Persona catalogue, flow definitions | `config/`, `helpers/flow.ts`, specs | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |

## Stack isolation — Playwright runs on its own Docker instance

* ~~**CI**~~ *(moot — GitHub Actions retired 2026-08-27, see R4/R5)* — the `playwright` job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` boots via `boot-platform-stack` with `stack_prefix: pr-playwright`, gateway **6982**, postgres 6532, redis 6479, pgbouncer 6533; pointed at by `API_BASE_URL: http://localhost:6982/api`. Distinct `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` / `STACK_PREFIX` → separate containers, volumes, networks. Siblings sit on 6882 / 7082 / 7182.
* **Local** — the suite does not start or stop a server (`playwright.config.ts`); it attaches to whatever `API_BASE_URL` points at. Use its own instance for destructive flows (F14 erasure, F5 revoke).

Any environment posture we choose applies to Playwright alone. The only shared thing is the composite action's *source file*.

## Scope boundary

Playwright asserts **business outcomes of documented flows**. It does not re-test what the sibling suites own — see `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` §2–3 and the Coverage & Scenario Matrix in `QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

| Excluded from Playwright | Owner |
| -- | -- |
| Boundary values, negative **data**, fuzzing | Schemathesis |
| Status/header compliance, undeclared verbs, redirects, rate-limit headers, 429 | Schemathesis |
| RBAC matrices, cross-tenant, IDOR/BOLA | Schemathesis (+ Akto) |
| Unauthenticated 401/403 sweeps | Schemathesis + the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight |
| OWASP API Top 10, injection, SSRF, BFLA | Akto |
| Throughput, latency, saturation | Performance (k6) |
| Real Cardano chain integrity / anchor-vs-chain | anchoring Integration suite ([KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489/review-d-blockchain-anchoring-smart-contract-integrity)-D) — see Risk 3 |

**A distinction that matters, because it looks like the excluded category but is not:** a *documented business outcome that is not success* — a verification returning **Expired**, a tampered document returning **Failed**, a certifier **Rejecting** a request — is in scope. Those are product states the stakeholder guides describe, reached with valid inputs. What is excluded is malformed **data** (missing fields, oversize values, type confusion). F6 and F7 exist precisely to cover the former.

Consistent with Playwright's Best Practices — *"Only test what you control."* — which is why provider-gated paths (Stripe, M365) record a by-design 503 rather than reaching for the third party. **\[ref 1\]**

**Two existing specs are duplicates and are retired in Phase 0**: `notifications.spec.ts` (both tests assert unauth → 401/403, already swept for every bearer op by the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight) and the invalid-credentials / missing-email cases in `login.spec.ts` (negative data, owned by Schemathesis `test_authentication.py`).

## Persona policy

**Use the existing** `default`**-tenant personas first.** The seeder (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` → `demoAccounts`) provides 17 accounts across 7 tenants. A new persona is created **only where an existing one provably cannot serve**. Permissions on seeded accounts are **not** changed. Non-default tenants are not used.

### Existing personas — the working set (`default` tenant)

| Email | Role | Verification | Password env (fallback) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `issuer@secuura.com` | ISSUER_ADMIN | ENHANCED | `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` (`issuer123`) |
| `admin@secuura.com` | SYSTEM_ADMIN | HIGH | `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` (`admin123`) |
| `demo@secuura.io` | OWNER | ENHANCED | `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` (`demo123`) |
| `holder@secuura.com` | OWNER | BASIC | `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` (`holder123`) |
| `verifier@secuura.com` | VERIFIER | STANDARD | `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD` (`verifier123`) |

Seeding is gated on `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true`; the `config/environment.ts` getters must read the **same env names** with these fallbacks. `kam@secuura.ai` is a real person's account — **do not use**.

### Additions — three, each with a blocking justification

Created at runtime by F2 via `POST /api/users/admin/create` as `admin@secuura.com`. Confirmed viable: the handler assigns `role` from the body, and admin-created users are `emailVerified: true` / `status: ACTIVE`.

| Proposed name | Role / level | Flow | Why no existing persona works |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `pw-approver-<run>@secuura-test.invalid` | ISSUER_APPROVER / ENHANCED | F3, F7 | **Role gap.** `ISSUER_APPROVER` is in the `UserRole` union (`services/auth/src/types/index.ts:8`) but no seeded account holds it |
| `pw-gdpr-subject-<run>@…` | OWNER / BASIC | F14 | **Erasure is irreversible.** Running it on `holder@secuura.com` destroys a persona F9 and F20 depend on |
| `pw-kyc-subject-<run>@…` | OWNER / **NONE** | F15 | **KYC state is one-way.** A reused persona is already-verified on re-run, breaking determinism |

Plus one **non-user identity**: the platform API key (`SECUURA_PLATFORM_API_KEY`, already used by Akto) for **F8**'s machine path. Not an account; no new seed data.

### Deliberately not added

| Considered | Why not |
| -- | -- |
| Default-tenant ORG_ADMIN | `admin@secuura.com` performs the org/tenant operations; ORG_ADMIN-vs-SYSTEM_ADMIN is RBAC → Schemathesis |
| Second rights holder for F9 | Two OWNERs already exist in `default`: `demo@secuura.io` → `holder@secuura.com` |
| Two governance participants for F20 | The same two OWNERs serve; re-registration conflict handled as a valid state |
| Dedicated billing customer | Billing customer creation is 503-by-design locally; `demo@secuura.io` suffices |
| Any non-default-tenant account | Cross-tenant behaviour belongs to Schemathesis |

## ⚠ Two platform capabilities we do not have — needed by F6 and F13

Two flows assert a documented product state that **cannot currently be reached on demand**. Neither blocks Phase 0, but both block their own flow's plan from being finalised. Raised with @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson in the comments — **and probed ourselves first** (see Risk mitigation), because the capability may already exist.

| Need | Flow | Why it is needed | What "available" looks like |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Induce an expired certification** | **F6** | The Verifier guide documents **Expired** as one of five verification result states. Verifying it requires a certification that is *already* past its expiry. If expiry is purely wall-clock with no way to set a past date, F6's expired leg is unreachable and the state stays permanently untested | Either an issuance parameter accepting a past `expiresAt` (non-prod only), or a supported way to age an existing certification. A test must be able to produce one deterministically, in-run, without clock manipulation on the host |
| **Raise a system error on demand** | **F13** | F13's only real journey is *error → resolve*. Asserting it requires a system error to exist first. Provoking one by genuinely breaking a service is not acceptable in a shared or CI stack | A non-prod-only way to emit a synthetic entry into the system-errors surface with a known signature, so the test can find it, resolve it, and assert it reflects as resolved |

**If either already exists**, this is a documentation gap rather than a build ask. **If neither is feasible**, the affected leg is recorded as a documented coverage gap rather than quietly dropped: F6 keeps its tampered + not-found legs, F13 falls back to `positive-path` for the whole read surface.

## Flow catalogue

**Restructured 2026-07-24** and now supersedes the earlier 14-entry list. Three problems were fixed: two entries were *buckets* rather than flows (the old F13 carried 66 operations under a single criterion about one proposal; the old F9 carried 37 across seven unrelated domains), sizing was so uneven that "phase" was a meaningless unit of work, and three documented outcomes plus the entire partner/machine path had no home. Each entry below is now **one actor goal, one acceptance criterion, 4–25 operations**, sized so a child plan can be written per flow.

Flows are transcribed from the product docs — the five `Projects Documents/Stakeholder-Guide-*.md`, `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md`, `USER_TESTING/02-Happy-Path-Testing.md`, `VERIFICATION.md`, `SCOPES.md`, `METERING-USAGE-API.md`, `TOKENISATION.md`, `CONNECTORS_PATTERN.md`. Take the flow **semantics**, not the UI steps.

**Data strategy** — every flow declares one: **Own** (creates and tears down everything it needs) · **Spine** (part of the shared-document chain) · **Setup** (creates a disposable persona or prerequisite first).

| \# | Actor goal | Persona(s) | Domains (ops) | Data | Expected dominant class | Source |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **F1** | *As any user, I sign in and manage my session* | all 5 | Auth 10 · Sessions 2 = **12** | Own | flow-verified | E2E Ph 2 + 8 |
| **F2** | *As a platform admin, I onboard an organisation and its team* | admin | Tenants 6 · Users 4 · API Keys 4 · IssuerCerts 6 = **20** | Own (**creates the 3 personas**) | flow-verified | Issuer §4, Admin §5–7 |
| **F3** | *As an issuer, I certify a document* **\[SPINE 1\]** | issuer, approver | Documents 13 · Certifications 3 · Timestamps 6 · Anchoring 3 = **25** | Spine | flow-verified (anchor leg per D1) | Issuer §6, E2E Ph 4–5 |
| **F4** | *As a verifier, I prove a document is authentic* **\[SPINE 2\]** | verifier + public | Verification 1 · Batch 3 = **4** | Spine | flow-verified | Verifier §4–7, VERIFICATION.md |
| **F5** | *As an issuer, I revoke a certification and verification reflects it* **\[SPINE 3\]** | issuer, verifier | Status List 8 · revoke routes = **8** | Spine | flow-verified | Issuer §7, Certifier §8 |
| **F6** | *As a verifier, I get the right answer when a document should NOT pass* | public | (reuses F4's ops — new **outcomes**) = **0 new** | Setup | flow-verified — **expired leg blocked, see capability gap** | Verifier §6 — Expired, Failed/tampered |
| **F7** | *As an approver, I reject a certification request* | approver | (reuses F3's ops — new **outcome**) = **0 new** | Setup | flow-verified | Certifier §7 |
| **F8** | *As a partner system (Platform S), I certify a document with an API key* | **machine** (`SECUURA_PLATFORM_API_KEY`) | (reuses F3's ops — different **auth path**) = **0 new** | Own | flow-verified | S↔K integration; mirrors Schemathesis `test_document_creation_with_api_key` |
| **F9** | *As a document owner, I share it and transfer rights to someone else* | demo → holder | Notifications 6 · Transfers 9 · Delegations 8 = **23** | Own | flow-verified | Issuer §9, Rights-Holder §5–6 |
| **F10** | *As an issuer, I register a webhook and receive deliveries* | issuer | Webhooks 7 = **7** | Own | flow-verified | — (**pilot flow**, see Risk mitigation) |
| **F11** | *As an issuer, I issue a verifiable credential and it verifies as a presentation* | issuer | VC 8 · VP 4 · DID 4 = **16** | Own | mixed — `POST /api/credentials` is 503-tolerated | VOCABULARY.md |
| **F12** | *As an admin, I export analytics asynchronously* | admin | Analytics 12 = **12** | Own | flow-verified | Admin §4 |
| **F13** | *As an admin, I monitor platform health and audit activity* | admin | Dashboard 8 · Audit 4 · System Errors 6 · Security Events 3 · Rate Limits 2 · Health 1 · Admin 1 = **25** | Own | **mostly** `positive-path` — read surface; its one journey (error → resolve) is **blocked, see capability gap** | Admin §9 |
| **F14** | *As a rights holder, I exercise my privacy rights* | gdpr-subject, admin | GDPR 15 = **15** | Setup (disposable subject) | flow-verified | Rights-Holder §7 (GDPR Art. 15/17/20) |
| **F15** | *As a user, I prove my identity through KYC* | kyc-subject | KYC 16 = **16** | Setup (disposable subject) | flow-verified | KYC surface |

| **F17** | *As a developer, I authorise a third-party app against my account* | demo | OAuth 11 = **11** | Own | flow-verified | OAuth surface |

| **F19** | *As a customer, I buy credits and consume them* | demo | Billing 21 = **21** | Own | **mostly 503-tolerated** — no Stripe locally | METERING-USAGE-API.md |

### Acceptance criterion per flow

Each flow is accepted on **one stated business outcome**, not a set of status codes. These are what the child plans must satisfy.

* **F1** — a token issued at login authenticates `GET /users/me` as the expected persona for all five accounts; a refreshed token works, and the pre-logout token stops working.
* **F2** — a document type created by admin is returned by the subsequent list, and each of the three new personas can log in at its intended role.
* **F3** — a document created by `issuer@secuura.com` is retrievable by id and its certification appears in the certification list. **The anchor leg is blocked on D1.**
* **F4** — verifying the spine document's content hash returns `verified: true` and identifies the issuing party.
* **F5** — after revoke, the same verify call that previously returned verified now reports **revoked**, and the status list reflects it.
* **F6** — a **tampered** payload verifies as failed, and an unknown hash returns `verified: false` without an error. The **expired** leg — an expired certification verifying as expired, not as valid or missing — requires the capability gap above to be closed; until then it is a documented gap, not a silent omission.
* **F7** — a rejected certification request ends in a rejected state, the requester can see the rejection, and the document is **not** certified.
* **F8** — a document certified with `x-api-key` (no bearer, no cookies) is retrievable and verifies identically to one certified by a browser persona. Proves the partner path end-to-end.
* **F9** — custody transfers from `demo@secuura.io` to `holder@secuura.com`: the recipient is notified (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**), and the prior owner can no longer mutate the document.
* **F10** — a registered webhook's test delivery appears in its delivery list (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**); rotating the secret changes the signing secret without dropping the registration.
* **F11** — a credential issued for a document verifies as a presentation and its DID resolves — **or** the by-design 503 on `POST /api/credentials` is the recorded outcome.
* **F12** — an async export reaches a downloadable state within `EXPORT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT` and the downloaded artefact contains the requesting tenant's data.
* **F13** — the audit trail contains the lifecycle events of a document **this flow created itself**. The *error → resolve* journey requires the capability gap above; until then the whole read surface is asserted as `positive-path` and **declared as such**.
* **F14** — the subject's export contains their record; after erasure the same export no longer returns personal data and the deletion log records the event.
* **F15** — a KYC session initiated at verification level `NONE` reaches a terminal reviewed state and the subject's verification level changes.
* **F16** — a wallet challenge is issued and the account reflects the linked wallet address. **Stops short of asserting signature validity** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature and is an open Known Failure ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C).
* **F17** — an authorised app receives a token that can call an in-scope operation, and revoking the grant stops it working.
* **F18** — a connector reaches a connected state and a sync lists at least one document — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F19** — a customer's purchase appears in their purchase list and their credit balance reflects it — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F20** — a proposal created by `demo@secuura.io` receives a vote from `holder@secuura.com` and reaches a terminal state — **or** the documented precondition refusal ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) is recorded.
* **F21** — a stake is recorded and the resulting reward balance reflects it — **or** the documented precondition refusal is recorded.
* **F22** — a referral code applied by a second user is attributed to the referrer and moves a milestone — **or** the documented precondition refusal is recorded.
* **F23** — a minted NFT certificate is retrievable and its asset verifies — **or** the chain/IPFS-dependent outcome is recorded as such.

### Notes for whoever writes the child plans

* **The spine (F3 → F4 → F5) is one spec, one test.** F6, F7 and F8 sit outside it and create their own prerequisites.
* **A flow whose dominant class is not** `flow-verified` **must say so up front** (F13, F18, F19).
* **Flows marked "Setup"** (F6, F7, F14, F15) create a disposable persona or artefact first; that setup is plumbing and does not count toward `COVERAGE_FLOOR`.
* **F6 and F13 have an open platform dependency** — plan the unblocked legs; record the blocked ones as documented gaps.
* **Every flow declares its own teardown** — fixture-scoped, so it runs on failure too.
* **Each flow plan carries its own estimate** — the programme total is the sum, which is how this work gets scheduled.
* **F10 is written first as the pilot** (see Risk mitigation) — later plans should follow whatever shape F10 proves out.

## Driving the flows — per-flow contexts and in-test persona switching

Each flow runs with its own isolated client session, and a single test can act as several personas in sequence so cross-persona interaction is directly observable.

Both are straightforward **because the suite has no browser**. The API analogue of a private window is `playwright.request.newContext()`, and the docs confirm the isolation property: *"If you don't want APIRequestContext to use and update cookies from the browser context, you can manually create a new instance of APIRequestContext which will have its own isolated cookies."* **\[ref 2\]**

| Isolated per flow / persona | Shared across all flows |
| -- | -- |
| Cookie jar, `XSRF-TOKEN`, storage state, `Authorization` bearer | Documents, users, anchors, webhooks — the platform's own state |

**Not hypothetical — the suite already has the bug isolation prevents.** `notifications.spec.ts` documents unauthenticated POSTs returning 403 instead of 401 because a server-set `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie rode along on the *shared* unauth context, making the outcome order-dependent.

### Switching persona inside one test

Every client takes `(api, token)` in its constructor, so the same class bound to different contexts yields `documentsAsDemo`, `documentsAsHolder`, `documentsAsVerifier`. F9's criterion is then close to verbatim:

```ts
test('custody transfers from demo to holder', async ({
    documentsAsDemo, documentsAsHolder, notificationsAsHolder,
}) => {
    const { body: doc } = await documentsAsDemo.create(buildDocumentPayload('f9'));
    await documentsAsDemo.transferCustody(doc.id, holderUserId);

    const received = await documentsAsHolder.get(doc.id);   // recipient can now read
    expect(received.status).toBe(200);

    const stale = await documentsAsDemo.revoke(doc.id);      // prior owner cannot mutate
    expect(stale.status).toBe(403);
});
```

**Calls are always asynchronous** — Playwright has no sync API. Stages within a flow are strictly sequential (each depends on prior state); independent reads may be batched with `Promise.all`, bounded by the \~2000/60s platform limit. Because batched calls complete out of order, **the exchange recorder stamps its sequence at request start** and carries a duration.

### The F3 → F4 → F5 spine is ONE test with steps — not `describe.serial`

F4 verifies *F3's* document and F5 revokes *that same* document, so the chain needs shared state. A `test.describe.serial` block is the wrong instrument **\[ref 3\]**:

* *"If one of the serial tests fails, all subsequent tests are skipped."* — downstream stages would report as **skips**, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` is explicit that a skip is neither red nor green and proves nothing.
* *"All tests in a group are retried together."* — serial buys no retry granularity over a single test.
* *"Using serial is not recommended."* — and Best Practices: *"Each test should be completely isolated from another test…"* **\[ref 1\]**

**Resolution:** `tests/spine/document-lifecycle.spec.ts` holds the chain as **one test** whose stages are `test.step()` calls sharing one document. Tagged `@smoke`. `describe.serial` is not used anywhere.

### Evidence capture — we must build our own

**Both** `video` **and** `trace` **are inert for this suite.**

* **Video** records a browser-context viewport; there is no page here. `playwright.config.ts:54-59` already says so and the docs confirm: *"Videos are saved upon browser context closure."* **\[ref 4\]**
* **Trace** is a `browserContext.tracing` facility and does not capture a standalone `APIRequestContext` created via `playwright.request.newContext()`. **\[ref 5\]**

**The upstream request was closed unimplemented — settled, not pending.** microsoft/playwright#18891 was closed by a maintainer on 30 Jun 2023: *"This issue was closed due to limited engagement (upvotes/activity), lack of recent activity, and insufficient actionability."* GitHub renders the state as "closed as completed", which is misleading — the comment is explicit that it was a housekeeping closure, **not** a shipped feature.

Per the **Implementation principle**, we build our substitute *on* Playwright's own primitives **\[ref 6\]**: `testInfo.attach(name, { path, contentType })` and `testInfo.outputPath()`.

### The exchange recorder — design and tidy-up

Today `helpers/api-report.ts` → `recordApiExchange` attaches **three entries per call**. A 40-call flow produces 120 attachments and none of it is machine-readable as a whole. Split into two modules:

`helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` **— collect + persist (new)**

* Ordered typed record per call: sequence **stamped at request start**, acting persona, enclosing `test.step()` name, method, URL, headers, bodies, status, duration, repro curl. Reuses `format.ts`'s `RequestParts` / `ResponseParts`.
* At test end (fixture teardown) writes **one** file — `testInfo.outputPath('api-exchanges.json')` — attached once with `contentType: 'application/json'`.

`helpers/api-report.ts` **— render (existing, slimmed)**

* One human-readable markdown attachment per call; cookies and curl fold into the JSON record.
* ~~Redaction unchanged: masked when ~~`~~getRedactSecrets()~~`~~ is on (default in CI, off locally).~~ *Superseded (R12):* GDPR personal data, access tokens and secret/API keys are masked in every run.

**Hard review rule, now enforced by lint (see Risk mitigation):** all transport goes through `performApiCall`.

### Constraints

* **Switching identity never means logging in again** — contexts are built from `.auth/token-<persona>.json`.
* **Context isolation does not solve data races** — hence the per-flow data strategy.
* **Teardown must be fixture-scoped, not trailing statements.** *(The docs never explicitly address the failure case — so we prove it with the mid-flow failure check.)* **\[ref 7\]**
* *(Cost note:* `RECORD_HAR=true` *sources the context from real chromium —* `fixtures/api.fixture.ts:116-128`*. Opt-in, never in the PR gate.)*

## Coverage is classified, not just counted

| Class | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `flow-verified` | Exercised inside a flow whose business-outcome criterion passes — the strongest class |
| `positive-path` | A single valid authenticated call asserting the documented success response; no flow reaches it |
| `503-tolerated` | Provider unconfigured locally; the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome (`_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`) |
| `precondition-refused` | Precondition unmeetable locally; the enveloped business 4xx is the recorded outcome ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) |
| `no-documented-flow` | Reached by no product-documented flow — a finding in its own right, triaged at the end |

The catalogue's **Expected dominant class** column is the planning-time prediction; the matrix records what actually happened. A flow landing materially weaker than predicted is a finding, not a silent downgrade.

## Toggles — two of them, and they work differently

### 1. CSRF hardening — test-side, ON by default

The gateway mounts a double-submit guard (`api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts`, mounted `index.ts:370-371` inside `if (NODE_ENV !== 'test')`): the server mints an HMAC-signed token, sets the readable `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and mirrors it in the `X-CSRF-Token` **response** header; a client echoes it back as `X-XSRF-TOKEN`.

The [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and) rewrite short-circuits `protectMiddleware` for any request carrying `Authorization: Bearer …` or `x-api-key`, so authenticated writes are **not expected to need the token today**. **We send it anyway** — the suite behaves like a correct client and keeps passing if that bypass is narrowed.

* **Local:** `getCsrfEnabled()` in `config/environment.ts`, default `true`: `readEnv('CSRF_ENABLED', 'true') !== 'false'`. Commented override in `.env.example`.
* ~~**CI:**~~ *(moot — R4)* `CSRF_ENABLED: ${{ vars.PLAYWRIGHT_CSRF_ENABLED || 'true' }}` on the `playwright` job only.

### 2. Login rate limiter (`LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED`) — platform-side, read at gateway boot

**A test cannot flip this at runtime.** `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:858` passes it into `shouldSkipLoginLimiter({ nodeEnv, disableEnv })`; `middleware/rateLimitSkip.ts:68-69` honours it **only** when the value is `'true'` **and** `NODE_ENV` is in the non-prod allow-list. Never honoured in production ([KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)).

| Where | Today | Effect |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Local | `docker-compose.yml:368` → `${LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED:-false}` | **ACTIVE** unless exported before `docker compose up -d`. *(Verified 2026-07-24: the running developer stack has it* `true` *— something in the boot path exported it. Don't infer the default from a running container.)* |
| CI | `boot-platform-stack/action.yml:123` → hardcoded `"true"` | **DISABLED** for every suite's stack, with no way to change it |

What this ticket adds: a documented local runbook line; a `getLoginLimiterDisabled()` accessor so `auth.setup.ts` can annotate the report and decide whether a login 429 gets bounded backoff; and a `login-limiter-disabled` **input** on the composite (**default** `"true"`, additive) fed by `${{ vars.PLAYWRIGHT_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED || 'true' }}` from the Playwright caller only. The design rule that makes the toggle optional: **one login per persona per run**.

*Setting either repo Variable is a human action in repo settings —* `gh variable set` *is a GitHub API call, barred for systemTest work.*

## Risk mitigation

Most of the risks below are removable — not by being careful, but by deciding, probing, or automating a detector. What remains is labelled honestly rather than managed.

### 1. Prove the pattern once before repeating it 22 times

Do **Phase 0 + Phase 0b + the spine + F10** as a complete vertical slice, and only then write the remaining plans. F10 is deliberately the pilot: 7 operations, self-contained, `Own` data, and it exercises an async boundary — so it stresses every enabler without being large.

Every shared mechanism (CSRF, personas, per-persona contexts, the exchange recorder, `expect.poll` settle, fixture teardown, the coverage matrix) gets validated against the real stack **once**. If an assumption is wrong it is wrong in one flow, not twenty-three. **Reduces Risks 1, 8, 9, 11, 12** — all of which are "does the shared plumbing actually work" in disguise.

### 2. Four probes that turn a risk into a fact (each under an hour, all in Phase 0)

| Probe | Question it answers | Kills |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **A** — authenticated `POST /api/documents` with `CSRF_ENABLED=false` | Does the [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and) Bearer bypass actually hold? | Risk 1 |
| **B** — force a mid-flow failure, check cleanup ran | Does fixture teardown run on failure? | the ref-7 doc gap |
| **C** — create a certification with a past `expiresAt` | Can we reach the Expired state ourselves? | Risk 14 |
| **D** — POST a synthetic entry to system-errors | Can we raise an error on demand? | Risk 15 |

**Run C and D before waiting on a reply** — the capability may already exist, in which case the ask resolves itself and both flow plans proceed unchanged.

### 3. Three risks need a decision, not work

**D1, D2 and D3 at the top of this ticket.** They cost nothing to settle and currently block F3/the spine, the tier split, and the child-plan layout respectively. **Deciding them is the cheapest risk reduction available.**

### 4. Turn conventions into gates

A rule enforced only at review will eventually be broken. Three become automated:

| Was | Becomes | Kills |
| -- | -- | -- |
| "All transport goes through `performApiCall`" (review rule) | **oxlint rule** *(R7)* forbidding `api.fetch(` / direct `request.` outside `helpers/api-call.ts` — the repo already uses `no-restricted-properties` this way to keep `process.env` inside the config module | Risk 12 |
| "A change to `/api/users/admin/*` breaks Phase 0 silently" | **Guard assertion** that the endpoint still assigns the role it is given — fails loudly and immediately | Risk 2 |
| ~~"The composite action is shared source"~~ *(moot — R4)* | **Cross-suite diff** — after the change, run one job from each of the other three suites and compare boot output | Risk 7 |

Plus the guards already planned: the residue check (Risk 8), the order-independence check (Risk 9), and the per-class floors in `coverage.test.ts` (Risk 4).

### 5. What is irreducible — and what we do instead

Risks **5, 6, 13** and the provider-gated parts of **4** cannot be engineered away: they are properties of the local environment, the platform's state machines, and an open defect ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C). The mitigation is **honest labelling** — the verification classes and the per-flow *Expected dominant class* column make each one visible in the matrix rather than hidden inside a green run. A risk that shows up in the report is not a risk; it is a documented limitation.

13. **F16 must not encode a known bug as expected behaviour** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature ([KS-488](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet>)-C). F16 stops at wallet linkage. *Irreducible; labelled. Schemathesis's xfail will xpass loudly when the fix lands, prompting a revisit.*
14. **F6's expired leg depends on a platform capability we do not have.** *Probe C first; then the ask to* @kamil.kreiser */* @stuart.jamieson\*; else a documented gap.\*
15. **F13's only journey depends on a platform capability we do not have.** *Probe D first; same escalation; else F13 is labelled a read surface.*

nodes.body: Mask all GDPR data, access and secret keys

@kamil.kreiser @stuart.jamieson — a small ask, whenever it suits you. No urgency; neither of these blocks the work starting.

Two of the 23 flows in this ticket assert a **documented product state that we currently have no way to reach on demand**. In both cases the endpoint exists and works — what's missing is a supported way to *get the system into the state* the test needs to observe.

### 1. A way to produce an already-expired certification — needed by **F6**

The Verifier stakeholder guide (§6) documents **five** verification result states: Verified, Failed, Revoked, Expired, Not Found. We can reach four of them. **Expired** we cannot, because a certification created during a test run is by definition not yet expired.

What would unblock it: either an issuance parameter that accepts a past `expiresAt` (non-prod only), or a supported way to age an existing certification. The test needs to produce one **deterministically, within a run**, without manipulating the host clock — a CI runner's clock is shared with everything else on it.

*Why it matters:* it's one of the five states a real verifier will see, and it's the one that silently looks like success if the platform ever gets it wrong. Right now nothing in any suite covers it.

### 2. A way to raise a synthetic system error — needed by **F13**

F13's only genuine journey is **error → resolve**: an entry appears on the system-errors surface, an admin resolves it, and it reflects as resolved. Asserting that needs an error to exist first, and the only way we have today is to actually break a service — which is not acceptable on a shared or CI stack.

What would unblock it: a non-prod-only way to emit a synthetic entry with a known signature, so the test can find its own error, resolve it, and assert the transition.

*Why it matters:* without it, F13's 25 operations are a pure read surface. We'd rather label that honestly than imply journey coverage we don't have — but the resolve path is real product behaviour and currently untested.

### What we need from you

Whichever is easiest:

* **"That already exists"** — perfect, just point us at it; this becomes a docs gap, and both plans proceed unchanged.
* **"Yes, we can add that"** — a rough sense of when helps us sequence the two flow plans; everything else proceeds regardless.
* **"Not feasible / not worth it"** — also completely fine. We record each as a **documented coverage gap** rather than dropping it quietly: F6 keeps its tampered and not-found legs, and F13 gets labelled as a read surface. No further action needed from you.

Both are captured as Risks 14 and 15 in the description with the same detail. Thanks both.

title: KMS: move platform wallet mnemonic to Key Vault (KS-326 follow-up)
description:
**Follow-up carved out of** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms)**.** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) (Phase 0 — crypto-agility + KMS) was closed as Done, but only the **JWT signing key** half of its KMS item actually shipped (PR #361/#362 — JWT private key now loads from Azure Key Vault with an env fallback). The **platform wallet mnemonic** was left behind and is still loaded from an env var.

**Current state (verified in code):**

* `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` is read from `process.env` in `services/anchoring` (e.g. `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:850`), then passed to `initWallet(mnemonic, network)` in `services/anchoring/src/cardano/wallet.ts` to derive the BIP-39 → BIP-32 → Ed25519 signing key.
* The JWT-key KMS plumbing already exists to reuse: `packages/shared/src/vault/key-vault.ts` (Key Vault `getSecret` with env fallback).

**Ask:**

- [ ] Load `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` from Azure Key Vault via the existing `key-vault.ts` helper, with an always-on env fallback (mirror the JWT-key pattern, so local/dev with no Key Vault still works).
- [ ] Support rotation (versioned secret) — note a mnemonic rotation also rotates the derived wallet address, so document the operational impact.
- [ ] Keep behaviour-preserving defaults: no Key Vault configured → falls back to `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` env, identical to today.

**Why it matters:** the mnemonic is the platform wallet's root secret; leaving it in env is a wider blast radius than the JWT key that already moved. Not urgent (env is the current accepted posture), but it closes the gap [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) implied was done.

**Refs:** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) (parent, closed), PR #361/#362 (JWT-key KMS pattern to follow), `docs/security/POST-QUANTUM-CRYPTO-MIGRATION-PLAN.md` §5 Phase 0 / §7.

title: anchoring threadTokenMint test fails only under root-visible npm install layout — nested @lucid-evolution/plutus duplicate-instance (pre-existing, layout-dependent; KS-559 A/B-cleared)
description:
**Found during KS-559 validation (2026-08-04, Agent Teams pilot) — pre-existing, NOT caused by the dep sweep (controlled A/B in two independent environments: identical failure with pre-KS-559 and post-KS-559 locks).**

`services/anchoring` test `threadTokenMint.test.ts › parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId` fails with `Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type` in `applyParamsToScript` — the classic **duplicate-instance** signature: the test's `Constr` comes from the top-level `@lucid-evolution/plutus@0.1.31` while `@lucid-evolution/utils@0.1.70` serializes against its own nested `plutus@0.1.33` copy, and the cross-copy instanceof check fails.

**It is INSTALL-LAYOUT-DEPENDENT, which is why it looks flaky across setups:**

* `npm ci` in a **parentless standalone** copy of services/anchoring (= what the Dockerfile does) → **110/110 pass**. Verified on macOS host for both develop and KS-559 locks.
* `npm ci --workspaces=false` with the **monorepo root visible** as a parent dir (worktree, full-repo container mount) → **109/110, this test fails**. Verified on macOS host AND in node:24-alpine, again for both locks.

Same lock file both ways (`packages` dict byte-identical to develop) — npm physically lays the tree out differently when it can see a parent workspace root, and one layout resolves the utils→plutus import to the nested copy.

**Why it matters:** (1) any dev running anchoring tests inside the monorepo checkout with a standalone install hits a phantom red; (2) the nested plutus duplication itself (0.1.31 vs 0.1.33) is fragile — a future hoist change could flip the shipped image's behaviour. Fix options: dedupe/pin `@lucid-evolution/plutus` so one copy exists; or make the test/lib resolution layout-proof; or document the supported install layout for the suite.

Evidence + repro commands in the KS-559 PR thread and session history 2026-08-04. Credit: caught by the KS-559 deps teammate's controlled A/B refusing to accept an unqualified 110/110.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** QA gate 248 (PR 2081, KS-1171 8k, 2026-11-07) re-measured the cause this ticket describes and says the product mint has the same shape, which is the question the gate 70 comment on this ticket leaves open ("whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container"). It is still unmeasured. Kam's card `secuura-anchoring-second-fee-on-empty-reply-1107` = a, "Merge PR 2081, and fix the empty reply before anchoring next deploys (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:31:42 +11:00, names "Medium to measure the mint on an image". This ticket (Backlog, Medium) already carries that work, and Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-01 put the gate 70 finding here instead of on a new ticket, so no second ticket was filed. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME for the identity check; READ ONLY for the product mint and the image's lock file. No state, assignee or priority of this ticket was changed.

**What gate 248 measured:** at develop and at the PR 2081 head the same cell fails with the same message, "Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type", 2 of 2 alone in each tree. The cell imports only the lucid-evolution packages, and none of the PR's three product files is in its import graph. `Constr` comes from one copy of `lucid-evolution/plutus` (0.1.31) and `applyParamsToScript` serialises with another (0.1.33 in that tree): `l.Constr === p.Constr` is false, and the same call with the other copy's `Constr` succeeds.

**New here (read only):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/threadTokenMint.ts` line 92, lines 267 to 269, and the `applyParamsToScript` call below them use the same pairing, so the real thread-token mint may throw the same error. The failing step is before signing, so by read no fee is at risk. The image installs from `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/package-lock.json`, which also splits plutus (0.1.31 and 0.1.36), by gate 248's read.

**Also new:** the cell goes green if the blueprint is absent (it warns and returns): gate 248's own first run read 856 of 856 for exactly that reason, and the same holds for a failed lucid import. Fix shape (gate 248): a missing blueprint fails the cell.

**Still unmeasured:** the mint on any image or box, with any key. Anchoring's deploy stays held for Kam's word.

**Source:** gate 248 verdict, finding F2 and ask 2, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate248-tier1-pr2081-ks1171/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and the lines named above and ran nothing else. The High half, the empty reply, is KS-2103.

**BLUF:** QA gate 70 (KS 1384 R2b, 2026-11-01) measured this failure again and found it deterministic, NOT host-dependent. The `threadTokenMint.test.ts` emulator round-trip fails because two copies of the scoped npm package `lucid-evolution/plutus` are installed: the test's `Constr` and the serializer inside `applyParamsToScript` come from different copies, so `Constr` identity is false. The product mint imports the same pair.

What the gate measured:
* `lucid.Constr === utils-plutus Constr: false`, its log `evidence/q7_constr_identity.log`. The cell fails with "Could not serialize the data: Unsupported type".
* The product `services/anchoring/src/threadTokenMint.ts` (lines 267-269 at the R2b head `ecfe4f07fdce`) imports `lucid-evolution/lucid` from the workspace root and `lucid-evolution/utils` from anchoring's own `node_modules`: the same pair of copies.
* Not tested: whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container.

It is outside the KS 1384 train: that delta touches no package or lockfile.

Source: QA gate 70 verdict, finding G70-F6 and Q7, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-01_gate70-ks1384-r2b-1884/verdict.md`. Recorded here on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-01 00:55:12Z, instead of a new ticket.

**Seen again 2026-10-18 (Seat R 48th), with one layout detail this ticket does not yet record.** While raising KS-1626, anchoring's full suite read **370/371 at the untouched develop tip `5d1be7b06279`** — this exact test, `threadTokenMint.test.ts › parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId`, `Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type` at `applyParamsToScript` — and identically after the change (375/376).

**The new detail:** the install was a plain **root-workspace `npm ci`** at `Blockchain/Dev` (not `npm ci --workspaces=false`), in a fresh git worktree. That layout splits the copies the same way: `@lucid-evolution/plutus` **0.1.31** at the root and **0.1.33** nested under `services/anchoring/node_modules`; `utils` 0.1.68 / 0.1.70. From inside anchoring, Node resolves `@lucid-evolution/lucid` to the **root** copy and `plutus` / `utils` to the **nested** ones. So the phantom red also hits anyone who installs the monorepo the ordinary workspace way, not only the `--workspaces=false` variant measured here.

Not acted on — recorded so the next seat that sees 1 failure in anchoring does not mistake it for its own change.

## It reproduces again at develop `6ab9d5021e96` — the 2026-08-14 sweep note's own prediction has come true

That note closed with: *"A `npm install` that re-resolves `utils` to 0.1.70 in the root tree brings it straight back, and nothing prevents that."* Nothing did. Re-measured today from a fresh worktree at develop `6ab9d5021e96ea1481cb6c6ff2d6d33b414aecb7`, `npm ci --offline` from `Blockchain/Dev` (the hoisted workspace layout — the same layout the sweep note found GREEN).

**Deterministic, 2 of 2 runs, same cell, same throw. Not flaky.**

```
FAIL src/__tests__/threadTokenMint.test.ts > threadTokenMint emulator round-trip
     > parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId
Error: Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type
  at serialize            node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus/dist/index.js:272:13
  at Object.to            node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus/dist/index.js:276:61
  at applyParamsToScript  node_modules/@lucid-evolution/utils/dist/index.js:306:37
  at                      src/__tests__/threadTokenMint.test.ts:71:31
```

Whole-suite effect: `services/anchoring` reads **334 passed / 1 failed over 24 files** at develop, bare, before any edit — so no seat can currently report the anchoring suite as green.

## The duplicate is back in the INSTALLED tree, in a different shape from the one this ticket describes

The sweep note verified one hoisted copy each (`plutus 0.1.31`, `utils 0.1.68`). Today there are two of each — measured on disk, not read off a lock:

| package | `Blockchain/Dev/node_modules` | `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/node_modules` |
|---|---|---|
| `@lucid-evolution/plutus` | 0.1.31 | **0.1.33** |
| `@lucid-evolution/utils` | 0.1.68 | **0.1.70** |
| `@lucid-evolution/core-types` | 0.1.24 | **0.2.1** |
| `@lucid-evolution/uplc` | 0.2.21 | **0.2.22** |

**The shape differs from the ticket's description in one way worth recording.** The ticket (and the sweep note) describe top-level `utils@0.1.70` carrying a *nested* `plutus@0.1.33`. What is installed today is the duplicate one level out: the root tree holds the 0.1.31/0.1.68 pair, and `services/anchoring/node_modules` holds the 0.1.33/0.1.70 pair beside it. Vitest runs with `services/anchoring` as its root, so that directory is the first one Node resolves from.

**This is the ROOT lock's own shape, not a bad install.** `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` pins both sets explicitly — `node_modules/@lucid-evolution/{utils 0.1.68, plutus 0.1.31}` *and* `services/anchoring/node_modules/@lucid-evolution/{utils 0.1.70, plutus 0.1.33}` — and the installed versions match it exactly. So the condition is no longer only in anchoring's standalone lock, as the sweep note recorded; the hoisted workspace install now reproduces it too.

## What I did NOT establish

**I am not claiming which copy threw.** Both `plutus` copies carry `throw new Error("Could not serialize the data: …")` at line **272**, and both `utils` copies have the `parameters.reduce` at line **306**, so the stack trace's line numbers do not discriminate between them. The cross-copy `instanceof` mechanism this ticket already names remains the obvious candidate and is consistent with everything above — but it is a hypothesis here, not a measurement. Resolving it needs the module-identity check, not the trace.

## Nothing touched

Every `package.json` and lockfile is out of scope for this round's seats, so I changed none of them, and this ticket's own fix options (dedupe/pin `plutus`, align `utils` across both trees, or make the resolution layout-proof) are unchanged. Recording the evidence only.

The sweep note's instruction still stands and is now doubly earned: **do not close on a green run in one layout.**

*Measured by Seat L2 (security + anchoring lane), 2026-09-25, while building KS-1129. Found because the anchoring baseline for that ticket was red before any edit of mine.*

## Sweep note — **does not reproduce today, and I am not closing it on that alone**

Re-run on `develop` `454a64ebb`, this Mac, hoisted workspace layout — i.e. the layout the ticket says FAILS:

```
services/anchoring $ npx vitest run src/__tests__/threadTokenMint.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       1 passed (1)
```

## Why it passes — the duplicate is gone from the INSTALLED tree

The ticket's mechanism is two `@lucid-evolution/plutus` instances, so a `Constr` built by one fails the `instanceof` check in the other. Checked the actual installed layout rather than the lock:

```
@lucid-evolution/plutus : 0.1.31   (one copy, hoisted)
@lucid-evolution/utils  : 0.1.68   (one copy, hoisted)
```

**One `plutus`, so no cross-copy `instanceof` to fail.** The ticket's failing tree had top-level `plutus@0.1.31` against `utils@0.1.70` carrying its own nested `plutus@0.1.33`.

## Why it is NOT closed — the condition is still pinned where it ships

`services/anchoring/package-lock.json` — the lock the Dockerfile actually installs from — **still pins exactly the failing combination**:

```
node_modules/@lucid-evolution/utils               -> 0.1.70
node_modules/@lucid-evolution/utils/node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus -> 0.1.33
node_modules/@lucid-evolution/plutus              -> 0.1.31
```

So the duplicate has not been resolved; it has been **hoisted away locally**. A `npm install` that re-resolves `utils` to 0.1.70 in the root tree brings it straight back, and nothing prevents that.

## The more interesting finding

The hoisted tree runs **`utils@0.1.68`** while anchoring's own standalone lock ships **`0.1.70`**. Local dev and the built image are on different minors of a Cardano serialisation library. That is the [KS-531](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-531) class — the standalone locks diverging from the hoisted tree — showing up on a dependency that does on-chain script parameterisation, where a serialisation difference is not cosmetic.

## What it is waiting for

Pin one `@lucid-evolution/plutus` (an `overrides` entry, or align `utils` across both trees) so the duplicate cannot re-form, then re-run in both layouts. **Do not close on a green run in one layout** — that is what makes this ticket layout-dependent in the first place.

*Backlog sweep 2026-08-14.*
