## Detail — the source line
`Launch_Claude.command:475`:

```sh
DRIFT_COUNT="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" log --oneline --since="$EARLIEST_START" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
```

`git log` is given **no ref argument**, so it defaults to **`HEAD`**. The label on line 476 is hard-coded to say `on main`. That is the entire bug: the ref is implicit and the label is a literal, and the two have never agreed.

## Why it read as "develop" before
On sessions 44 and 45 the checked-out branch sat **1 commit** over `develop`, so `HEAD` and `develop` differed by one and the number looked develop-shaped. My branch today sits **6** commits over `develop` (12 + 6 = 18), which is what made the divergence large enough to be unmissable. The earlier reading was a coincidence of branch shape, not a wrong measurement.

## Practical consequence
The warning's purpose is to say *"your running containers are older than the code."* Counting `HEAD` means the number inflates with **your own unmerged work** — commits that were never going to be in the running stack and whose absence is not drift. On a long-lived feature branch the warning gets louder the more you work, independent of any real staleness, which is how a useful signal becomes one people learn to skip.

*Posted 2026-08-18. Comment only — no edit to `Launch_Claude.command`, hold observed and named.*

title: The demo VM runs every service as NODE_ENV=development while the code names "demo" as prod-like — ~6 production guards are silently inert, and the public API-docs exposure is one symptom
description:
## BLUF

**The live demo runs all 27 Node services with** `NODE_ENV=development`**.** The codebase explicitly
treats `demo` as a prod-like environment (`services/auth/src/index.ts:220`:
`IS_PROD_LIKE = ['production','staging','demo'].includes(NODE_ENV)`), so a set of guards written to
protect prod-like deployments do not fire on the demo. **Found 2026-08-17 (session 44) as a control**,
while disproving an unrelated claim about KS-656 — nobody was looking for it.

**Filed, deliberately not fixed.** Changing what the demo is counts as demo-affecting config and is
Kam's call. There is also a **live disagreement between three artefacts** about what the demo is
supposed to be, and flipping anything now would destroy the evidence that the question was ever open.

## The disagreement — three artefacts, three answers

| Artefact | Says the demo should be |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/src/index.ts:220` | `demo` — an explicit prod-like value |
| `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:578-582` (comment) + `deployment/azure/services.bicep:626` | prod-like: public API docs "never in demo/prod", bicep sets the flag `true` only for `dev` |
| `docker-compose.yml` (the file the VM actually runs) + the VM's `.env:165` | `development` |

**Someone may have set this deliberately** — Stuart or Peter driving Swagger against the demo is
entirely plausible, and it has probably been this way a long time. **Establish which artefact is****
****authoritative before reconciling any of it.**

## Measured on the live demo VM (read-only; values never printed)

```
docker exec <svc> printenv NODE_ENV   -> development     (26 of 26 Node services; 5 infra containers unset)
/home/secuura/secuura/Dev/.env:165    -> NODE_ENV=development
```

**The fix is not a one-line env change**, which is the part worth knowing up front:

```
docker-compose.yml:  "- NODE_ENV=development"           -> 26 occurrences  (hardcoded)
docker-compose.yml:  "- NODE_ENV=${NODE_ENV:-development}" ->  1 occurrence  (api-gateway, :319)
```

So setting `NODE_ENV=demo` in the VM's `.env` would move **exactly one service** and leave the other
26 on `development` — a change that would look applied and mostly not be.

## What is actually inert as a result — argued, and bounded

**Real:**

1. **Full API surface published unauthenticated at the internet edge.** `apiDocsGuard`
   (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:584`) is opt-in via `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS`; the VM's `.env:217` sets it
   `true`, and `docker-compose.yml:327` defaults it `false`, so the VM is overriding the default. Both
   spec routes serve real content (verified by content-type; an invented sibling path returns the
   Swagger HTML catch-all, which is the control that makes those 200s evidence). The guard's own
   comment calls this "a free attack-surface map for anyone (audit F-04)". **342 endpoints, every****
****parameter and every auth mechanism — no credentials in it.**
2. **5xx responses return the raw internal error message to the caller.**
   `api-gateway/src/index.ts:1031` masks to "An unexpected error occurred" only when
   `NODE_ENV === 'production'`; `:1038` adds `details.details = err.message` whenever it is not.
   Live example of the class from the local stack, same code path:
   `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml'` — an internal
   filesystem path in a client-visible body. (`err.stack` goes to the **logger** only, not the response.)
3. **Session/auth and CSRF cookies are not marked** `Secure` — `secure: NODE_ENV === 'production'` at
   `auth/src/routes/auth.ts:369,536,615` and `api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:60`, on an origin that
   is HTTPS-only via Caddy. ⚠ **Code-level only — deliberately NOT runtime-verified**, because
   confirming it means authenticating against the demo and minting a session.
4. **The** `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` **fail-fast cannot fire.** `auth/src/index.ts:225-227` exits 1 when the key
   is missing *in a prod-like env* — protecting PII **and** MFA TOTP secrets (KS-158). On the demo it
   degrades to a warning. **Latent, not live: the key IS set (measured present, 64 chars).** So this is
   a guard that cannot fire, not exposed PII.
5. **Password-reset and email-verification links are logged in full when SMTP send fails**
   (`auth/src/routes/auth.ts:230,686`, both gated `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`). Tokens reach the VM's
   container logs. Relevant next to KS-488 C-5, which turned the SMTP transport off by default.

**Checked and NOT true — recorded so nobody re-derives it:**

* **Mock endpoints are OFF.** `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` measured literal `false` on the gateway; the gate
  at `:752` needs `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS === 'true'`, so only one half is open.
* `CSRF_SECRET` **is set** on the gateway (36 chars), so the `:50`/`:276` production-only requirement
  not firing costs nothing today.
* **No PII is exposed** — see 4.
* Demo seeding being enabled is plausibly intentional for a demo, not counted as a defect here.

## Severity — argued as Medium, and explicitly not inflated

Every individual inert guard is either backed by a secret that is actually present (4), mitigated by
the HTTPS-only edge (3), or off on its second condition (mocks). Nothing here is exploitable for
credentials or PII as it stands. **What makes it worth fixing is that it is a class, not an item:** one
env value silently disables roughly six independent protections at once on the only internet-facing
Secuura deployment, and the artefacts disagree about whether that is intended.

**What would raise this to High:** `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` going missing (4 becomes live and silent), or
`ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` being flipped (2 of 2 conditions open). Both are one env edit away, and today
nothing would fail loudly to tell you.

## Tracked nowhere until now

Searched the board three ways before filing — `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS`, `public API docs`, `F-04`.
No result covers this. F-04 lives in **KS-491 (Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation)**, which
records the docs-exposure *finding* against the code but not the *live demo state*.

## Proposed disposition (needs Kam)

1. **Decide what the demo is** — prod-like (`demo`) or a dev sandbox that happens to face the internet.
   That single ruling resolves all six items.
2. If prod-like: the compose `NODE_ENV` hardcoding (26 sites) has to be parameterised first, or the
   change is cosmetic.
3. If it stays a sandbox: say so in the compose file and retire the "never in demo/prod" comment at
   `api-gateway/src/index.ts:578-582`, so the artefacts stop contradicting each other.

**No change has been made to the VM, its** `.env`**, or the repo.**

nodes.body:
**Kintsugi too — this is not demo-only.** Facts only; no change made, no state change, and nothing on either box was touched to establish it.

`ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true` on **both** boxes, so `/api/docs/openapi.yaml` is served publicly on kintsugi as well as demo. Measured read-only by **Seat D 35th** on 2026-10-26 during the `c3eb63c9d23b` deploy and reported in its DEPLOYED mail (2026-10-27T00:14:29Z), verbatim:

> `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true on BOTH boxes, so /api/docs/openapi.yaml is publicly served and the` / `BACKLOG row "API docs are exposed on the public demo again, since 2026-07-31" is live on kintsugi` / `too, not only demo. Reported, not fixed, out of scope.`

So the `BACKLOG.md` row that frames this as a demo exposure understates it by one box.

**On `NODE_ENV`, attributed precisely rather than loosely.** The same mail treats `NODE_ENV=development` as the state on each box inside its 405-attribution paragraph — *"On each box the HOST file was already … NODE_ENV=development did not trigger a re-read"* — but it carries no standalone sentence asserting the value per box. The per-box assertion is in that seat's history entry, which lists `NODE_ENV=development` and `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true` "on both" among the UNMEASUREDs it closed. Two sources, one of them indirect; read the box if the exact value per service matters.

This ticket's description and both its comments name kintsugi **zero** times (measured; controls on the same matcher fired — `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS` 7 occurrences, `NODE_ENV` 19, a nonsense token 0), which is why this is being recorded rather than assumed known.

*Seat G 23rd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief. Read-only; this ticket remains Backlog and this seat proposes nothing — the ticket already names the posture as Kam's call.*

## BLUF
The demo-`.env` fingerprint that PR #720's `BACKLOG.md` API-docs row carried is moved HERE at Peter's #720 ask 5 (2026-08-31 §5.5 / 2026-09-09 §8.5): the row keeps its conclusion, the detail lives on this ticket. Verbatim below from `BACKLOG.md` at `fcc611d29:610-616`, dated as originally measured (the 2026-08-17 finding, re-verified in the 2026-08-31 sweep). Nothing new was measured for this move and no environment was read — the text moved.

## The detail, verbatim from `fcc611d29:610-616`
> - **The blast radius is the whole file, not this one variable.** The VM `.env` and the local dev
>   `.env` have an **identical MD5 of their key-name sequence** (`1f94a0bb02f6d33e38fb8f2cf9817597`),
>   identical key count (98) and identical line count (217); every posture flag matches at the same
>   line number — `NODE_ENV=development` (:165), `LOG_LEVEL=debug` (:83), `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true`
>   (:217). Control: `env.example` digests differently (`ad0ec492…`, 95 keys, 342 lines), so the
>   digest discriminates. **The demo has never had a curated `.env`; it is running a developer's.**
>   That is also the real explanation for KS-658's `NODE_ENV` finding.

## Where it sits now
- `BACKLOG.md` on #720 at `cd62c9f89`: the API-docs row keeps "The blast radius is the whole file, not this one variable" and "The demo has never had a curated `.env`; it is running a developer's", names the three posture flags without values or line numbers, and points here for the fingerprint ("comment of 2026-09-14").
- Posture unchanged: nothing flipped, nothing restarted — the row's "Not flipped" line stands, as does this ticket's file-don't-flip ruling.

## BLUF

**This is not a new finding — it is a regression of a fix that was verified closed on
2026-07-19, and the cause is already on the record under a different incident.** I filed this
ticket yesterday saying the exposure was "tracked nowhere" after searching Linear three ways.
That was true of Linear and **false of the project's own `BACKLOG.md`**, which carried a ticked
`[x]` row for exactly this, closed 2026-07-19 by PR
[#559](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/559) (`ec628ad61`).

**The row has been asserting a closed security exposure for 17 days while the exposure was
live.** I have re-opened it.

**And the scope is bigger than this one variable: the demo VM's `.env` *is* a developer's local
`.env`.** That is also the real explanation for this ticket's `NODE_ENV=development` finding.

## How it regressed — dated, and collateral of a different incident

1. **2026-07-19** — #559 sets the compose default to `false` *and* flips the demo VM's own `.env`
   to false. Verified at the time: demo `/api/docs` + raw spec **404**, local opt-in 200.
2. **2026-07-31** — a local `.env` is **rsynced wholesale over the VM's `.env`** because the
   deploy runbook's rsync had no `.env` exclusion. This is not speculation: it is the recorded
   root cause of the demo mock-anchoring incident, in
   `5_Project_History/history.md` §2026-08-02. The local `.env` carries
   `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true` — the documented local opt-in at `env.example:342` — so the docs
   exposure came back inside that same copy.
3. **2026-08-02 00:28:58Z** — the incident is remediated: the wallet mnemonic is restored and a
   rsync `.env*` exclusion is added to the runbook. **The remediation fixed the casualty it had
   noticed and never asked what else the overwrite had changed.** The VM `.env` mtime is exactly
   that timestamp — 14 days after the fix it undid.
4. **2026-08-17** — still live.

**The guard added on 08-02 prevents recurrence but repaired nothing.** Future rsyncs are safe;
the damage already done was never audited.

## Evidence the demo `.env` is the local dev `.env`

Compared **without moving any secret off the VM** — key *names* only, no values:

| | VM `/home/secuura/secuura/Dev/.env` | local `Blockchain/Dev/.env` | control: `env.example` |
|---|---|---|---|
| MD5 of key-name sequence | `1f94a0bb02f6d33e38fb8f2cf9817597` | **`1f94a0bb02f6d33e38fb8f2cf9817597`** | `ad0ec49218d0e53e2c3cf920cafcc26b` |
| keys | 98 | 98 | 95 |
| lines | 217 | 217 | 342 |

Identical digest, identical counts — and the control digests differently, so the comparison
discriminates. Every posture flag also matches **at the same line number**:
`LOG_LEVEL=debug` (:83), `NODE_ENV=development` (:165), `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true` (:217).

Honest bound: this proves the **structure** is identical and that every non-secret posture flag I
checked is identical. It does not prove every *value* is identical, and at least one is not —
the mnemonic was repaired on 08-02. The accurate statement is: **the demo is running a
developer's `.env` with the wallet repaired.**

## Live confirmation of the exposure, read-only

- `/api/docs/openapi.yaml` → **200**, `text/yaml`, **1,152,555 bytes**, OpenAPI 3.1.0, **287 paths**
- `/api/docs/openapi.json` → **200**, `application/json`, 860,171 bytes
- Control 1: `/api/docs/NOT_A_ROUTE_s45_ctrl` → 200 but **`text/html`**, 3,147 B — the Swagger UI
  catch-all, so the 200 on the real route is not a catch-all artefact
- Control 2: `/api/health` → genuine **404 JSON**
- Running container env: `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true`, `NODE_ENV=development`
- The VM's own `docker-compose.yml` **does** carry the #559 fix (`${ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS:-false}`
  at :327) — the `.env` is overriding a correct default

## What this changes about the fix

**It is not "flip one variable on the VM".** Two things are now true that were not obvious when I
filed this:

1. **A flip is not durable.** It was flipped once already and lasted 12 days. Nothing enforces the
   `env.example` instruction *"Leave unset/false on any deployed environment"* — it is a comment.
2. **The demo has never had a curated `.env`.** The fix shape is to author one deliberately for
   the demo — or to make the compose file refuse to start prod-like services under a dev posture
   — not to hand-edit values that the next copy will overwrite.

## Severity — deliberately not changed

Filed Medium with an explicit "why not High". **The consequence has not changed** and I am not
inflating it: still no PII exposed, mocks still off (`ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS=false`), `CSRF_SECRET`
set, `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` set. What has changed is **durability and provenance** — a verified fix
silently reverted and went unnoticed for 17 days. If that argues for a raise, it argues on
process grounds, and that is Kam's call, not a unilateral re-prioritisation.

**Not flipped** — the file-don't-flip ruling stands, and flipping now would destroy the evidence
that the question was open. Posture remains Kam's sitting decision.

## One more thing worth naming

`LOG_LEVEL=debug` is also live on the internet-facing demo, and it arrived by the same route. On
its own it is noise; paired with this ticket's finding that `NODE_ENV=development` makes 5xx
responses return the raw internal `err.message`, the two compound. Recording it here rather than
filing separately, since both have the same single cause and the same single fix.

title: Compose seeds published *123 credentials by default, and the 11 rotation vars never reach the auth container from .env — every compose deploy (local, demo VM, Kintsugi)
description:
## BLUF

**Any compose deploy of this platform comes up seeding the published** `*123` **credentials, and the documented way to rotate them silently does nothing unless you happen to put them in the one undocumented file.** Two halves of the same asymmetry in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

* the single variable that **enables** published default passwords is interpolated from `.env` and **defaults to** `true`;
* the eleven variables that **replace** those passwords are not interpolated at all, and reach the container only via `.env.local` — which no example file and no doc mentions.

So the natural path (`.env`, which is what `env.example` and the deploy docs use) gives you: seeding **on**, published credentials **live**, and your rotation **ignored** — while the seeder logs that it updated the accounts.

Blast radius is **every compose deploy**: local, the demo VM, and Kintsugi. `docker-compose.local.yml` `include:`s `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, so the canonical local stack inherits it, and the demo VM + Kintsugi run that file directly.

## Recommendation

Two small changes, both in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

1. Flip the default: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-false}`, and set it explicitly to `true` in the local-dev path that actually wants it. Opting in should be an act, not an omission.
2. Interpolate the eleven rotation variables in the `auth` service's `environment:` block the same way every other secret is (`- DEMO_USER_PASSWORD=${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD:-}` …), so `.env` — the file everyone edits — is a working channel. Then document them in `env.example`.

Neither is a code change to the auth service; the seeder's logic (`userRepo.ts:965-995`) is correct as written.

## A — the gate defaults to ON, and its stated premise is dead

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:626`

```yaml
- ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-true}
```

The pen-test **F-05** fix gated the demo seeder on this variable. The auth service states the premise the gate rests on, at `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:987-991`:

> *"The hardcoded fallbacks remain only because the seeder itself is now gated on* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` *(above) — i.e. **a deploy that doesn't explicitly opt in never sees these strings**."*

That premise is false for every compose deploy, because the compose file opts in on your behalf.

The justification for the default is at `:623-625`:

> *"Defaults to true here ONLY because docker-compose.yml is the local-dev compose; production is on Container Apps where this env var is unset and the gate stays closed."*

**That reasoning died with the KS-414 VM pivot (2026-07-08).** The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31. Since the pivot, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` is not "the local-dev compose" — it is *the* deployment artefact for the demo VM and now for Kintsugi as well. The comment describes an architecture the project no longer has.

Measured on the running local stack:

```
$ docker exec secuura-auth sh -c 'echo $ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS'
true
```

## B — the eleven rotation variables never reach the container from `.env`

Derived from source rather than from any prior write-up — every `seedPw()` call site in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`:

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_APEX_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_BUPA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_DELTA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_GREENFIELD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_OXFORD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD`

| check | result | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| occurrences of each of the 11 in `docker-compose.yml` | **0 / 11** | `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` → **1** |
| present in the running `secuura-auth` container | **0 / 11** | gate present, value `true`; 95 env vars total |

Both zero-results carry a control that fires independently, so they are real absences and not a grep that could never match.

The code's own rotation instruction (`userRepo.ts:992-993`) is:

> *"For per-tenant rotation, set* `DEMO_<TENANT>_PASSWORD` *env vars in Azure Key Vault and **surface them to the auth container**."*

"Surface them to the auth container" is the whole problem — it names no channel, and only one of the two obvious ones works.

## The correction — this is NOT "rotation is impossible"

An earlier write-up of this (KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a`) concluded the documented rotation *cannot work*. **That over-claims, and the correction matters because it changes the fix.** The `auth` service does declare an env_file:

```yaml
env_file:
  - path: .env.local
    required: false
```

Tested rather than assumed: of the **66** variables declared in `.env.local`, **66** are present in the running container. `.env.local` is a fully working injection channel.

So the accurate finding is an **asymmetry of channel**, which is worse than a flat "it doesn't work" because it fails silently in exactly one direction:

| variable | channel | reaches container from `.env`? | effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` | `${…:-true}` interpolation | **yes**, and defaults **true** | published `*123` credentials get seeded |
| the 11 `*_PASSWORD` vars | `.env.local` env_file only | **no** | rotation silently ignored |

`.env` is the file `env.example` is copied to, the file the setup instructions name, and the file compose reads for `${…}` interpolation — but it is *not* an env_file for `auth`, so values placed there are invisible to the seeder. Neither `env.example` nor `.env.local.example` mentions any of the eleven, or the gate.

## Why it fails convincingly

Recorded on Kintsugi during the KS-601 Stage C build (2026-08-20) — **this half is that session's on-box measurement; I have not re-run it here**, because reproducing it locally means changing `demo@`'s password and breaking the preflight persona:

Setting the eleven in `.env` and recreating the auth container printed `Demo user updated to match seed config` account after account — on a code path that genuinely does execute an `UPDATE … password_hash`. **The old password still authenticated.** Only a negative control (attempting a login with the *old* credential and expecting it to fail) caught it. Fixed on that box with a compose override making all 11 visible, then verified both directions: old `demo123` → **401**, new credential → **200**.

That is the part worth carrying: the failure produces success-shaped log output, so anyone rotating credentials and checking the logs will believe they succeeded.

## Scope note

Not in scope here: whether the demo VM *should* keep its seeded public credentials. Those are deliberate, documented sample logins for public demos (project `CLAUDE.md`). This ticket is about a deploy coming up more permissive than its operator intended, and a rotation that reports success without doing anything.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:570-666` — `auth` service; `:626` the gate; `:623-625` the dead premise; `env_file` at `:576-578`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:965-995` — the F-05 gate, the `seedPw()` helper and its rotation instruction.
* `docker-compose.local.yml:33-35` — `include:` of `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example`, `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` — neither names the eleven or the gate.
* KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a` — the Kintsugi on-box record (superseded on the "cannot work" point by the correction above).

## Suggested owner

Unassigned deliberately. Compose/deploy topology rather than service logic — @peter or @stuart to route; happy to take it myself if neither has context loaded.

nodes.body:
**One more instance of the same mechanism, found during the KS-1016 verification run (2026-09-10).**

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is read by `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:1123` (`requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')`) and listed in `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:133`, but it does not appear anywhere in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` on develop — so a value in a local `.env` never reaches the auth container. Observed on a fresh slot-4 stack with the key set in `.env`:

```
[auth] Demo user seeding skipped — no password supplied, and no pre-existing row to remediate
       {"email":"admin@secuura.com","hint":"set ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD to seed this account instead"}
```

and `env` inside `secuura-s4-auth` has no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` entry. The hint in the log therefore points at something the operator cannot make work locally. `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` shows the same skip line for `platform.admin@secuura-test.invalid`, so it is likely the same gap.

Effect on the harness: every `super_admin` persona login is 401, which on the Schemathesis pre-merge run reads as 18 pytest failures plus the sweep's persona auth and the coverage gate (runs `pre-merge-ks-1016-2026-09-10T07-56-30Z-slot3` and `…T08-33-27Z-slot4`, identical sets). Attributed here rather than to that branch — it is compose plumbing, not test code.

**Update, same day:** the forwarding already exists on PR #896 (KS-682) — `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` appears 3× in its `docker-compose.yml`, 0× on develop and 0× on #933. So this instance closes when #896 merges; nothing further is needed here for it beyond the record. KS-955 §5 describes the wider chain this sits in (401 → 429 → account lockout); the 429 half was confirmed removable with `LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED=true` on slot 4 (12 rapid logins, all 200), the 401 half is this.

Related: KS-966 (the change that made the key required), KS-972 (the banner still printing the old value), KS-955, KS-969. Branch under verification: `feature/ks-1016-test_anchor_read_honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura`. Host: local Docker Desktop, one slot at a time, macOS arm64.

title: #568 publishes 17 URLs on secuura.io — an unresolving, seemingly unowned domain (KS-669 class; no guard rule covers URLs)
description:
## BLUF

**#568 publishes 17 URLs on** `secuura.io` **— a domain that does not resolve and that we do not appear to own.** This is the same class as [[KS-669]] (`exports.secuura.com`, an unowned for-sale domain in the published spec), three weeks on, and it is back because **no guard rule covers URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only sees email addresses.

Filed separately from KS-669 rather than as a comment on it, deliberately: KS-669 is In Progress with its own scope (17 of its 18 URLs are still open work) and its operative defect is that it is **unassigned**. Folding a second, differently-sourced class into it makes it bigger, not more actionable. Cross-linked both ways.

**Stated fairly in both directions: #568 is a net improvement here.** It *removes* all **3** `demo@secuura.io` addresses that `develop` publishes today — E1 doing exactly its job. The URL class is the part nothing checks.

---

## Evidence

**DNS, with a control set** (2026-08-21):

| Domain | rcode | NS | SOA |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none | none |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns2.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns4.afternic.com.` | present |

The three controls resolve, so the resolver works and the NXDOMAIN discriminates.

⚠ **A limit on this evidence, stated rather than glossed:** `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` describes the TLD, not the domain. **I am reporting DNS only — NXDOMAIN with no NS and no SOA. I am not claiming a registration status.** Someone with registrar access should confirm ownership before this is closed either way.

**Occurrences in the published spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`):

| Pattern | `c114ceddd` (#568) | `origin/develop` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | **0** |
| `demo@secuura.io` | **0** | **3** |

Repo-wide on #568 the string appears **35** times across 7 files — the 17 published ones plus 18 in the generating sources (`auth`, `billing`, `m365-integration`, `originate`, `prism` `.openapi.ts`, and `synthesize.ts`). Fixing the source fixes both.

**The 17, by field** — these are not all cosmetic:

* `redirectUri` ×1 · `webhookUrl` ×1 · `successUrl` ×2 · `cancelUrl` ×2 · `siteUrl` ×1
* `serviceEndpoint` ×5 · `url` ×3 · bare array items ×2

`redirectUri`, `webhookUrl`, `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` and `serviceEndpoint` are all fields an integrator may copy into a working configuration. A published spec that points them at an unregistered domain is a domain anyone can register.

**Source** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`:

```ts
case 'uri':
case 'url':
    return 'https://example.secuura.io/resource';
```

Every `format: uri` / `format: url` field gets this one literal.

---

## Fix direction

Use a domain reserved for the purpose. `example.com` **is reserved by RFC 2606 / RFC 6761** and can never be registered by anyone — which is the same guarantee the email side already relies on (E1 permits `example.com` addresses). `https://example.com/resource` is a one-line change at `synthesize.ts:203`, plus a regeneration.

**Then close the hole that let it back in:** add a URL rule to the guard — an example whose value parses as a URL must have a host in the reserved set (`example.com`/`.org`/`.net`, `localhost`), or be allowlisted with a reason. Without it this class returns a third time. That rule belongs with the guard-coverage work in the sibling ticket.

---

## Calls needed from @PeterD

1. **Do we own** `secuura.io`**?** If we do, this drops to "point it somewhere real or use `example.com` anyway". If we don't, it should not be in a published spec at all.
2. Is `example.com` acceptable as the synthesised URL host, or do you want a real owned host (e.g. under `secuura.ai`)?

---

**Verified by:** @kamil.kreiser, 2026-08-21 — DNS with control set, occurrence counts on both refs, source line read. Working tree untouched. Related: KS-669 (same class, `exports.secuura.com`), KS-256/#568, KS-665.

nodes.body:
**In Review reconciliation 2026-09-05 → Backlog.**

Never started — no PR and no remote branch. In Review was the wrong state, not a stale ticket: inert since the day it opened, 2026-08-21.

This is a state correction, not a judgement on the work's value.

## BLUF

**Fixed and pushed — but the fix is four times bigger than this ticket implies, because changing the generator alone would have fixed nothing.** The 17 published URLs are **not** synthesised at generation time; they are baked literals in five service sources, and `generate-openapi` reproduces them verbatim from there. Published spec now carries **`secuura.io` zero times in any form** (17 → 0).

Branch `feature/ks-677-check-spec-examples-is-blind-to-path-parameter-and-scalar`, commit `511956f04`. **Based on `c114ceddd` (#568's head), pushed, no PR** — develop has no `scripts/openapi-examples/` at all and publishes none of these URLs, so there is nothing to fix there. **Patch for #568**: cherry-pick the commit, or take the branch.

## RECOMMENDATION

Take it if you are happy with `example.com` as the synthesised host. If you would rather each field carried a semantically distinct host, say so and I will redo it — `successUrl`, `cancelUrl`, `redirectUri`, `webhookUrl` and `serviceEndpoint` currently all share one string, and choosing otherwise is a design call I deliberately did not make for you.

## THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS

The plan I was given said *"develop publishes 0 instances, so this branch changes generator behaviour only — the 17 published instances get fixed when Peter regenerates."* **Regenerating would not have touched them.** Where the 17 actually live:

| file | count |
|---|---|
| `services/prism/src/prism.openapi.ts` | 5 |
| `services/billing/src/billing.openapi.ts` | 5 |
| `services/m365-integration/src/m365-integration.openapi.ts` | 3 |
| `services/auth/src/auth.openapi.ts` | 2 |
| `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts` | 2 |
| **total** | **17** — exactly the published count |

`generate-openapi` builds the YAML *from* those sources, so a regenerated unchanged tree emits the same 17. The commit therefore changes the generator (`synthesize.ts:203`) **and** the 17 baked literals **and** the generated spec — the last of which is also what keeps `generate-openapi --check` green.

## WHY `example.com`, VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED

I was pointed at another project's finding that `.invalid` / `.test` get rejected by validators while `example.com` survives. I did not rely on it. The local reason is stronger: **`EXAMPLE_DOMAIN` in `packages/shared/src/openapi/examples/fixtures.ts:67` is already `example.com`**, and it is the domain rule E1 accepts for addresses. The spec now has one reserved domain instead of one reserved domain plus one unregistered one.

Checked against this repo's own validators:

| validator | result |
|---|---|
| `ssrf-guard` `checkUrlLiteral` | `https://example.com/resource` → **ok** |
| … controls | `localhost` (loopback), `10.0.0.5` (RFC1918), `169.254.169.254` (link-local) all **rejected on host grounds** — so the host path demonstrably runs rather than the scheme check short-circuiting it |
| `generate-openapi --check` | **exit 0** — and it **failed** before the regen, so the drift check discriminates |
| `check:spec-examples` | exit 0, 394 example blocks |
| KS-256 contract suite | 27/27 |
| pre-push preflight | 7/7 |

## DNS, RE-VERIFIED WITH A CONTROL SET

| domain | status | A | NS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none | none |
| `example.com` | NOERROR | 172.66.147.243 | elliott.ns.cloudflare.com |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | 216.198.79.1 | dns2.registrar-servers.com |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | 216.198.79.1 | dns2.registrar-servers.com |

DNS only. As noted when this was filed, `whois secuura.io` falls through to the `.io` TLD record, so it cannot support a claim about registration either way.

## RESULT

`example.secuura.io` **17 → 0** · `example.com/resource` **0 → 17** · `secuura.io` in any form in the published spec **17 → 0**. The regeneration diff is **17 changed lines and nothing else** — a control looking for any non-URL change in the regenerated YAML returns empty, so nothing unrelated rode along.

## STILL YOURS, @PeterD

Do we own `secuura.io`? If we do, this may be the wrong fix and the domain should simply be pointed somewhere. If we do not, this is the change, and the remaining call is the per-field-host question above.

title: Anchor-status standoff: a consumer repolls anchors K reports as terminally failed — K's labelling is already honest (KS-587), so the fix is terminal-state handling, not a new K signal
description:
## BLUF

**The standoff is real, but its stated mechanism is wrong — and measuring demo inverted the ownership.** The premise going in was *"K reports simulated anchors as* `confirmed`*; Platform S's honesty rule refuses a* `mock_tx_` *hash; S repolls forever."* Measured on demo tonight, **K does not report them as confirmed.** All 83 simulated anchors on demo are flagged `simulated = true`, `status = failed`, carrying the explicit error `KS-587: simulated placeholder — never on chain; marked …`. **Zero rows on demo are** `simulated = true` **and** `confirmed`**.** K already fixed this — that is what **KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587** were.

So the accurate statement is: **a consumer is polling anchors that K reports as terminally** `failed`**, forever.** That is not a labelling defect on our side. It is a missing terminal-state rule on the consumer side.

## Recommendation

1. **Layer 1 — the actual fix, PS-side (Stuart's):** treat `status: failed` as **terminal** and stop polling. No new K signal is required; the one already published is sufficient and has been since KS-587 deployed.
2. **Layer 2 — K exposes** `simulated` **machine-readably: ALREADY DONE. This is a no-op, closed here, and no work should be raised for it.** Verified in the **shipped** demo image, not just the source tree.
3. **Layer 3 — env hygiene (Stuart's call):** whatever is polling demo from `52.74.18.212` should not be pointed at demo at all.
4. **Layer 4 — per-environment Blockfrost keys:** still open, still pending the credential question below.

## Detail — what was measured, on demo, read-only

**Demo is not simulating.** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is **absent** from the anchoring container's environment (0 matches against a 22-line env, so the read itself is proven). Boot logs: `Cardano integration active — real blockchain anchoring enabled`, `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"`, network `preview`.

`anchor_store` **composition — 285 rows total:**

| shape | `simulated` | `status` | n | first | last |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| real 64-hex | false | **confirmed** | **194** | 2026-07-08 | 2026-08-14 |
| `mock_tx_*` | **true** | **failed** | **83** | 2026-07-31 | 2026-08-01 |
| NULL | false | failed | 6 | 2026-07-11 | 2026-08-05 |
| real 64-hex | false | failed | 2 | 2026-08-04 | 2026-08-10 |

Crosstab, stated plainly because it is the whole argument: `simulated = true` appears **only** with `status = failed`. **There is no (**`simulated = true`**,** `confirmed`**) row on demo.** Controls: `simulated` is never NULL (0 of 285); totals reconcile 194 + 83 + 6 + 2 = 285.

**The loop's corpus is fully resident on demo — the cross-instance hypothesis is dead.** All **71** distinct anchor ids the loop requests are present in demo's `anchor_store`: **71 present / 0 absent**. Controls both fired: a fabricated id `anchor_0000…0000` matched **0**, a known-real id matched **1**. So these anchors were minted **on demo**; they were not minted on a simulated instance elsewhere and verified here.

**And every one of them is a failed anchor:**

|  | n |
| -- | -- |
| `simulated = true`, `failed`, mock hash | **68** |
| `simulated = false`, `failed`, NULL hash | **3** |
| **confirmed** | **0** |

That is the finding. The loop is polling **71 anchors that can never succeed**, 68 of which K has explicitly labelled as simulated placeholders that were never on chain.

**The** `simulated` **flag is machine-readable, and it ships.** In the **running** demo image (`/app/dist/index.js`, and `docker inspect` shows **no bind-mounts**, so the image *is* what serves):

* `...(simulated ? { simulated: true, simulatedTxRef: rawTxHash } : {})` — 3 emit sites
* `verified: !txView.simulated && anchor.status === 'confirmed'`
* a placeholder hash is moved to `simulatedTxRef` and `transactionHash` is set to **null**, so a mock hash is never presented as a transaction hash

Control: a nonsense token grepped for in the same file returned 0. Source agrees (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `honestTxView`, `anchoring.openapi.ts` `simulated: z.boolean().optional()` + `simulatedTxRef`).

**The Blockfrost split — both "zero Blockfrost calls" and "quota exhausted" are true at once.** They describe **different routes**:

| route | behaviour | last 60 min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` | **pure DB read**, ~1 ms, no Blockfrost | **1,970 × 200** |
| `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` | **live Blockfrost** | **608 × 200 · 460 × 500** |

**457** of those 500s carry Blockfrost's own string `"Usage is over limit."` (against 3,935 total anchoring log lines). So Stuart's agent's *"zero Blockfrost calls in two hours"* is **correct for status GETs** — that is exactly what they observed, and it is a real property of the code. Our *"quota exhausted"* is **correct for verify-by-hash**. Neither observation refutes the other; the earlier reconciliation hypothesis (creation-simulated / verify-live) was the right shape but the wrong axis — it is **status-read vs verify-by-hash**, not creation vs verification.

**Traffic, for scale.** Last 6 h at demo's edge: **23,515 requests from** `52.74.18.212`**, of 23,515 total — 100.0%** of demo's inbound. Split: `POST /api/verification/verify` 11,620 · `GET /api/anchors/{id}` 9,704 · `GET /api/documents/{id}` 2,190 — **all 200 at the gateway.** ~3,919/hr, consistent with the ~3,850/hr measured on KS-670 across 08-14 → 08-21.

## Attribution, corrected gently

Stuart's agent read the honesty rule as **S's**. The record says the honest-labelling rule was implemented **in K**: **KS-520** (Urgent, Done) — anchoring fabricated a `tx_sim_` hash and marked the document anchored under `SIMULATE_ANCHORING`; **KS-522** (High, Done) — a simulated anchor presented as genuinely verified, no honest-labelling signal; **KS-587** (High, Deployed to UAT) — *"84 demo anchors carry* `mock_tx_` *hashes but are flagged* `simulated=false` *+ confirmed"*. KS-587 is the direct ancestor of this ticket: it found **84** mis-flagged rows and remediated them. Tonight demo holds **83** rows carrying its remediation message. **The defect Stuart's agent describes is one K already found and fixed** — which is worth saying clearly, because it means no K change is needed and the polling behaviour is unaffected by anything we ship.

Credit where due: their diagnosis of the *mechanism* — a consumer refusing a mock hash and retrying forever — is correct and is what made this tractable. Only the direction of the labelling defect was off, and their own caveat (which K instance they queried was unstated) is what prompted the measurement that found it.

## What their numbers describe

Their **1,638 anchors, all simulated** is **not demo** — demo has **285** anchors, of which 83 are simulated. Since all 71 polled ids resolve on demo, the polling target is demo; the 1,638-row instance they inspected is a different K (most likely one of the local development stacks). **Not asserted, and it does not change the finding:** the fix is terminal-state handling regardless of which K holds the larger simulated corpus.

## Still open

* **The credential question, unanswered since 2026-08-20:** does the local K stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key or its own? If demo's, per-environment key scoping becomes the durable fix, and Kintsugi (its own free-tier project per environment) is the working precedent.
* **The Blockfrost allowance *period* is still unverified** — nothing here should be sized on a 50k/day assumption.

## Provenance

* Demo measurements | read-only SSH to `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-08-21 10:26–10:40Z | container env, `docker logs`, `psql` SELECTs, and one `docker inspect`. **No writes, no config change, no key action, no restarts.** Two scratch files created under the VM's `/tmp` during extraction were removed in the same command.
* Loop corpus | demo nginx gateway logs, 6 h window | two of my own extraction patterns were wrong on the first pass (`doc_` vs `doc-`, and verify hashes ride in the POST body rather than the URL); both corrected before any figure here was written down.
* KS-520 / KS-522 / KS-587 / PS-522 | live Linear reads, 2026-08-21 | `PS-522` returns nothing; `KS-999` used as a not-found control.

nodes.body:
## Confirmed at demo's edge — the loop is gone, and the slow lane left its own signature rather than just a silence

## BLUF

@stuart.jamieson — **measured on demo, your fix works, and the evidence is better than "the traffic stopped."** The loop from `52.74.18.212` has collapsed **from ~3,906 requests/hour to 60/hour**, a **98.5%** reduction, and the Blockfrost-consuming route is down **~99.9%**. More usefully: at **18:16–18:18Z** all **71** parked anchors were polled **exactly once each** — the 6-hour revisit lane firing for the first time, on schedule. That pattern is the fix running. A merely-dead process would have produced zero.

**One thing this does *not* fix, and it is ours, not yours: the Blockfrost allowance has not rolled.** Probed live just now from inside `secuura-anchoring` — demo key **402 Project Over Limit**, deliberately wrong key **403** as the control. So demo's on-chain verification is **still down**; the *cause* of the exhaustion is gone, the exhaustion itself has not lapsed yet. That is KS-670, not this ticket, and not your fix's job.

## RECOMMENDATION

Nothing needed from you here. Layer 1 is closed on the evidence below. What remains is ours (KS-670's quota recovery), yours-but-separate (**Layer 3** — the residual poller below), and still-open (**Layer 4**).

---

## The measurement

Instrument unchanged from the sessions before this one: demo's nginx gateway log, whole-loop rate by hour, plus the corpus. Buffer covers **2026-08-14T05:06:59Z → 2026-08-21T20:17:30Z**, so the window is fully inside the retained log — no clipping.

| window | requests/hour from `52.74.18.212` |
| -- | -- |
| 20 Aug 15:00–23:00Z | 3,856–3,956 |
| 21 Aug 00:00–11:00Z | 3,390–3,957 |
| **21 Aug 13:00–19:00Z** | **60** |

Share of demo's total inbound: **100%** before, **100%** after — it is still the only caller, just a vastly quieter one.

By route, the part that matters for the quota:

| route | before (per hour) | after (7 hours total) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/verification/verify` — the Blockfrost-backed path | ~1,930 | **17** |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` — DB read | ~1,560 | **71** |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}` — DB read | ~350 | 432 |

## 🔴 A correction to my own first reading, because it changes the attribution

My first pass read the collapse as **12:51Z** from hourly buckets and I nearly wrote that down. At minute resolution it is **12:17Z** — the 12:00 bucket simply held its last 17 minutes at full rate. The sequence:

- **12:17Z** — anchor GETs and verify POSTs both stop dead. Not a taper: 12:17 has 33 anchor + 5 verify, 12:18 has 0 and 0.
- **12:51Z** — the steady document poll halves, 2/min → 1/min. That is your container replacement (image built 12:48:44Z, up 12:51Z, per PS-645).
- **18:16–18:18Z** — the burst below.

So the *stop* preceded your deploy by 34 minutes, which is exactly what taking the old service down for a redeploy looks like. **The stop alone therefore proves nothing about the fix** — a killed process gives the same picture. Worth being explicit about, because it would have been easy and wrong to credit the fix with the silence.

## The evidence that *is* about the fix

| | |
| -- | -- |
| anchors polled 18:16–18:18Z | **71** |
| times each was polled | **exactly 1** — the histogram is 71 anchors × 1 poll, no other bucket |
| corroborating verifies in the same burst | 17 |
| requests in the gap 12:18Z → 18:15Z | **0**, against a control of 1,072 in the surrounding hours |
| interval from last pre-stop poll (12:16–12:17Z) | **~6h 00m** |

**That is `RefreshFailedRevisitHours` = 6 firing, and nothing else looks like it.** Each parked row revisited once and re-parked; none re-entered the fast lane. Your design description — a cadence rather than a tombstone, because PS-577 exists — is doing precisely what you said it would, and I can see the shape of it in someone else's logs, which is the nicest way to have a claim confirmed.

The 17 verifies against 71 anchors also matches your account: simulated rows park **without** corroboration, only genuine faileds pay for a chain lookup on revisit.

## PS-645 read before writing this

Your estate check closes cleanly and its uat-ps numbers reconcile with mine from the other side: **86 placeholders of which 71 are `anchor_` refs** — the same 71-anchor corpus I count at demo's gateway, independently. dev-ps empty, prod out of scope on the unexplained changed ED25519 host key. Not bypassing strict checking on a production box was the right call.

## The residual — one poller is still pointed at demo (Layer 3)

Steady, unbroken, through all of the above:

```
GET /api/documents/doc-1786170172896-935abaa5    once per minute
```

**438 of the 452 document GETs since 13:00Z are that single document id** — one document, 1/min, **~1,440 requests/day**. It is a DB read and touches no Blockfrost, so it costs demo almost nothing — but it is the whole of demo's remaining inbound traffic, and it is the concrete form of the Layer 3 question: *should that box be pointed at demo at all?* Flagging, not asking you to act today.

## Still open, and not re-asked

**Layer 4 — the credential question** (does that stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key, or its own?) remains asked and unanswered from 2026-08-20. Recording it as open; per-environment keys are still the durable fix and Kintsugi is the precedent.

---

*Measured read-only on demo: nginx and anchoring log reads, plus the two staged Blockfrost probes from inside the container. No writes, no config, no restarts. Quota state and its control recorded on KS-670.*

**Layer 1 is merged** — PS-644's slow-lane parking landed on Platform-S develop (`f29173c`, PR #581) and PS-644 is Done. Verified live before merge: 19 suite-created anchors all parked after one status poll each, and 0 anchor GETs + 0 verify POSTs in idle sampling where the old loop produced ~228.

Local estate update relevant to your traffic figures: the machine's last old-code poller — a host-run S from a stale worktree, up since 08-14, which was the "105 anchors / 1,638-row local K" driver — was stopped today, so this machine now contributes zero anchor polling to any K.

**Unchanged and still yours/Stuart's:** the 52.74.18.212→demo loop continues until the fix deploys to that environment (S-side deploys are manual while GitHub Actions billing is dead), your Layer 3 (whether that box should point at demo at all) and Layer 4 (per-environment Blockfrost keys + the 2026-08-20 credential question), and the estate check now tracked on PS-645.

Layer 1 is implemented on Platform-S: https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/581 (PS-644, In Review).

Your measurement reshaped the fix, so recording what changed because of it:

- **`failed` is now effectively terminal — as a cadence, not a tombstone.** Rows last observed failed/simulated leave the fast lane for `RefreshFailedRevisitHours` (default 6 h) and re-enter by themselves. We kept a slow-lane revisit rather than a hard stop deliberately: PS-577 exists because 91 UAT anchors sat "failed" on the anchors endpoint while your verify reported them confirmed with real hashes — if K's reconcile ever heals a row again, S still collects it, just hours later instead of never.
- **Your Blockfrost split is what killed the corroboration cost.** Since status GETs are pure DB reads and verify-by-hash is the Blockfrost-backed route, the expensive part of S's loop was PS-577's corroborating verify on every failed poll. Simulated anchors now park **without** corroboration at all (no chain fact exists to find), and genuine faileds corroborate only on slow-lane revisits.
- **Attribution accepted:** the honest-labelling chain (KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587) is K's, and your read that the 1,638-row instance was a local dev K is right — it's the laptop stack, which predates KS-587 and still reports simulated anchors as `confirmed` + `mock_tx_`. S handles both shapes: your `simulated: true` flag first, mock-prefix fallback for older images.

Verified live on that local stack rebuilt with the fix: 19 suite-created anchors all parked after one status poll each; 3 idle minutes = **0** anchor GETs and **0** verify POSTs where the old loop produced ~228. Once this deploys to the environment behind `52.74.18.212`, the 71-anchor loop against demo should collapse the same way — your Layer 3 (whether that box should point at demo at all) and Layer 4 (per-environment Blockfrost keys, plus the credential question from 2026-08-20) remain open for Stuart.

title: Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic — three runs on near-identical code gave 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH (different endpoint) / 0 HIGH
description:
## BLUF

**Three Akto** `test:pr` **runs tonight, same harness, same command, gave three different answers — and none of the three carried a captured request or response.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot be read either way: its PASS is not evidence of absence, and its FAIL is not evidence of a defect until re-derived by hand.

## Measured — 2026-08-27, all three within ~20 minutes

| run | target | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- |
| baseline (s76) | `develop ca5b643e0` | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on a **GDPR** route |
| KS-694 fix branch | `develop` + the KS-694 role-gate fix (touches `gdpr.ts` + `systemErrors.ts` only) | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on `GET /api/documents` |
| 17-PR integration stack | `develop cc65abad5` + 17 open PRs | **0** — `verdict: PASS`, 804 clean, 2 known-FP |

The middle run is the one that rules out "the code changed": that branch touches two route files and cannot have introduced or removed a finding on `/api/documents`.

## The `/api/documents` finding does not reproduce

Derived by hand rather than trusted:

* `?userId=` **injection changes nothing.** The identical document set comes back with no `userId`, with another user's, and with a third user's.
* **Cross-tenant isolation holds.** A default-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 18 documents, an oxford-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 70, **full-id overlap 0**. (An earlier probe of my own appeared to show a shared document — that was an 8-character id truncation in my script, not a leak. Recording the false alarm so nobody re-derives it.)

## Why this matters now

Since 2026-08-27 the four local suites are the **only** merge gate (Kam: *"billing will not be fixed"*). Akto is one of the four. **Two of tonight's three runs would have produced a different merge decision on the same code.** That is the same failure mode `KS-519` names for permanently-red checks, arriving from the other direction.

## Related, already known

`KS-694` came out of the first of these runs — the finding was real but its **label** (`BOLA / ADD_USER_ID`) was wrong, and re-deriving it produced a more precise and more serious defect. Same pattern: the scanner points at something; the label and the endpoint are both unreliable.

## Suggested next step

Establish whether the variance is in the scan (endpoint sampling / timing / auth state) or the reporting, by running `test:pr` N times against a frozen commit with the stack untouched between runs, and recording the HIGH set each time. **Not started** — filed so tonight's measurement is not lost.

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — could you take a look? Some of the variance you measured here may now have a mechanism.

Your six-run table showed buckets moving on identical code with the total exactly conserved (4,702 every time), `known-fp` going `2 / 1 / 0 / 2 / 0 / 0`, and `authzPrecondition` co-varying inversely with `clean`. Your stated hypothesis was Akto's own per-run auth-context setup, flagged explicitly as untested.

**A second variable was present in every one of those runs and was invisible to the instrument.** Under KS-709 we found that Akto records an HTTP 429 as a *completed result carrying no error*, so a rate-limited test matched no branch of our classifier and fell through its `default:"clean"`. Measured on slot 2, 2026-09-28, full OWASP run `6aba139ce86558333055a8f9`: **8,735 of 50,018 results were 429s, 0 had any error, and all 8,735 sat in `clean`** — 79% of that run's entire clean bucket, under a verdict of PASS.

That is consistent with the shape you recorded: throttling is load- and timing-dependent, so it moves run to run; the total is conserved because the results still exist and are still counted; and it lands precisely in `clean`, the bucket you saw absorbing the movement.

**I am not claiming it explains your variance** — your runs were on a different commit and a different tier, `known-fp` movement is a detection difference that throttling does not obviously produce, and I have not re-run your six. It is a candidate that was not on the table when you measured, and it was unmeasurable then because the bucket did not exist.

`rateLimited` is now a first-class bucket, so a repeat of your six-run experiment would separate the two axes for the first time. That seems worth doing before anyone pays for the auth-context instrumentation you identified as the next step.

Your standing rule from this ticket — **"compare failing sets, never counts"** — is carried unchanged; nothing here weakens it.

## BLUF

**Re-measured on the fixed harness: six runs on one frozen commit, all with healthy captures. The variance is real — but this ticket's headline figure was partly an artifact of [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700), and I need to correct my own s79 conclusion.**

## 🔴 Correction — s79's `2 / 0 / 2` middle term was never measured

The three-run table on this ticket records `countIssues.HIGH` as **2 / 0 / 2** and concludes *"the platform never changes its answer; Akto changes its verdict."*

Run 2 of that set — `pr-2026-08-27T11-28-03Z` — is **the run whose Mongo capture failed**. It is the exact run KS-700 was filed about. Verified directly in its artifact just now: `skipBreakdown` is **absent**, so no bucket data was ever recorded, and its "0" is the false zero, not a measurement.

The two runs in that set that *did* measure agreed **exactly**:

| s79 run | known-fp | clean | authz-precondition | total |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `11-27-28Z` | 2 | 804 | 255 | 4702 |
| `11-28-03Z` | — | — | — | **CAPTURE FAILED — nothing measured** |
| `11-28-50Z` | 2 | 804 | 257 | 4702 |

So the evidence s79 offered for non-determinism was two runs that agreed and one that did not report. **The conclusion happened to be right — the new data below shows real variance — but it was not supported by the data it was drawn from.** This is exactly the failure mode KS-700 describes: a capture failure is indistinguishable from a measurement, and it got read as one.

## New measurement — 6 runs, one commit, all captures healthy

Commit `2e3800a71`, stack untouched, runs 20–40 s apart, `testResultsCount` = **4702** every time:

| run | known-fp | clean | connectivity | authz-precondition | not-applicable | total | capture |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | **2** | 803 | 1 | 257 | 3279 | 4702 | OK |
| 2 | **1** | 806 | 1 | 253 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 3 | **0** | 810 | 0 | 251 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 4 | **2** | 804 | 0 | 255 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 5 | **0** | 810 | 0 | 251 | 3281 | 4702 | OK |
| 6 | **0** | 810 | 0 | 253 | 3279 | 4702 | OK |

**The variance is confirmed: `2 / 1 / 0 / 2 / 0 / 0`.** Every run: verdict PASS, `vulnerable 0`, and the flagged endpoints are always the same two — `GET /api/identity-credentials/types` and `GET /api/oauth/scopes`, both `REMOVE_TOKENS`, both caught by the endpoint-scoped FP register (hence known-fp rather than vulnerable).

### Three things the six runs establish that three could not

1. **It is not warming.** Runs 1→3 declined 2→1→0, which looks like accumulated state — and then run 4 went back to **2**. A three-run window would have supported a warming hypothesis that six runs refute.
2. **The total is exactly conserved.** 4702 in all six, and the per-bucket sums reconcile to it every time. Results **move between buckets**; none are lost. So this is a classification difference, not a coverage difference.
3. **`clean` tracks the flag inversely and `authzPrecondition` co-varies.** known-fp 2 → clean 803–804; known-fp 0 → clean 810. `authzPrecondition` moves 251–257 across the same runs.

### What that points at (hypothesis, not a finding)

The co-variation of `authzPrecondition` with the flag suggests the variable is **Akto's own per-run auth-context setup**, not its detection logic: when more results execute cleanly, fewer land in the authz-precondition bucket and the no-auth template has a different baseline to compare against. s79 established the platform side is stable — both endpoints answered **200 unauthenticated, 20/20**, with controls firing.

**I have not tested this.** It is the next thing to measure, and it needs a run that records Akto's auth setup per run, which the harness does not currently capture.

## Status of the KS-700 blocker

s79 recorded KS-700 as blocking this ticket's root cause. Partly cleared: the six runs above all captured successfully, so the false zero **did not recur** and this data is trustworthy. But that also means run 2 of s79 — the one run that would have told us what a divergent run looks like from the inside — remains unexplained, and the false zero is **intermittent**, so it can still corrupt a future measurement. The KS-700 fix (PR [#752](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/752)) makes such a run **fail loudly** rather than report zeros, which is what makes measurements like this one safe to trust going forward.

---

*Measured 2026-08-27, session 80, on the KS-700 branch. Read-only against the local stack; demo untouched.*

## BLUF

**Measured: three `test:pr` runs on a frozen commit and an untouched stack, 35–47 s apart. Akto's own issue count came back 2 / 0 / 2 — and the platform answers those endpoints identically 20/20.** So the variance is inside Akto's verdict engine: not the code under test, not the platform, and not our reporting.

**Two further things fell out, and both change what this ticket is about:**

1. **"No captured request" is ours, not Akto's.** Akto captured a full request+response for **every** flagged result — verified directly in Mongo (3,030–46,378 characters of `testResults[0].message`). Our report says `request: null` and prints a placeholder curl reading *"Akto returned no captured request for this result"*. The data is one field away from the report.
2. 🔴 **The harness can fail its capture silently and then print a FALSE ZERO.** Run 2 emitted `throughput: 0 results (0 executed) in 36s — no executed requests`. Mongo says run 2 executed **4,702** results. Nothing was logged at default level. Filed separately as **KS-700**.

## Recommendation

Fix the capture before chasing the engine. Two of the three problems here are ours and are cheap; the Akto-engine variance is real but is the expensive one, and it cannot be triaged while findings arrive without a reproducer.

## Detail — the three runs (item 1's ask)

Commit `cd52a6a7a` (#751's head — the running `originate` container was built from it at 11:00:30Z, two minutes after the commit). Stack untouched between runs: 37 containers, 0 unhealthy. All three runs `state=COMPLETED`, `testResultsCount=4702`, 4,702 docs in Mongo.

| run | wall | Akto `countIssues.HIGH` | flagged results in Mongo | identity | captured request **in Mongo** | captured request **in our report** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 · `pr-2026-08-27T11-27-28Z` | 19.2 s | **2** | 2 | `REMOVE_TOKENS` `/api/oauth/scopes` · `REMOVE_TOKENS` `/api/identity-credentials/types` | yes — 3,526 / 3,031 chars | **none captured** |
| 2 · `pr-2026-08-27T11-28-03Z` | 39.8 s | **0** | 0 | — | n/a | **none captured** + every rich field `null` |
| 3 · `pr-2026-08-27T11-28-50Z` | 29.8 s | **2** | 2 | the same two | yes — 3,030 / 3,527 chars | **none captured** |

Runs 1 and 3 reported `verdict: PASS` because both findings are known-FPs; run 2 reported PASS with no bucket data at all. **All three PASS — for three different reasons.**

Bucket detail also moved between runs 1 and 3, conserving the total: `authzPrecondition` 255 → 257 and `byDesignFilter` 3281 → 3279. Two results changed classification on identical input.

### The discriminator: the platform is deterministic, Akto is not

`REMOVE_TOKENS` strips auth and checks whether data still comes back. Both flipping endpoints, probed unauthenticated 20 times each:

```
/api/oauth/scopes               200 ×20
/api/identity-credentials/types 200 ×20
controls: /api/documents 401 ×5   ·   /health 200 ×5
```

The controls discriminate. The platform's answer **never changes**, yet Akto flags these two in runs 1 and 3 and not in run 2. Both are intentionally-public reference endpoints, unrelated to #751's diff — so nothing about the code under test is involved.

**Per Wednesday's discriminator rule: no run flagged a route #751 touches (`transfer-custody` / `/api/documents`), so the extra clean-`develop` run was not required and was not done.**

### Root cause — stated as a HYPOTHESIS, not a result

**Not established.** What the evidence supports and does not:

- **Supports a timing/load-sensitivity hypothesis:** engine execution time varied 4× on identical work (`exec 3s` run 1 vs `exec 13s` run 3), and run 2 — the zero-finding run — had the longest wall clock (39.8 s).
- **Argues against it:** runs 1 and 3 differ by that same 4× and produced the *identical* finding set. So slower does not simply mean fewer findings.
- **Cannot be evaluated:** run 2's `engineTiming` is `null` (its capture failed), so the one run that matters most has no engine breakdown. That is a direct consequence of KS-700 — **the reporting gap is currently blocking the root-cause analysis.**

### KS-698 poisoning tested as a hypothesis — REFUTED

Asked whether KS-698's rate-limit poisoning could drive this. **It cannot**, and the first probe was inconclusive before it was refuted properly:

| probe | result | reading |
| -- | -- | -- |
| poisoned key, **no** bearer | 401 | inconclusive — never reached the handler |
| fresh key, **no** bearer (control) | 401 | **control agreed with the null → instrument not discriminating** |
| poisoned key, bearer | **500** ×2 | poisoning is live and still persistent ~40 min on |
| fresh key + valid `windowMs`, bearer (control) | **200** ×2 | control discriminates |

So KS-698 reproduces and persists — but the flipping findings are on two endpoints that are not the rate-limit route and that answer identically 20/20, so poisoning is not the mechanism here. Recording the first, non-discriminating probe because a control that agrees with the null is the signature that says suspect the instrument.

## Where the captured request is lost

`fetchRunResults` (`src/client/aktoTestRuns.ts:161`) POSTs to Akto's REST `/api/fetchTestingRunResults`, and that response carries the result documents **without** their `testResults[]` array — so `parseFinding` (`src/client/findingParser.ts:38`) reads `attempt.message ?? attempt.originalMessage` on an empty object and sets `request: null`.

The harness already knows this path is lossy. `src/report/resultsCapture.ts` says so in its own module docstring:

> *"Akto's REST `fetchTestingRunResults` is paginated, queryMode-segmented, and routed to a vulnerable-only collection — so for a clean run it returns nothing... All per-test detail, however, lives plainly in MongoDB."*

That module reads Mongo directly and is where the buckets/matrix/known-FP rows come from — but it derives **counts and classification only**, and never reads `testResults[].message`. So the reproducer is available in the same collection the rich capture already queries, one field away.

**Suggested fix direction (not built this session, per scope):** have `captureRunResults` project `testResults[0].message` for flagged results and use it to populate `request`/`response`, so `buildCurl` produces a real reproducer instead of the placeholder. That makes an Akto FAIL re-derivable by hand, which is the precondition for ever comparing finding *sets* on this gate the way we now do on Schemathesis.

## What this does to the merge gate

Two of tonight's three runs would have produced different bucket evidence on identical code, and one produced none at all while still reading PASS. Combined with KS-700, an Akto PASS currently means one of: nothing was flagged · things were flagged and reclassified as known-FP · or the capture failed and the run reported zeros it never measured. **Those three are not distinguishable from the console line**, which is the practical problem for the four-suite rule.

---

*Measured 2026-08-27, session 79. Runs on `cd52a6a7a`; artifacts under `systemTest/akto/output/reports/pr-2026-08-27T11-2*`. Read-only against Mongo; nothing merged, no deploy, demo untouched.*

## Schemathesis varies run-to-run too — but for the OPPOSITE reason, and the distinction matters

Not the measurement this ticket asks for (three Akto runs with capture on) — that is still to do. This is a finding from the same night that changes what this ticket is comparing against.

**Three Schemathesis `pr` runs on the same base commit gave three different failing sets:**

| run | count | set |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `pr-2026-08-27T10-12-12Z` | 9 | the KS-693 floor |
| `pr-2026-08-27T10-29-58Z` | 10 | floor **+ transfer-custody** (found KS-697) |
| `pr-2026-08-27T11-04-05Z` | 10 | floor **− transfer-custody + rate-limit/check** |

So **two of the four merge gates now vary run-to-run.** But they are not the same problem and should not be fixed as one:

| | Akto (this ticket) | Schemathesis |
| -- | -- | -- |
| varies across runs | yes — 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH / 0 HIGH | yes — 9 / 10 / 10 |
| **captured request** | **none** | **yes, replayable** |
| reproduces on demand | **no** | **100%** |
| what the variance means | the harness cannot show its work | the harness is doing its job on a latent bug |

The Schemathesis variance is **stochastic discovery of a deterministic defect** — Hypothesis has to generate a body that clears validation *and* carries an out-of-range value. Once it does, the captured curl reproduces every time. That is a working fuzzer, not a broken one. (The defect it found is now [KS-698](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-698) — one request permanently poisons a rate-limit key.)

Akto's variance has no captured request behind it, so there is nothing to replay and no way to tell a real finding from a phantom. **That is the thing this ticket should fix**, and it is a harness problem, not a platform one.

## Consequence for the merge gate, worth stating plainly

**"Schemathesis FAIL 9, byte-identical to baseline" is a weaker claim than it reads** — and it is the phrasing used on several PRs today, mine among them. A count is not a signature. The *set* of failing operations is, and only the set showed that the KS-697 fix had landed: this branch also scored 10, the same number as the run that found the bug.

Suggest the same rule lands on both gates: **compare failing sets, never counts.** For Akto that is blocked until findings carry a captured request — which is this ticket.

title: No table references `users`: 0 of the database's 29 foreign keys point at it, across 52 user-reference columns — KS-697 was this hole being exercised
description:
## BLUF

**No table in the platform database has a foreign key to** `users`**.** Not one — across **52** columns named `%user_id` / `%holder_id` / `%_by_id`. The schema *does* use foreign keys (**29** of them), which is what makes this a gap rather than a deliberate house style.

Every one of those 52 columns can therefore hold a uuid that references nobody, and nothing in the database will object.

## Measured — live local DB, `develop cc65abad5`

| measure | value |
| -- | -- |
| foreign keys in the database | **29** |
| of those, pointing at `users` | **0** |
| columns named like a user reference | **52** |
| FKs on `shares` (any) | **0** |
| FKs on `custody_events` | **1** — `document_id` only |

The `custody_events` row is the tell: that table *does* carry an FK, on `document_id`, and `to_holder_id` sits beside it without one.

## Why this is being filed now

[KS-697](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-697) was exactly this hole being exercised: `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` accepted an invented `newHolderId`, returned 201, and **minted an anchor** for a custody chain pointing at a user that has never existed. That route is fixed in application code ([PR #751](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/751>)) — but the fix is one handler, and the underlying condition covers 51 other columns.

Known second instance, unfixed: `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` format-checks `recipients[].userId` (KS-536) but **never checks it exists** — `shares.recipient_user_id` is cast to `::uuid` and inserted with no FK behind it. Lower blast radius than custody (no ownership flip, no anchor), but the same class.

## Not a "just add the FKs" ticket

Recording the reasons up front so whoever picks this up does not discover them the hard way:

1. `users` **is** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` **fail-closed** (migration 039). FK validation runs as the referencing statement's role, so adding FKs to an RLS-forced table needs thought about which role validates the reference and whether the tenant GUC is set at that moment. This is the KS-458 surface.
2. **Multi-tenancy may put** `users` **in a different database** from the referencing table under the per-tenant-DB model — a cross-database FK is not expressible. That has to be established per table before anything is added.
3. **Existing rows may already violate** what a new FK would assert. KS-697 alone wrote several on local. Any `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT` needs a survey first, and `NOT VALID` + a later `VALIDATE` is probably the shape.
4. **A count guard will lie here. **`users` under FORCE RLS returns 0 rows to a non-superuser without the tenant GUC — an "are there orphans?" query can read clean on a table full of them. Set `app.tenant_scope_bypass` before counting.

## Suggested first step

Not a migration. An **inventory**: for each of the 52 columns, which are genuinely user references, which live in the same database as `users`, and how many current rows are already orphaned. That survey decides whether this is one migration, several, or an application-layer rule instead.

Found during KS-697, 2026-08-27. Filed separately so it does not die when that ticket closes.

nodes.body:
## FINDING (recorded, not fixed here) — `data_subject_requests` declares a foreign key it does not have

Found while measuring the live schema for ask 1. **Not this ticket's work** and deliberately not fixed
tonight — recording it so it is not lost, and so nobody re-derives it from the migration file and reaches
the wrong answer.

`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:460` declares:

```sql
user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
```

The live table has **zero** foreign-key constraints.

**Controls, because "a query returned nothing" and "the query cannot match" look identical:**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| FKs on `data_subject_requests` | **0** |
| FKs in the database overall | **29** — so the schema does use them |
| FKs on `data_deletion_log`, declared in the *same migration* with `REFERENCES` clauses | **1** — so the same query does find them on a sibling table |

The absence is real, not a broken lookup.

**Why it matters beyond tidiness.** The `ON DELETE CASCADE` in that declaration is exactly the mechanism
[KS-293](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-293) found *not* firing for `refresh_tokens` — erasure
anonymises the user row with an `UPDATE` rather than deleting it, so a cascade never runs. Here the
cascade does not exist at all, which is a different failure with the same visible symptom: a reader of the
migration would conclude DSR rows are cleaned up by the database, and they are not.

It also compounds **[KS-699](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-699)** — *"No table references `users`:
0 of the database's 29 foreign keys point at it, across 52 user-reference columns"* — which is the same
class measured platform-wide. **This finding belongs with KS-699**, and I am not filing a separate ticket
for it: `issueCreate` still refuses at the workspace cap, and one more comment on a related open ticket is
better than a finding that lives only in a session log.

**What ask 1 does about it: nothing.** The `NOT NULL` is what the design turns on, and that is present and
enforced. The missing FK is noted and not relied on in either direction.

title: The whole super-admin surface is silently unscanned — no system_admin block means the HAR replay fallback never fires (0 of 16 endpoints, incl. KS-694's GDPR routes)
description:
## BLUF

Every **super-admin-only** endpoint is invisible to Akto on a stock local checkout, and nothing says so. `config/secrets.yml` carries no `system_admin` block — `config/secrets.example.yml` documents one — so `resolveReplayTokens()` returns `adminToken: null`, the issuer→admin fallback never fires, and each endpoint `ISSUER_ADMIN` cannot get a 2xx from stays a spec-imported placeholder (`responseCode: -1`) that `api_selection_filters` excludes from **every** BOLA/BFLA/authz template.

The bias is the problem: the endpoints that are hardest to authenticate to are the privileged ones, so the harness systematically skips the surface where an authz defect matters most — and reports green.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2

```
collection 56068490 "OpenAPI Secuura API": 323 endpoints
  absolute (scannable)  : 307
  relative (unscannable):  16

endpoints scanned, BOLA run:
  relative : 0 / 16
  absolute : 46 / 80 sampled     <-- discriminating control
```

The 16 that never get scanned:

```
/api/admin/audit/export      /api/analytics/activity        /api/analytics/certifications
/api/analytics/governance    /api/analytics/overview        /api/analytics/revenue
/api/analytics/users         /api/analytics/verifications   /api/audit-log
/api/billing/customers/by-email  /api/gdpr/consent/check    /api/gdpr/deletion-log
/api/m365/callback           /api/oauth/authorize           /api/onedrive/files
/api/system-errors
```

The 7 `analytics` paths are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS-357). **The other 9 are not excluded by anything — they are simply unreachable by the replay persona.** They include `/api/gdpr/deletion-log`, `/api/gdpr/consent/check` and `/api/system-errors` — the exact routes **KS-694 (Urgent)** just put a role gate on, and `/api/oauth/authorize`.

Note the tell: an unscannable entry is stored as a bare path (`/api/audit-log` — the tenant-provisioning upstream path) while a scanned one is a full gateway URL (`http://localhost:6882/api/documents`). That difference is a cheap, reliable detector.

## Proof of causation

Adding the documented `system_admin` block to local `secrets.yml` (gitignored; seeded `admin@secuura.com`, per `secrets.example.yml`):

```
captured 2xx samples : 71 → 79
audit-log in api_info: /api/audit-log  →  http://localhost:6882/api/platform/audit-log
ADD_USER_ID on it    : 0 rows → 1 row
```

That change is what made **KS-708** reproducible at all. Before it, `ADD_USER_ID` reported *"188 tested, 0 vulnerable"* while never touching the endpoint under investigation.

## The documentation understates it

`secrets.example.yml:30-34` says `system_admin` is *"optional. Only needed to seed the locked-account test-role… Absent ⇒ that one role is skipped (best-effort), and* `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` *keeps skipping honestly."*
