That is not the whole consequence. Absent, it also removes the entire super-admin surface from HAR replay, and therefore from every similarity-based authz template. Nobody reading that comment would expect it.

## Suggested shape

1. **Warn loudly when** `adminToken` **is null** — name the count of endpoints that will consequently have no 2xx sample. Silence is the actual defect; a skipped endpoint should never be indistinguishable from a clean one (the KS-700 / KS-709 principle, applied to coverage rather than results).
2. Correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence.
3. Consider failing `test:setup` when the block is absent, or defaulting it to the seeded local admin.

## Done means

1. A run without a system-admin token says so, with the affected endpoint count.
2. `secrets.example.yml` states the real consequence.
3. The relative-vs-absolute URL split is asserted somewhere, so this cannot silently regress.

nodes.body:
## BLUF

One observation for this ticket, measured rather than reasoned: when the **issuer** token is dead, the system-admin fallback feeds the replay **completely on its own**. So the fallback does work where a `system_admin` block exists. The side effect is that every uploaded sample then carries the system-admin bearer instead of the issuer's.

## What was run

Slot 4, 2026-09-30, Akto 2.36.4, found while verifying KS-1363:

| Run | Issuer token | Replay result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `test:pre-merge`, normal | real login | 61 samples in pass 1, **76** total, from 138 GET endpoints |
| `test:pre-merge`, `ISSUER_TOKEN=<deliberately invalid>` | invalid (every issuer GET 401s) | 61 in pass 1, **76** total, from 138 GET endpoints |

Identical counts: every endpoint the invalid issuer couldn't reach fell back to the system-admin session (`resolveReplayTokens` → `captureGetSamples` in `systemTest/akto/src/setup/harReplay.ts`), and it reached all of them.

## Why it may matter here

* The BOLA/BFLA templates then mutate a **super-admin** request, not an issuer one, and nothing in the run says which identity fed the samples. A dead issuer credential is invisible behind a full replay.
* KS-1363 now reports *whether* the replay fed, but deliberately not *as whom* (kept out of scope, per this ticket).

No code change made. Offered only as evidence for whoever picks up item 1 ("warn loudly when `adminToken` is null"), since the reverse case (a null *issuer* masked by the admin) is the same visibility gap.

title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — could you take a look? This is your ticket and I have **not** touched it, but there is now a measured reason it matters more than when you filed it.

Re-verified today on `feature/ks-1286-…` (2026-09-28): the premise still holds exactly as you wrote it. `test:pr` is `vitest run tests/prScan.test.ts` and `test:pre-merge` / `test:security` are the same shape — **none of them import**. The import lives only in `bin/setup.ts`, run separately, so a re-import still depends on someone remembering.

**Why it now looks like the largest lever on scan coverage.** Full OWASP run on slot 2, 50,162 results:

| bucket | count | share |
|---|---|---|
| `byDesignFilter` (template did not match the endpoint) | 36,946 | **74%** |
| `rateLimited` (429, new under KS-709) | 8,730 | 17% |
| `clean` | 2,338 | 5% |
| `notApplicableStack` | 1,717 | 3% |
| `authzPrecondition` | 419 | 1% |

`byDesignFilter` is by far the biggest bucket, and Akto's `api_selection_filters` match on **parameters** — which is precisely what your measurement showed the import restores: `loadParamsOfEndpoint` saw `identityCommitment` only *after* a re-import, and collection `urlsCount` went **190 → 352**.

**I am being careful not to overclaim:** most of that 74% is legitimate (194 templates × 348 endpoints — most genuinely do not apply), and I have not measured how much a re-import would recover. It could be a few percent. But it is the only bucket big enough for the answer to matter, and nobody has measured it.

Your false-zero warning is carried forward and is the part I would most want preserved in any fix: `getCollectionEndpointCount` read **325 before and after** an import that actually took it to 361, so the result must be verified on a **fresh re-read**, never on the value the import call returns.

Not picking this up — it is assigned to you and I did not want to take it without asking. If you would rather I did the harness side, say so here.

## BLUF

**Measured today: after a spec re-import, Akto CAN see `identityCommitment` at parameter level.** This ticket's premise — that `test:pr` never re-imports, so a newly declared field is invisible to Akto — is confirmed by the fact that the re-import was what changed it.

## Evidence

Ran the OpenAPI import against the widened spec (Peter's requirement 3 on [#760](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760)), on a tree rebased onto `436f37bed` so it carried KS-721's field.

Two Akto instruments queried for `POST /api/anchors`:

```
/api/loadParamsOfEndpoint   identityCommitment 1x    control 'metadata' 4x
/api/fetchAllParams         identityCommitment 0x    control 'metadata' 0x
```

One instrument sees it, the other sees neither it nor the control — so the positive comes from the endpoint that actually holds request-parameter data, not from a lucky substring match.

**Collection state, before → after the import:** `OpenAPI Secuura API` urlsCount **190 → 352**, api_info **325 → 361**. 27 collections before and after, none created, none lost.

## ⚠ A false zero that will bite the next person

**The endpoint count read 325 before the import and 325 after.** `getCollectionEndpointCount` called immediately after ingest returns a stale `api_info` list; a fresh capture moments later shows 361. That is the KS-700 shape — an operation that plainly worked, reporting a number that says it did nothing. Anyone automating a re-import check against that call will conclude the import is a no-op.

Worth folding into this ticket's fix: whatever makes `test:pr` re-import should verify the result on a **re-read**, not on the value the import call returns.

## What this does not settle

The re-import here was manual and one-off. This ticket is about `test:pr` doing it as a matter of course, and that is unchanged — the next `test:pr` run still will not re-import. So the KS-712 sweep benefit remains dependent on someone remembering to import by hand.

*Measured 2026-08-31 (session 93) on the local Akto stack, from the #760 review thread. Local containers only, not a shared instance. No code written for this ticket.*

title: Verify results show the user nothing about what was registered — a renamed file confirms green with no explanation (PS-723)
description:
## BLUF

**A verify result shows the user nothing about what was registered, so a renamed file confirms green with no way to notice the rename.** Stuart hit this on PS-723 and ruled the direction: *"it should be explained to the user, otherwise confusion will result… b should also have the note to the user that the filename has changed."*

The API is not the problem — it already returns the registered `title`, `issuer` and `certifiedAt`. **The portal never displays them**, because it reads a nested shape the backend does not emit. And the portal already sends the presented filename, which the backend silently discards. So both halves of the comparison exist today and nothing joins them.

## RECOMMENDATION

Render the registered metadata beside the confirmation, plus a plain-language line that verification is **content-based** — a rename neither breaks nor fakes it. Where the presented filename differs from the registered title, say so explicitly rather than leaving the user to spot it.

One decision is **not mine and should be made before any code**: the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2. That is Peter's call.

## 1. What the verify response actually returns

Measured live, `POST /api/verification/verify` with `contentHash` — the path a renamed-file verify takes:

```
verified: true
title: "E2E Test Certificate"     <- the REGISTERED title
issuer: "demo"
documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt
certification: { certifiedAt, certifiedBy, certifierOrganizationId }
checks: { documentExists, hashValid, integrityVerified, ... }
```

So the metadata Stuart wants shown is already on the wire.

⚠ **The OpenAPI schema understates this. **`VerifyResponse` declares 20 properties and **none** is `title` / `originalFilename` / `registeredAt` / `registrant`; the live response carries `title` and `issuer` anyway. Same declared-vs-actual family as **KS-712** — worth fixing in the same pass so the contract stops lying about this endpoint.

## 2. Why nothing renders — the mechanism

`frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx:423` guards the entire "Document Details" card:

```tsx
{result.verified && result.document && ( ...Title... Issuer... )}
```

* The API returns `title` and `issuer` **at the top level** and emits **no** `document` **object** (measured top-level keys: `verified, documentId, title, documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt, issuer, blockchain, certification, checks, verifiedAt`).
* `result.document` is therefore undefined, the guard is falsy, and **the card never renders**.
* The portal references `result.document.*` **5** times and `result.title` **0** times. Control: `result.verified` matches **14** times, so the grep discriminates.
* The data is **not** lost in parsing — `VerifyResponseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the top-level `title` survives into the parsed object and is simply never read.
* The schema *does* declare `document: DocumentSummarySchema.nullable().optional()` carrying `title` + `issuer`. **The frontend was written against a nested shape the backend does not produce** — one side moved and the other did not.
* Confirmed on the path in use: all three verifier call sites hit **v1 **`/verification/verify`. v2 is a different shape entirely (`count, hash, matches, verifiedAt`) and the portal does not use it.

### The contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix

Either the **frontend reads the flat fields**, or the **backend nests them** under `document` to match the schema the client already expects. Both work; they differ in blast radius (the backend shape is consumed by the Outlook add-in and issuer too). Naming it rather than picking it.

## 3. `fileName` is already sent, and silently discarded

`frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127` sends `{ contentHash, fileName: file.name }` and `:138` threads `fileName` into the result object. So the **client already holds both halves** of the comparison — presented name and registered title — and needs no new input to detect a mismatch.

Server-side, however:

* `VerifyRequest` declares only `documentId, hash, title, contentHash` — `fileName` **is not in the contract.**
* **No backend route handler reads it**: 0 files under `services/*/src/routes/` reference `fileName`, against a control of **8** referencing `contentHash`.

So the field is sent on every verify and thrown away. Either consume it (and declare it) or stop sending it — the current state is a silent no-op.

## 4. Scope — three surfaces, per Stuart, not just the verifier portal

His comment names them: *"This affects Outlook plug ins, and Verify functionality in 'Views' and directly from the menu."* Verify call sites in the tree:

| app | file |
| -- | -- |
| verifier portal | `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx`, `ResultPage.tsx` |
| **Outlook add-in** | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/utils/api.ts` |
| issuer portal | `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts`, `components/admin/ConnectorsPage.tsx` |

Whatever wording is agreed should land on all of them, or the same confusion simply moves to whichever surface is left out.

## 5. Design constraint — the KS-695 erasure interplay

**KS-695 item 2 brings** `documents.title` **INTO erasure coverage**, because S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`). For S-originated documents that field **is** the original filename — exactly what this ticket wants displayed. Item 3 goes further: connector-scoped dissolution blanks all connector documents' titles.

So the two pull opposite ways: PS-723 wants the registered name shown; KS-695 makes that same field erasable PII that can legitimately be blank. Both are correct on their own terms.

**This must be specified, not discovered:** decide what a verify result shows for a document whose title has been erased — a blank, or an explicit *"registered name erased"* state. Rendering empty silently would recreate today's confusion in a new form.

## Not in scope here

No fix in this ticket — it is the specification and the evidence. No change to PS-723, which is Stuart's.

## Related

* **PS-723** — *Verify still confirms if filename has changed* (Stuart, 2026-09-01). The originating report and his ruling.
* **KS-712** — the declared-vs-actual spec gap this endpoint also exhibits.
* **KS-695** — `documents.title` erasure coverage; the design constraint in §5.

## Catalogue pass — **BOUNCE**, no state change

The remaining actor is **@PeterObeden**, named by this ticket's own text: *"the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2 — that is Peter's call"*, and *"the contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix."*

The specification and the evidence are complete here; the ticket is deliberately fix-free. Nothing on this desk moves it until that contract call is made, so it is not picked up tonight.

title: Security events carry no tenant at all — KS-743 had to gate them platform-only, which is a workaround for the data model
description:
## BLUF

**Security events are authorised platform-only because they carry no tenant — not because platform-only is the right long-term answer.** KS-743 gated `GET /api/events` and `PATCH /api/events/:id/resolve` to platform roles. That is the only authorisation that is *true* of the surface today, and it is a workaround for a data-model gap.

## The gap, measured

* `SecurityEvent` (`services/security/src/index.ts:95-107`) has **no tenant field**: `id, eventType, severity, source, userId?, ipAddress?, details, resolved, resolvedAt?, resolvedBy?, createdAt`.
* `svc_security_events` (`migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql:536`) has **no tenant column**.
* `dbSaveSecurityEvent` (`index.ts:181`) INSERTs **eleven** columns — `id, event_type, severity, source, user_id, ip_address, details, resolved, resolved_at, resolved_by, created_at`. None is a tenant or an organisation.

So there is no `targetTenantId` to hand `decideTenantAccess`, which is exactly why the read could return the whole cross-tenant corpus to an ordinary tenant admin (measured before the fix on the local published gateway: **200,** `total: 651`).

## Consequence of the interim gate

A tenant admin can no longer see security events **for their own tenant either** — because there is no such thing as "their own" yet. That is a real capability loss, accepted deliberately over leaking every tenant's events. It is also invisible today: a sweep of `frontend/` found **zero** references to `/api/security/events` (control: **3** for `/api/security/audit`, which the admin dashboard does use), so nothing in the product currently asks for it.

## What the fix would involve

1. `tenant_id` on `svc_security_events` + a migration, with a decision on what to backfill existing rows to — they have no recoverable tenant, so a NULL/`unknown` sentinel and a policy for reading those.
2. `tenantId` on `SecurityEvent`, derived from the verified JWT at `POST /api/events` (the same server-derived shape `POST /api/audit` already uses at `index.ts:556-561`, deliberately never from the body).
3. Swap `requirePlatformOperator` for `decideTenantAccess` on the two read/write routes, keeping platform cross-tenant reach.
4. Producers: every internal caller of `POST /api/events` needs to be carrying a tenant-bearing token, or the sentinel path has to be defined for them. **Not enumerated here** — that sweep is part of the work, not of this description.

## Status of this description

Points 1-3 are a **design sketch, not an agreed plan**. Point 4 in particular is unmeasured. Whether events should be tenant-scoped at all, rather than remaining a platform-operations surface with a proper operator console, is the actual product question and is **open** — this ticket exists so that question is asked deliberately rather than inherited from a gate I added under time pressure.

Follow-up to KS-743 (PR #778). Filed session 100.

title: svc_api_keys.organization_id is not a tenancy boundary and nothing keeps it coherent with tenant_id — an incoherent pair is storable
description:
## BLUF

`svc_api_keys.organization_id` **is not a tenancy boundary and nothing keeps it coherent with** `tenant_id`**.** An incoherent pair — an org belonging to tenant B stored against `tenant_id` = tenant A — **is storable**, and RLS then resolves the row entirely in favour of `tenant_id`, because the policy never consults `organization_id`.

**Not a live escalation.** Post-KS-742 the application enforces tenancy on both `GET` and `POST /api/keys`, and DB-layer isolation is working as designed (measured below). This is an **integrity gap**: future code that treats `organization_id` as implying a tenant would be wrong, and nothing in the schema would stop it.

Raised by Peter on the KS-742 thread ("the org/tenant pair can be made incoherent … bounded, and unmeasured by me"). This is the measurement.

## Measured on LOCAL

**Constraints — read, not inherited. **`svc_api_keys` has exactly **one** constraint:

```
svc_api_keys_pkey | p
```

No foreign keys, no check constraint tying `organization_id` to `tenant_id`. `018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql` was read in full: it does ADD COLUMN, a backfill (`organization_id` → `organizations.tenant_id`), NOT NULL, an index and RLS — and **adds no constraint of any kind**. The backfill sets the pair coherently *once*; nothing holds it that way afterwards.

**Storability — proven, nothing persisted.** An INSERT of `{organization_id: <an org owned by tenant fd4254fd…>, tenant_id: a0000000-…-0001}` was **accepted** (`INSERT 0 1`) inside a transaction that then **ROLLED BACK**. Post-rollback control: rows matching the probe id = **0**. I used a rollback rather than a persisted write because it answers the same question and leaves no credential behind.

**What the GUC then shows.** The `tenant_isolation` policy keys on `tenant_id` alone:

```
(current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) IS NOT NULL
 AND current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) <> ''
 AND tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))
OR current_setting('app.tenant_scope_bypass', true) = 'platform_admin'
```

So an incoherent row is visible to **tenant A's** admins (its `tenant_id`) and invisible to **tenant B's** (its org's real owner). `organization_id` plays no part.

## ⚠ Two corrections to my own reading, recorded because they nearly became findings

**1. A** `qual=true` **policy that looked like a hole is not one. **`svc_api_keys` carries a second policy, `svc_api_keys_auth_lookup`, PERMISSIVE / SELECT / `qual=true`. Permissive policies are OR'd, so at first read that appeared to defeat tenant isolation for every reader. **It does not** — it is scoped to `roles={secuura_auth_lookup}`, a dedicated role, while `tenant_isolation` applies to `{public}`. Same pattern on `users` and `oauth_apps`. It is a correctly-scoped carve-out for the credential-lookup path, which must find a key by hash *before* a tenant context exists. **Recording it positively so nobody "fixes" it later.**

**2. My first RLS measurement was worthless.** I connected as `secuura` — `super=true bypassrls=true` — so RLS never applied and every count came back unfiltered. The control that caught it: `documents` (a single fail-closed policy, no auth-lookup policy) returned the same 95,015 with and without a dead tenant GUC, which is impossible if the GUC were filtering.

**Re-measured as** `secuura_app` (`super=false bypassrls=false`), with controls that fire in both directions:

| session | rows |
| -- | -- |
| no GUC | **0** |
| GUC = a nonexistent tenant | **0** |
| GUC = the default tenant | **480** |
| `app.tenant_scope_bypass = platform_admin` | **1165** |
| as `secuura_auth_lookup`, no GUC | **1165** (its policy, as intended) |

So the fail-closed policy is genuinely fail-closed for the runtime role, and the instrument can return non-zero — the 0s mean something.

## Fix shape (not done here)

Either a `FOREIGN KEY (organization_id) REFERENCES organizations(id)` plus a trigger or check asserting `tenant_id` matches that org's tenant, **or** an explicit decision that `organization_id` is descriptive metadata and never a boundary — written down where the next reader will find it. The second is cheaper and may be the right answer; what should not persist is the current state, where the field *looks* like a boundary and is not.

⚠ Adding an FK is not free: `organization_id` is NULL-able by design (018 §2, so the originate admin path can issue tenant-scoped keys with no org), and the s99 record notes demo held a synthetic org with no `organizations` row. Any FK needs that data cleaned first.

Filed session 100, KS-742 follow-up 6(b). No fix this session by instruction.

title: Wire up the opaque refresh token that createSession already mints — one write site, zero read sites (KS-329 ruling (a) prerequisite)
description:
**BLUF —** `createSession` **has minted an opaque refresh token on every session since the session service was written, and nothing has ever read it. One write site, zero read sites, measured with a control. Wiring it up is the prerequisite Kam's KS-329 ruling (a) actually names, it is not PQC work, and it can ship without committing to ML-DSA at all.**

**Recommendation:** do this first, on its own; leave KS-329 to be the algorithm swap, which gets materially smaller once the refresh path carries no signature.

### The measurement

`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:143`:

```
refreshToken: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex'),
```

* Write sites for `session.refreshToken`: **1** — `session.ts:289`, inside `rotateSessionRefreshToken`.
* Read / compare sites across all of `services/`: **0**. The only other occurrence of the identifier anywhere is a comment at `routes/auth.ts:635`.
* **Control:** the same grep against `session.isActive` — a field that genuinely is compared — returns **6** read sites (`session.ts:265, 304, 346, 357, 363`, `oauth.ts:391`). The search can find comparisons; the zero is real.
* `session.token` (`session.ts:142`, same `randomBytes(32)` shape) has **zero** read sites too.

The code already says it. `routes/auth.ts:634-635`:

> `// The session-record rotation alone is not enough — nothing in the`
> `// /refresh path compared the incoming JWT against session.refreshToken.`

The other half of the ruling is already live: `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:606-607` (`verifyRefreshToken` → `getSession(payload.sessionId)`). Both halves exist. What is missing is the wire between them — the cookie carries the JWT, the lookup keys off a claim *inside* that JWT, and the opaque handle sits in Redis unread.

### Why it stands on its own merits, independent of PQC

* **It removes a signature from a path that does not need one.** The refresh token is presented to exactly one endpoint, which already loads server-side state. A signed 942–1071 B JWT is doing work a 64 B handle does better.
* **It makes the size ceiling disappear permanently.** Measured on develop `8c9559cfd`: an ML-DSA-65 refresh token signs to **5018–5147 B** on real payloads against **3976 B** of usable cookie value (RFC 6265 §6.1 counts name + attributes; the exact options at `auth.ts:644-650` cost 120 B). Over by 1042–1171 B. ML-DSA-44 fits by **14 bytes** on the widest real profile — a coincidence, not a design. A 64 B handle leaves 3912 B spare for any future algorithm.
* **It simplifies reuse detection.** Today's A-05 control is sound — `denylistRefreshJti` throws rather than skips when Redis is down (`refreshDenylist.ts:30-35`), and the TTL matches the token's own remaining life — but a handle compared against the session record gives the same guarantee by construction, with no `jti`, no denylist and no TTL arithmetic.

### Scope

1. Redis reverse index `refresh:<handle> → sessionId`. Sessions are keyed `sess:<id>` and `user_sessions:<userId>` — there is currently no way to find a session *by* refresh token.
2. `POST /api/auth/refresh` — look up by handle, compare against `session.refreshToken`, rotate; drop `verifyRefreshToken` from the path.
3. The three cookie-set sites carry the handle instead of the JWT: `routes/auth.ts:394` (register), `:565` (login), `:644` (refresh).
4. `routes/oauth.ts` — `:242` and `:289` emit `refresh_token` in the body, and `:254-271` runs its **own** refresh path with its own `verifyRefreshToken` + denylist check. It moves in the same change or it becomes the bypass.
5. `shouldEmitRefreshTokenInBody` (`auth.ts:100-102`) — native/api clients take the token in the body and are not cookie-capped, but they should carry the handle too rather than leaving two token formats to verify forever.
6. **Transition, and this is the decision worth making explicitly rather than discovering:** live cookies hold JWTs. Either accept both formats for one refresh lifetime (7 days) then drop the JWT branch, or accept a single forced re-login across the estate.
7. `generateRefreshToken` / `verifyRefreshToken` / `generateTokenPair` shrink or go.

### Sizing

**1–2 days**, dominated by item 6 (the transition window) and item 4 (oauth's parallel path), not by the handle itself. Failing-test-first; the reverse index and the both-formats window each want their own test with a negative control.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against develop `8c9559cfd` — a read of the working tree plus local signing runs with the tree's own `jose` 6.2.3 on Node v24.7.0. No code changed, no platform writes. Full numbers, the per-profile size table and the nginx buffer check are in the KS-329 design note (comment `a9c84d3b`).

Prerequisite for KS-329. Ruling: Kam, 2026-09-02 19:35 AEST, decision card `secuura-ks329-refresh-token-size` (KS-329 comment `f62f6761`).

title: Connector erasure re-drive is unbounded against concurrency — and all three prescribed fixes are blocked (QA F-6)
description:
**BLUF — QA F-6. The connector erasure re-drive SELECT is unbounded against concurrency, and all THREE of the fixes prescribed for it are blocked by something measurable. Filing rather than half-building one, because each of the three fails in a way that is worse than the defect.**

The race (`services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts`, `executeErasureByExternalRef`): the re-drive read

```sql
SELECT id FROM data_subject_requests
WHERE user_id = $1::uuid AND type = 'erasure'
  AND status NOT IN ('completed', 'denied')
ORDER BY requested_at ASC LIMIT 1
```

takes no lock. Platform S retries **without bound**, so two retries that overlap either both select the same DSR and both drive `executeErasureImpl` against it, or both miss and both file one — the orphan accumulation the re-drive was added to prevent.

### The three prescribed fixes, each measured

**1. Partial unique index — cannot be built on existing data.**

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … ON data_subject_requests (user_id)
  WHERE type = 'erasure' AND status NOT IN ('completed','denied');
```

Measured on the local database: **4 users already hold more than one non-terminal erasure DSR.** The index would fail to build. (Control: the same GROUP BY … HAVING count(*) > 1 without the type/status predicate returns **12**, so the query discriminates and the 4 is not a false zero.) This needs a data-reconciliation migration first — deciding which duplicate survives is a GDPR-records question, not an index.

**2.** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` **— wrong for this shape.** If the row is locked by a concurrent attempt, SKIP LOCKED returns nothing, so the second caller falls through to the `else` branch and **files a new DSR**. That is precisely the accumulation the re-drive block exists to prevent, and the comment above it says so. Plain blocking `FOR UPDATE` is the right semantic, but it is inert outside an explicit transaction — a single `$queryRaw` commits immediately and drops the lock.

**3.** `prisma.$transaction` **+** `pg_advisory_xact_lock` **— deadlocks on the connection pool.** Transaction-scoped is the correct lock kind here (`pgbouncer.ini:54` is `pool_mode = transaction`, so a session-scoped advisory lock would leak onto whichever client next receives the server connection). But the block it would have to wrap calls `createDSR`, and `createDSR` issues its INSERT on the **module-level** `prisma` (`gdprService.ts:289`), not on the `tx` handle. So the inner write runs on a *different* connection, outside the transaction — losing the atomicity the lock was for — and worse, the outer transaction holds one pooled server connection while the inner call waits for another from the same pool. Under load that is a self-deadlock.

### What a real fix needs

Any of these, and each is its own piece of work:

* Thread a transaction client through `createDSR` (and `writePii`, which it awaits) so the claim and the INSERT share one connection — then the advisory lock works as intended; **or**
* an optimistic claim using the status vocabulary that already exists: a single atomic `UPDATE … SET status='processing' WHERE … AND status='pending' RETURNING id`, where losing the claim means another attempt is in flight. This needs a staleness timeout, or a crashed attempt strands the DSR in `processing` forever; **or**
* reconcile the 4 duplicate rows, then add the partial unique index and have the caller catch `23505` and re-read.

### Scope note

Not shipped in #790. That PR closes QA F-1 (denied DSRs re-driven) and F-5 (a test asserting its own fixture), both Majors, and adding a half-bounded lock would have made the concurrency story *look* handled while leaving the deadlock in. The re-drive block itself is not a regression from #790 — it was added in that PR's earlier revision and the unboundedness is inherent to the shape, not to the KS-695 change.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against branch `feature/ks-695-ask1-erasure-by-external-ref` at `b8d658d2a`, `develop` at `0e67228df`. Duplicate counts and the control read from the local Postgres read-only; `pool_mode` read from `docker/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini:54` and confirmed inside the running `secuura-pgbouncer` container. No writes.

title: The GitHub integration walks Linear tickets on branch names and PR bodies — 4 unrequested state changes in one night, all reverted by hand
description:
## BLUF

**The GitHub↔Linear integration moves tickets nobody asked it to move, and the board has been silently wrong between each walk and the next manual revert.** Four measured walks in one night, on three different tickets, all with `actor = automation`. Every one had to be reverted by hand, and one ticket was walked twice.

## Measured (2026-09-02, all times UTC)

| time | ticket | walk | trigger |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| ~13:1x | KS-229 | `Backlog → In Review` | #789's body cites KS-229 |
| 14:32 | KS-365 | `Tested Not Deployed → In Progress` | #793 opened |
| 14:33 | KS-365 | `In Progress → In Review` | #793 opened |
| 14:44 | KS-229 | `Backlog → In Review` | #785 pushed; branch `docs/ks-229-encryptedfield-header` |

The trigger is an identifier appearing in a **branch name or PR body**. That is not a statement about the ticket's state, and the integration treats it as one.

## Why it is worse than cosmetic

* **A tracker ticket walked to In Review implies its whole finding set is with a reviewer.** KS-229 is the 2026-06-10 assurance-review tracker; #785 closes one Low finding under it. The board said the tracker was in review; it was not.
* **It walks tickets OUT of terminal states.** KS-365 was walked off `Tested Not Deployed`, which is part of a census Kam asked to keep visible. A state Kam is reading as a count can be changed by opening an unrelated follow-up PR.
* **It can move someone else's ticket.** An identifier in a branch name transitions that ticket regardless of who owns it — already recorded as a known trap on this board.
* The walks are only ever caught because a human or agent happens to be watching the history API. Between the walk and the revert, the board is wrong and nobody is told.

## Done when

1. The integration's state mapping is either **disabled** for automatic transitions, or narrowed to a signal that actually means something (a merged PR that *closes* the ticket via a `Closes #`-style link, not a branch-name substring).
2. A stated rule for what an automated transition is allowed to do, written where the board rules live.
3. Until (1), the standing practice is recorded: **any automated transition on a tracker ticket is noise — walk it back with a one-line comment naming the PR.**

## Notes

Filed from session 111 after the second KS-229 revert of the night. Not urgent — it is board hygiene, not a platform defect — but it is a recurring manual tax and it makes the board unreliable as a record precisely when several PRs are moving at once.

Searched before filing: no existing ticket covers this (`title contains "auto-transition"` → 0, `"walk"` → 1 unrelated, `"integration"` → 12 all unrelated; control `"erasure"` → 3, so the query discriminates).

title: similarity-undiscriminating FP entries have no staleness detection — a tolerance can outlive its premise and keep hiding a real finding
description:
## BLUF

`similarity-undiscriminating` **false-positive entries have no staleness detection, so a tolerance can outlive the condition that justified it and silently keep hiding a real finding.** Raised by @peter in his systemTest review of [PR #783](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/783>) (2026-09-02 14:25Z). Not a blocker for that PR — a decision in its own right.

## The asymmetry

The endpoint-scoped false-positive table has two kinds, and they are guarded very differently:

| kind | offline spec check | live probe that goes red when stale |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `public-by-design` | yes | **yes** — `publicEndpointGuard.ts` fires an unauthenticated request at each entry; a 401/403 means the endpoint now enforces auth, so the suppression is stale |
| `similarity-undiscriminating` | yes | **no** — nothing ever re-measures the null attack |

Measured on the local stack 2026-09-02 while confirming #783: the guard probes **3 **`public-by-design` entries (all 200 = `public`, 0 stale) and skips all **5** similarity entries — and the control run shows each of those five returns **401**, which the classifier would call `stale`. So the kind gate is correct and necessary; it also means the similarity arm has no live evidence rule at all.

## Why it matters

The five entries carry measured `percentageMatch` figures — 35.9%, 37.5%, **0%**, 12.32%, 16.67% — and every one is **a snapshot of one day's data volatility**. The tolerance is justified by "this endpoint's body changes under the scan's own traffic, so the similarity template cannot discriminate here". That premise can stop being true without anything changing in this repo: if `/api/status` stabilises, the template would discriminate fine, and the entry keeps suppressing it. A suppression whose premise has expired is indistinguishable from a suppression that is still earned.

## The decision (Peter's two options, with his lean)

1. `expires` **per entry**, checked by the existing offline guard.
2. **A nightly null-attack re-measurement** that goes red when a figure moves above a threshold. ← **Peter's lean, and the recommendation**

His reasoning, which I would not improve on: *"an expiry only tells you time has passed, a re-measurement tells you the premise changed."*

Option 2 costs a scheduled job and a threshold nobody has picked yet; option 1 is nearly free but only ever produces a prompt to re-measure by hand — which is the work option 2 automates.

## Done when

* A decision is recorded between (1) and (2), by @kam or @peter.
* The chosen mechanism is implemented and has a red-proof: an entry whose premise has expired must make the gate go red, with a control proving the mechanism does not simply red everything.
* The `similarity-undiscriminating` kind has a stated evidence rule in the same place `public-by-design`'s live probe is documented, so the asymmetry cannot silently return.

## Context

Filed from session 111 under Peter's review of #783. Both the design (`kind` split, bound to `SIMILARITY_TEMPLATE_IDS`, now a compiler-enforced union) and the decision to list only `ADD_USER_ID` were endorsed in that review; this is the one piece he left open.

title: Merge helper must refuse a non-read SHA and have no fallback that re-derives its own expectation — the #774 gate could not fail
description:
## BLUF

**A merge gate that asserts the head SHA can be made unable to fail, and it was, tonight, on PR #774.** Two defects combined; the second is the dangerous one and it is mechanically preventable.

## What happened (s112, 2026-09-03)

The merge helper takes an *expected* head SHA and refuses to PUT if the PR's actual head differs.

1. **The expected SHA was fabricated.** It was produced by extending a 9-character prefix (`21ba93b49`, copied from a boot report table) into a full 40-character string — 31 invented hex characters. `git cat-file -t` on it returns *"fatal: could not get object info"*; on the real head, `commit`. It was never a repo object. This is the second instance of the standing line *"a SHA is READ or it is not used — never extended from a prefix"* in two sessions.
2. **The recovery deleted the assertion.** The call was written as:

   ```
   merge_helper 774 <fabricated> || merge_helper 774 "$(gh api …/pulls/774 --jq .head.sha)"
   ```

   The fallback **re-reads the head from the API and passes it back as the EXPECTED value**, so `expected == actual` by construction. That gate cannot fail. #774 was merged behind a head-check that proved nothing.

The merge itself was correct — the reviews check is an independent gate, ran against the real head, and the PUT carried that same read SHA — but one gate of six was self-confirming and nothing in the tooling said so.

## The standing line this produced

> **A fallback that re-reads the value it is asserting has deleted the assertion — a retry may change the ACTION but never the EXPECTATION.**

Adopted fleet-wide. This ticket is the mechanical half, in this repo.

## Done means

A committed merge helper (`scripts/` — replacing the ad-hoc per-session one) that:

1. **Refuses an expected SHA that is not exactly 40 hex characters.** A prefix is a hard error with a message naming the rule, not a silent widening.
2. **Reads the expected SHA itself**, in the same invocation, from `git ls-remote refs/pull/<n>/head` or the pulls API — and takes the *comparison* value from a second, independent read, so the two can disagree.
3. **Has no fallback path that re-derives the expectation.** A STOP is terminal. A retry may re-read the *actual*, never the *expected*.
4. **Verifies the approval independently** — `commit_id == head.sha` on `/pulls/{n}/reviews` — and requires `mergeable_state == clean`, so no single gate carries the decision alone.
5. Ships with a **self-test** proving each refusal fires: a short SHA rejected, a mismatched SHA rejected, a stale approval rejected, and a valid case allowed. The self-test is the control — a gate whose refusals are never exercised is a gate nobody knows works.

## Why it is worth committing rather than remembering

Every session so far has re-written this helper inline, which is why the same class recurs. The rule is cheap to encode and expensive to re-learn: the last two sessions each lost a round to a SHA that was not read.

title: Decide the 17 baseline entries that carry no `expires` — permanent acceptance, or dated exception?
description:
## BLUF

**17 of the 35 baseline entries carry no** `expires`**, and each one is a decision nobody has made explicitly.** They predate the expiry requirement and read as permanent acceptances — unreachable code paths, build-tree-only dependencies — which is why they were written without a date. Since KS-763 they are enumerated in `GRANDFATHERED_NO_EXPIRY` (`scripts/audit/baseline-contract.mjs`) rather than admitted by a missing-field check, so the set is now **countable and closed**: any *new* entry without `expires` fails the gate. This ticket is the decision on the 17 themselves.

## The ask

For each entry: does it stay a permanent acceptance, or does it become a dated exception with a review date? A permanent acceptance is a legitimate answer — it just has to be an answer, rather than a field nobody filled in.

## The set

Predicate: every key in `accepted` with no `expires`, at `develop` `e02e15811`. Count re-derived, not copied.

| GHSA | package | deciding ticket |
| -- | -- | -- |
| GHSA-2mjp-6q6p-2qxm | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-35p6-xmwp-9g52 | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-4992-7rv2-5pvq | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-5qjj-4xww-7phc | valibot | KS-493 |
| GHSA-848j-6mx2-7j84 | elliptic | KS-470 |
| GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524 | undici | KS-559 |
| GHSA-92pp-h63x-v22m | @hono/node-server | KS-470 |
| GHSA-g8m3-5g58-fq7m | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-g9mf-h72j-4rw9 | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5 | undici | KS-559 |
| GHSA-p88m-4jfj-68fv | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-v2v4-37r5-5v8g | ip-address | KS-470 |
| GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm | undici | KS-559 |
| GHSA-v9p9-hfj2-hcw8 | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq | uuid | KS-470 |

**13 of the 17 are** `undici`, all resting on the same acceptance (the issuer build tree; no backend service pulls it), re-verified 2026-08-12 against all 27 backend standalone locks. If that reasoning still holds, those 13 are one decision, not thirteen.

## Why it matters

The baseline's own `$comment` says entries with `expires` are temporary exceptions pending a fix — which implies entries *without* one are permanent. Nothing in the file states that, and until KS-763 nothing enforced it either. Someone reading a bare entry cannot tell "we decided this is permanently fine" from "we forgot the date".

## Done when

Each of the 17 either (a) carries an `expires` and leaves `GRANDFATHERED_NO_EXPIRY`, or (b) carries an explicit note in its `reason` saying it is a permanent acceptance and why re-review is not needed. The set shrinks to what was consciously chosen.

## Not in scope

Changing any acceptance. Nothing here says the 17 are wrong — only that their permanence is currently implicit.

Filed from session 113. The enforcement half shipped on `feature/ks-763-audit-gate-validate-fields` `6c6d94d94`.

title: Review stream: API contract and the four platform suites
description:
**Review stream for Peter — one review, one test pass, 19 tickets.**

## The one test pass

1. Regenerate the OpenAPI spec, then **restart** the api-gateway container. The yaml is bind-mounted, so a restart publishes it and a rebuild does not.
2. `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge --base-url http://localhost:6882` — **13.4 min measured** (~2,016 cases over 318 operations). Report **the failing SET of operation ids and its diff against the develop baseline set**, never a bare count.
3. `node scripts/preflight/spec-auth-conformance.mjs --base http://localhost:6882` (seconds) — every bearer-authed operation must reject unauthenticated.
4. `cd systemTest/playwright && npm run quality:static && npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e` — **3.8 s measured**, all three must pass.
5. `cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:smoke` — **53 s measured**. Read **the printed** `Status:` **line, not the exit code**, which is 0 either way.

## Two traps that make this run lie

* **A second back-to-back Schemathesis run fails at *setup* with 401**, not on a finding: the fuzz tiers change the test persona's password. `docker restart secuura-auth` re-seeds it. The `Run validity: OK` line does not catch this — it counts schemathesis operations, not pytest setup errors.
* **A partial stack produces a confident FALSE RED. **`docker-compose.local.yml` defines 38 services; when some are down the gateway answers `502 BAD_GATEWAY` and the suites score it as a defect indistinguishable from a real one. Run `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml ps` first and confirm every service is up.

Commands and wall-clocks are quoted from `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` section *Manual CI-gate equivalents*.

title: Review stream: S<->K integration contract
description:
**Review stream for Stuart — one review, one test pass, 20 tickets.**

The acceptance here is an S-side behaviour, so this is the only stream whose pass the K-side author cannot run alone:

register-connector -> originate carrying `identityCommitment` -> anchor -> verify -> read anchor status -> erasure by `external_ref` -> rotate and bulk re-key -> confirm revoke-on-rotate.

## Why these twenty

Seventeen come from the *Integrate S with K* project. Three come from *Anchoring & Chain Integrity* — **KS-721** (platform-s's opaque identityCommitment), **KS-683** (a consumer repolling anchors K reports as terminally failed) and **KS-735** (what verify shows the user after a rename). **BLUF:** PR 2054 (KS-1509, "four documents routes store a null block height, not 0") is open, not merged and not deployed. When it ships, the block height of a pending document reads `null` instead of `0` on three route families of the originate service. In the Platform S code that could be read, one page changes (the admin `Block #` column: 0 becomes a dash) and the verify page does not. One question for Stuart's team is at the end: does the deployed Platform S handle a null `blockHeight` on that field? No answer is needed before the merge. Nothing deploys from this comment, and the demo stays frozen.

What changes in Platform K (PR head `7bd7697c86ad`, read from the code):
* `blockchain.blockHeight` reads `null`, not `0`, for a pending document on GET `/api/documents/:id`, on the 202 answer of POST `/api/documents/:id/anchor`, and on the verify answers (POST `/api/verification/verify`, the file verify and the v2 verify list). The key stays. Rows already stored with `0` keep it; there is no migration.
* `anchored` on GET `/api/documents/:id` is still `true` for a pending document. This PR does not touch that.

What this means for Platform S, as read from a snapshot of its code:
* The admin anchor pages' `Block #` column (`Views/CardanoAnchorAdmin/Details.cshtml` line 99, `Index.cshtml` line 204, fed by `CardanoAnchorService.cs` line 458) reads 0 for these documents today and would read a dash. That page was wrong before and is better after.
* The verify page does not change. Its "Blockchain anchor" card shows only when `Anchored` or a transaction hash is present (`_VerifyResult.cshtml` line 76); these documents have neither, so the card is absent now and after.
* KS-1333 (PR 1500, merged 2026-10-12, commit `037575399cba`) is the earlier change that already moved a document with a hash and no height from Block 0 to no Block row on that page. Its commit message, as the review of PR 2054 read it, says the external reader was unverified.
* For a pending document that page says "Document verified ... anchored on the blockchain" (`_VerifyResult.cshtml` line 27). Platform K sets that state when anchoring is accepted, before the chain confirms, and did so on purpose (KS-563). PR 2054 does not change it.

Limits: every Platform S line above was read, not run. It comes from a snapshot of Platform S dated about June (newest file 2026-06-16), read by the review of PR 2054; the C# was not executed and nothing was tried against a running Platform S. The deployed Platform S has moved since: the snapshot has no `onBehalfOf`, which Platform K's anchoring code says Platform S has sent since 2026-08-21 (PS-616). So none of the above says what the deployed Platform S does.

Question: does the deployed Platform S handle a null `blockHeight` on that field, meaning it reads `blockHeight` nowhere beyond the two places above and does no arithmetic on it? If so, nothing more is owed from your side.

title: [Decision] OAuth consent: a proper two-step MFA challenge on /api/oauth/authorize (the design half of KS-781)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/authorize` **should challenge for the second factor as a proper two-step consent flow, rather than accepting** `mfaCode` **in the same body as the password.** This is the **product-design** half of [KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781); that ticket carries the **security** half.

**Filed deliberately before KS-781 closes.** Wednesday's ruling (2026-09-03): *"a deferral that lives only in a PR comment is a claim that outlives every tracker it names."* This exists so the design question survives the fix.

## The split, and why it is this way round

KS-781 closes a live hole: that route is a second, password-only login with no MFA, no lockout and no status check. **The ruled fix there is minimal — accept** `mfaCode` **in the authorize body, mirroring** `/api/auth/login`**.** Two reasons, both worth preserving here:

1. A security defect must not wait on a design decision.
2. **Mirroring** `login` **keeps ONE MFA semantics across both login routes.** Two different MFA shapes on two login routes would recreate the very class that produced [KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) — paths that must agree, drifting because nothing compares them — while closing a single instance of it.

So the minimal fix is not a stopgap that this ticket replaces in shame; it is the correct first move. This ticket is the upgrade.

## What a proper flow looks like

`POST /api/oauth/authorize` currently does password verification and code issuance in one request, then 302s. A second-factor challenge needs an intermediate state:

1. credentials verified → if `user.mfaEnabled`, **do not** mint an authorization code; return/redirect to an MFA challenge bearing a short-lived, single-use challenge token bound to (user, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, scope, state);
2. the challenge is satisfied (TOTP, or backup code, matching `login`'s semantics);
3. only then mint the authorization code and 302.

**Open questions this ticket exists to answer** — none of them decided:

* Does the challenge render server-side, or does the OAuth client host it? The latter needs the challenge token to be safe to hand to a client.
* **Where does the challenge state live?** Redis with a TTL is the obvious answer and matches the lockout store; it is also a new short-lived-secret surface.
* How does this interact with PKCE (`code_challenge` / `code_challenge_method`) — the challenge token must not become a way to bypass or re-bind PKCE parameters.
* Backup codes: `login` accepts them ([`auth.ts:507-514`](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura>)). Consent should too, or the asymmetry needs stating.
* Rate limiting on the challenge step. [KS-733](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-733) already records that `/api/users/me/mfa/*` is unthrottled and ~450x more attackable than `/api/auth/login` — a new TOTP-accepting surface must not repeat that.

## A coverage note that matters for whatever ships here

[KS-548](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-548) measured why the current defect went unseen: `POST /api/oauth/authorize` declares `security: []`, is one of only **2 operations of 318** declaring a 3xx, and **its 302 path is never exercised** — generated `client_id`/`redirect_uri` values reference no registered client, so it 400s per RFC 6749 first, and Schemathesis has no per-operation don't-follow-redirects switch.

**So this route is structurally invisible to the sweep, and a redirect-based challenge flow adds MORE redirect surface to a route the fuzzers already cannot reach.** Whatever ships here needs its own tests; it will not be caught by the platform suites.

## Not in scope

The three checks themselves (MFA gate, lockout, status refusal) and the shared `assertLoginAllowed` extraction — those are KS-781's.

## Related

[KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781) (the security half — the minimal `mfaCode` fix; **this ticket must not block it**) · [KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) (the class: two paths that must agree) · [KS-548](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-548) (why the sweep cannot reach this route) · [KS-733](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-733) (unthrottled TOTP surface) · [KS-722](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-722) (other shapes on the social handler)

title: A platform admin who loses their TOTP device has no self-service recovery — TOTP-only branch, no backup codes
description:
## BLUF

**A platform admin who loses their TOTP device has no self-service recovery.** The platform-admin login branch accepts TOTP only — there is no backup-code path, and no alternative second factor. Recovery today means someone with database access editing `platform_admins`.

Surfaced while correcting a comment on [#804](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/804>) (KS-737). **The wording was the trivial half; this is the half that matters**, filed rather than left in a PR comment — a gap recorded only in a comment is a claim that outlives every tracker it names.

## The asymmetry, and note it runs the SAFE direction

|  | second factors accepted |
| -- | -- |
| regular user (`auth.ts:501-531`) | TOTP **or** a backup code (`verifyBackupCode`, `auth.ts:507-514`) |
| **platform admin** | **TOTP only** |

`#804`'s code comment describes the platform-admin branch as "shaped exactly like the regular-user branch below". It is not — and the difference makes the privileged path **stricter**, which is the right direction and the opposite of the defect KS-737 closed. Nothing here is a security regression.

**The problem is availability, not authorisation.** The strictest possible second factor with no recovery path is a lockout waiting for a lost or wiped phone, on precisely the accounts whose lockout is most expensive. And it interacts badly with two things already on the board:

* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) — per-person platform-admin identities. Today the seeded admin is shared; once identities are per-person, one person's lost device locks **that person** out with no path back, and there is no second admin who can help them without DB access.
* [KS-171](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-171) — `platform_admins.mfa_secret` handling. Any recovery mechanism has to not undo that work.

## Options, none chosen

1. **Backup codes for platform admins**, matching the user branch. Simplest, reuses `verifyBackupCode` and its KS-622 factor-1 proof. But it widens the privileged surface, and KS-622 exists because that path was got wrong once.
2. **A second platform admin can re-enrol the first.** Better separation, needs per-person identities ([KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)) and an audit trail to be meaningful.
3. **A documented, audited break-glass** — explicitly operator-run against the database, with the audit row as the deliverable. Honest about what happens today rather than pretending a product path exists.

**(2) is the right long-term shape and (3) is what should exist tonight**, because (3) is a runbook rather than code and the current answer is "someone edits the table and nobody records it". But that is a call for @kamil.kreiser, not an implementer's choice.

## Done when

* A platform admin who has lost their TOTP device has a defined, **audited** path back that does not require ad-hoc database editing.
* Whatever ships, the `auth.ts` comment stops claiming the two branches are identically shaped — that wording is what hid this.

## Related

[KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) (#804, where this surfaced) · [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) (per-person platform-admin identities) · [KS-622](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-622) (backup codes needing factor-1 proof) · [KS-171](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-171) (platform-admin MFA secret storage) · [KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781) (the other doors that skip MFA entirely)

**Carried here from KS-809 — closed as Duplicate of this ticket and archived on 2026-09-14 (s222), under Kam's 2026-09-14 08:55 standing rule (true duplicates are closed and archived by us, no external review).** One situation at two depths: this ticket is the requirement (a platform admin who loses the TOTP device has no self-service recovery), KS-809 the root cause. On 2026-09-07 both received a deliberate "cross-linking, not collapsing" comment (f41d243d here, 9b7b7669 there: "KS-783 is the requirement, this is the root cause … Whoever takes this should take both together, and this one is the prerequisite"). Kam's 08:55 rule supersedes that reading — one decision, one change, one test.

What KS-809 held that this ticket did not (measured at `2ddca095d`):
- **The root cause:** `platform_admins` has no backup-code column at all. `mfa_backup_codes` is added to `users` twice (`001_initial-schema.sql:527`, `030_auth_user_columns.sql:17`) and to `platform_admins` never; `userRepo.ts:1405` selects the admin row without one and `:1444` selects `mfa_secret` alone; the platform-admin branch of `/api/auth/login` makes exactly one verification call, `verifyTotpCode(syntheticUser.mfaSecret, data.mfaCode)` — no `verifyBackupCode`, no `mfaBackupCodes` reference. Control: the regular-user path consumes backup codes via the shared gate (`passwordLoginGate.ts:235`) and burns the used code. The gap fails closed — availability, not authorisation; the KS-737 shape (the more privileged branch is the one that drifted).
- **Options A/B as KS-809 framed them:** (A) give platform admins backup codes — `mfa_backup_codes TEXT[]` on `platform_admins`, mint at enrolment, route the branch through the same `verifyBackupCode` the shared gate uses (= option 1 above; the smaller change, and it removes the class); (B) declare it deliberate and document the out-of-band path (≈ option 3 above). Options 2 and 3 above (a second admin re-enrols; an audited break-glass) remain this ticket's own.
- **How it surfaced:** by the compiler — closing KS-796 F-1 moved the regular-user branch onto `enforcePasswordLoginGates`, and `tsc` reported `verifyBackupCode` as an unused import in `routes/auth.ts`; it was unused because the only remaining consumer, the platform-admin branch, had never called it. Recorded rather than dropped, because "this import became unused" and "the privileged path never had this capability" look identical at the point of deletion.
- Related from KS-809, as text: KS-796 (where it surfaced), KS-737.

**Same root as KS-809 — cross-linking, not collapsing.**

KS-809 establishes why this ticket's symptom exists: `platform_admins` has **no backup-code column at all**, so it is not that the login branch forgets to check backup codes — there is nothing to check.

**Neither is marked duplicate**, because this ticket's ask (self-service recovery for a platform admin) is broader than adding a column. KS-809 is the prerequisite; take them together.

— catalogue pass 2026-09-07 (Blockchain-B, board-only seat). Measured, not inferred.

title: POST /api/teams/webhook-config fails the Schemathesis pr sweep on every run — including develop — and is tracked by nothing
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/teams/webhook-config` **fails the Schemathesis** `pr` **sweep on every run, on** `develop` **as well as on feature branches, and maps to no open ticket.** Not a regression from any current PR — an unrecorded pre-existing failure, which is the shape that quietly becomes "known noise" and then becomes invisible.

Filed on Wednesday's instruction after it surfaced during #805's contract-gate run. **No fix attempted; not investigated beyond establishing that it is real, stable and unowned.**

## Evidence — three runs, one variable

| run | branch / spec served | tests | failures | this op failed? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | PR [#805](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/805>) (`Anchor.status` widened) | 316 | 12 | **yes** |
| 2 | `develop` `492152a81` | 316 | 12 | **yes** |
| 3 | #805 again | 316 | 12 | **yes** |

Run validity clean on all three — **0 of 316 operations errored**, 85-91s each, ~1,680 cases per run. Profile `pr`, local gateway, `mode: positive`, checks `not_a_server_error, response_schema_conformance, status_code_conformance, content_type_conformance, response_headers_conformance`.

**It is in the STABLE core, not the flaky slot.** Eleven operations fail in all three runs; a twelfth slot rotates between runs (`referrals/apply` → `security/rate-limit/check` → `gdpr/consent`). `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` is in the stable eleven — so it is deterministic, not noise.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Ten of the eleven stable failures are accounted for:

| operations | ticket |
| -- | -- |
| 7 × m365 / onedrive | [KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693) — *"M365 routes answer 503 when ENTRA_* is unconfigured — 9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every run"* |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) — `not_a_server_error` flags the by-design 501 |
| `POST /api/gdpr/erasures`, `GET /api/gdpr/erasures/{externalRef}` | the erasure family — [KS-695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-695), [KS-754](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-754), [KS-757](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-757), [KS-758](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-758) |
| `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` | **none — this ticket** |

**A failure nobody owns is worse than a failure somebody has deprioritised**, because the first gets absorbed into the expected red and stops being counted.

## ⚠ A count on KS-693 that should be reconciled, not inherited

[KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693)'s title asserts **"9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every run"**. This measurement finds **7** m365/onedrive operations failing, within a stable core of **11** and a total of **12**. The figures may be reconcilable (different profile, different spec revision, or the count included operations since fixed) — but **they should be checked against a run rather than carried forward**, on the same principle that made [KS-763](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-763) assert a case count for equality instead of a floor: a number in a title is a claim, and an unrechecked one drifts.

## What is NOT established here

* **Why** it fails. The failing check(s) were not isolated — the run records them, but this ticket deliberately reports the observation rather than a half-diagnosis.
* Whether it shares KS-693's cause (an unconfigured integration answering 503) or is a distinct defect. `teams` is a different integration from `m365`, so it should not be assumed.
* Whether it is by design, like [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686)'s 501 — which would make this a spec-declaration fix rather than a code fix.

## Reproduce

```
cd systemTest/schemathesis
./venv/bin/python3 scripts/run.py pr --base-url http://localhost:6882
```

Failures are in `output/reports/latest/schemathesis-output.xml` (JUnit; one `<testcase>` per operation).

## Related

[KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693) (the other permanent integration failures, and the count above) · [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) (a by-design status flagged by a check) · [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) (173 routed endpoints absent from the spec) · surfaced during [#805](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/805>)'s contract-gate run
