title: Per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations — CORE_MIGRATIONS FORCEs RLS with ZERO policies, so a per-tenant DB is dark on 5 core tables from boot 1 (permanent)
description:
## BLUF

**Per-tenant databases receive** `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **and NEVER the file migrations — not on any boot.** Measured, not read. The consequence is not "039 is missing": `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **enables and FORCEs** row-level security on five core tables while **every policy for them lives only in** `migrations/*.sql`, so a per-tenant DB lands with **FORCE RLS and ZERO policies**. A non-superuser runtime role then reads **zero rows** from `documents`, `certifications`, `audit_logs`, `custody_events` and `shares` — unconditionally, with no GUC able to fix it — and the boot log reports `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

**Latent today, live the moment** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB=true` — i.e. the moment KS-160 Path A (per-tenant-DB isolation) ships. This is a landmine directly under that roadmap item.

## The defect, in source

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`

* **:932** `applyFileMigrations(pg, dbUrl, 'main', fileMigrations)`
* **:939** `applyFileMigrations(pg, platformDbUrl, 'platform', fileMigrations)`
* **:1108** `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` ← the tenant loop, **no** `applyFileMigrations` **call anywhere in it**

`applyFileMigrations`' own signature makes it structural, not an oversight in one call: `dbName: 'main' | 'platform'`. A tenant database is not a value that type admits, and the routing inside it (`if (dbName === 'main' && m.isPlatform) continue`) has no third branch.

**The trap is the split:** `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in the whole of `startup-migrations.ts` (control: the same grep finds **19** in `migrations/*.sql`), while CORE_MIGRATIONS runs `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` at :439-440 (`custody_events`), :485-486 (`shares`), :551-552 (`documents`) and a `format()` loop at :633-634. **Enforcement ships in the array; permission ships in the files. Tenant DBs get only the array.**

The second path that can seed a tenant DB does not close the gap either: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:62` `createTenantDatabase()` applies `INIT_SCRIPTS_DIR` (`docker/init`, bind-mounted at `docker-compose.yml:2038`) — **12 .sql files, 0** `CREATE POLICY`**, 0** `tenant_scope_bypass` (control: `migrations/` has 17 files with `CREATE POLICY`, 3 with `tenant_scope_bypass`).

## Measurement

Disposable `postgres:15-alpine`, SSL enabled with a locally-signed CA so the product's hard-coded `?sslmode=require` tenant connection could genuinely succeed. Product's own `runStartupMigrations()` driven from source; `startup-migrations.ts` blob verified **identical on** `origin/develop` **and HEAD** (`6a1b53bafa1ad707e663814f95ed92a668e96280`), `migrations/` identical too. Platform DB + main DB + one genuinely separate tenant DB (`tenant_alpha`). Four boots.

| read on `tenant_alpha` after 3 boots | value |
| -- | -- |
| public tables (**connection proof**) | **27** — `documents`, `users`, `anchor_store` all present |
| `_secuura_migrations` table exists | **0 — the file stage never ran, once** |
| `pg_policy` rows | **0** |
| tables with RLS **enabled** | **5** — all also `FORCE` |

**Same reader on the main DB (positive control):** `_secuura_migrations` **48 rows**, `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **recorded**, `pg_policy` **28**, RLS tables **25**.

### The consequence, measured as an action (not asserted)

`secuuraadmin` is a superuser and bypasses RLS, so the owner read proves nothing. Re-measured as `s163_app` — `LOGIN NOBYPASSRLS`, non-superuser, the KS-109 runtime-role shape:

```
tenant_alpha  documents / certifications / audit_logs   ->  0 , 0 , 0
tenant_alpha  documents WITH both GUCs the product sets ->  0    (no policy exists to satisfy)
tenant_alpha  organizations (non-RLS table, 1 row)      ->  1    <- NON-ZERO CONTROL: login + grants work
superuser, row_security=off, tenant_alpha documents     ->  1    <- the row DOES exist
secuura       documents, NO GUC set                     ->  0
secuura       documents WITH app.tenant_scope_bypass    ->  1    <- DISCRIMINATION CONTROL
secuura       documents WITH app.current_tenant_id      ->  1
```

The zeros on `tenant_alpha` are real zeros, not an unreachable database: the same role, in the same database, reads 1 from a non-RLS table.

## Scope — honest in both directions

**REFUTED for the configuration running today.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false (`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245`), so every `tenant_config` row points at the shared app DB — which *does* get the file migrations via the `'main'` path. Confirmed in my own run: the 6 seeded tenants all carried `db_name = secuura`. **5 occurrences of the flag repo-wide, all code/comment, ZERO config sites** (control: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` appears in `docker-compose.yml`).

⚠ **NOT measured against demo or UAT** — both are held. The above is source + a local reproduction.

**CONFIRMED for per-tenant DBs.** Set the flag — or provision any tenant whose `db_name` differs from the app DB — and that tenant is dark on its five core tables from its first boot, permanently, with a success line in the log.

## Fix shape (not implemented here)

Give `applyFileMigrations` a tenant arm and call it from the loop before `migrateDatabase`, with the file corpus filtered the way `'main'` filters it. The `'main' | 'platform'` union is the thing to widen — an omission should stop compiling rather than be remembered. Any fix must also address the **ordering** KS-1054 documents (039 needs tables CORE creates), or a tenant DB simply reproduces the boot-1 window instead of the permanent one.

## Provenance

QA gate finding **F-928-3**, read-from-source and explicitly UNMEASURED, carried inside KS-1054. Measured here by s163 on 2026-09-09, local disposable containers only, removed at close. Demo, UAT and every shared database untouched.

---

## TLS: the tenant connection is VERIFY-FULL, and that is what makes F-928-4's counter load-bearing

**The product hard-codes** `?sslmode=require` **on the tenant connection string** (`startup-migrations.ts:1105`), and `pg-connection-string` **2.12.0 treats** `require` **as** `verify-full` — it says so itself at runtime: *"The SSL modes 'prefer', 'require', and 'verify-ca' are treated as aliases for 'verify-full'."* So the tenant loop does not merely want TLS; it requires a **CA-verifiable certificate chain and a matching hostname**.

**Proved both ways before any of the measurement above was trusted**, against the same container and the same connection-string shape:

```
no trusted CA   ->  "unable to verify the first certificate"
trusted CA      ->  connected, current_database() = tenant_alpha
```

That is why this ticket's zeros mean something: had I not stood the CA up, the tenant DB would have been unreachable and I would have measured my own container instead of the product.

**The consequence on a real deployment:** on any deployment whose tenant database does not present a CA-verifiable certificate, **the tenant loop connects to nothing at all** — and because of the counter defect below, the boot still logs `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

### F-928-4 — the counter cannot report a failure under any condition (measured)

Registered a tenant pointing at `tenant_does_not_exist` — **proved absent** in `pg_database`, **proved present** in the loop's own `SELECT` — and booted:

```
[INFO] Tenant DB migrations complete {"migrated":8,"skipped":0,"total":8}
```

**Mechanism, to the line:** `migrateDatabase` (`startup-migrations.ts:800`) swallows every per-statement error in its own inner `try/catch` and returns `applied`, so it **never throws**, so the tenant loop's `catch` arm at `:1112` is **dead code**. And `new pg.Pool()` does not connect eagerly, so even total connection failure surfaces inside `pool.query` and is swallowed with the rest. `migrated++` therefore counts a tenant whose database does not exist.

### These three legs are ONE path, which is why they are on one ticket

**Tenant provisioning is broken and nothing reports it:**

1. a per-tenant DB arrives **deny-all** on five core tables (the body of this ticket),
2. it **cannot be connected to at all** without a CA-verifiable cert,
3. and the boot **reports success under every one of those failures**.

Filed together deliberately — as three separate tickets each one looks survivable on its own.

title: No Playwright e2e test has run on any PR since 2026-09-07 — the suite dies at a static lint gate before any browser opens, and the job name hides it
description:
**BLUF — no Playwright test has executed on any PR since 2026-09-07. The** `Playwright suite` **job goes red at a static lint gate that runs BEFORE any browser opens, so the red names the wrong subject and the coverage hole has been invisible for three days.**

This is a **test-coverage** ticket, not a CI-config ticket. It was found while measuring CI gate failures (KS-1075) but must not be closed as gate tuning: the gate is a symptom, the missing e2e coverage is the defect.

## What happens

`Playwright suite` (job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml`) fails at **step 6, "Quality gate — static (tsc/ESLint/Prettier/knip/audit)"**. That step runs `npm run format:check && npm run lint && …` ahead of the suite. It exits 1, so **the job stops before a single browser test runs.**

```
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @param "label" declaration  jsdoc/require-param
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @throws declaration         jsdoc/require-throws
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @example declaration        jsdoc/require-example
  48:1  error  Missing JSDoc comment                     jsdoc/require-jsdoc
✖ 4 problems (4 errors, 0 warnings)
```

All four in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`. Prettier passes cleanly — it is the ESLint jsdoc rules alone. ESLint's own output says **3 of the 4 are** `--fix`**-able**.

## Why it hid — the part worth keeping

**The job's name names the wrong subject.** "Playwright suite :: failure" reads as *browser tests ran and failed*. Nobody re-reads a suite they believe is already running. The same shape as a wrapper printing a banner it did not earn: the red was true, and what it implied was false.

## Proven pre-existing, with controls

* Measured identically on **two unrelated PRs** — #938 (one nginx `location` block, zero service code) and #939 (TypeScript type declarations in one service): same rules, same line numbers, same count.
* `global-setup.ts` is touched by **neither** — 0 hits in each diff, against controls of 4 and 3 files actually touched.
* Last changed `42e778203`, **2026-09-07**, *"KS-969 round 2: a role collapse is not a success…"* — three days before either PR.

## What needs doing

1. Fix the four jsdoc errors in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts` (3 are `--fix`-able).
2. **Then confirm the suite actually runs and report what it finds** — three days of unrun e2e may be hiding real failures. A green job after the lint fix is not the same as a suite that was green all along, and it must not be reported as one.
3. Consider whether a static lint gate belongs *ahead* of the suite in the same job at all: as configured, any lint error in the harness silently converts "e2e coverage" into "no e2e coverage" while still reporting a normal-looking red.

## Related

Found during KS-1075 (CI gate measurement, commissioned by Kam as `measure-then-decide`). KS-1075 covers the two *other* gate causes — a `bash -e` swallowed diagnostic and an empty npm-audit allow-list — and should not absorb this one.

title: kintsugi lost demo-service to the KS-641 fail-closed gate — the flag is unset on BOTH boxes and enabling it is a one-line decision with no owner
description:
**BLUF — kintsugi served** `demo-service` **for 20 hours and now refuses to start it. That is KS-641's fail-closed gate working correctly, not a bug. The point of this ticket is that the box lost a running service and the decision to restore it has no owner.**

Found during the s169 whole-estate rebuild of kintsugi (KS-601, under Kam's 2026-09-10 15:24 AEST ruling).

## What changed

|  | before the rebuild | after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-demo-service` on kintsugi | `Up 20 hours (healthy)` (measured 05:35Z) | `restarting`**, exit 1, 18 restarts** |
| image | `62fb55bf4fa1` (2026-08-19) | `c4823b0d2fc1` (2026-09-10) |

Log, every restart:

```
FATAL: DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly "true" to run demo-service.
This is a deliberate opt-in, not a default — refusing to start.
```

**The swap itself succeeded** — the container is on the new image. The service declines to start.

## Why — and why it is not a regression in the code

**KS-641** ("inbound auth + fail-closed non-prod gate on demo-service") introduced the gate. `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` is **unset on both kintsugi and demo**. The old image kintsugi was running had no such check, which is why it served for 20 hours — *it ran because the gate did not exist yet, which is the defect KS-641 fixed, not a capability that was lost.*

On **demo** this is the status quo, already recorded in the s168 handover as *"a deliberate opt-in guard working as designed"*. **On kintsugi it is new**, because kintsugi was three weeks behind and had never received KS-641.

## The decision, and why it is deliberately not taken here

`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` **stays OFF** — ruled 2026-09-10, on three grounds: it matches demo (and Kam ruled the same day that *"everything that we do this week is replicated and fixed on both servers"*, making parity an instruction); OFF is the gate's own intent as a fail-closed opt-in; and OFF is the branch that requires no signature, since enabling a fail-closed non-prod auth gate is a config change with a security shape.

**So this ticket is not a request to flip the flag.** It exists because a service that was serving is now not, on both boxes, and *"enabling it is a one-line change nobody has decided to make"* is precisely the kind of state that gets rediscovered by accident weeks later.

## What is needed

1. **A decision with a stated reason** on whether `demo-service` should run on either box at all — or a decision that it should not, recorded so the next rebuild does not re-raise this.
2. If it should run: set `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED=true` in that box's `.env` (gitignored, so this is a per-box config action, not a code change) and recreate the container.

## Note on classification, recorded because it cost a correction

This was initially reported as *"the known demo-service down"*. **That classification was borrowed from the s168 record of DEMO and applied to KINTSUGI, a different box, where nothing had established it.** The mechanism was evidenced; the *expectation* was not. Flagged here so the distinction survives: on demo this is status quo, on kintsugi it is a state change.

⚠ The rebuild did not hide it — the swap ran with an exception keyed to the **failure signature** (`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly`), not the service name, so the same service failing for any other reason still halts the run. Every hit is recorded in `.rebuild/blocked.txt` on the box.

title: SECURITY (local test stack): akto-autoheal runs as root with /var/run/docker.sock RW — env-scoping is only as strong as who holds the socket
description:
**BLUF —** `akto-autoheal` **runs as uid=0 root with** `/var/run/docker.sock` **mounted read-write, which grants host-equivalent read of EVERY container's environment through the daemon API and therefore defeats environment-variable scoping as a security control — but it is confined to the local Akto test harness: it sits on network** `akto_default` **rather than the platform's** `dev_secuura-network`**, and it is defined only in** `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml`**, so it does not exist on demo or kintsugi.**

The bound is in that sentence deliberately. A reader who stops after the first clause should not walk away believing this is live on a VM, and a reader who stops after the second should not walk away believing it is nothing.

## What was measured

| probe | result |
| -- | -- |
| containers with a bind mount of `/var/run/docker.sock` | **1 —** `akto-autoheal` (`willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0`), mount **RW=true** |
| its user | `uid=0(root) gid=0(root)`, `Config.User` empty |
| tooling present inside it | `curl` **PRESENT**, `wget` **PRESENT** (no `docker` CLI, which is not a mitigation — the daemon API is HTTP over that socket) |
| its networks | `akto_default` — **not** `dev_secuura-network` |
| defining compose file | `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` only |
| occurrences of `autoheal` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` (the file the VMs run) | **0** |

**Controls, so the zeros discriminate:**

* The bind-mount scan enumerates and prints **all six** distinct bind sources across the 38 running containers (`docker/init`, `docker/init-platform`, `docker/seed`, one `secuura-api.yaml`, one `nginx-demo.conf`, `/var/run/docker.sock`) — so it can see bind mounts, and the absence of a repo-root or `.env` mount is a real null.
* The `0` for `autoheal` in the VM compose file is measured against a positive control in the same file: `originate` returns **1**. So the grep matches when the string is there.

## Why this matters beyond the container itself

**It is the general case of the specific control being shipped in KS-1041 Step 2.** That work scopes a gateway-vouch secret to exactly two of 34 containers by declaring it per-service, and verifies the scoping by probing container environments. **Any container with root + RW** `docker.sock` **can read those same environments through the daemon regardless of how narrowly they were declared** — so env-scoping is a control whose strength is bounded by who holds the socket, and nothing today records that dependency.

That is why this is filed separately rather than inside the KS-1041 PR: a finding about the estate's secret-handling as a class, buried in another ticket's PR description, is discoverable only by someone reading that PR, and it outlives the change that surfaced it.

## Explicitly NOT proposed

No fix, no privilege change, no compose edit. Changing a test stack's privileges was outside the commission this was found under and outside the current deploy grant. **Scoped and evidenced only — the remedy is a decision for whoever picks this up.**

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) while measuring the blast radius of the KS-1041 Step 2 vouch secret, at Wednesday's instruction to establish who can read it before building a control that depends on it. All readings taken read-only against the running local stack; nothing was changed.

Related: KS-1041 (the specific control this generalises).

nodes.body:
**Risk classification — this lands in Peter's §1b "systemTest gate / report / baseline logic" high-risk class.**

Added per Wednesday's routing note, because the class is not obvious from the title. `akto-autoheal` is part of the **Akto systemTest harness**, and a root container holding a read-write `docker.sock` alongside that harness sits squarely in the "gate / report / baseline logic" band — the band where a compromise does not merely leak, it can rewrite what a gate reports.

Under the PR verification protocol Kam adopted 2026-09-10, that classification means any change here needs the full reviewer pass rather than a spot-check. **Recording the class now so whoever picks it up does not have to re-derive it — and note the ticket still asks for scoping and a decision, not a fix.**

title: The Playwright env guard added in #896 reads config/ only — the variable breaking the CI run is read from fixtures/ and appears in no template
description:
## BLUF

PR #896 (KS-682) adds `systemTest/playwright/tests-unit/env-example.test.ts`. It pins `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` to every variable that `config/` **reads**. **The variable now failing the Playwright run in CI,** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`**, is read outside that scope**, so the guard stays green over exactly the gap that breaks the run.

**This is measured on #896's head** `a7b588a05f1a40b29b429e7dafa4a84d9a6283d0`**, which is unmerged. The guard does not exist on** `develop`**.** s171 found it by reading during its Phase 1 review of #896 (2026-09-10), not by running a test, so it was not filed then. Filing, not fixing: `systemTest/` is Peter's authority.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Guard scope (#896 head) | `env-example.test.ts:23-24`: `PACKAGE_ROOT` = `systemTest/playwright`, `CONFIG_DIR = path.join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'config')`. `:40` reads only `readdirSync(CONFIG_DIR)` |
| Where the variable is read (#896 head) | `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts:155`, `password: process.env.BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? ''`. This is outside `systemTest/playwright/` entirely (`:110` on `develop` `2d864ae92`) |
| How the Playwright run reaches it | `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:40` spawns `fixtures/pre-suite.ts`, which provisions the actors |
| In the `.env.example` the guard pins | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `API_BASE_URL` **1** |
| Readers inside the guard's scope | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** under `playwright/config/` · control `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **1 file** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `DATABASE_URL` **2** |
| `.github/workflows/` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** · control `API_BASE_URL` **4 files** |

## Why it matters

The guard's claim is true as written: it covers what `config/` reads. But a green guard reads as "the Playwright environment is documented", and the variable that decides whether the run can authenticate at all is read by the shared `fixtures/` the run spawns.

It also compounds with KS-969. Without `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` the pre-suite reports DEGRADED and exits 0, the actor manifest is not published, and `auth.setup` logs in with `''`. In CI that login returns HTTP 400, and 11 of the 12 tests never run. See KS-969 comment `e1358ef7`.

## Not decided here

Two questions for Peter:

* Should the guard also scan the `fixtures/` the suite spawns?
* Does `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` belong in any `.env.example` at all? It is a privileged bootstrap credential, and KS-969's open question comes first: what supplies it now that the published default is retired?

## Searched before filing

* Exact: `CONFIG_DIR` (10 hits, none about this guard), `env-example.test.ts`, `PACKAGE_ROOT`, `getTestAdminPassword` (KS-969 only).
* Fuzzy: "env-example guard", "readEnv config .env.example guard", "env drift guard fixtures directory".
* Opened, none carries this finding:
  * KS-967: a different pair of guards, the credential scanners.
  * KS-1081: two templates disagreeing with each other.
  * KS-973: pre-suite step items.
  * KS-682's 19 comments: `env-example` appears only in a bite table.
* Control: `KS-682` returns 1 hit.

Links: KS-969 · KS-966 · KS-682 · [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896>)

title: GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET: nothing provisions it and no deploy order or rotation is written — #951's control ships inert, and a gateway/originate mismatch drops gateway identity
description:
## BLUF

PR #951 (KS-1041 Step 2) adds a secret that lets originate tell a gateway-routed request from a direct one. **No tracked deploy, bootstrap or CI path supplies** `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, so every environment boots with the control **DISABLED** (fail-open by design, with a WARN). And **when the gateway and originate disagree about the secret** — originate deployed first, a gateway rollback, a rotation, or a gateway container not recreated after `.env` changes — originate drops every gateway-set identity. This is one logical path: provisioning, deploy order, rotation. It is also where the **provisioning-safety question** lives — whether switching the control on breaks the gateway's own non-proxy writes to originate (Detail, first section).

## Recommendation

Needs decisions before code. Decide:

1. where each environment's value comes from — Key Vault → `deploy.sh` `--parameters gatewayVouchSecret=…`, and a `fill_if_blank "GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET" "openssl rand -hex 32"` line in `bootstrap-env.sh` for local;
2. the gateway-first deploy order and a rotation procedure (a dual-accept window or a transition flag), written into the runbook **before any box receives the secret**;
3. whether production should REQUIRE it (`enforceProductionConfig` in originate).
4. **Before provisioning on ANY box, answer the provisioning-safety question below.** The #951 round-2 tier-1 gate (commissioned 2026-09-10 22:52Z against `02a22f4bb`) is measuring it as a separate PROVISIONING SAFETY verdict.

## Detail

**Provisioning-safety question — READ ONLY, not driven (added by s174, 2026-09-11).** The gateway's own `POST /api/documents` handler (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:879`; the verification router is not mock-gated — `index.ts:876-891`) forwards to originate through its own `http.request` (`:1044`, headers built at `:1024-1042`) carrying `x-user-id`, `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug` and **no vouch** — the file has zero `vouch` mentions at `02a22f4bb`. With `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` set, originate's provenance middleware strips those headers. The handler's own KS-39 #4 comment (`:1036-1040`) states what a missing `x-tenant-id` does: the POST writes to the fallback tenant and the new document looks invisible / 404s on the next read. The workflow-approve forward (route `:700`, `http.request` at `:785`, `x-user-id` at `:783`) has the same shape. **Unknown:** whether originate's `authenticate()` recovers the tenant from the forwarded JWT — if it does, the consequence shrinks. If the question holds, the fix is the one #951's F5 residual already names: send every gateway→originate call through one helper that adds the vouch.

**F4 — nothing supplies it.** Re-measured at `dd0a0c934` from git objects: **0 mentions** of the secret in `deployment/azure/deploy.sh`, `services.parameters.json`, `env.demo.json`, `env.dev.json`, `sync-secrets.sh`, `setup-keyvault.sh`, `deploy-all.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh`, and 0 files under `.github` (control: `services.bicep` → 10). `bootstrap-env.sh:198,200,208` generate `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY` and `DEMO_SERVICE_KEY`, not this. originate's `enforceProductionConfig` requires `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` only. The #951 tier-1 gate counted 35 `--parameters` at `deploy.sh:721-757`, none of them this. Azure deploys therefore take the bicep default `''` and wire neither app.

**F3 — mismatch.** Measured in-process by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, cells S2.1 and S4.1): a merge-base gateway, or a head gateway with the secret unset, in front of an originate that has it → gateway-set `x-tenant-id` / `x-user-id` are stripped. Consequences read from source: the metering connector shim (`originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42`) stops matching and `authenticate()` answers 401; with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` in production `extractTenantContext` answers 400 "Missing tenant context" (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:67-74`); single-tenant falls to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`originate/src/index.ts:248-256`). **No forgeability window in any order** (gate cells S2.2–S2.4) — order affects availability and tenant scoping, not the hole.

**Board searched before filing** (exact to decide, fuzzy to discover): `gatewayVouchSecret` → 0; `vouch` → 12, none about provisioning (KS-1041, KS-1080 akto-autoheal, KS-1081 env-template drift, the rest Platform S identity/verify work); `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, `deploy order`, `bootstrap-env.sh` → fuzzy noise, nothing about this secret; control `KS-1041` → 1.

Related: KS-1041 · KS-1081 (whichever env template wins must carry this variable) · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · round-1 gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (F3, F4).

**FYI, Kamil: KS-955 is going in, and it touches this ticket's area.** PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1756

**BLUF:** KS-955 does two things here:
- It fixes the unvouched gateway → originate forwards (your R2-1, "provisioning unsafe").
- It has `bootstrap-env.sh` generate `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` for fresh **local** clones. That changes the 2026-09-11 position, *"Do not set `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` on any environment yet"*, for local stacks. It went in only once the forward fix was in place and proven.

Nothing touches the VM demo, Container Apps or `deploy.sh`.

**What changes**

1. **P2a (api-gateway).**
   * `utils/originateForward.ts` reads the secret in one place and sends `x-gateway-vouch` to originate only.
   * The five hand-built forwards now use it: `POST /api/documents` and the workflow-approve forward (`verification.ts`); the upload, signatories and third-party-verifiers forwards (`proxy.ts`).
2. **P2c (`bootstrap-env.sh`).**
   * `fill_if_blank "GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET" "openssl rand -hex 32"`, written to `.env` only. An existing value is never overwritten.
   * A fresh local clone now boots originate `ACTIVE`, not `FAIL-CLOSED`.
3. **Not done:** O-4 (`SENSITIVE_KEYS`). It is recorded on this ticket (comment of 2026-10-26): shared-logger redaction runs only in production, and the gateway logs through its own winston logger.

**Evidence** (Peter's Mac, 2026-10-27; full Test Evidence on the PR and on KS-955)

* **Unit, red on develop and green on the branch:**
  * `ks955-hand-forwards-carry-the-vouch.test.ts`: 3 of 7 red on develop, 7 of 7 green.
  * `bootstrap_env_gateway_vouch.test.sh`: 4 of 7 red on develop, 7 of 7 green.
* **Live, R2-1 end to end:** new cell `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_tenant_isolation_gateway_create.py`. A super-admin creates a document through the gateway's `POST /api/documents` under a non-default tenant's override.
  * **Develop `a105a9df1` with a vouch secret set by hand:** create 201, then a **404** reading it in that tenant. It landed in the default tenant, as your gate measured.
  * **KS-955:** 200 in the tenant, 404 in the default tenant.
* **The cross-tenant pair (KS-1704):** both tests fail on develop because the secret is unset, and pass with it set.
* **Gates on the branch head all green,** including preflight 16/16. The remaining Schemathesis reds are the same as develop's, and all ticketed.

**Still with this ticket:** deployed provisioning (Key Vault → `deploy.sh`), deploy order, rotation, and whether production should require the secret.

No action is needed from you for KS-955. If you see a problem with local stacks booting `ACTIVE`, a note here would be very welcome. Thank you.

**P2b (your O-4 from 2026-09-11) was not done in KS-955. Recorded here so it is not lost.**

Adding `x-gateway-vouch` to the shared logger's `SENSITIVE_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/logger/index.ts:19`, still 0 mentions) would not protect the gateway today, for two reasons:
- `redactValue` returns early unless `NODE_ENV === 'production'`.
- api-gateway logs through its own winston logger (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/logger.ts`), not the shared one.

Touching `packages/shared` also rebuilds every image. So the real fix belongs to whatever decides redaction for the gateway's logger; a key in a list it never consults would not do it.

**What KS-955 did do on your list:**
- **Item 1:** the five hand-built originate forwards now send the vouch through one helper (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/originateForward.ts`). It reads the secret in one place, sends it to originate only, and is red→green unit-tested.
- **P2c:** `bootstrap-env.sh` now generates the secret for a **local** fresh clone. Measured: a fresh worktree boots originate `ACTIVE`, and the KS-1704 tenant-isolation pair passes.

**Still open here:** deployed provisioning (Key Vault → `deploy.sh`), deploy order, rotation, and whether production must require it. Not yet run live: a document saved through the gateway's `POST /api/documents` with the secret set.

**BLUF:** reproduced again on 2026-10-16 (slot 2, develop `a92f46e14`). The Schemathesis `pre-merge` live integration suite had **2 failed of 436**, both tenant isolation, the same pair recorded on KS-1478 on 2026-10-14.

- `test_cross_tenant_isolation`: a document created as the super-admin was readable (200) with `X-Tenant-Override` set to a foreign tenant ("BUG-ISOLATION-001 regression").
- `test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation`: a key created under Oxford was listed under the BUPA tenant override (KS-513 assertion).
- `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is set (non-empty) in **0 of 2** containers checked (`api-gateway`, `originate`), and `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` still has 0 mentions of it. Checked by key presence only; no value was read.

**Proposed acceptance criteria:**
- Local bootstrap and every deploy path provision the secret.
- The deploy order and rotation are written down.
- **A test demonstrates the fix:** both tests above pass on a freshly built slot with the secret provisioned, and fail with it unset.

## Since KS-1032 (2026-10-13) the unprovisioned secret is no longer inert: on every templated slot it silently drops the super-admin tenant override

**BLUF:** this ticket's title says the control "ships inert". After commit `d53d80cbb` (KS-1032, merged 2026-10-13) that is no longer true. With `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, originate **drops** identity/tenant/role headers from every request, so a super-admin's `X-Tenant-Override` never reaches the RLS context. Nothing errors; the request reads the default tenant. That matches KS-1032's own commit message: *"a silent switch to the wrong tenant, not a refusal"*. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour on an unconfigured box. The gap is that **nothing provisions the secret**, so every box built from the templates is in that state.

**Measured, 2026-10-14, slot 1 of Peter's Mac, `develop` 3c0a52221:**
* originate at boot (container log): `[gateway-provenance] FAIL-CLOSED — GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET is unset, so identity/tenant/role headers are DROPPED from every request`.
* Templates: `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:478` and `.env.example:343` both read `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET=` (blank). `bootstrap-env.sh` generates `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` / `REDIS_PASSWORD` per clone (KS-731) but not this key.
* Consequence: the systemTest tenant-isolation tests (`test_cross_tenant_isolation`, `test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation`) passed in all 7 archived runs on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12, and **fail in 3 of 3 runs on 2026-10-14**, with a message that reads like a P0 leak. Detail and the misleading-verdict half are on **KS-955**.

**Not verified:** the green path with the secret set. Setting it means writing a secret value, which a person has to do. Nothing in any env file was read to establish the above; only the templates and the container log were.

**Proposed acceptance criteria (provisioning half):**
1. `bootstrap-env.sh` generates `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` per clone when blank (the KS-731 pattern) and writes the same value for gateway and originate.
2. The deploy order and rotation are written down, as this ticket's title asks.
3. **A test demonstrating the fix:** a bootstrap shell test proves a fresh `.env` gets a non-empty secret. On a stack built from it, originate does **not** log `FAIL-CLOSED … unset`, and the systemTest tenant-isolation tests pass.

Found during KS-1478 (Akto / Schemathesis tool bump), which did not cause it.

## BLUF

- **Do not set `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` on any environment yet.** The QA agent's round-2 tier-1 gate on #951 (`02a22f4bb`, 2026-09-11) returned GO WITH FINDINGS on the PR, and **PROVISIONING SAFETY: UNSAFE** as a separate verdict.
- **Why:** once originate has the secret, the gateway's own `POST /api/documents` forward carries no vouch. originate strips `x-tenant-id` and `x-user-id`, and the document is saved under **`DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`** instead of the caller's tenant. No error is returned. Measured at runtime, in-process, with real modules and a synthetic secret and key.
- **Merging #951 does not change this.** develop `2d864ae92` has the same forward (READ ONLY, not driven).

## Recommendation

A precondition for ANY provisioning, in this ticket's scope:

1. **One helper that adds the vouch to every gateway → originate call that bypasses the proxy middleware:**
   - `api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1044` at `02a22f4bb` (develop `:1125`), POST /api/documents;
   - `verification.ts:785` (develop `:866`), the workflow-approve forward;
   - `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:522-526` at `02a22f4bb`, the multipart upload forward (latent: originate registers no `/upload` route).
2. **The gate's regression test:** record the real `verification.ts` forward, replay it into the real originate app with the secret set, and assert the tenant passed to `saveDocument` equals the JWT tenant. Include a vouched control and an unset control.
3. **O-4 (latent, READ):** add `x-gateway-vouch` to the shared logger's `SENSITIVE_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/logger/index.ts:19`; 0 mentions today).

No action needed from anyone on this comment beyond keeping the secret unset.

## Detail

**The measurement (report R2-1):**

| cell | originate secret UNSET | originate secret SET (synthetic) |
|---|---|---|
| P1: recorded POST /api/documents forward, tenant the handler writes under | the forwarded JWT tenant | **`DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`**: `x-tenant-id` and `x-user-id` stripped, RLS = default, `saveDocument` = default |
| P1v control: the same forward plus a correct vouch | the forwarded JWT tenant | the forwarded JWT tenant |
| P2: recorded workflow-approve forward | 401, handler not reached | 401, handler not reached |

**Mechanism** (line numbers at `02a22f4bb`, from the report):

- `createGatewayProvenanceMiddleware` strips the unvouched trust headers.
- The KS-458 block (`originate/src/index.ts:248-256`) then sets `req.tenantId = DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, and `tenantGucContext` seeds RLS from it. Both run at app level, before `documentsRouter.use(authenticate())` (`routes/documents.ts:145`), which sets `req.user` only.
- The gateway handler's own KS-39 #4 comment (`verification.ts:1036-1040`) describes the consequence: the new document looks invisible, or 404s, to its owner.

**Every gateway → originate call outside the proxy middleware:**

| call site (at `02a22f4bb`) | changed by provisioning? |
|---|---|
| `verification.ts:1044` POST /api/documents | **yes (R2-1)** |
| `proxy.ts:522-526` upload | yes, latent |
| `verification.ts:785` workflow-approve | no: 401 in both modes. Its own data-loss defect is filed as KS-1087. |
| `proxy.ts:606/630`, `platform.ts:248`, `verification.ts:129/167`, `batch.ts:91` (Authorization only) | no, see KS-1084 |

**NOT tested by the gate:**

- multi-tenant mode (`MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`);
- `NODE_ENV=production` variants (the KS-458 block is unconditional, READ);
- R2-1 on develop (READ ONLY, not driven);
- the upload forward under provisioning (not replayed);
- any live stack, and how many live JWTs carry a non-default tenant.

**Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-02a22f4bb-tier1-r2/report.md`, sections R2-1, Open (O-4) and NOT TESTED. Posted by Platform K seat s177 on Wednesday's brief; the QA agent cannot post.

title: Launcher preflight: four findings — a concurrent seat clobbers the warnings file, KS-907 miscounts sessions, F-02 names a missing key, rule 7 still says extranet
description:
## BLUF

Four defects in `Launch_Claude.command`. **This ticket files them; it does not fix them.** None blocks a session today. Each one either loses a boot warning, misreports seat state, or tells a seat to do something wrong.

1. **The warnings file is one file per project, so a second seat's launch overwrites the first seat's warnings.** Measured by s172 on 2026-09-11: s173's launch at 07:11:31 overwrote s172's at 07:11:14, 17 s apart, and s172's own warnings were lost.
2. **The KS-907 seat registry counted a session running in** `Testing Agent MAIN` **as "a live session on this project".** Measured by s173 on 2026-09-11. The mechanism is not verified.
3. **The F-02 remedy tells the operator to** `ssh-add ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` **— a file that does not exist on this machine.** git works regardless, through the repo-local `core.sshCommand` → `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw`.
4. **Launch-prompt rule 7 still prescribes "an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment".** That contradicts Kam's 2026-09-05 ruling that everything goes through the tickets. The project `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was corrected on 2026-09-11; the launcher was not.

A fifth finding already has a home: the SessionStart hook still tells every seat to `POST /api/seen`. That is **KS-925**, and the evidence is added there.

## Recommendation

Fix all four in the **master launcher template** as well as this copy. Per the launcher notes, `Launch_Claude.command` is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing one copy fixes no other project. One pass proves all four:

* launch two seats about 10 s apart and check both warnings survive;
* run with a non-Blockchain Claude session alive and check it is not counted;
* read the F-02 text against `ls`;
* grep the assembled boot prompt for `extranet to-do` and expect 0.

## Detail

**1 — clobbered warnings file.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:90` writes `PREFLIGHT_LOG="$PROJECT_DIR/4_Credentials/.launch_preflight_last.txt"`, one path per project. The boot prompt then tells the seat to relay that file verbatim (`:392`).
* s172 (PID 64454, launched 07:11:14 AEST) read a file stamped `# launch 2026-09-10T21:11:31Z`, which is s173's launch.
* In that file, the KS-907 line listed s172's own PID as an "other" seat.
* Control from s176 today: the stamp `2026-09-10T22:36:54Z` equals `ps -o lstart= -p $PPID`. The file is not always clobbered — only when two launches race.
* Workaround in use: compare the stamp with your own start before relaying the warnings.

**2 — KS-907 miscount.**

* s173 attributed one of the two "other live sessions" in its KS-907 line to the fleet QA agent, by its cwd (`Testing Agent MAIN`).
* The registry lives at `Launch_Claude.command:244-379`. It reads `ps -eo pid=,command=` at `:328`.
* Not re-measured here, and which predicate matched is not verified.

**3 — F-02 names a missing key.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:107`, `:133` and `:138` all say `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw`.
* On this machine (s176, 2026-09-11 ~23:3xZ), `ls ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` → `No such file or directory`.
* `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw` is present, and `git fetch` returned rc 0 through `core.sshCommand` while the F-02 warning was showing.

**4 — rule 7.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:476` says: *"notify Stuart AND Peter — an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment @-mentioning them"*.
* Kam, 2026-09-05 13:55, verbatim: *"The team is not using the extranet much. I mentioned this yesterday. If anything needs to be escalated, please tell me and I'll send a WhatsApp message. Otherwise, everything has to be done through the tickets."*
* The project-root `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was rewritten to "on the tickets only" by s176 on 2026-09-11, as ruled by Wednesday. The pre-edit copy is in `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-11-s176/`.

**Searched before filing:**

* `launch_preflight_last` — 14 KS hits. KS-907 and KS-911 name the file only as test hygiene ("every run overwrites it"); none covers the clobber.
* `secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` — no launcher ticket.
* `extranet-session-check` and `api/seen` — found **KS-925**, which is finding 5, so it is not duplicated here.
* `Launch_Claude.command` — KS-907, KS-925, KS-655, KS-911, KS-912, KS-681, KS-78; none covers these four.
* Control: `KS-907` → 1 hit.

Filed by s176. Findings 1 and 2 are other seats' measurements, credited above. Findings 3 and 4 were re-measured at source by s176.

## BLUF
**Finding 2's mechanism is now identified: the launcher's argv scan, not the registry.** It recurred at the 2026-09-17 09:41:16Z Platform K launch. The KS-907 line listed `PID 73954 (live claude session on this project)`. That process was the fleet QA agent gating PR #1025: cwd `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN`, started 19:40:27 AEST, argv beginning `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model opus ultrathink` followed by "You are the fleet QA agent running a TIER 2 (through code) gate, ROUND 1, on Secuura/Blockchain PR #1025 (KS-528, Seat B)". It held no checkout and was not a seat.

## Recommendation
No action needed from this comment. It adds evidence to this ticket's single fix pass: the scan's predicate should require the process's working directory to be inside the project tree, not only that its argv names the project, and `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` should gain a cell for a `claude` process whose argv names the project path while its cwd is elsewhere.

## Detail
- **Which arm matched, read at source** (`Launch_Claude.command`, sha256 `35413bab27864a0e9d407bcdb522dcabe36a221cae205c1cec5f53cb31bb874c`):
  - The registry arm labels a kept row `PID <n> (up since <lstart>)`.
  - The second detector (`:327` opens it, `:328` reads `ps -eo pid=,command=`) keeps a row whose command contains `"claude "` (`:333`) AND contains `$PROJECT_DIR` (`:334`), and labels it `PID <n> (live claude session on this project)` (`:338`).
  - The 09:41:16Z line used the second label, so the argv scan matched.
- **Why a gate matches:** a gate is launched as `claude … <prompt>`. For `:334` to match, the prompt must also carry the project directory path, for example a brief or report path under it. That part is inferred from the label; the argv was not read in full before the process exited.
- **Measured at boot (19:4x AEST):** PID 73954 `ps -o lstart=` Thu 17 Sep 19:40:27 2026; `lsof -a -p 73954 -d cwd` → `Testing Agent MAIN`. Control, the real other seat: PID 35278, started 17:01:36, cwd `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain` (Seat B). By 19:58 AEST PID 73954 had exited (`ps -p` empty).
- **Consequence, unchanged from the finding:** the boot is read-only (the safe direction, which the comment above `:327` accepts), and the relayed seat count reads 2 where the true count was 1.
- **Searched before writing:** `KS-907` (1 hit, KS-907 itself), `other live session` (1: this ticket), `live claude session` (0), `SECUURA_SEAT_SCAN` (2: KS-940, KS-907), `seat registry` (3: this ticket, KS-911, KS-939). Only this ticket records the miscount, so this is a comment and not a new ticket.

## BLUF
**Three more launch-prompt sites carry superseded instructions, beyond this ticket's four findings.** s181 measured them at source in `Launch_Claude.command` on 2026-09-11, about 08:15Z.
- **`:539`, boot step 8.** It names the shared inbox `coagent@agentmail.to`, which this project's key reads as 404. It also ends *"RULE: CC Kam (kamil.kreiser@secuura.ai) on every email you send."*
- **`:537`, boot step 7.** It still ends *"mark seen afterwards."* KS-925's 2026-09-10 comment says the boot prompt no longer does; measured today, it does.
- **`:461-473`, scope rule 7.** It still says every deployable change *"ships to BOTH the local stack AND the new Azure demo env"*. That contradicts Kam's 2026-09-11 16:56 ruling, as the coordinator read it: demo (UAT) is updated only after Peter's formal test pass.
- **No launcher or hook line states the approval rule** that Kam's 16:56 ruling replaced: 0 hits, and the control fired.

## Recommendation
No action needed from this comment. It adds evidence to this ticket's single fix pass. The hook's `/api/seen` line stays on KS-925.

## Detail
**Frame searched:**
- `Launch_Claude.command`;
- `.claude/settings.local.json` and its two conflict copies;
- `.claude/hooks/extranet-session-check.sh`;
- root `CLAUDE.md` and `2_Project_Files/CLAUDE.md`;
- `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md` and `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md`.

The instrument was `/usr/bin/grep -rnaiF`.
- **Approval-rule patterns:** `No approval → no merge` · `no approval` · `Peter's approval` · `approval at head` · `AUTHOR merges` · `reviewer's **approval**` · `red pen`.
  - Positive control: root `CLAUDE.md:237` hit, before that line was amended.
  - Launcher: 0 hits. Hook and settings: 0 hits.
- **Superseded-instruction patterns:**
  - `mark seen` → `:537`;
  - `api/seen` → launcher 0; hook `:13` (a comment) and `:45` (the emitted line, unchanged since KS-925's comment);
  - `CC Kam` → `:539`;
  - `an extranet to-do` → `:476` (this ticket's finding 4);
  - `Update BOTH targets` → `:461`.
  - Control: `FIRST ACTIONS` → `:482`.

**The three sites, verbatim:**
- `:537`: "…GET the summary for this operator (EXTRANET_ME), and fold my open tasks + replies-to-me + new documents into the confirmation below; mark seen afterwards."
- `:539`: "Shared inbox: coagent@agentmail.to. List recent inbox messages via the AgentMail API (GET https://api.agentmail.to/v0/inboxes/coagent@agentmail.to/messages, …) … RULE: CC Kam (kamil.kreiser@secuura.ai) on every email you send."
- `:461-467`: "7. Update BOTH targets — local AND the new Azure demo … any change with a deployable surface (services / frontends) ships to BOTH the local stack AND the new Azure demo env … Validate on local first (green), THEN deploy the SAME change to Azure demo".

**What each one conflicts with:**
- **`:539`, the inbox.** Measured this session with the project's key: `GET /v0/inboxes/coagent@agentmail.to` → 404; `GET /v0/inboxes/secuura-blockchain@agentmail.to` → 200; `GET /v0/inboxes` → count 1. A seat that follows the line reads nothing.
- **`:539`, the CC.** The fleet rule is that agent-to-agent mail carries no CC (Kam, 2026-08-12). That is as recorded in this project's agent memory, not re-read at source here.
- **`:537`.** `skills/Current/extranet.md:110` says agents MUST NOT call `/api/seen`. Kam also ruled it out on 2026-09-10 (card `secuura-extranet-seen-marking-hook-and-skill`), as recorded; that ruling was not re-read at source.
- **`:461-473`.** Kam, 2026-09-11 16:56:00: *"For the time being, I / you will approve our own elements"*. The coordinator reads it to mean demo (UAT) waits for Peter's nod, and the project-root `CLAUDE.md` Merge flow now says so (amended by s181, 2026-09-11). That file's own both-targets wording at `:173` and `:178` is owed separately.

**Board searched before posting.** Method: Linear `searchIssues`, every result page read, literal match on title, description and up to 40 comments.

title: run-shell-suites.sh restores git discovery but does not isolate suites: a suite that runs git from its cwd writes the repository it runs in (KS-1086 QA-6)
description:
## BLUF

* **The boundary.** KS-1086's fix (PR #953) clears the hook's repository-local git variables before the shell suites run. A suite's `git` calls then fall back to normal discovery. That restores discovery; it does not isolate.
* **The consequence.** A suite that runs `git` from its working directory, without first moving into a temp repo of its own, still writes to whichever repository it started in. Under a push, that is the pushing repository.
* **Today, no current suite does this.** All 18 ran under the fixed runner from a linked worktree, and the shared config, refs and HEADs came out identical. This is a boundary for a future suite, not a live defect.

## Recommendation

Low priority. Decide whether the runner should enforce isolation, or whether the fixture convention is enough.

The gate named two fix shapes:

* run each suite with its cwd in a fresh temp dir;
* or have the runner snapshot its own repo's config, refs and HEADs around the loop, and fail loudly on any change.

The second overlaps KS-948's proposed runner-level check that a suite run left nothing behind, so one change could close both. This is filing only; nothing is scheduled.

## Detail

**Source.** Tier-1 QA gate on PR #953 @ `de1ab62c0`, finding QA-6 (Observation), arm M3. MEASURED in scratch repositories.

* The suite was `git config qa.cwdplant 1` with no `cd`, run under the head runner from a linked worktree.
* It saw `GIT_DIR=unset`, with a cwd of `<worktree>/Blockchain/Dev`.
* The shared config gained `[qa] cwdplant = 1`.

**Current suites.** Gate arm F2 ran all 18 real suites under the head runner from a linked worktree. Shared config, refs, main HEAD and worktree HEADs were IDENTICAL.

**Scope, reasoned from the mechanism and NOT run:** the same would happen from a normal clone, and from a manual `npm run test:shell`.

**Where.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`, in the suite loop (`bash "$REPO_ROOT/$rel"`). Each suite starts in the runner's own cwd.

**Board searched before filing.** The issue columns search title and description, archived included; the comment column searches comment bodies.

| term | issues | comments on |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `run-shell-suites` | KS-1086, KS-1046, KS-948, KS-926, KS-910, KS-903 | KS-1027, KS-1086, KS-909, KS-926, KS-936, KS-945, KS-948 |
| `run_shell_suites` | KS-1086, KS-971 | KS-1086, KS-731 |
| `git_local_env` | 0 | 0 |
| `local-env-vars` | 0 | 0 |
| `suite isolation` | 0 | 0 |
| `temp dir` | PS-529 | KS-1027, KS-682 |
| control: `leg 14` | KS-1086 | KS-1086, KS-485, KS-731, KS-772, KS-926 |

None of them covers a suite writing the repository it runs in through a cwd-relative `git` call. Two are adjacent but do not cover it:

* **KS-948:** a backtick in a case name executes as a command. Its fix shape includes a runner-level left-nothing-behind check.
* **KS-903:** a survey of repo-root derivations, including the env-dependent ones.

**Report.** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1086-953-de1ab62c0-tier1/report.md`

title: KS-1041 residual: the cross-tenant JWT probe on originate's direct path — reasoned, never run, not commissioned
description:
## BLUF

* **Recorded from KS-1041, so it stays on a live ticket when KS-1041 is archived.** It was outside KS-1041's Step 1 and Step 2, and it is **not commissioned and not ruled**.
* **The open question:** can a caller already inside the compose network, holding a **valid** JWT, go straight to originate and have an `x-tenant-id` for **another** tenant honoured?
  * KS-1041 **measured** only the credential-free connector-header case.
  * This wider case was **reasoned, never tested**.
* **What has changed since:**
  * #938 (Step 1, `0f8fb33c3`) closed nginx `/originate/`.
  * #951 (Step 2) adds originate middleware that strips unvouched trust headers — but only once `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is provisioned. That is unset everywhere (PROVISIONING SAFETY: UNSAFE, KS-1083), so originate's direct path behaves as before.

## Recommendation

No action until Kam rules. Running the probe needs a fresh commission — KS-1041 `116ed2d6`: *"If it should be run, that goes back to Kam."*

## Detail

* **KS-1041's measured/reasoned split, verbatim** (`116ed2d6`):
  * MEASURED:
    * direct to `originate:4000`, no headers → 401;
    * direct, with forged `x-user-role: connector` + `x-tenant-id` → 200;
    * the same request through `api-gateway:8080` → 401;
    * not externally reachable, but reachable by any of the 34 peers on `dev_secuura-network`.

* **Why it was not run:**

  * `47e0b331`: *"Not done and deliberately so: the cross-tenant JWT probe. It is the next measurement and belongs to a seat with room to act on the answer."*
* **Where it sits:** `originate/src/index.ts:230` reads `x-tenant-id` before auth (`ba0f7402`). Once the secret is provisioned, #951's middleware strips unvouched trust headers ahead of it; KS-1083 holds that precondition.
* **Neighbours, not duplicates:**
  * KS-619 — the gateway's conditional `x-tenant-id` overwrite (the gateway path, not originate's direct path);
  * KS-1032 — trust-header reads outside auth middleware (a code census);
  * KS-1084 — the gateway's Authorization-only calls to originate.
* **Why its own ticket, not a comment on KS-1032:** this is a live measurement, and KS-1032 is a code census and guard. Separate workloads get separate tickets under Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.
* **Board searched before filing** (literal, live tickets only):

  * `originate:4000` → KS-1041 only;

### What each gap needs (measured at develop `4554b25e2`)

nodes.body:
**BLUF: two small additions for whoever picks this up. Neither changes the finding or its priority.** (1) The published spec says the dashboard is already gated in demo, and the code on `develop` doesn't gate it. (2) A systemTest test is now tied to this route's auth, so the fix will turn it red on purpose.

**1. The spec's description disagrees with the code (re-checked at `origin/develop` @ `8c810023f`).**

* `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, under `GET /api/system/health/dashboard`, declares `security: []`. Its description says: *"Authentication is configurable per env (open in dev, gated behind admin in demo)."*
* The gateway mounts the router with no auth middleware in front of it: `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:773`, `app.use('/api/system/health', healthDashboardRouter)`.
* I found nothing in `routes/health-dashboard.ts` or the gateway that reads an env setting to gate it.
* Probed without a credential on a local slot-1 stack (built at `8af6ab821`), it answered **200 with 19 service entries**, each carrying an internal `url` (host and port).
* So on `develop`, "gated behind admin in demo" is not true at the code level. I did **not** probe the demo VM, so I can't say what it serves.
* Whichever fix is chosen, the description should end up matching it.

**2. The api-explorer is tied to this route's `security` on purpose (KS-1386, not yet merged).**

* The explorer's quick-start panel shows the dashboard `curl` **without** an Authorization header, labelled "No Auth", because the spec declares it public.
* `systemTest/api-explorer/tests/unit/.../quickStartSection.test.ts` reads that operation's `security` from the spec and asserts `[]`.
* **When this ticket gates the route and the spec changes, that test goes red by design.** The fix is to put the header back on that one `curl` and update the label. The test exists so the explorer can't go on telling people the route is open once it isn't.

Thank you, Kamil. The dedupe census here made this quick to confirm as the right home.

title: POST /api/auth/register accepts a client-supplied organizationId with no existence or membership check — impact not traced
description:
## BLUF

* `POST /api/auth/register` **lets an anonymous caller choose the organisation its new account belongs to.**
  * `registerSchema` accepts `organizationId` as any UUID (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:139`).
  * The handler stores it on the new user unchanged (`auth.ts:233`, `organizationId: data.organizationId`).
  * Nothing checks that the organisation exists, or that the caller has any relationship to it.
* **Impact NOT traced.** What an account carrying another organisation's id can reach has not been established. That covers the token's `organizationId`, organisation-scoped reads and the KS-597 issuer binding. Nothing was exercised on any environment.
* **Found by s189** while measuring the public account-creation path for KS-1100, on develop `4554b25e2`, which is the code kintsugi runs.

## Recommendation

* **Trace every consumer of a user's** `organizationId` **before choosing a fix.** Then either drop `organizationId` from the public register schema, or bind it to a verified invitation or membership.
* **Do not exercise it on a running environment** without explicit authorisation. Registering under another organisation's id is testing an exploit.
* **Priority High:** it sits on the organisation trust boundary Kam ruled `bind` (card `secuura-org-trust-boundary-within-tenant`, shipped in #954).

## Detail

### Code (develop `4554b25e2`)

* `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:133-142` defines `registerSchema` with `organizationId: z.string().uuid().optional()` and `.strip()`.
* `auth.ts:156` is `authRoutes.post('/register', ...)`. It is unauthenticated, and the gateway exempts it from CSRF (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:85`).
* `auth.ts:221-243` builds the new `User`:
  * the role is fixed server-side as `OWNER`, and a client-sent `role` is refused (KS-82);
  * but `organizationId: data.organizationId` comes straight from the request body.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:611-672`: `createUser` writes that value to `users.organization_id`.
* **Contrast:** `POST /api/users/admin/create` requires an ORG_ADMIN or SYSTEM_ADMIN caller and pins the tenant (KS-467). The public route has no equivalent check on the organisation.

### Not established

* Which reads, grants or attributions key off `users.organization_id`, or the token's `organizationId`, for an OWNER.
* Whether any downstream check already neutralises it. One candidate is originate's KS-597 binding (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:454-469`).

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive search over KS issue titles, descriptions and all comments, archived included. Run 2026-09-12 by s189.
* **Results:**
  * `registerSchema`: 3 issues and 4 comments, across KS-283, KS-202, KS-94, KS-266, KS-255 and KS-82. All are Done and archived, and none mentions `organizationId`.
  * `organizationId: data.organizationId`: 0.
  * `register accepts organizationId`: 0.
  * `self-assign organization`: 0.
* **Controls (the instrument can hit):** `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash` found KS-732 and KS-1005; `UUID_V4_RE` found KS-663.

### Related

* KS-1100: where this was found.
* KS-597: issuer organisation attribution (option B, #954).

title: anchor_store.status has no CHECK constraint — an out-of-union status can be stored silently (producer side of KS-1071 F10)
description:
**BLUF:** `anchor_store.status` is `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` with **no CHECK constraint**, so a status outside anchoring's union (`'pending' | 'submitted' | 'confirmed' | 'failed'`, `anchoring/src/index.ts:112`) can be written silently. KS-1071 closed the *consumer* side (the gateway's one status→confidence mapping now falls **closed** on any out-of-union value); this ticket is the *producer* side — a schema guard so the value cannot be stored in the first place.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:714` and `003_consolidate-anchors.sql:26` — the column, verified 0 CHECKs in the block against a control of 5 elsewhere in 001 (KS-1071's measurement).

**Fix shape:** a new migration adding `CHECK (status IN ('pending','submitted','confirmed','failed'))` on `anchor_store.status` — after a read-only census of the live rows on every environment (a row already holding another value would fail the migration; that row is a finding, not a reason to skip the constraint). Consider a shared TS status union exported from anchoring alongside it, so the code and the schema cannot drift apart silently.

**Why deferred from KS-1071:** a migration is out of that PR's scope by ruling (Wednesday, 2026-09-13 plan confirmation s199: "CHECK constraint → one Low ticket, not this round"). Migrations on this repo are baked into the `migrations` image — see the project CLAUDE.md note on rebuilding it, and KS-1031/#914's "migration 048 first" line before any deploy.

**Not covered here:** originate's own `document.blockchain.status` vocabulary (`anchor_failed`, `submitted`, `confirmed`) is a JSONB field, not this column; it lands on the gateway mapping's closed default and needs no schema change.

Source: KS-1071 F10 (QA tier-1 gate round 2 on #935); filed by s199 after a literal census of 1,104 issues for `anchor_store` + `CHECK` found no home (the only hit was KS-1071 itself). Related: KS-1071.

title: getPlatformAdmin swallows an infrastructure failure to null — platform-admin login reads "platform DB down" as "not an admin" and answers InvalidCredentialsError (the class KS-963 removed)
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` `getPlatformAdmin` (`:1714-1741` at develop after #970) catches every error from the platform-database lookup, logs `Platform admin lookup failed (platform DB may not be configured)` and **returns** `null` (`:1739-1741`). Its caller, `routes/auth.ts:345` `const platformAdmin = await userRepo.getPlatformAdmin(data.email);`, reads `null` as "not a platform admin" and falls through to the regular-user gate, which answers `InvalidCredentialsError` — the KS-253 shape ("a DB failure reported as no such user") on the highest-privilege door. This is exactly the class KS-963 / PR #970 removed from the five `getUserByIdPreAuth` callers, on a branch **outside KS-963's include** (Kam's scope named `getUserById` → widened to `getUserByIdPreAuth`). Named by the tier-1 gate as F-6 under "hunt the class"; needs its own ruling before a build.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks963-970-ae274f7cb-tier1-r1/report.md` — §9 HUNT THE CLASS (F-6 and the 15-catch census), WHAT WAS NOT TESTED item 3 (the branch was not exercised: `getPlatformAdmin` answered `null` because `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` was unset in the harness — which is itself the swallow at work).

## What is and is not established

* **READ ONLY (source at** `ae274f7cb`**):** the catch, its message, the `return null`, the caller at `auth.ts:345`, the fall-through to the regular-user gate (`auth.ts:344-482` is the platform-admin branch).
* **Catch census at head, brace-matched (the gate's):** 15 `catch` blocks in `userRepo.ts` — `return null` at `decryptPlatformAdminMfaSecret :206`, `getOrganizationTenant :541` (documented "treating as not found"), `getPlatformAdmin :1739` (this ticket); `return undefined` at `decryptPiiCol :109`, `decryptMfaSecret :186`; `return ''` at `decryptEmail :158`; void swallows at `seedDemoUsersInner :1658`, `reencryptMfaSecretIfLegacy :1708`, `reencryptPlatformAdminMfaSecretIfLegacy :1776`; rethrows at `getUserById :394`, `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash :430`, `getUserByIdPreAuth :496`, `getUserByEmail :578`, `getUserBySocialId :611`, `emailExists :638`.
* **NOT MEASURED:** the platform-admin branch was not driven at the gate (persona untouched); whether a platform-DB outage today produces a 401 on a genuine platform admin is inferred from the source, not observed. The "platform DB may not be configured" comment suggests the swallow is deliberate for single-DB deployments — the ruling has to say whether "not configured" and "configured but down" are the same case.

## Decision needed, then the build

1. **Ruling:** treat a platform-DB failure on the admin login path like KS-963 treats the five pre-auth callers (rethrow → 503, no token consumed, no write) — OR keep the swallow for the not-configured case and distinguish it from a connection/query failure (e.g. swallow only when `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` is unset; rethrow otherwise).
2. **Build (after the ruling):** the change at `:1739-1741` per the ruling + a cell in `ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` (or a sibling) driving `POST /api/auth/login` for a platform-admin email with the platform lookup rejecting → 503, and the not-configured case → unchanged behaviour if the ruling keeps it.

## Neighbours (archived, named for context)

* KS-737 (archived; platform-admin login skipped MFA when `mfaCode` was omitted — the same `auth.ts` admin branch, a different defect).
* KS-171 (archived; `platform_admins.mfa_secret` plaintext — the same `getPlatformAdmin` read, a different defect).
* KS-999 (open, High): `getUserById`'s decrypt path escapes the KS-253 classifier — the same class one function over; related to KS-963 already.

## Dedupe, before filing (s205, 2026-09-13)

Literal census over 1,120 KS issues (692 archived) and 911 comments — `getPlatformAdmin` → KS-171 (archived), KS-737 (archived), KS-963 (the gate's own READY comment) · `Platform admin lookup failed` 0 · `auth.ts:345` 0 · `InvalidCredentialsError` → KS-486, KS-622 (archived), KS-732, KS-737, KS-963 · `getUserByIdPreAuth` → KS-1013, KS-1052, KS-790, KS-796, KS-943, KS-963, KS-999. Every open hit's description read: none names the `getPlatformAdmin` swallow. Filed new.

## Provenance

Tier-1 gate on PR #970 at `ae274f7cb`, 2026-09-13: §9 F-6 (named, not raised against #970; outside KS-963's include). Wednesday's ADDENDUM to s205, 2026-09-13 16:57 AEST: ONE Low ticket, related KS-963, dedupe by symbol first. Filed by s205 at the per-PR order's step 1, before KS-963's archive.

title: QUESTION: are `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts:44` SCAN_DIRS and `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:150` SCAN_ROOTS (both `['services', 'packages']`) the INTENDED scopes now that ks879 walks the whole Dev tree?
description:
## BLUF

A scope question, not a defect and not a merge blocker — filed from the #978 (KS-885 + KS-886) tier-2 gate's class hunt (R2) so it has a home. KS-886 widened the ks879 control-byte guard from `services/` + `packages/` to the whole Dev tree because the class had lived twice under `tests/` (KS-847, KS-879). Two sibling guards in the same directory still walk `['services', 'packages']` only, and each SAYS so — the gate read both as scoped claims with no over-claim. The question is whether those scopes are what we INTEND, given what ks879 just learned. Measured by the builder; ruled by Wednesday on the measurement. KS-573 (Peter's: "a corpus inherits the blind spot of whatever found its members") is the nearest neighbour on the board and is named here, not related.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks885-886-978-13b767a7f-tier2-r1/report.md` — Records R2. Line numbers at `13b767a7f` = develop after the squash (M14).

## The two sites (read at the head)

1. `packages/shared/src/__tests__/crypto-agility.guard.test.ts:44` — `const SCAN_DIRS = ['services', 'packages'];` — its docblock `:5-6` says "introduced in an `algorithm(s):` position anywhere under services/ or packages/ — outside the one place algorithm identifiers are allowed to live"; its cells say "outside the crypto registry" / "found a non-trivial number of source files". **Claim = walk; no over-claim.** Question: is a hard-coded algorithm identifier under `frontend/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` or `Testing/` out of scope by design (the registry is server-side), or a blind spot?
2. `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:150` — `const SCAN_ROOTS = ['services', 'packages'];` — `:149` `/** Trees that hold first-party runtime source. Walked recursively, in full. */`; the titles name "every service entrypoint", never "repo-wide" / "anywhere in the tree"; its CORPUS section states what it does not cover. **Scoped claim; no over-claim.** Question: do `frontend/` (three React apps with their own `app.listen`-free entrypoints) or `tests/` "hold first-party runtime source" in the sense the guard means, or is the class (an error handler mounted before the routes it must catch) definitionally an Express-service concern?

## What a ruling should say

For each site: (a) scope INTENDED — add one sentence to the docblock naming the excluded trees and why; or (b) widen — the builder measures the walk cost and the red set on the wider tree first (ks879's widening cost ≈0.8 s per walk and found 0 offenders), then files the change as its own test pass. Either answer closes this ticket.

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over 1,125 KS issues + 914 comments (includeArchived): `SCAN_DIRS` → 0; `SCAN_ROOTS` → 0; `crypto-agility.guard` → 0; `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard` → 7 hits, none about its roots (KS-573 Peter's corpus claim — the neighbour named above; KS-764 a flake mention; KS-876 a listen site; KS-818/832/833 archived residues; KS-830 canceled). No home; filed new.

title: The push preflight has no `services/auth` unit-suite leg — 14 `step` legs, 0 hits for services/auth or vitest; a merge that reddens auth's vitest passes the preflight (the F-973-1 class)
description:

A gap, not a fix: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (blob `acfb7fa3e` at develop M15 `1c38077ba`, 521 lines) runs 14 `step` legs and none of them runs a service's unit suite — `services/auth` 0 hits, `vitest` 0 hits, `services/originate` 0 hits (controls: `step` 20 hits). So a commit that turns `services/auth`'s vitest red still prints `PREFLIGHT PASSED.` and pushes. The tier-1 gate on PR #973 (KS-950 / KS-962) found the auth suite's red-first pair (`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:344` and `:382`, 2 failed of 30 against M6's `startup-migrations.ts`) by running the suite itself; nothing in the push path would have. Same class as KS-1051 (develop RED on the originate jest suite and nothing catches it) and KS-1046 (the verdict has no skip accounting); this ticket names the auth instance and the cross-service-reader shape that makes it bite. Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks950-962-973-ca2a9109c-tier1-r2/report.md` — §2 F-973-1 (the red-first pair), §11 the cross-service reader class ("the preflight … 14 `step` legs, 0 hits for `services/auth` … has no auth-vitest leg"), CLOSING 6.

## The shape that makes it bite

A change to the gateway file alone can red the auth suite — a red no per-service run of "the touched service's tests" sees, and no preflight leg runs either.
* The preflight's 14 legs at M15 (`:99` … `:423`): spec drift, lockfile clean-room, spec-auth conformance, path resolvability, audit-contract suites, npm-audit gate, standalone-lock advisories, served-spec consistency, no tracked credentials, script modes, pinned actions, shell suites reached, runtime stage re-link, shell suites run. Decide whether a service unit-suite leg belongs in the preflight (auth first, since it is the service whose suite reads across services), or whether the merge gate stays the only instrument — and say which in the KS-1046 / KS-1051 write-up. Not a fix to build blind: the preflight already runs minutes per push (KS-1135, KS-1127 are its runner-level neighbours).

By symbol over the KS board, title + description, includeArchived (s211 ITEM 0 (g)): `auth vitest` 0 · `auth-vitest` 0 · `preflight leg` 24 · `preflight.sh` 21 · `step(` 2 (KS-813 — "PREFLIGHT PASSED is unconditional, step() only prints a banner", a neighbour; KS-525 — Playwright's test.step) · `services/auth` 112 (a page; none by title a preflight-leg ticket). Of the 45 preflight hits none names `services/auth` together with `vitest`; KS-1051 is the nearest neighbour (a service suite with no gate), KS-1046 the class parent, KS-813 the verdict-side neighbour.
