nodes.body:
## BLUF
Record from the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1010 (KS-1183, merged as `1125607e9`), for whoever designs this ticket's fix. After a lost 201, the gateway answers **502 with the pending document kept while originate's copy exists**. A caller retry answers **400 "Workflow already completed"**, so a retry makes **no duplicate**. **Any re-forward path this ticket adds must send a `documentUuid`, or it will mint a second document.** No state change here.

## Recommendation
If the fix is "re-forward an approved instance whose pending document still exists", make the forward idempotent. Send a stable `documentUuid` (for example the pending document id), so that originate's KS-596 idempotency answers 200 with the existing row instead of creating another.

## Detail
Measured by the gate (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1183-1010-c3213b04e-tier1-r1/report.md`, section 5, Record R1), at the head and on the merged tree:
- `O-late-201-persist-then-lost+retry`: 502 at 804 ms, pending document KEPT, originate created 1, instance `approved`. The caller's retry answered 400 "Workflow already completed", and originate hits stayed at 1.
- Base: 200 + delete at 1,503 ms. No residual, but no bound either.
- Worse than the base only in one band. If originate takes 15–30 s, the base answered a truthful late 200, while the head now answers 502 though originate's copy exists. If originate is slower than the proxy (over 30 s in production), the base already answered nginx 504 plus a later delete, so the head is not worse. Any bound under the proxy's forces that trade.

Read at source by the gate (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:616-648`): originate is idempotent only on a caller-supplied `documentUuid` (KS-596: same hash → 200 with the existing document; a different hash → 409). The gateway's forward payload in `routes/verification.ts` is `{ title, documentType, description, contentHash, data }` and carries **no** `documentUuid`.

Nothing deployed.

title: Audit log (KS-871 gate R-3/R-5): H29 attemptedEmail is never written for proxied logins; production rows are v1.* on base and #1011 round 2 changes them
description:
## BLUF

Two pre-existing audit-log gaps, recorded by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1011 (KS-871) round 1 as R-3 and R-5. Both were re-read against #1011's round-2 head `6dc8256448b50de6a15519001a4f7032ace1ae19`. Neither is built.

* **R-3: H29** `attemptedEmail` **is never written for a login through the gateway.**
  * The audit middleware reads the email from `req.body`. The gateway does not parse bodies on `/api/auth` (a proxied prefix), so the field is absent from every login audit row, on base and on round-1 head, in test and in production mode.
  * #1011 round 2 does not change this (READ).
  * The other half of R-3: on base, a login refused 429 by the login rate limiter is audited as `unknown.create` with path `/`. The gate MEASURED its D3 shape writing `auth.login` / `/api/auth/login` instead. Round 2 uses that shape, so this half moves if #1011 merges (not measured at `6dc825644` itself).
* **R-5: in production mode the audit trail on base already spells mounted and proxied routes** `v1.*`**.**
  * In production mode (`NODE_ENV=production`) the gateway answers the measured `/api/...` writes with a 307 to their `/api/v1/...` spelling. So `v1.login` / `/api/v1/auth/login` is written where a canonical row would be `auth.login` / `/api/auth/login`.
  * **#1011 round 2 changes these rows.** It captures the canonical path at entry, which is the gate's D3 shape, and the gate measured D3 turning those production rows canonical.
  * If #1011 merges, production audit rows change spelling. Anything reading `v1.*` action names would see the change.

## Recommendation

Not built; Backlog. Two things for the owner, neither a fix decided here:

1. **R-3 (H29):** decide whether the attempted-email capture should work at all for proxied logins, and where the email should come from. Today the code expects a parsed body that the gateway deliberately does not parse on `/api/auth`.
2. **R-5:** before or when #1011 merges, check whether anything outside the repo reads audit `action` values. The gate did not test this (its NOT TESTED item 6: "the blast radius of `v1.*` actions is argued, not measured"). Candidates are the security service's audit reader, dashboards and any SIEM export. If nothing depends on `v1.*`, R-5 needs no work.

## Detail

**Source:** gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/report.md` (section Records, R-3 and R-5). The census covered 1115 requests over 119 audited routes on the real app with an in-memory sink, in test and production modes. The D3 comparison is `evidence/compare_production_base_d3.out`.

### R-3: H29 `attemptedEmail`

* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts` at round-2 head `6dc825644` (unchanged from develop `e0f41a8fa` on these lines):
  * `:287-291` sets `attemptedEmail` only when `req.path === '/api/auth/login' && req.body && typeof req.body === 'object'`.
* `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` at develop `e0f41a8fa`:
  * `:400-404` `proxyPaths` includes `'/api/auth'`;
  * `:413` `shouldParseBody` returns false for those prefixes;
  * `:416` the JSON body parser runs only when `shouldParseBody` is true.
  * So `req.body` is never populated for a proxied login.
* **Measured by the gate:** `details.attemptedEmail` absent on 7 + 3 login rows, for every login spelling, on every tree, in both modes.
* **Unchanged by round 2 (READ):** round 2's `audit.ts` diff touches `deriveAction`'s path source and `details.path` only. The two other finish-time `req.path` reads, the login user-id extraction (`:261`) and the warning-log path (`:333`), are also untouched.
* **The 429 half.** Production mode, same client IP, requests 5 to 7 answered 429 by the login rate limiter:

| Tree | Audit row for a 429 login |
| -- | -- |
| Base | `unknown.create`, resource type `unknown`, path `/`, success false |
| Round-1 head | `auth.login` (test mode) / `v1.login` (production mode) |
| Gate's D3 shape | `auth.login`, resource type `session`, path `/api/auth/login`, success false |

### R-5: the production trail is `v1.*` on base

* **Gate record:** in production mode, 441 base rows equal round-1 head rows and differ from D3, for proxied and mounted admitted routes (`v1.login`, `v1.upload`, `v1.erasures` and so on).
* Example from `compare_production_base_d3.out`, a proxied login answered 200:
  * base: `v1.login`, resource type `v1`, path `/api/v1/auth/login`
  * D3: `auth.login`, resource type `session`, path `/api/auth/login`
* **Re-read against round 2:** `audit.ts` at `6dc825644` vs its merge-base `1125607e9`:
  * `:224` `const auditPath = req.path;` is captured when the middleware runs. It is mounted at the app root after the `/api/v1` strip (`index.ts:570`).
  * That value feeds `deriveAction(req, auditPath)` (`:244`) and `details.path` (`:294`).
  * These are the same two uses as the gate's D3 counterfactual edit (`evidence/d3_apply.py`). So R-5's "a canonical-path fix changes production rows too" now describes #1011 round 2 itself.
  * MEASURED on D3; READ-equivalent for round 2; NOT measured at `6dc825644` (its round-2 gate was being drafted when this was filed).
* develop `e0f41a8fa`'s `audit.ts` is byte-identical to `1125607e9`'s (`git diff --quiet` rc 0), so "base" above is current develop.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches in title, description or comments:

* `attemptedEmail`: 1 fuzzy, 1 literal (KS-871, in comments).
* `H29`: 1 fuzzy, 1 literal (KS-871, in comments).
* `middleware/audit.ts`: 101 fuzzy, 3 literal (KS-871; KS-661 and KS-28, both archived and unrelated).
* `v1.`: 105 fuzzy, 35 literal. None is about audit action names; the nearest is KS-1177, a different v1 verify-route defect.

None covers R-3 or R-5. Related: KS-871.

nodes.body:
## Update from the KS-1457 work (PR #1481) and its Sonnet-tier gate, 2026-10-12

* **The cause stated here is confirmed, re-read at develop `d38302a9a27e`:** `index.ts:385` lists `/api/auth` in `proxyPaths` and `index.ts:399-402` skips the gateway's body parsing for it, so `req.body` is undefined when the audit row is written at `'finish'`. `details.attemptedEmail` is never written for `/api/auth/login` in production, throttled or not. The gate's production-shaped harness (same gating, the real login limiter) confirmed it on head and base.
* **R-3's "other half" and the two other finish-time `req.path` reads:** KS-871 (#1011) fixed the row's path and the 429 row's shape. PR #1481 (KS-1457) fixes the remaining finish-time reads (the login user-id lift and the write-failed warning's path, plus the email read) by using the path captured at entry. Of those, only the warning's path was live in production; the email read and the user-id lift are latent while the body is unparsed and the proxy streams the response. PR #1481's cell B4 passes only because its test parses bodies globally.
* **New, from the gate:** if someone enables parsing for `/api/auth/login` to make this field work, `audit.ts:290-292` stores the lower-cased email with **no length cap**, so each throttled attempt could store an unvalidated string up to the body limit (1 MB), and the only cap on audit rows is the global limiter (300 per minute per IP). **Cap the length when it is turned on.**
* **Follow-ups for KS-1457's tests (its head cannot change):** reword the header comment at `ks1457-audit-finish-reads-use-the-entry-path.test.ts:15-17` and cell B4, and make B4 mirror the `proxyPaths` gating, so they state what is live.
* I filed this as a new ticket (KS-1488) before noticing this one; KS-1488 is closed as a duplicate of KS-1189.

## BLUF
PR #1011 (KS-871) merged as `523f283c6cd2550263ec9869dc5ee722be40df4e`, and its round-2 QA gate measured both halves of this ticket:
- **R-5 is CLOSED by that merge.** Production audit rows for mounted and proxied routes are now written canonically (e.g. `auth.login` / `/api/auth/login`, not `v1.login` / `/api/v1/auth/login`). The census over the real app measured 574 production rows changed, all toward canonical, 0 regressions.
- **R-3 has MOVED, not closed.** The login rate limiter's 429 row is now `auth.login` in both test and production mode. The **H29 `attemptedEmail` is still never written** for a login through the gateway.

## Recommendation
This ticket's remaining scope is H29 alone, plus the unmeasured consumer check below. Not built.
1. **H29:** decide whether attempted-email capture should work for proxied logins at all, and where the email should come from. The gateway deliberately does not parse bodies on `/api/auth`.
2. **Consumers:** check whether anything outside the repo groups audit rows by `action` (the security service's reader, dashboards, a SIEM export). The rename from `v1.*` has already shipped to develop.

## Detail
- Gate report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-6dc825644-tier1-r2/report.md` (Round-1 carry-forward, census, Merge-seat ADDENDUM).
- **R-3 (login 429):** base wrote `unknown.create` at `/`; the merged code writes `auth.login` at `/api/auth/login`, in both modes. H29: `middleware/audit.ts` still sets `attemptedEmail` only from a parsed `req.body`, which `index.ts`'s `shouldParseBody` skips for `/api/auth`. The merge did not touch either line.
- **R-5 (production `v1.*`):**
  - base → merged tree in production mode: 574 of 1115 census rows changed, every one toward canonical.
  - Canonical rows went from 527 / 1101 to 1101 / 1101.
  - Routes whose row is the same whatever the request spelling went from 109 to 119 of 119.
  - Response status sequences are identical.
- The out-of-repo blast radius of the action rename is NOT TESTED by the gate.

title: api-gateway meetsVerificationLevel fails open on an unknown REQUIRED level: an off-canonical document-type level admits every authenticated caller
description:
## BLUF

The api-gateway's `meetsVerificationLevel` fails OPEN when a document type's *required* level is a string outside the known order. `indexOf` returns -1 for the requirement, and every user index is `>= -1`, so any authenticated caller passes: every human level, and a connector key.

* An anonymous caller is still refused (`enforceDocumentTypeRules` answers 401 for any non-`none` level with no user).
* So a document type stored with an off-canonical level, e.g. `standrd`, admits every authenticated principal to create it (`POST /api/documents`) and to verify it (`POST /api/documents/:id/verify`).
* This is a READ-only chain. Nothing has been measured against a stored catalogue.

## Recommendation

Not built; Backlog. **Do not make it fail closed yet.** Two measurements come first; without them, a fail-closed fix could lock out every document type whose stored level string is off-canonical:

1. **The level strings actually stored in the catalogue:** `document_type_configs` in each tenant DB, and the gateway's Redis document types. Any value outside `none, basic, social, standard, enhanced, high, government` (after lowercasing) is exposed today.
2. **Who can create or edit a document type:** the auth guards on originate's admin-config router and on the gateway's template clone. That sets how reachable an off-canonical value is.

KS-1176 (the connector-key fix) deliberately leaves this behaviour unchanged, and its PR carries a cell that pins it as it is at base, so the fix cannot move it silently.

## Detail

**The comparison** (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts` at develop `e0f41a8fafd64fa31524390cfeab320e822f3d15`):

* `:39-47` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`.
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` returns `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`, both lowercased. An unknown requirement makes `reqIdx` -1, so the result is true for every user index, including -1.
* **Creation:** `:143-151` compares `creatorVerificationLevel`. With no user, `:136-141` refuses any non-`none` string with 401, so anonymous callers are not affected.
* **Verification:** `routes/verification.ts:554-557` compares `verifierVerificationLevel` when it is not `none`, with the same -1 semantics.

**Where the level strings come from (READ):**

* originate `routes/adminConfig.ts:156-172`: `POST /document-types` checks only `name` and `code`, then inserts `creatorVerificationLevel` (default `basic`) and the other three levels as given. No level validation was found.
* api-gateway `routes/platform.ts:880-894`: the template clone inserts `creator_verification_level` / `verifier_verification_level` from `platform_document_type_templates` rows as stored. Validation was not traced.
* The gateway's Redis catalogue has a writer at `services/redis.ts:511` (`setDocumentType`). **Untraced: how the Redis catalogue is filled from those database rows**, and so whether an off-canonical DB value reaches the gateway's comparison unchanged.

**Found by** the KS-1176 census (seat A, 2026-09-17). Wednesday's ANSWER at 19:52:15Z ruled it a separate ticket, not built, with the KS-1176 fix leaving it unchanged.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches in title, description or comments:

* `meetsVerificationLevel`: 2 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-1176, PS-519).
* `creatorVerificationLevel`: 3 fuzzy, 3 literal (KS-1176, PS-519, KS-364 archived).
* `reqIdx`: 0 fuzzy, 0 literal.
* `document-types`: 121 fuzzy, 13 literal (KS-1176, PS-519, and archived catalogue, Akto and conformance tickets: KS-388, KS-397, KS-364, KS-40, KS-510, KS-357, KS-118, KS-39, KS-37, KS-465, KS-144).

None is about an unknown required level. Related: KS-1176.

title: Audit log records the caller's spelling: case splits the action namespace, /API/ is unaudited, unrouted 404s put caller text in action (KS-871 gate R-4)
description:
## BLUF

The api-gateway audit log writes `action` and `details.path` from the request's own spelling of the path. It never folds case, and never normalises spelling variants of a route. So the same logical route can appear under several action names, some requests are not audited at all, and caller-chosen text reaches the `action` column. This is pre-existing: it is identical on base and on the merged KS-871 fix. It was recorded as R-4 by both QA gate rounds on PR #1011 (KS-871, merged `523f283c6cd2550263ec9869dc5ee722be40df4e`), which widened it in round 2.

Measured on the real app in test and production mode:

* **Case splits the action namespace:**
  * `POST /api/GDPR/erasures` (refused 403) → `GDPR.create`.
  * `POST /api/LOGS` (204) → `LOGS.create`.
  * `POST /api/gdpr/ERASURES` → `gdpr.create`, but `details.path` keeps `/api/gdpr/ERASURES`.
* **An upper-case** `/API/` **prefix is not audited at all:** `POST /API/logs` (204) and `POST /API/GDPR/ERASURES` (403) write no row. The middleware's `/api/` prefix check is case-sensitive.
* **Unrouted 404s put caller text into** `action`**,** identically on base and head:
  * `qa-attacker-chosen.create`, `%6cogs.create`, `logs;x=1.create`, `..create`;
  * `V1.create` and `v1.create` (`/api/v1/v1/logs`, a bare `/api/v1`);
  * `unknown.create` at `/api/` (`/api/v1/`).

## Recommendation

Not built; Backlog. This is a design decision for the audit trail's owner, not a one-line fix. Two choices:

1. **Normalisation:** should the audited path be case-folded, and should dot-segment, `;param` and percent-encoded spellings be normalised before `deriveAction`? Or should the raw spelling be kept in `details.path` and only the `action` be normalised?
2. **Unrouted requests:** should a 404 write a fixed action (e.g. `unrouted.create`) rather than one built from caller text?

Before deciding, check which spellings the edge (nginx / Caddy / Container Apps) actually forwards. The gates marked that NOT TESTED, and it sets how reachable each row above is in a deployment.

## Detail

**Source:**

* Round-2 gate report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-6dc825644-tier1-r2/report.md` (carry-forward table, Item 2, Item 3 (ii), Merge-seat ADDENDUM R-4).
* Round-1 report: `…/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/report.md` (Records, R-4).

**Code at develop** `523f283c6` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts`):

* the middleware returns early unless `req.path.startsWith('/api/')`;
* `deriveAction(req, path)` splits `path` on `/` and builds `<segment>.<verb>` with no case folding.

**Not in this ticket:** the gate also measured routed spelling variants (dot-segment, `;param`, percent-encoded) that keep the caller's text in `details.path` / `action`. Those examples are not reproduced here; Wednesday holds them.

**Not tested by either gate:**

* request-target rewriting at the edge;
* out-of-repo consumers that group rows by `action`.

### Dedupe before filing

Searched with the board's `searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), keeping only literal, case-insensitive matches:

* `GDPR.create`: 92 fuzzy, 1 literal (KS-871 comments).
* `LOGS.create`: 116 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-5 archived, unrelated; KS-871 comments).
* `unaudited`: 8 fuzzy, 4 literal (KS-903, PS-726, PS-536, KS-229; none about the gateway audit middleware).
* `case-split`: 125 fuzzy, 0 literal.
* `deriveAction`: 2 fuzzy, 2 literal (KS-871; KS-1189, which carries R-3 and R-5 but not R-4).

Related: KS-871, KS-1189.

## BLUF
For the audit trail's owner: the case-sensitivity half of this ticket is now the only part of the gateway's path-spelling class that is **deliberately left unfixed**, and it is yours to decide. PR #1466 (KS-1461) folds the other gateway checks and leaves `middleware/audit.ts` alone on purpose. Nothing was built here.

## What changed since this was filed
- `middleware/pathFold.ts` (`foldAsciiCase`, ASCII only) is on develop (KS-801, squash `672352369b8a`). If you decide the audit prefix test should ignore case, `audit.ts:210-212` can use it as the other gateway checks now do; the open design question stays as written above (whether `action` should be normalised, and what an unrouted 404 should write).
- Routing stays case insensitive on purpose. Making it case sensitive instead turned a `403` into a `200` on a scope-gated route (measured on KS-801), so please do not take that route to make `/API/...` consistent.

## One fact toward your edge check
This ticket asks which spellings the edge forwards. Measured on Kintsugi on 2026-10-12 (a `POST` with a `text/plain` body, no credentials): `/api/oauth/apps` reaches the gateway (`415`), while `/API/oauth/apps`, `/Api/oauth/apps` and `/API/documents` get a static `405 Not Allowed` page from nginx before the gateway. A lowercase `/api` prefix with a cased tail was not probed live. So on Kintsugi the unaudited `/API/` write you describe is not reachable through the edge; it is reachable wherever the gateway is exposed without a case-sensitive edge.

## Also related, filed separately
KS-1457 (three finish-time reads in `audit.ts` still use `req.path` rather than `auditPath`; one-line fixes, Backlog).

title: anchor_store's (document_id, network) unique is declared only by migration 031 and anchoring's fresh-DB path; 9 other schema sources omit it (#1016 gate R-1016-5)
description:
## BLUF

**Pre-existing; reported, NOT reconciled.** Ten places create `anchor_store`. Only migration 031, which replaced 007's `(document_id)` unique, and anchoring's own fresh-database path declare the `(document_id, network)` unique. The other **nine** `CREATE TABLE` sources carry none. Anchoring's `ensureTables` returns early when the table already exists, so on a database built from one of those nine sources the unique exists only if migrations 007/031 ran. Both upserts depend on it: `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)` in anchoring and in originate. Which source a deployed database is built from was NOT determined.

## Recommendation

Not built. The owner decides **which schema source is authoritative** for `anchor_store`, then reconciles the others to it or retires them. Until then, the one-row-per-`(document_id, network)` assumption holds only where migration 031 ran. The KS-1072 selector's tie reachability rests on that assumption.

## Detail

* **Source:** tier-1 QA gate on PR #1016 (KS-1072), Record R-1016-5 and §12. Report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1072-1016-a226d94fe-tier1-r1/report.md`. The gate's evidence class is READ ONLY.
* **Re-read by Seat A at develop** `7e89318bcedbc9a35757d4298ace54a6a23020bd`**.** Instruments: `git grep -n -i 'CREATE TABLE.*anchor_store'` gave 10 hits; `git grep -n -i 'document_id, *network'` located the unique.
  * **No unique (9):**
    * `docker/init/01-schema.sql:188`
    * `docker/init/03-service-tables.sql:89`
    * `docker/init/06-consolidate-anchors.sql:26`
    * `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:150`, `:733` and `:2045`
    * `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:704`
    * `migrations/003_consolidate-anchors.sql:16`
    * `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:316`
  * **Unique:**
    * `migrations/031_anchor_store_network_unique.sql:39-40`: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS anchor_store_document_network_uniq ON anchor_store (document_id, network)`.
    * anchoring `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:209`, the same index. It is reached only when `ensureTables` does not return early.
  * **The early return:** anchoring `index.ts:172-175` reads `to_regclass('public.anchor_store')` and `to_regclass('public.anchor_batches')`; when both exist it sets `tablesEnsured = true` and returns.
  * **The upserts:** anchoring `index.ts:1400` and originate `routes/anchors.ts:121`, both `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)`.
* **The gateway source also diverges** (gate R-1016-5, compare R-1005-1 recorded on KS-1073): `network TEXT DEFAULT 'preprod'`, with columns `id, document_id, content_hash, tx_hash, block_hash, slot, network, status, metadata, created_at, confirmed_at`.
* **Also READ by the gate:** originate defaults a row's network to `'preview'`, while anchoring writes `CARDANO_NETWORK || 'preprod'`. One database written by both could therefore hold two rows for one document.

### Dedupe before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive:

* `(document_id, network)`: 118 fuzzy / 2 literal. KS-281 and KS-705, both archived: the 031 decision and submission idempotency, not the source disagreement.
* `ensureTables`: 4 / 3. KS-110, KS-419 and KS-92, all archived: runtime DDL roles and boot order.
* `startup-migrations.ts`: 88 / 36. None is about `anchor_store`. The nearest class is KS-960 (two schema sources disagree on `users.email` uniqueness), a different table.
* `R-1005-1`: 117 / 1. KS-1073 comments: the gate record, not a ticket.
* `R-1016-5`: 117 / 1. KS-1072: Seat A's own facts comment, posted minutes before this ticket.

None covers this. Related: KS-1072, KS-960.

title: A verified token without a role or userId claim still 500s every proxied route (x-user-role / x-user-id set unguarded) — KS-744 residue
description:
## BLUF

A verified JWT that lacks the `role` or `userId` claim still makes every proxied route answer **500**, with the internal message `Invalid value "undefined" for header "x-user-role"` (or `"x-user-id"`). The upstream is never reached. The mechanism is KS-744's: the verified-JWT branch of `authenticateToken` copies the claim onto a forwarded header unguarded (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:388` `x-user-id`, `:390` `x-user-role`, the same line numbers at develop `d7e95cd9f` and at KS-744's local fix `6252f06ac`), and the proxy's outbound `setHeader` throws. KS-744 fixes only `email` and `verificationLevel`. Latent today: no signer mints a token without `userId` or `role` (READ in KS-744's brief).

## Recommendation

A shape decision first, not a copy of KS-744's guard. A token with no principal id or no role arguably should be refused **401** at the gateway rather than forwarded without `x-user-id` / `x-user-role`, because those headers are what the upstreams authorise on. Proposal: in the verified-JWT branch, answer 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` when `decoded.userId` or `decoded.role` is missing, before any header is set; cells for each claim on the KS-744 harness. Not built. Low: latent, but it leaks an internal error string (the KS-703 / KS-727 shape).

## Detail

* **Source:** the residue line of Wednesday's KS-744 brief (P3, measured by the brief writer at `d7e95cd9f`) and seat A's KS-744 build, 2026-09-17.
* **Re-measured by seat A** at the KS-744 head `6252f06ac7c913619888cb20e07cc5a0c846043d` (local, not pushed), 02:25Z, in-process. The harness is the KS-744 test's own: the real `authenticateToken(true)` and a real `http-proxy-middleware` proxy on a bare express app, in front of a recording upstream on loopback, with RS256 tokens carrying every claim except the one named:
  * no `role` → **500**, 0 upstream hits, `{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Invalid value \"undefined\" for header \"x-user-role\""}`;
  * no `userId` → **500**, 0 hits, the same for `x-user-id`;
  * control, no `email` (fixed by KS-744) → 200, 1 hit;
  * control, every claim → 200, 1 hit.
* **The 500 body** in that harness comes from its own error handler; the gateway's real error shape is quoted on KS-744.
* **Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-09-17_seatA-4th/tickets/ks744-residue/` (`rows.json`, `probe.out`, the probe file, run once and moved out of the worktree).
* **Not measured:** the real app's error handler for this case; running upstream services.

### Search before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches only: `x-user-role` 109 fuzzy / 4 literal (KS-1032, KS-741, KS-1041, KS-1091: trust-header reads and stripping, not a missing claim) · `x-user-id` 103 / 8 (KS-1087, KS-1032, KS-1084, KS-1041, KS-1083, KS-719, KS-736, KS-708: none about a missing claim) · `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE` 101 / 2 (KS-744, the parent; KS-742 by mention) · `Invalid value` 113 / 5 (KS-744; KS-465, KS-703, KS-386, KS-283 unrelated) · `decoded.role` 111 / 1 (KS-486, archived review). None covers it. Related: KS-744.

## BLUF
**Recorded for this ticket's shape decision:** a verified claim that IS present but is not a legal HTTP header value also 500s every http-proxy route. It is the same class as this ticket, a claim copied onto a proxy header. It is pre-existing, and it behaves identically before and after PR #1028 (KS-744, merged to develop as `0a2b1603f`). Found by #1028's tier-1 gate as finding N-1, which recommends folding it into this ticket rather than a new one.

## Recommendation
Decide this ticket's shape with N-1 in it. One structural guard for every claim-derived header would close both the missing-claim case here and N-1: either refuse 401, or reject or encode any value that is not a valid header string. A per-claim presence check closes only the missing case. No separate ticket is filed for N-1.

## Detail
- **Measured at runtime by the gate** on the real gateway app:
  - Inputs: an email claim containing U+0142, a verificationLevel containing U+0142, and a verificationLevel containing CR-LF.
  - Result for each: `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with the generic body and 0 upstream hits.
  - Where: optional `/api/credentials`, `/api/certifications` (with requireScope) and required `/api/documents`, in test, production and development mode.
  - Trees: identical on develop `19f1e5475`, the #1028 head `e39521cfb` and the merged tree. A Latin-1 `é` forwards.
- **After #1028,** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:393` and `:398` guard email and verificationLevel on presence only, so a present but illegal value still reaches the proxy's outbound `setHeader`. That is the same throw KS-744 fixed for a missing value.
- **Likelihood** (as read by the gate, not measured): auth validates email with zod `.email()` (ASCII-only) at register and login; `verificationLevel` is copied straight off the user row when the token is signed.

title: Bundled js-yaml copies ship in service runtime images and are invisible to audit-gate/audit-locks
description:
**BLUF:** two service runtime trees carry their own bundled copies of js-yaml code. Both audit gates (`audit-gate`, `audit-locks`) look for packages by name, so neither copy can ever be reported. The originate copy accepts the GHSA-2883 input shape, the same way vulnerable js-yaml 3.15.1 does. Whether any request path reaches either copy is **NOT traced**. **Severity: UNMEASURED.** It is not "High" until the first item below is measured.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1027 (finding F1, recorded as pre-existing and not moved by #1027). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1027-d7fc6cc55-tier2-r1/report.md`, "F1 detail".

## First item: a measurement, not a fix

1. **Runtime load trace in a built originate image.** Does anything load `confbox/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs` at start-up or on a request, and does `/shared`'s `@effect/platform` `httpApiSwagger` bundle load at all?
2. **Input reach.** Does any code path parse attacker-controlled YAML through either copy?

Only after both are measured: set a severity, and decide the fix shape (below).

## The gate's F1 paragraph, quoted

> * **Instrument, count-from-the-cause:** besides the package census (`*/node_modules/<name>/package.json`), every runtime tree was grepped for js-yaml's exception class `YAMLException` in `*.js/*.cjs/*.mjs`. Positive control (full installs): 8/9/8/8 files, including `node_modules/js-yaml/lib/*`. Runtime trees: governance 0, referral 0, vc-issuer 0, **originate 1** (`confbox/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs`), **/shared 2** (`@effect/platform/dist/{esm,cjs}/internal/httpApiSwagger.js`, a swagger-ui bundle with its own `YAMLException$1`). The package-name census reads NONE in the same trees. That is the blind spot: the drafter's D1 "none" is true of packages and false of code.
> * **Where they ship:** originate runner `:79 npm ci --omit=dev` keeps confbox (lock `node_modules/confbox` 0.2.4, `node_modules/c12` 3.3.4, `node_modules/@prisma/config` 7.8.0, none dev-flagged). Every service image `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared` (governance :74, originate :88, referral :89, vc-issuer :81), and shared-builder is a full `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, never pruned.
> * **Not moved by #1027:** develop vs head lock entries are identical for confbox, c12, @prisma/config and @effect/platform, and the `packages/shared` diff is empty (evidence/parse.out, and the census step in evidence/runtime.out).
> * **Vulnerable shape present?** Neither bundle contains `maxTotalMergeKeys` (count 0; js-yaml 3.15.2's loader.js has 7). The confbox chunk carries a "4.1.1" string once (version identity by string only, not proven). Bounded probe (evidence/loader_probe.out), shape derived from the 3.15.1→3.15.2 loader.js diff (evidence/dev_jsyaml.out):
>
> | input | js-yaml 3.15.1 | js-yaml 3.15.2 | confbox 0.2.4 bundled |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | CONTROL in-bounds, 5 empty merges (45 B) | accepted `{x:1}` | accepted `{x:1}` | accepted `{x:1}` |
> | 1 key × 150 empty merges (625 B) | accepted | **THREW abnormal merge sequence size** | accepted |
> | 200 keys × 100 empty merges (82 KB) | accepted 4.6 ms | **THREW exceeded maxTotalMergeKeys (10000)** | accepted 5.3 ms |
> | 4000 keys × 100 (1.65 MB) | accepted 31.6 ms | **THREW** 1.3 ms | accepted 37.8 ms |
>
> Cost was linear and bounded within these sizes. No super-linear amplification was demonstrated.
>
> * **Reachability (assumed, not traced):** 0 tracked files under `Blockchain/Dev/services` or `packages` import confbox, c12 or @prisma/config, 0 import `@effect/platform`, and 0 mention `HttpApiSwagger` (control: `from 'express'` in 250 files). No `prisma.config*` is tracked. Plausibly unreachable from request handling. A runtime load trace in a running image was NOT done (no image, by bounds).
> * **Fix-shape (for the owner, prose only):** decide whether bundled-copy advisories are in the audit gates' contract. If yes, add a code-signature leg (e.g. a `YAMLException`/version-banner census over each image's runtime tree), with a positive control on a full install. If no, state the exclusion in the gate's OK line. Regression test the owner could add: a fixture runtime tree carrying a bundled copy must be reported, or explicitly named as out of scope.

## In short

* **originate runtime:** `confbox@0.2.4/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs`, on a prod chain (`c12` ← `@prisma/config`). Probed: it accepts the GHSA-2883 shape as js-yaml 3.15.1 does.
* `/shared` **in every service image:** the `@effect/platform@0.71.7` `httpApiSwagger` bundle carries its own js-yaml copy. **Not probed.**
* **0 tracked source importers** of confbox, c12, @prisma/config or @effect/platform.
* **Runtime reachability: NOT traced.**

## Board search before filing (2026-09-17, team Secuura-PK, archived issues included, literal match on title, description and comments)

* `confbox`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `@effect/platform`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `YAMLException`: 4 issues (KS-1117, KS-1109, KS-1108, KS-1099) and 1 comment thread (KS-1099). All four are about k6 and Akto config-loader error handling, not bundled copies.
* `GHSA-2883`: KS-1211 only, plus comments on KS-1024 and KS-1211 (the audit-baseline row).
* Control: `js-yaml` hits 13 issues, so the search can match. 1205 issues and 3440 comments were scanned.

title: POST /api/documents/upload never reaches the gateway's blocked-extension / MIME screen (proxy.ts:551-620): 415 with a multipart body, 405 without
description:
## BLUF

**The gateway's upload screen never runs.** `POST /api/documents/upload` has a hand-forward branch in the gateway (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:551-620`) that refuses blocked file extensions (`BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS`, `:134`) and blocked MIME types before forwarding to originate. On the real app no request reaches it: a multipart request with a body is answered `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` by `middleware/contentType.ts`, and an empty multipart request `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`. Pre-existing. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1028 (KS-744) as finding N-2. **Severity is unmeasured**, and so is the priority set here: whether uploads reach originate by another path was not measured.

## Recommendation

The owners decide what the route should be:

* if gateway-side upload screening is meant to exist, make the route reachable (the JSON-only content-type rule would need a narrow, exact-path exception for multipart, like the KS-791 one for `application/octet-stream`), with a cell proving a blocked extension is refused through the real app;
* if uploads are meant to go some other way, remove or document the dead branch.
  First measure whether and how uploads reach originate today.

## Detail

* **Measured at runtime by the gate** on the real gateway app: 297 + 297 cells per tree (every token, every leg), 0 upstream hits, identical on develop `19f1e5475`, the PR head `e39521cfb` and the merged tree. Multipart with a body → 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`. Empty multipart → 405 `"Method POST not allowed for /api/documents/{id}."` (the spec method gate).

title: Under multi-tenancy, auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC: with fail-closed RLS every approve's level UPDATE matches 0 rows
description:
## BLUF

**With** `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` **on, auth's** `db.ts` **sends every statement that carries a tenant argument through** `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query()`**: a raw pool query with no tenant GUC.** Under fail-closed RLS, a tenant-scoped UPDATE then matches 0 rows.

* On the verification approve, develop answers a false **200 APPROVED while the level stays basic**. #1032's head instead refuses every approve (503, PENDING).
* **Major while that configuration runs; latent today.** The auth container in `services.bicep` does not set `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (read).
* **Evidence class:** MEASURED on the real `db.ts` and `TenantPoolManager` with `pg` faked and RLS MODELLED. Whether the runtime database role enforces RLS on that pool is unverified (no Postgres was run).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (E-1, an escalation candidate).

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here.

* Route the tenant-pool branch through the GUC path (`queryWithTenantGuc`, with the GUC in the same transaction), or drop the tenant-pool branch while per-tenant databases are off.
* **Resolve the overlap first.** KS-174 (In Progress) step 1 plans this remedy: "Tenant-pool-manager (or a query wrapper) sets `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction". It never names `tenantManager`, `getPool` or auth's `db.ts`. KS-458 (Done) bundled the GUC for the default pool only. If KS-174 is the live home, merge this ticket into it; this one carries the measured location and consequence.
* **Census every** `query(…, tenantId)` **caller** before fixing. The gate's single-line grep found one, which is not a count.
* **Regression cell:** with multi-tenancy on and fail-closed RLS, an approve whose UPDATE carries the tenant either raises the level or is refused. Never a 200 over an unchanged level.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**,** `services/auth/src/db.ts:47-70`**:**
  * `query(text, params, tenantId)`: `if (tenantId && tenantManager)` returns `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query(text, params)` (`:53-60`). No GUC. The `try` does not `await`, so a rejected query is not caught by its fallback.
  * Only without a tenant manager does it use `runWithTenantId(tenantId, () => queryWithTenantGuc(getPool(), …))` (the KS-458 path).
* **When the branch is taken** (the gate's read): `initTenantManager` needs `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED === 'true'` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`. `TenantPoolManager.getPool` returns the default pool unless `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'` and the tenant resolves to another database.
* **The gate's pool table** (approve, RLS modelled on):
  * manager on, no per-tenant DB: the UPDATE runs on the default pool with no GUC and matches 0 rows. Develop answers 200 APPROVED with the level basic (a false success). Head answers 503 PENDING basic, even with no fault.
  * a distinct tenant DB: the level UPDATE lands in the tenant database while the request row stays in the default database (a pre-existing split).
* **Callers read so far:** `getUserById(id, tenantId)` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:407`) and `updateUser`'s UPDATE (`:796`). The census is not done.
* **Config** (READ; unverifiable without `az`, not run):
  * the auth container in `services.bicep` has no `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (the only bicep hit, `:798`, is originate's);
  * `env.dev.json` / `env.demo.json` set it `true` in a shared block (whether [deploy.sh](<http://deploy.sh>) consumes it was not re-read);
  * `docker-compose.yml` auth uses `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}`;
  * `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is set nowhere in deployment or compose.
* **Related:** KS-1194 (where it was measured), KS-174, KS-458, KS-1055 (per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations).
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `tenantManager.getPool`: 0 of 3 scanned.
  * `getPool`: 1, KS-213 (originate's per-tenant pool fan-out through pgbouncer; a different defect).
  * `applyTenantGuc`: 0, but the search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`: 12, and `tenant GUC`: 19. The closest are KS-174 (above), KS-458, KS-468 (GUC not seeded on gateway proxy routes) and KS-1055. None names the tenant-pool branch in auth's `db.ts`.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §7 and E-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: T-1: authenticateToken is an async express-4 middleware with no catch — a throw after the await can kill the process
description:
`authenticateToken` in the api-gateway is an **async express-4 middleware with no catch**. Express 4 does not await a middleware's returned promise, so any future throw after the `await` becomes an **unhandled rejection**.

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

**Not request-reachable today** — the gate could not reach it, and it is identical at develop. Graded **Major *if* reached**.

The consequence depends on a setting most deployments do not set:

* `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE` **unset =** `exit`**, the default** → the process **exits 0**, and later requests get `ECONNREFUSED`;
* under `survive` → only that one request hangs.

`survive` **is set in only two places:** `docker-compose.yml:441` and `deployment/azure/services.bicep:617`. `deploy/docker-swarm/docker-stack.yml` **and any bare** `node dist/index.js` **run in** `exit` **mode** — so the harshest behaviour is what an unconfigured deployment gets.

## What to do

Wrap the await, or adopt an async-middleware wrapper that forwards rejections to `next`. Worth doing for the whole gateway, not just this one middleware.

---

title: KS-1101 follow-up: the out-of-repo consumers of the gateway health endpoints are unmeasured
description:
#1037 changed what the gateway health aggregates **say**. A degraded service now reads `degraded` in `/health/deep`, `/system/status`, `/api/system/status`, the `/status/simple` body and `/api/system/health/dashboard`, where before it read `up`. HTTP statuses and readiness are unchanged.

**Any consumer outside this repository** (monitoring, alerting, uptime checks, dashboards, anything parsing those bodies) may now see a value it has never seen before. **None of them was measured.**

## What to do

Inventory who reads these endpoints outside the repo, and check each one handles `degraded`.

title: N-2: a 2xx whose body is not exactly top-level 'degraded' — including 200 {status:'unhealthy'} — still reads up
description:
#1037 reads a 2xx body as degraded only when it is **exactly** top-level `"degraded"`. Any other 2xx body **still reads up**, including **200** `{status:'unhealthy'}`.

Pre-existing: develop already read it as up, and #1037 neither introduced it nor fixed it. It's a real correctness gap, though. A service reporting itself unhealthy on a 200 is shown as healthy.

## What to do

Decide the vocabulary the aggregates accept (`ok`/`up`/`healthy`, `degraded`, `unhealthy`/`down`), and treat an unrecognised or unhealthy body on a 2xx as at least degraded rather than up.

title: api-gateway vitest suite is not isolation-safe: --no-isolate reds 10 of 30 runs non-deterministically at develop
description:
**From the #1040 / KS-1125 batch gate, finding N40-1: Minor, pre-existing (measured AT DEVELOP).**

## What's wrong

The api-gateway suite passes only because vitest isolates each file. With `--no-isolate`, it reds **10 of 30 runs, non-deterministically**, at develop, before any of the batch's PRs. Files leak module state, `process.env` changes and globals into each other. KS-1125's new file adds to the pattern (N40-2: unrestored `process.env` deletes and a global it never removes), though isolation contains it.

## Why it matters

A suite that needs isolation to pass hides order-dependent bugs, and switching to a faster pool or a shared worker would turn them into flaky reds.

## What to do

Run the suite with `--no-isolate` repeatedly and bisect the leaking files. Restore env and globals in each file's `afterAll`, and add a CI-equivalent local check that runs the suite un-isolated.

---
