title: POST /api/certifications/:id/verify forwards a revoked session's Bearer to originate: the gateway's session check never runs on this route
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (api-gateway `routes/verification.ts:784`, mounted with no `authenticateToken`) forwards whatever `Authorization` the caller sent to originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:788`). Measured in-process: a **REVOKED** session's JWT, alone or beside a valid connector key, reaches originate as that user's Bearer, because the gateway's session check never runs on this route. On `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`:488`, `authenticateToken(true)`) the same revoked JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`. What originate does with that token is **NOT measured**.

## Recommendation

Measure originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` with a revoked session's JWT. That sets the severity, which the gate graded Minor pending that measurement.

## Detail

* Surfaced by the #1070-#1076 gate (`2026-09-19-batch1070-1076-tier1-r1`, finding N76-2).
* Pre-existing, not introduced by that batch: api-gateway product bytes are identical at develop `51dbedd39` and at every head of the batch. `verification.ts` is unchanged at develop `f9c28a8b8`.
* How the gate measured it: in-process, the real gateway app with loopback doubles; not against a live stack or a real session store.
* Related: KS-834, the pending decision on whether this route stays public. KS-834's text says a caller who sends a token "is still scoped downstream"; this finding is that a *revoked* session's token passes the gateway here unchecked.
* Also related: the revocation property established on the authenticated mounts (KS-1207, KS-1215).
* Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included):
  * literal title/description contains `certifications/:id/verify`: KS-834, KS-815 (archived, a control-byte guard);
  * `certifications/{id}/verify`: 0; `verification.ts:78`: 0;
  * `api/certifications/`: 38, none about Bearer forwarding;
  * `searchIssues("certifications verify")`, literal re-match: KS-834, KS-815.
  * None records the revoked-session forwarding.

title: Lockfile edits move platform discriminators silently: an npm command inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the ROOT lock (0 version changes, 12 lines of dev/devOptional churn), and an isolated resolve on darwin/arm64 strips os/cpu/libc markers (26 entries from frontend/issuer, 30 libc lines from services/mcp-server incl. the musl markers node:24-alpine needs, 103 entries on a full root re-resolution) — cause side of KS-1154; push-gate leg PROPOSED for Kam
description:
## BLUF

Two measured hazards in how this repo's lockfiles get edited on a developer host. Both produced wrong bytes in a working tree on 2026-09-25 before a per-file check caught them; neither is visible in `git diff --numstat` as anything but a small diff.

**TRAP 1 — an npm command run inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the workspace ROOT lock, not the member's own lock.** `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*","services/*","frontend/*"]`, so `services/originate`, `services/mcp-server` and the frontends are members — while each also carries its own tracked standalone `package-lock.json`, which is what `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` reads (43 of the 45 tracked locks). Measured: `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` run **inside** `services/originate` left `services/originate/package-lock.json` **byte-unchanged** and instead rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 lines, eleven `lightningcss-*` platform binaries plus `magicast` flipping `devOptional` → `dev: true`, with **0 packages added, 0 removed, 0 version-changed**. `npm update @hono/node-server` inside `services/mcp-server` moved **nothing at all**. So the in-place route silently misses its target and dirties a file the change must not touch.

**TRAP 2 — resolving a standalone lock in an isolated copy STRIPS platform discriminators for every host but the one resolving.** The isolated route writes the right file, but re-resolves optional platform deps for the current host (Darwin/arm64) and drops the rest. Measured, same session, npm 11.5.1 / node 24.7.0:

| lock | collateral |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/issuer/package-lock.json` | **26 entries removed** — `emnapi/runtime` plus **25** `rollup/rollup-<platform>` **binaries** |
| `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` | 1 entry removed each |
| `services/mcp-server/package-lock.json` | **30 lines of** `libc` **blocks deleted** — ten `"libc": ["glibc"]` / `["musl"]` markers |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (full re-resolution) | **103 entries removed** — esbuild 75, rolldown 13, lightningcss 10, cbor-extract 5. **103 of 103 carry an** `os`**/**`cpu` **constraint; 0 do not.** |

**Every service Dockerfile is** `node:24-alpine`**, i.e. musl**, so removing a `"libc": ["musl"]` discriminator is not cosmetic. And the frontends are built in Linux containers, so removing `rollup-linux-*` breaks their build.

*(npm scope sigils are omitted above —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

## Relation to KS-1154 — read both; they are cause and symptom

**KS-1154** (Backlog) is *"Root package-lock.json carries only rollup-darwin-arm64 — npm ci on ubuntu installs no Linux rollup binary…"*. That is **one symptom**: a binary already absent from the root lock. This ticket is the **mechanism that keeps removing them**, in both directions and across every lock, plus TRAP 1, which KS-1154 does not mention at all.

KS-1154's own "Ancestors" paragraph states the link in its own words: *"The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it."* Its ancestors KS-653 and KS-376 (both Done, archived) are the two earlier recurrences. KS-1154's guard proposal is a **lockfile cell pinning the rollup set**; this ticket's proposal below is a **push-gate leg covering every discriminator in every lock**, which would have caught all three past recurrences and this one.

**Not a duplicate, and KS-1154 should not be closed by this:** KS-1154 has its own "Done when" (add `rollup-linux-x64-gnu`, green the advisory job's step 6). This ticket does not add that binary.

## The proven workaround, in use now

Both scripts live at `5_Project_History/2026-09-25_seatB-25th/raise/` and were used to build the KS-530 and KS-528 lock changes:

* `lockresolve21.sh` — copies a member's two manifests into an isolated dir **outside every workspace**, resolves there, copies the lock back. Fixes TRAP 1. Its header carries the measurement.
* `splice_lock21.py` — takes **only** the named packages' entries from npm's own output (authoritative `version` / `resolved` / `integrity` / inner pins) and splices them into the pristine lock; every other byte stays pristine. Fixes TRAP 2. It refuses if the two locks hold different keys for those packages.

Result on the two PRs built with them: **added 0 / removed 0 / version-changed N** in every lock touched, and `libc` / `os` / `cpu` / `devOptional` counts identical before and after in all seven files.

## PROPOSAL — needs Kam, not this ticket's author

**A push-gate leg: a lockfile change must not move a platform discriminator.** Per changed `package-lock.json`, compare the before/after count of `os`, `cpu`, `libc` and `devOptional` markers; refuse the push on any delta that the change does not declare. **This is a gate change, so it is Kam's call** — recorded here as a proposal, not a decision, and deliberately not built. Evidence that it works: the check read `libc` **10 → 0** on the bad `services/mcp-server` lock and **10 → 10** after the splice. It is a guard that failed when it should have.

## What was searched before filing

The whole KS board, **1,279 issues including archived**, literal substring match on title + description for: `workspace member` (3 hits, none related), `package-lock` (36), `libc` (1 — KS-366, Done/archived, a currency review), `musl` (**0**), `os/cpu` (**0**), `optional binar` (4), `platform binar` (5), `rollup-` (1 — KS-1154), `esbuild` (13), `lightningcss` (**0**), `arborist` (**0**), `devOptional` (2), `lock-regen` (6), `package-lock-only` (9). Controls: `gate` matched **930** issues (the reader fires); a symbol that cannot exist matched **0** (it does not invent). **The only candidate was KS-1154**, related above.

## Also recorded from the same session

* A **full re-resolution of the root lock does not fix** either advisory pin it was tried for: `node_modules/ip-address` stays 9.0.5 and `@prisma/dev/node_modules/@hono/node-server` stays 1.19.11, with and without `overrides`. So a regen is not a fix and is destructive — see the 103-entry row above.
* `npm install --package-lock-only` is **inert for a version bump** on npm 11.5.1: it prints `up to date` and moves nothing. `npm update <pkg>` is what moves it. A command that reports success while doing nothing.
* Resolving a workspace root **from bare manifests with no** `node_modules` crashes npm: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` at `#loadPeerSet` (`@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1314`) — peer-dependency resolution, reproducible. With `node_modules` present it completes. Not a repo defect; a constraint on how any future measurement must be run.

## Done when

- [ ] `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` carries both traps and names the two scripts as the way to edit a lockfile
- [ ] the two scripts live somewhere durable in the repo rather than in one seat's record folder
- [ ] the push-gate leg is decided by Kam — built, or recorded as declined with the reason

title: originate documents.ts is the first router to mix a tenant-pool READ with a default-pool WRITE — on a dedicated-DB tenant it fails closed
description:
## BLUF

At #1239's head the `/share` and `/transfer-custody` handlers **read** through `req.db` (the tenant pool set by `extractTenantContext`) and **write** through `withTenant`, which always uses `tenantManager.getDefaultPool()`. **On a tenant whose config resolves to a dedicated database those are two different databases.**

`documents.ts` **is the first router to do this.** Every other non-test `withTenant` call site — 9, all in `routes/adminConfig.ts` — sits under `adminConfig.ts:30` `(req as any).db = prisma // Always shared DB`, so that router reads and writes one database by design.

## Reach, measured

* A pool other than `getDefaultPool()` **is** reachable in code: `getPool` returns a dedicated `Pool` when `perTenantDbEnabled` (`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'`) **and** the tenant's config resolves elsewhere.
* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` **appears in 0 tracked config files** — compose, deployment and bicep; bicep sets only `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`. So it is **latent and gated on a variable no template sets**.

## Behaviour on a dedicated-DB tenant, by reading

It **fails closed** rather than misplacing rows: `/share`'s target subquery runs in the default DB → NULL → `SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` → 404. `/transfer-custody`'s INSERT names a `document_id` absent from the default DB's `documents` → 23503 → rollback → 500.

**That is the right failure direction**, and it is why this is Minor rather than Major. It is still a router whose read and write disagree about which database it is talking to.

## NOT claimed

**Live proof NOT RUN** — no slot was available, and no per-tenant-DB tenant was provisioned. The reach above is static: read from `tenant-context.ts:93`, `tenant-pool-manager.ts:152/201-260` and `db.ts:308`, not executed.

## Related, and NOT a duplicate

**KS-1235** concerns **auth**'s `db.ts` sending tenant-scoped statements through `getPool(tenantId).query()` with **no tenant GUC** under fail-closed RLS. Same neighbourhood — tenant pool versus default pool — but a different service and a different mechanism (a missing GUC there, a read/write pool mismatch here). Read in full before filing.

## Fix shape

`withTenant` checks out from `getPool(tenantId)` (or takes the request's pool). Cell: a manager stub whose `getPool(t) !== getDefaultPool()` must see **both** writes on `getPool(t)`'s client.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,291 issues incl. archived, 3,644 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1235**, KS-1055, KS-1054); `getPool(` -> 2 / 1 (KS-1235). **KS-1235 read in full — related, not a duplicate** (see above).
* `getDefaultPool` -> 1 total / **0 open**. `tenantPool` -> **0**.
* Control that fires: `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5. Nonsense control -> **0**.

`Refs KS-1263`; does not close it. Ruled TICKET (Minor) by the tier-1c gate, explicitly **not** part of #1239's round 2.

title: KS-980 N-2: the PR body claimed a 14/14 full run over 2 suites when the integration config runs 3
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** The PR body reported a full run as **14/14 over two suites**. `jest.integration.config.js` matches **three** suites. The number quoted is therefore not the full run it is presented as — it is a subset, described with the words of a complete one.

**Why it matters more than the number.** A count is a claim about what executed. A subset reported as a full run makes coverage look wider than it is, and the next reader has no way to tell from the body alone.

**What a fix looks like.** Quote the runner's own ratio and name the suites it covered, or say plainly which suite was excluded and why.

Refs KS-980

title: KS-980 N-3: a squash body named a base commit that is not an ancestor of the squash
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** The PR body's base line named `d9515f4a06e0`, which is **not an ancestor** of the merged result. The actual base at merge time was `e68e2f0e837df86da527d775a3a49c631b0f5b17`, and the squash's parent is that commit.

**Why it matters.** The base line is how a reviewer reconstructs what a change was measured against. A base that is not an ancestor cannot be the one the work was tested on, so any figure quoted against it is unverifiable after the fact.

**What a fix looks like.** Take the base from the same read that pins the head, at the moment the evidence is produced, rather than from an earlier draft of the body.

Refs KS-980

title: KS-980 N-5: an anonymous Docker volume was left behind by a disposable test Postgres
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** A disposable Postgres container used for the integration cells was removed, but its **anonymous volume** `0ec12181` was not, and remains on the host.

**Why it matters.** `docker rm -f` removes the container, not its anonymous volume. Volumes accumulate silently across sessions and are invisible to a `docker ps -a` check, so a teardown that looks complete is not.

**What a fix looks like.** Tear down with `docker rm -f -v`, or prove the volume gone as part of the teardown check rather than proving only the container gone.

Refs KS-980

title: Published spec descriptions carry internal ticket keys ("KS-1275:", "KS-1118 F-3", "KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER") — the owner's call
description:
## BLUF

The **served** OpenAPI description text now carries internal ticket keys. #1252 added `"KS-1275:"` and `"KS-1118 F-3"` to two descriptions in `originate.openapi.ts`, and they are published into `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` and served from `/api/docs`.

**This is a pre-existing style, not a new one** — `"KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER"` was already in the same file's v2 verify description before #1252.

Recorded by the tier-2 gate on #1252 (report `2026-09-26-batch1249-t2b`, finding **N-1252-b**, READ) as Polish and explicitly **the owner's call**.

## The decision, stated plainly

Ticket keys in a published description are useful to us and meaningless to an integrator reading the contract. Two defensible positions:

* **Keep them.** They make the reason for a wording discoverable, and the convention is already established in this file.
* **Strip them.** The published contract is customer-facing; internal identifiers belong in the source comment, not the served text. The source comment above each description can carry the key instead.

**No change should be made on a seat's own judgement** — hence a ticket rather than a fix. If the answer is "strip", it is a sweep across the spec (three known instances and possibly more), not a one-line edit.

## Scope, measured

Instances found in the published description text: `KS-1275:` and `KS-1118 F-3` (added by #1252), `KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER` (pre-existing). A full sweep of `originate.openapi.ts` description strings has not been done and is part of the work if the ruling is to strip.

## Done when

- [ ] a ruling is recorded: keep, or strip
- [ ] if strip: every instance in the published description text removed, the key moved to the adjacent source comment, and the yaml regenerated
- [ ] if keep: the convention written down where the next editor will find it, so it is a decision rather than an accident

## Board search before filing

Literal match over 1,310 issues incl. archived and 3,687 comments: `HASH ALIAS ORDER` and `SPEC-PROSE` searched alongside `originate.openapi.ts` (30 total / 11 open) and `docs/VOCABULARY.md` (13 / 7) — the path hits are about spec content generally, none about **internal keys in the published text**. No existing home. Controls fire as above.

Raised from the #1252 merge (develop `49bc69abae1528d8da76018aaa68b04749e5d93b`).

title: Seat push tooling reuses one push-log name per worktree, so a push record is overwritten and the earlier STOP-count evidence is lost
description:
## BLUF

`push24.sh` (and its predecessors `push22/23.sh`) name the push log by the **worktree basename**: `<worktree>-push.out`. A seat that pushes twice from the same worktree **overwrites the first push's log**, and with it the in-hook evidence — the fleet STOP counts, the leg-by-leg preflight output and the `FIXTURE BUILD FAILED` check for that push.

Confirmed by the tier-2 gate on #1255 (report `2026-09-26-batch1249-t2b`, finding **N-1255-a**, READ): `raise/s-b28-cells-push.out` held a push from `15:50:24Z` to `15:57:03Z`, overwritten again afterwards — **#1255's own push record is gone.** Non-blocking; nothing shipped wrongly, and the counts were quoted into the PR from the run at the time.

## Why it matters

A PR's Test Evidence block quotes the STOP counts from that push's log. If the log has been overwritten by a later push from the same worktree, the evidence behind a merged PR is no longer re-readable — the claim survives and its source does not. That is an evidence-integrity gap, not a correctness one, which is why it is non-blocking and still worth closing.

## Fix shape (the gate's)

Name the push log by the **head sha** (or append `-push-<n>`), never reused. Same for the `.start`, `.end`, `.rc` and `-stubs.txt` siblings, which share the defect.

## Done when

- [ ] two pushes from one worktree leave two distinct logs, both readable afterwards
- [ ] the naming includes something that cannot repeat (head sha preferred)
- [ ] a control: push twice from one worktree and assert both files exist with different names

## Board search before filing

Literal match over 1,310 issues incl. archived and 3,687 comments: `push24.sh` → 0; `-push.out` → 0; `push log` → 4 total / 3 open (KS-1201, KS-1047, KS-948), each about other things (login_stub orphans, the hook's leg naming, an unrelated script) — **none about log-name reuse.** No existing home. Controls: `withTenant` → 12, `ZZZNOSUCHSYMBOLZZZ` → 0.

Raised from the #1255 merge (develop `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086`).

title: A PTY harness so SIGINT can be asserted for run-shell-suites.sh in the foreground, in both the standalone and in-hook environments
description:
**BLUF: there is currently no way to assert that** `run-shell-suites.sh` **handles SIGINT, because every available harness either backgrounds the runner or runs with SIGINT already ignored - and bash discards the signal in both cases.** A pseudo-terminal harness is the only route to closing that gap. Nothing is broken today; the runner's INT/TERM arms exist and are correct. What is missing is the ability to *prove* the INT arm, and today that is recorded as UNREACHABLE rather than tested.

## The two measured rules that create the gap

Both measured on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, which is the only bash on this drive - there is no Homebrew bash cellar and every local project image is busybox/Alpine with no `bash` at all.

1. **A signal IGNORED ON ENTRY to bash cannot be trapped.** `trap '...' INT` is silently not installed and `trap -p INT` comes back empty. **The in-hook preflight runs with SIGINT ignored**, so an INT arm inside the hook cannot exist at all.
2. **bash ignores SIGINT in any ASYNCHRONOUS (background) job**, whatever the parent's disposition: `trap -p INT` empty, the signal discarded, rc 0. The identical trap in the **foreground** gives rc 130.

Between them, SIGINT-to-pid is unassertable by any harness that backgrounds the runner, which is what a test harness naturally does in order to hold its pid.

## Current state, so this is not read as a defect report

The runner's signal arms were built and accepted on the ruling that each arm **probes its own reachability** and either asserts all four properties or reports UNREACHABLE naming the rule above. That is the right behaviour given the constraint. TERM is assertable and is asserted. INT is not, and says so.

## What this ticket asks for

One harness that runs `run-shell-suites.sh` **in the foreground of a pseudo-terminal** so a real SIGINT can be delivered to it and its disposition observed, usable from:

* a standalone run, and
* the in-hook environment, where the parent's disposition is the thing being worked around.

Candidate mechanisms, none chosen here: `script -q` (present on macOS and on Linux with different argument orders), a small `openpty`/`forkpty` helper, or Python's `pty` module driving the runner. The acceptance criterion is the discriminating one: **the same harness must give rc 130 on a foreground INT and must show the arm reporting UNREACHABLE when the signal is ignored on entry** - a harness that only ever produces one of those has not measured anything.

## Proposed tier

**Tier 2.** It is test-infrastructure with no runtime surface, but it is the only path to converting a standing UNREACHABLE into an assertion, and the rules above will otherwise be re-derived by whoever next touches the runner's signal handling.

## Board search before filing

Searched, over 479 open issues on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `pseudo-terminal`, `pseudoterminal`, `SIGINT`, `script -q`, `openpty`, `forkpty`, `PTY harness` - **0 open hits each**. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `run-shell-suites` returned **14**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Note for anyone re-running this search: the bare term `pty` is useless here - it is a substring of "empty" and returned **69** open hits on this corpus. Use a word boundary or a longer term.

Refs KS-1302

title: childSuiteCounts reads a child KILLED by its own 180 s spawnSync timeout as a PASS - a lookalike summary pair is accepted as {7,0}
description:
**BLUF:** `childSuiteCounts` **can report a clean pass for a child process that was killed.** When a child is terminated by its own 180 s `spawnSync` timeout *after* it has already logged a summary-shaped pair, the reader takes that pair as the verdict and returns `{7,0}`. The kill is invisible to it. **Measured on both sides** - at PR #1245's head `65eb964271b0d6895e90fe8f5ffcbbbb9a484050` **and** on `develop` `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086` - so this is a property of the code on the mainline, not of one branch.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## The lookalike that is accepted

A child that logs

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

and is then killed still presents that pair to the reader. `childSuiteCounts` returns `{7,0}` - seven passed, zero failed - and nothing downstream can tell that outcome apart from a genuine completion. **A verdict composed separately from the work reproduces here exactly:** the summary text is not evidence that the run finished.

## Three residues, one test pass, one ticket

1. **KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE** - the defect above.
2. **CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT** - the call site still reaches the summary through text. The shape asked for is a pure `countsFromSpawn(result)` sitting behind `childSuiteCounts`, fed a synthetic spawn result, so the decision is made from the spawn outcome rather than from scraped output.
3. **JOINED-CLAIM** - the sentence *"measured to hold on the JOINED text"* should be dropped. It is not true: **10 real shapes are misread on joined text, 3 of them silently.** A claim about where a reader is safe, which is false, is worse than no claim.

## Fix shapes, any one of which closes the first residue

* **Refuse when the spawn says so:** `result.error` or `result.signal` set, or `result.status` not `0`/`1`.
* **Require vitest's trailing** `Start at` **/** `Duration` **block**, which a killed child never reaches.
* **Use the JSON reporter** instead of parsing human output.

## Cells the next attempt should carry

* The **H1 stdout capture** returns `null`.
* A spawn result of `{status 143, ETIMEDOUT}` **throws** rather than yielding counts.

Signal 143 is SIGTERM; a status of 143 with `ETIMEDOUT` is precisely the killed-child case, and it is the discriminating fixture.

## Reusable from the capped attempt - do not rebuild these

The round-2 **stdout-only reader**, the **whole-run cells**, and the `{3,2}` **row** are sound and are the parts to start from.

## Not covered

Preflight legs 3, 4 and 8 were not run for that attempt (no local stack). They are owed by nothing here; recorded so the absence is not mistaken for a pass.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **481 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `countsFromSpawn`, `KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE`, `CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT`, `JOINED-CLAIM`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `status 143`, `capturedChildOutput` - **0 open hits each**. `spawnSync` returned 2 (KS-1111, KS-1098), neither about this reader. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `childSuiteCounts` returned **1**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

**Not duplicates, deliberately:** KS-1313 is the parent this residue falls out of, and KS-1226 is its own parent. Both stay open and neither is closed by this ticket.

Refs KS-1313

nodes.body:
**#1245 round 3 is NO GO at the cap — this residue ticket is NOT discharged by it, and gains one item.**

Round 3 (head `cb31a58c190f86aad49b402c1c001429c037ed24`) ships nothing and the pull request stays open for the repository owner's disposition. The three residues this ticket carries remain open, and the round added a fourth, more serious one:

🔴 **ERRORS-LINE-LIVE — a REGRESSION, not a residue.** A test raising an **unhandled error** ends normally (status 1, no signal) and vitest prints `     Errors  1 error` **between** its `Tests` and `Start at` lines. Round 3 reads all three live captures as **NULL** and `childSuiteCounts` throws. **Round 2 read the same shapes correctly**, so this is ground lost, not ground not yet gained. Measured at runtime through the real `childSuiteCounts` and `readChildOutput`, at 246 tests.

**What that means for whoever picks this up:** round 3's anchor walks backwards from `Start at` to the nearest `Tests` line and refuses foreign content in the gap — but the file names only ` Test Files ` as possible there. An `Errors` line is also legitimate vitest output in that position. **Any next attempt must enumerate what vitest can print in that gap from captured real output, not from a list someone believed was complete** — which is the same discipline this ticket's KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE item already asks for.

The reusable parts named in this ticket still stand. Facts only; no proposal is made here.

**Round 3 of #1245 is pushed**, head **`cb31a58c190f86aad49b402c1c001429c037ed24`** (a fast-forward on the PR's own branch from `65eb964271b0`; never forced). Recorded here because this ticket carries the cap residue for #1245. Facts only.

The round-3 commit addresses gate24T2c's **KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE** finding: a child killed after printing a complete summary-block lookalike read `{ passed: 7, failed: 0 }` — a clean pass for a run that never finished. `readChildOutput` now anchors on vitest's own `   Start at` line and walks backwards to the nearest `Tests` line, and `childSuiteCounts` refuses a child that did not end normally before reading its stdout at all.

**Proof:** the round-2 anchor restored reddens H1 (31 passed / 3 failed) while **H1b and H1c stay green in every arm**; `systemTest/performance` unit suite **1115 → 1120**, 63 files both; `tsc` rc 0; `format:check` rc 0.

**If round 3 GOes and merges, this ticket's items are delivered** — that disposition is the coordinator's, not mine, and I have moved no ticket state. Full detail is on KS-1313.

⚠ One thing not to read into it: the `Blockchain/Dev` preflight and the fleet STOP quadruple did **not** run on this push (measured: 0 occurrences of each in the push log). The hook's Dev gate is path-scoped and this change is entirely under `systemTest/performance/`; the systemTest formatting gate is what ran, 1 package checked / 0 failed.

title: kyc verification writes are a whole-row read-modify-write: two timers, or a timer and an admin review, can still race
description:
## BLUF

`services/kyc` persists a verification by reading the **whole row**, mutating the object, and writing the **whole row** back through an upsert whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` names `status`, `current_level`, `documents`, `liveness_completed`, `liveness_score`, `checks`, `overall_score`, `risk_level`, `reviewed_by`, `review_notes`, `updated_at` and `completed_at`. Nothing serialises those writers. So any two of them overlapping — two mock timers, or a timer and an admin review — can still lose one side's changes.

KS-849's fix (re-reading inside each mock timer) **narrows the window from 1500/3000 ms to the read-modify-write's own microseconds, and that is all it can do.** It does not make the write atomic.

## The part KS-849 explicitly does NOT close, measured

The 3000 ms auto-approve timer at `services/kyc/src/index.ts` sets `status = 'approved'` and `currentLevel = requestedLevel` **itself**. So after the re-read:

* **FIXED** — every field the timer does not own survives an admin review landing inside the window: `reviewedBy`, `reviewNotes`, `documents`, `livenessCompleted`, `livenessScore`, and checks that are no longer `pending`.
* **NOT FIXED** — an admin **rejection** through `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` inside those 3 seconds is **still overwritten to** `approved`, and a `newLevel` supplied by the reviewer is still replaced by `requestedLevel`.

This correction matters because the KS-849 ticket's own fix-shape text ("re-read the verification inside the timer") reads as though it addresses the admin-overwrite case. **It does not**, and the ticket should not be read that way.

## Where it is pinned rather than left to be rediscovered

PR for KS-849 adds `services/kyc/src/__tests__/ks849-mock-timer-stale-write.test.ts`, whose cell **S3 asserts** `status === 'approved'` **after a rejection**, with a comment stating this is not fixed and is tracked here. A later reader cannot mistake the limit for closed.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. A **single-statement partial UPDATE** per writer, naming only the columns that writer owns, instead of the whole-row upsert. Removes the class for non-overlapping column sets; two writers to the *same* column still race.
2. **Row locking** (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction) around read-modify-write.
3. Move the mock auto-approve **off the request path** entirely, which removes the 3 s window but not the class.

Both (1) and (2) are behaviour changes to a persistence path and want their own gate, which is why this is a ticket rather than part of KS-849.

## Scope

The mock/demo path gates the timers (`KYC_PROVIDER === 'mock'`), but **the whole-row upsert is not mock-gated** — `/review`, `/complete`, `/document` and `/selfie` all write through it in every mode. So the timers are the reachable trigger today; the class is wider than the trigger.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,316 issues **including archived**, 3,705 comments; literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `auto-approve` → 0 titles/descriptions, 2 comments · `autoApprove` → 0 · `row locking` → 0 · `read-modify-write` → 0 titles, 1 comment · `stale write` → 0.
* `partial UPDATE` → 1 (KS-938, TOTP seed retention — unrelated).
* `svc_kyc_verifications` → KS-851 (column ordinal drift, a different defect) and KS-386 (archived, image payload).
* `KYC_PROVIDER` → KS-849 itself and KS-626 (archived, Entra callback).
* **Controls that fire:** `KS-1155` → 4 titles / 7 comments; `KS-849` → 1 / 1; a nonsense token `zzqx-l8-never-written-anywhere-7731` → **0 / 0**. So the search discriminates. (That token is now spent by appearing here.)

Nothing on the board describes this class in kyc.

Refs KS-849

title: pre-push fixture guard: re-land GUARDGAPS with a call-site reader that passes the aborting `||` / `if` / `&&` shapes and flags multi-line `$(` and group openers
description:
**BLUF: the fixture guard's round-2 work was measured correct in cells 7 and 8 and shipped nothing, because cell 9's reader flags shapes that DO abort and passes shapes that swallow the abort — wrong in both directions.** This ticket re-lands the work with a reader that discriminates, and it resolves a contradiction in the earlier hold text.

## What is on `develop` today

Guard blob `52c852203edc2d7b64c3e23bc2ab3f077cf07cc6` at 6 cells, with three gaps all open: unanchored abort counts, a `repo_state` blind to the worktree, and no call-site pin. **Reach is 0 today** — all 12 of 12 call sites are bare — so nothing is currently mis-scored; the guard simply cannot see a regression.

## What the reader must do

Through the real guard, cell 9 currently **FLAGS** the named aborting shapes:
`bf || true` · `false || bf` · `if bf; then :; fi` · `bf && :`
and **PASSES** the named swallowing shapes: a multi-line `x=$(` / call / `)` and `( : noop` / call / `)`.

That is backwards. `build_fixture` aborts with an explicit `exit 2`, so only a **subshell** call site swallows it; `|| true`, `if` and `&&` do not.

## Scope

Re-land the anchored counts (cell 7), the widened `repo_state` (cell 8) and cells 11-12 from blob `5189cf31a098a62c485367beedb78def2428d787`, with `c9_scan` **admitting** `bf || true`, `false || bf`, `if bf; then :; fi` and `bf && :`, and **flagging** a previous line ending in `$(` / `(` or holding an unclosed `(`. Cell 10 computes `c9_scan`; cell 12 asserts on a subject copy.

## The contradiction to resolve, named by the gate to the filer

The earlier hold asked for a **strict whitelist** AND for the `||` shapes to be **unflagged**. Those two contradict each other. **The admitting whitelist is the one to pick** — that is the gate's own note to whoever picks this up.

## A limit worth carrying forward rather than rediscovering

Do not attempt to track shell nesting by counting parentheses. A paren-depth counter over lines called 11 of 12 real call sites offending, because a subshell can close with `) > "$WORK/c0.out" 2>/dev/null` and a multi-line `$( … )` can end with `)"`. A guard that half-parses shell is worse than one with a declared limit: read one line of context and write the limitation down.

## Evidence produced by the gate

`evidence/reader1253/reader_rows.json` · `evidence/reader1253/guard_*.stdout` · `behav_*.stdout` · `evidence/g1253/garms_rows.json`.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **483 open issues**, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `c9_scan`, `call-site reader`, `5189cf31a098`, `GUARDGAPS`, `admitting whitelist` — **0 open hits each**. Controls as above: a fresh nonsense token **0**, `run-shell-suites.sh` **16**.

Refs KS-1297

title: KS-962 seed-idempotence suite skips all 27 cells on hosts without Postgres binaries — would an opt-in Docker runner help it run anywhere?
description:
## Summary

No rush at all on this one, Kamil. The [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) seed-idempotence suite (`ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh`) skips all 27 of its cells on any machine without Postgres binaries, and it does so honestly and loudly, exactly as designed. The only gap is that on such hosts the guard never runs. An opt-in Docker runner might let it run anywhere, but it's your suite, so whichever approach you'd prefer is the one to go with. Happy to help build or test it.

+++ Details and options

**Observed 2026-09-28** during the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) preflight: `SKIP — no PostgreSQL binaries (initdb pg_ctl postgres psql) found; … 0/27 cells run`. Shell suites 59 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (of 60).

**What the suite needs** (read from the file): the Postgres binaries (via `KS949_PG_BIN`, then the Homebrew / Debian paths); Node ≥18, tsx and a built `packages/shared`; and auth's path includes the native `argon2`, so a macOS `node_modules` can't simply be mounted into Linux.

**One possible shape:** an opt-in container runner (Postgres 15 + Node, repo mounted read-only, `node_modules` in a named volume), off by default (e.g. `KS949_PG_DOCKER=1`). The suite already searches `/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin`, so it would need no change itself.

**Other options, equally welcome:** connect to an already-running Postgres instead of `initdb`; reuse the stack's own `postgres` container; or document `brew install postgresql@15` as a prerequisite. (Not suggested: wrapping `pg_ctl` into a container, because Postgres's 0700 data-dir check is fragile across Docker Desktop's bind mounts.)

No defect was found; this is a coverage gap on Postgres-less hosts. Related: [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) · [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9).

title: api-gateway failed-login lockout is inert: createBruteForceProtection installs recordFailure, but no production code ever calls it — it can never block
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil. The gateway's failed-login lockout (`createBruteForceProtection`, `api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:146-192`) looks as though it never engages: it only blocks once `recordFailure()` has run, and nothing outside its own unit test seems to call it. The auth service's per-account lockout is still doing its job, so this is about the edge layer only. Either wiring it up or retiring it would be fine; whichever you prefer. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, and the two options

**What the code shows** (read-only, 2026-09-28)

* `security.ts:173-189` attaches `req.bruteForce = { recordFailure, recordSuccess }` and calls `next()`; nothing on the login's response path calls either helper.
* Searching `services/api-gateway/src` for `recordFailure` outside `middleware/security.ts` finds only `__tests__/security.test.ts:261`, which checks the helper exists.
* So `attempts` is never incremented, `blockedUntil` is never written, and the `429 "Too many failed attempts"` branch can't be reached.

**What the logs show**

* Slot 2's gateway, six hours of traffic including failed logins: **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT`, **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED`.
* The lockout that does work is the auth service's (`services/auth/src/services/accountLockout.ts`: (email, /24), 5 failures in 15 min → 15-min lock). It answers **401** (`routes/auth.ts:339-342`).

**Why it came up:** [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) first put some refused setup logins down to this lockout; on a closer look they were the global request window. It seemed worth recording that this layer isn't active, so no one leans on it.

**Options**

1. Wire it: call `recordFailure` / `recordSuccess` from the login proxy's response handling (401 / 2xx), with a test that shows a block after `freeRetries` failures.
2. Retire it: remove the middleware, its `bruteForce` config in `config/services.ts`, and the doc line at `security.ts:8`.

[KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every IP-keyed control is shared behind one address) applies either way.

**Done means:** a test red on today's code shows N+1 failed logins from one address aren't blocked at the gateway; after the change they are — or the middleware and its claims are gone.

+++

title: Security: certifications ends RLS FORCE with no tenant_isolation policy on every fresh database, permanently
description:
**Found by the gate39 QA pass over PR #1332 (N-G39-1, Major). Facts only.**

## What is wrong

On a **fresh bare database**, `public.certifications` ends with row-level security **ENABLED and FORCED but with no** `tenant_isolation` **policy**. RLS with no policy is **default-deny**, so the table is unreadable and unwritable by the application role — and unlike the defect #1332 fixed, **this does not heal on a later boot**. It is permanent for the life of that database.

Measured across all four head paths (gateway runner boot 1 and boot 2, `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, and both combined): identical, `4c59e2ebdc37`. The **merge-base differs** (`fd91b0ab5a48`) and **does** carry `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON public.certifications` — so the merge-base heals it and the current tip does not. An app-role `INSERT` carrying the tenant GUC is **refused**.

## Why it changed

`migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` (added in #1332) creates `certifications` **before** 039 runs. 039 then finds the table present and applies its RLS `ENABLE`/`FORCE` block to it — but the branch of 039 that creates the `tenant_isolation` policy does not cover it on that path. Before #1332, `certifications` did not exist when 039 ran, so 039 skipped it entirely and a later boot created it with its policy intact.

## A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE, filed here deliberately rather than separately (N-G39-4)

`038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` lines **16-17** describe this exact condition — `certifications` with RLS forced and no `tenant_isolation` policy — as one of the things the migration **fixes**. **It does not fix it; it is the cause of it.** The same header's claim that the schema equality is "proved … across … the docker/init seeded path" is also **wider than true**: the equality holds for `certifications` only, and fails for `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` because of a pre-existing docker/init DDL difference (extra indexes and the `svc_webhooks_app_id_fkey` foreign key). Both header claims need correcting in the same change that fixes the policy, so the file does not keep asserting a fix it does not deliver.

## Fix shape (from the gate)

A migration numbered **after 039** that applies 039's `tenant_isolation` block to `certifications`, plus a **real-PostgreSQL cell driven as the application role** (`secuura_app`) asserting that an `INSERT` carrying the correct tenant GUC succeeds and one carrying a foreign tenant is refused. A source-text assertion is not sufficient here: the defect is a runtime default-deny, and only a driven app-role probe distinguishes "policy present" from "policy absent but table reachable as owner".

## Scope

Not fixed in #1332 — that PR was round 2 of 2 under the class cap and shipped GO WITH FINDINGS with this as named residue. No board ticket covered it before this one (searched by symbol: `certifications` + `tenant_isolation`, `tenant_isolation policy certifications`, `038a`, `certifications RLS force default-deny`, `certifications no tenant_isolation` — zero title-relevant results; three positive controls each returned their expected ticket first, so the search was working).

Refs KS-1054

- Still there: Blockchain/Dev/migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql, read at origin/develop 035685291b9d, lines 16 and 17 still say the migration fixes tenant isolation on oauth_apps, svc_webhooks and charge_events and on certifications (RLS forced, no tenant_isolation policy).
- Added fact (measured by comparing the four CREATE TABLE bodies by script, whitespace normalised): 038a's DDL is identical to the CORE definition in Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts for oauth_apps, svc_webhooks, certifications and charge_events. Only charge_events, oauth_apps and svc_webhooks have a tenant_id column; certifications has none in either definition, and no ALTER TABLE certifications under Blockchain/Dev/migrations adds one. Migration 039 (the tenant-table loop that starts at line 96 at develop) skips a table with no tenant_id column, with the notice "no tenant_id column", which is the mechanism this ticket describes.
