title: PR #1339's standalone locks were re-resolved from bare manifests: ~1,000 non-target moves, incl. runtime bullmq/msgpackr 2 and @azure/identity/msal-node 6
description:
Raised from **gate41's finding N-1339-2** (Major, non-blocking) on PR #1339 (KS-1378, the four-package advisory bump). Wednesday ruled this a ticket rather than a fold-in for round 2, because the only mechanism the gate's own fix-shape offers is `npm install --package-lock-only`, and host npm 11.5.1 dies with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` on this machine — measured by Seat B 43rd even on a bare `package.json` in an empty temp dir, so it is the host npm build and not the workspace layout.

## What happened

#1339's 13 standalone `package-lock.json` files were regenerated **from their bare manifests** rather than from their committed locks. That resolved every dependency afresh, so about **1,000 versions moved that the bump did not target**. All are inside their declared ranges, so nothing is a range violation — but nothing exercises them either: the suites run from the **root** lock, which moved **0** non-target versions.

## The moves that matter (gate-measured)

* `services/queue`: **bullmq 5.76.2 → 5.81.5**, pulling **msgpackr 1 → 2** — runtime.
* `services/m365-integration` and `packages/shared`: **@azure/identity 4.13.1 → 4.13.3**, pulling **@azure/msal-node 5 → 6** — runtime.
* `services/originate`: minimatch 3 → 10, plus dev-only eslint-cache majors.

## Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from gate41's report

> Fix-shape: regenerate each standalone lock FROM its committed lock (`npm install <pkg>@<ver> --package-lock-only`), or declare the drift and add a standalone-install smoke (build + boot) per service.

## The condition attached to #1339 merging without this

Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat B 44th, 2026-09-29T03:54:40Z: the two runtime moves above **get a clean standalone** `npm ci` **plus that service's own suite in the next gate**, so what ships untested by the root-lock suites is tested once. **Merged is not deployed:** no deploy carries these until this ticket is done or Kam says otherwise.

## Blocked on, and why it is not just "run the command"

`npm install` in any form is unavailable on this host. Seat B 43rd's workaround for #1339 was `node:24-alpine` (npm 11.19.0), mounted at `/src` — **never** `/dev`, which clobbers the container's `/dev/null` and dies rc 127 before starting. Whoever takes this needs either that container route explicitly permitted, or a working host npm.

## Neighbours (cross-reference only)

KS-1290 (an npm command inside a workspace member moves platform discriminators silently) and KS-1154 (the root lock carries only the darwin rollup binary) are the same family — lockfile regeneration doing more than it was asked to — but neither covers this drift.

Discovered 2026-09-29 by gate41 on PR #1339; ticketed by the Platform K build seat under Wednesday's ruling.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Facts only, no state change. PR 1339's deploy hold names this ticket, and the packages it holds are already running on both boxes; this comment keeps that on record before KS-1378 closes.

**The hold, quoted from PR 1339's squash message (2cb858335472, read from the commit today):** "MERGED IS NOT DEPLOYED: the deploy hold on the moved runtime packages stands until KS 1379 is done or Kam says otherwise. A live sweep of nodemailer 10 sending real mail through the deployed auth and originate images is owed and is not done here."

**What runs, from KS-1378's comment 00a3675c (2026-11-05T03:08Z):** package.json version reads inside the running containers at 03:06Z, identical on Kintsugi and demo: nodemailer 10.2.1 in secuura-auth and secuura-originate, and morgan 1.12.1 in secuura-auth, secuura-api-gateway, secuura-m365-integration and secuura-queue. So the moved runtime packages are deployed on both boxes while this ticket is still in Backlog.

**What happens next:** KS-1378 is being closed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-06 00:53:47Z, which says a follow-up with its own ticket does not hold its parent. This ticket, KS-1379, is unchanged: its own scope stays, and the real-mail sweep of nodemailer 10 through the auth and originate images stays unrun.

**Added from gate42 (QA/Secuura-batch1339r2) as a checklist item on this ticket, not a new ticket.**

The gate found this ticket's condition **met to the letter but not in substance**: `services/queue` and `services/m365-integration` each got a clean standalone `npm ci` plus their own suite, green at base and head — but those suites barely touch the packages that moved.

- [ ] **N-1339r2-1 (Major, non-blocking).** Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from the gate report: *"add a cell that drives `getSecretsManager({ fallbackToEnv:true })` with `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL` set and a network-refusing guard, asserting that the vault client initialises on the installed identity/msal major. Also add a queue cell that imports what queue ships, or drop `bullmq` from queue's dependencies if it is unused."* **Regression cell**, also verbatim: *"a standalone-install smoke per service (build + boot) that runs in CI over each service's OWN lock"*.

Why it matters, as the gate measured it:
- **queue** — its only test is a placeholder (`expect(true).toBe(true)`), and `services/queue/src` never imports `bullmq` (the single hit is a doc comment). So msgpackr 2 is exercised by nothing.
- **m365-integration** — its suite reaches only the DIRECT `@azure/msal-node` 3.8.10 in `token-manager.ts`, which did not move. The moved 6.0.1 sits under `@azure/identity`, which m365's source never imports.
- **shared — the real exposure.** shared's moved msal-node 6.0.1 **is** reachable in a shipped service: auth `jwt.ts:11,109` → `getSecretsManager` → `import('@azure/identity')` from `/shared/node_modules` whenever `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL` is set. **That is the JWT signing-key load.**

**This keeps the deploy hold in place: merged is not deployed.** #1339 merged to develop as `2cb858335472fafcce535ca4ad328c897ed87bfb`; nothing carrying these moved runtime packages is deployed until this ticket is done or Kam rules otherwise. This ticket stays open.

title: Verify is not bound to the credential's proof: a revoked credential resubmitted with another LIVE id still verifies true
description:
`Refs KS-1375`

## BLUF

Credential verification is not bound to the credential's own proof. A **revoked** credential
resubmitted carrying **another live credential's id** verifies `true` on **both** verify routes. This
is pre-existing: it reproduces at the merged head of PR #1341 *and* at develop before it. A forged
subject also verifies.

No DID resolver is wired, so the proof is not validated on these routes (structurally checked only,
outside production). PR #1341's fail-closed change covers ids that **no authority holds**, which is
why it is partial against its ruling's phrase "closes the id-edit trick": an id that *is* held by a
live credential is not an unknown id.

## Provenance

The ruling card for the unknown-id policy said this work was coming, and said it goes ahead either
way: "Separately, a ticket is being filed to bind the check to the credential's proof (wire the
issuer's DID resolver), which would close the edit trick whatever you choose here" and "The
proof-binding ticket goes ahead either way."

That ticket was never filed — searched by symbol (`didResolver`, `DID resolver`, `resolver`,
`proof-binding`) with two positive controls that each found a ticket known to exist. The only match
for `didResolver` was KS 1375 itself. This ticket is that filing.

Adjacent but **not** this: KS 624 (prism issues VCs with random bytes as the proof), KS 625
(`/presentations/verify` never checks the holder signature), KS 627 (wallet CIP-8/COSE verification).
Each was read before filing; none covers the credential-verify path's proof binding.

## Evidence

QA finding N-1341-1 (Major, not blocking), gate43 batch #1341-#1345, evidence under
`evidence/07_probe1341_*idswap*` in that gate's report directory.

## Not measured

The production path was not driven: the vc-issuer app refuses to boot without `DATABASE_URL` and
`PRISM_AGENT_URL`, so the finding is measured on the structural path only. The fix shape is
deliberately blank — it needs a decision on where the resolver lives and what it costs a stack with
no network to an issuer's DID document.

nodes.body:
**BLUF: where the bypass exists, measured; and the priority is raised from none to High (2) on Wednesday's ruling.**

**Environments, in one line:** the bypass exists wherever the proof is not verified, that is `NODE_ENV` other than `production`: measured in-process on the real verify routes and verifier (development: a revoked credential resubmitted with another live credential's id verifies `true`, and so does one with a tampered `credentialSubject`; production: all five cases answered `verified: false` with `No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production`, including a genuine unrevoked credential, so there is no bypass there and nothing verifies either); **NOT measured:** a booted production app or any deployed production environment (the app refuses to boot without `DATABASE_URL` and `PRISM_AGENT_URL`), and the demo VM. Kintsugi runs `NODE_ENV=development`, and its running vc-issuer files are byte-identical (full sha256) to the code that was measured.

How: the same five cases through `POST /api/credentials/verify`'s handler with `NODE_ENV` set per call (the verifier reads it at call time, `verifier.ts:410`), on develop `c63cec1f6070`, which differs from the deployed pin in no product file of `services/vc-issuer` or `packages/shared/src/vc`. Rows: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-4th/evidence/` (`L10_probe_residual_live_id_edit.txt`, `probe.env.txt`). Nothing was reassigned.

title: Sourcing systemTest/slot-target.sh with no slot named silently exports slot 1's targets — and preflight leg 13 + the pre-push hook depend on that, so it cannot be fixed in systemTest alone
description:
## BLUF

**No action is needed today, and nothing is broken on the trunk.** This asks for your view on one coordinated change that sits across your files and systemTest.

`systemTest/slot-target.sh`, sourced with **no** slot named, silently exports slot 1's targets. Every harness now refuses an unslotted local run in its own code, so the export itself is the last place a slot is silently defaulted. It can't simply be made to refuse, though: **preflight leg 13 and the pre-push hook source it with no slot, on purpose**, and leg 13's positive control would then refuse every push.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## What happens today

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` resolves `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT="${SECUURA_STACK_SLOT:-${STACK_SLOT:-1}}"`: an unnamed slot becomes **1**.
* `systemTest/slot-target.sh:51` records whether a slot was actually requested (`SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED`), then sources `stack_env.sh` and exports slot 1's `SECUURA_GATEWAY_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_API_URL`, `PERF_BASE_URL`, the `AKTO_*` set and `SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX=-slot1`. `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is only used by `retarget()`.
* The TypeScript harnesses still refuse an unslotted local run, because `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` itself is never exported. Akto and Schemathesis read several of these exports directly, though. [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) is adding their own entry-point guards so they no longer depend on this.

## Why it can't be fixed in systemTest alone

* `.githooks/pre-push:273-285` ([KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail)) sources it deliberately, `|| true`, so the stack-dependent legs probe *this* slot's gateway rather than preflight's own `localhost:6882` default. When the developer's shell names no slot, that is the slot-1 export.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:589-630` (leg 13, [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the)) **measures** the variables `slot-target.sh` exports under `env -i`, **with no slot named**, and has a positive control: an empty list refuses the leg. If `slot-target.sh` refused (exported nothing) when unslotted, that control would fire and **every push would be refused.**

So the three pieces have to move together, and the hook and preflight are yours.

## A possible shape (entirely your call)

1. `slot-target.sh`: when `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is empty and `CI` is not truthy, export nothing target-bearing and print a one-line notice, or `return 2`, matching the refusal the TS harnesses use (`systemTest/fixtures/slot-required.ts:76-91`).
2. **Leg 13:** measure the export set with an explicit slot (e.g. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1` inside the `env -i` subshell) rather than relying on the unslotted default. Its purpose, the full clear-list, is unchanged.
3. **Pre-push:** when no slot is named, say so and let the stack-dependent legs report SKIPPED (the [KS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1046/preflight-passed-is-printed-identically-whether-13-legs-ran-or-10-the) verdict), rather than probing slot 1.

Related: [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (stack tooling not slot-derived end to end), [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the) (leg 13's origin), [KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail) (why the hook sources it).

## Not done here

No change to `slot-target.sh`, the hook or preflight on the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) branch. Peter's ruling (2026-09-29): raise it for you rather than change your files.

Thank you, and apologies for another slot ticket. This one felt worth raising because the obvious fix would have quietly blocked every push.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 2 and 3 — `slot-target.sh` refusing when unslotted is point 2; leg 13 is coordinated with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s spot 4. This ticket had no acceptance section of its own, so these points are its acceptance, together with the three steps of its possible shape.

title: The e2e-v2 harness is platform-k's only browser, portal and accessibility coverage — 222 tests, runnable by hand, named in no gate and absent from the gate inventory
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/` holds **24 spec files and 222 tests** across four tiers — including every browser journey and the only accessibility coverage platform-k has — and it is wired into nothing. It is not in `.githooks/pre-push`, it has no row in the "Manual CI-gate equivalents" table that `KS-685` commissioned, and the workflow its own README points at (`.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`) does not exist on `develop`. Meanwhile the suite people *are* pointed at, `systemTest/playwright`, is API-only: 3 spec files, 11 tests, no browser. So the documented estate says platform-k has a Playwright tier, and the thing that actually opens a browser is the one nobody is told to run. Counted on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026. Nothing was executed — this is about wiring, not results.

## What is there

Measured from the tree, not from the docs:

| Tier | Specs | Tests | What it covers |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `tier1-api` | 12 | 174 | API over HTTP |
| `tier2-smoke` | 5 | 43 | Smoke journeys |
| `tier3-e2e` | 4 | 40 | **Real browser journeys** — issuer, admin, verifier |
| `tier4-a11y` | 3 | 6 | **axe on admin, issuer and verifier** |
| **Total** | **24** | **222** |  |

It is runnable today. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` declares `test`, `test:api`, `test:smoke`, `test:e2e`, `test:a11y`, `install:browsers` and `report`, and `playwright.config.ts` defines the four matching projects (`api`, `smoke`, `e2e`, `a11y`). `@axe-core/playwright` is a devDependency there.

## What is missing

1. **No gate names it.** `grep -rn "e2e-v2" .githooks/pre-push Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` returns nothing. The manual-gate table at `DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` maps *former CI job → local command* for 13 rows and has no row for e2e-v2, and none for accessibility at all.
2. **Its README cites a workflow that does not exist.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` sends the reader to `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`; `git ls-tree origin/develop .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is empty.
3. **The plan doc under-reports it.** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` still says *"only the verifier portal has a tier-4 spec. Issuer + admin coverage is a follow-up."* That follow-up is `KS-44`, which is **Done** — there are three tier-4 specs in the tree today. The row understates the coverage that exists.

## Why it matters

* It is the whole UI answer. Without it the honest statement about platform-k is that no browser opens anywhere in the estate — `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` says so itself, and `DEV-PROCESS.md:141` spells it out: *"Despite the name, this suite drives no browser… Read a green here as '12 API assertions passed', not as 'the portals work'."*
* It is the whole accessibility answer. There is no `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` anywhere in the repo and no axe inside any frontend, so `tier4-a11y` is the only thing that would catch a regression against WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549 — relevant to the same obligations the platform-s side tracks. WCAG 2.2: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549 v3.2.1: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA Directive 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>)
* An ungated suite rots quietly. `KS-557` / `KS-560` are the precedent — the tier reported 126 failures, of which only 11 were real, and the cause was a harness defect that had gone unnoticed. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` keeps that lesson as a standing rule.
* Actions being retired makes this the *only* route to the coverage, not a redundant one.

## Suggested shape

1. Give e2e-v2 a row in the `DEV-PROCESS.md` manual-gate table: the exact command, the pass criterion, and a measured wall-clock — matching the 13 rows already there.
2. Decide the tier split deliberately. `tier4-a11y` is 6 tests and needs only a running stack; it is the cheapest thing in the estate to make routine. `tier3-e2e` is slower and flakier (single-session collisions, `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md` § "Worker-session collisions") so it may belong in a nightly/manual tier rather than a per-push one.
3. Fix the two stale pointers: the dead workflow reference in `tests/e2e/README.md:4`, and the tier-4 row in `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` that `KS-44` has already overtaken.
4. Say in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` where the browser tier actually lives, so "Playwright" stops meaning two different things in the same repo.

## Acceptance

* `DEV-PROCESS.md`'s gate table has an e2e-v2 row (or rows) with a command and a measured time.
* A named person can run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source.
* No document points at `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`, and the tier-4 row reflects the three specs that exist.

## Decision needed before fixing — naming the three Playwright estates

Worth settling the naming in the same pass: `systemTest/playwright` (API-only, 11 tests) and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2` (browser, 222 tests) are both "Playwright", and a third corpus sits at `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` (`KS-734`, In Review — not a workspace member, cannot install from a clean checkout; `KS-1038`, Backlog — races its own lockout). Three Playwright estates with one name is the reason a reader can believe the portals are covered when the suite in the gate never opens a browser. One decision about which survives, which is gated, and what each is called would close this ticket and shrink two others.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` · `playwright.config.ts:29-73` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, `:141` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:316-345` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` · `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` · related: `KS-1076` (Urgent, Todo — no Playwright e2e on a PR since 7 Sep), `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-44` (Done), `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-685`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — no stack started, no suite executed; all counts measured from the tree at that commit. GitHub Actions executes nothing on this repo (billing), so no workflow is a live alternative to the local route.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Hi Kamil, thanks for picking this up. While grounding a plan for this ticket I found six more things that bear on it. Each one was re-checked from source on `develop` **`8c810023f`** (29 Sep), not taken from memory. The most important is #1: once e2e-v2 is named in a gate, a bare local run of it hits slot 1's gateway without saying so. Nothing was edited or run. These are notes for you to take or leave as you see fit.

**1. e2e-v2 has no slot awareness, so a local run naming no slot targets slot 1.**
- `playwright.config.ts:3` defaults `GATEWAY_URL` to `http://localhost:6882`.
- `fixtures/api-client.ts:17` and `:22` do the same for the API and issuer bases.
- Nothing under `tests/e2e-v2` reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` or `STACK_SLOT` (0 matches).

On a shared machine that means another ticket's stack. The systemTest harnesses refuse this case (KS-1016), and e2e-v2 would be the one browser suite that doesn't.

The good news is that `systemTest/slot-target.sh:99` already exports a slot-derived `GATEWAY_URL`, and that's the first variable e2e-v2 reads. So wrapping the gate command, e.g. `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh <N> npm --prefix Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2 run test:a11y`, would target the right stack and hold the per-slot lock with no typed port. A small refusal guard in the config would cover the bare `npm run` case. That's your call.

**2. The runbook the acceptance line relies on is itself stale.** "Run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source" needs these fixed first.
- `RUNBOOK.md`:
  - `:16` lists tier 4 as 2 tests; there are 6.
  - `:189` says a11y is "admin/verifier-only"; issuer is covered too.
  - `:63-72` give the decommissioned Container Apps demo URLs.
  - `:48` hand-rolls `docker compose up -d` rather than `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`.
- `README.md`:
  - 8 lines still carry the dead secuura01 `yellowground-ae96b9b1` URLs, which KS-333 repointed elsewhere.
  - `:24` says "3 Tiers"; there are four.
  - Its credentials table names the retired admin password, which may already fall under KS-965's documentary cleanup if it isn't one of its 55 files.
- `tests/tier4-a11y/README.md`:
  - `:11` says to install axe at `Blockchain/Dev`; it's in e2e-v2's own `package.json` and lock now.
  - `:71-73` describe `button-name` / `color-contrast` as demoted under KS-45; no spec passes `knownIssueRules` any more.
  - `:26` runs against `GATEWAY_URL=https://secuura.com`, a domain we don't own. That's the KS-669 class, in a README rather than the spec.

**3. The admin a11y test needs `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and no e2e-v2 doc says so.** `fixtures/api-client.ts:61` leaves it empty when unset. That's deliberate (KS-964, no published fallback), so this is a docs gap rather than a code bug. But anyone following the runbook will get a failed admin login and nothing telling them why. The variable is documented only in `systemTest/playwright`'s docs.

**4. Stale suppression in `tests/tier4-a11y/_axe.ts:15`.** `// @ts-expect-error — package is not yet in the e2e-v2 lockfile`. It is in the lockfile now (`package-lock.json:16`). Nothing type-checks e2e-v2 (see #5), so this has never surfaced. Under a real `tsc` it would likely become an "unused @ts-expect-error" error.

**5. e2e-v2 has no quality gates of its own.**
- The package has no tsconfig, Prettier config or ESLint config.
- The repo-level `Blockchain/Dev/eslint.config.mjs` only targets `services/`, `packages/`, `sdk/`, `scripts/` and `frontend/`.

So a gate row for e2e-v2 would run specs that nothing lints or type-checks. Worth deciding whether a minimal `typecheck` belongs in the same change.

**6. A timing measurement can't use a current build yet (KS-1380).** The acceptance asks for a measured wall-clock, but `develop` still doesn't build: `packages/shared` locks `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.9 and `@types/pg` 8.23.1, while analytics, billing and governance still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0. Until KS-1380 lands, a timing run would need a stack built at `8af6ab821`, as other slots have been, and the evidence should say so.

**Smaller count notes:**
- The gate table in `DEV-PROCESS.md` has 14 rows at this commit, not 13.
- `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is also cited at `docs/REVIEW_NOTES.md:276` and `CHANGELOG.md:73`, as well as `tests/e2e/README.md:4`. The CHANGELOG line is history and probably wants to stay.

**Related, already tracked:** KS-1393 row 1 (31 uncovered specs; its note already suggests doing it together with this ticket and KS-734), KS-965 (retired admin credential in docs), KS-669 (URLs on domains we don't own), KS-1380 (build).

Happy to help with any of it if useful. Thank you!

title: ci.yml's contract job cannot work — all three Aiken steps use `contracts/secuura` from the repo root, where no such directory exists; deploy-demo.yml has the same steps correct
description:
## BLUF

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds and tests the Aiken contracts with `cd contracts/secuura`, relative to the repo root. There is no `contracts/` at the repo root — the project is at `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` — and the workflow sets no `working-directory` and no `defaults.run.working-directory`. All three steps are wrong the same way: `aiken build` (`:205-208`), `aiken check` (`:210-213`), and the artifact path `contracts/secuura/plutus.json` (`:219`). The job would fail on the first `cd`. Latent today because Actions executes nothing on this repo, and wrong the moment it returns. The fix already exists in the tree: `deploy-demo.yml` does the identical steps with `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura`. Verified on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Aiken appears in exactly two workflows, and they disagree.

**Broken —** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :207  — no such directory from the repo root
          aiken build

      - name: Run contract tests
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :212
          aiken check

      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: contracts/secuura/plutus.json   # :219
```

`grep -n "working-directory\|defaults:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, so there is no job-level default to rescue the relative path.

**Correct —** `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:84-100`, same steps:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Run contract tests
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json
```

So this is a straight port of a fix that was already made once, into the file that did not get it.

## Why it matters

The contracts are the best-covered thing in platform-k and the least exercised. Measured on this commit: **10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks**, including property/fuzz modules built on `aiken-lang/fuzz` v2.2.0 (`contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23`). The only routes to running them are:

* `ci.yml` — broken as above, and dispatch-only anyway (`on: workflow_dispatch`, header *"CI/CD PIPELINE (DISABLED — DEPLOY VIA CURSOR)"*).
* `deploy-demo.yml` — correct, but fenced behind an explicit opt-in input because it targets the Azure Container Apps estate that was deleted in the 2026-07-08 cost pivot (`:35-39`, `:52-70`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` — by hand, as a deploy prerequisite.

`KS-637` (Backlog, High) already records that the nightly Internal Audit has failed 40 runs straight and that *"the Aiken tests run nowhere else"*. This ticket is the narrower, immediately-fixable half: even if a runner came back tomorrow, the general-purpose job would still fail on the `cd`, so the contract tests would still not run. On-chain validators are the one area where a regression is unrecoverable after deploy — `KS-246` (Backlog) holds the external Aiken audit as the mainnet-readiness gate, and an audit is worth much less if the suite it rests on has no working automated home.

## Suggested shape

1. Port `deploy-demo.yml`'s shape into `ci.yml`: `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` on both run steps, and `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json` as the artifact path. Three lines.
2. Consider a job-level `defaults.run.working-directory` if other steps in that job are also root-relative — worth a read of the whole job rather than patching three lines blind.
3. While there: `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` instructs the reader to `cd /Volumes/KK_DEV_Local/NEW STRUCTURE/…`, a former machine's absolute path, and recommends `aiken test` where every script and workflow in the repo uses `aiken check`. Same defect class — a documented path that cannot work anywhere but one laptop.
4. Add a contracts row to the manual-gate table in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, which has none, so `aiken check` has a named local home while Actions is down.

## Acceptance

* `ci.yml`'s contract job reaches `aiken check` from a clean checkout — provable today by running the same commands locally from the repo root, without needing a runner.
* `TESTING.md` contains no machine-specific absolute path and names `aiken check`.
* `DEV-PROCESS.md` lists the contract command with its measured wall-clock, like the 13 rows already there.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Recommend one grep across `.github/workflows/` for every root-relative `cd ` and every `path:` in an upload step, rather than fixing this instance alone. The repo moved to the `Blockchain/Dev/` layout at some point and `deploy-demo.yml` was evidently updated while `ci.yml` was not, so other files may carry the same stale assumption — and none of them can fail visibly while Actions is retired, which is exactly the condition in which this class accumulates.

## References

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:198-219` · `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:79-100` · `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/` (10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks) · `contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23` · `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` · `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` · Aiken docs: [https://aiken-lang.org/](<https://aiken-lang.org/>) · related: `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-246` (Backlog), `KS-552` (Done — the Container Apps pivot that fenced deploy-demo.yml).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the two workflow files were read and compared at that commit; nothing was executed and no runner was invoked. GitHub Actions on this repo answers every job with *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed…"*, so the defect cannot surface until billing is restored.

title: Repo hygiene: 31 spec files under Blockchain/Dev/tests that no Playwright config covers, 708 branches on the remote, and a duplicated website package a major React version behind
description:
## BLUF

Three separate bits of accumulated debt, none urgent, all cheap to decide and none of which anyone will notice until it misleads someone. Grouped because they are one afternoon together and three tickets apart. Measured on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026 — branch count taken from the GitHub API, not the local clone, which is shallow here.

| \# | Where | Seen | Suggest |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` | **31 spec files** sitting directly in that directory, covered by no Playwright config. The repo has exactly three configs — `systemTest/playwright` (`testDir: ./tests`), `tests/e2e-v2` (`testDir: ./tests/tierN`), `tests/e2e` (`testDir: ./tests`) — and none of them resolves to `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` itself. Names read as exploratory leftovers: `admin-sidebar-collapse-{test,fresh,final}.spec.ts`, `issuer-portal-{quick,full,detailed,complete}.spec.ts`, several near-identical variants of one check | Delete, or move the ones worth keeping into `tests/e2e-v2/tests/tierN/` where a config can see them |
| 2 | The remote | **708 branches** (`gh api repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/branches --paginate`), of which 706 are neither `main` nor `develop`. The oldest carry no commit since March; ten are Dependabot branches whose PRs are open and stale | Prune merged and abandoned branches. Worth agreeing a rule — delete-on-merge, plus a sweep for anything with no commit in N months |
| 3 | `secuura-website-package/` | A hand-off bundle whose `source/` duplicates `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/` under the **same package name** `@secuura/website` v1.0.0, drifted to React 18 / Vite 5 / eslint 8 against the live copy's React 19 / Vite 8 / eslint 10; `diff -rq` over the two `src/` trees reports 19 differing files. Nothing outside itself references it — no compose service, no CI, no script | Decide: is it a deliverable that should be generated from `frontend/website` on demand, or dead weight? Either way it should not be a second copy of a shipped app under the same name |

## Why it matters

Each one is a small lie the repository tells a reader.

* **Row 1** — 31 files named `*.spec.ts` look like test coverage. They are not run by anything, cannot fail, and sit next to `tests/e2e`, `tests/e2e-v2` and `tests/connectors`, which are real. Someone counting specs to answer "how well is the admin portal covered?" gets a wrong answer. Same class as `KS-718`, where gitignored snapshots meant a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed.
* **Row 2** — 706 stale branches makes `git branch -r` useless for finding live work and slows every clone and fetch. It also hides the ten stale Dependabot branches behind noise.
* **Row 3** — two packages with the same name and different major versions of React is the shape that produces "it works in my build" confusion. `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` is the only place that mentions it, so nothing in the live docs explains why it exists.

None of this is a defect in the running platform, which is why Low.

## Suggested shape

1. Row 1 is a judgement call per file, but the duplicated-variant names (`-quick`, `-full`, `-detailed`, `-complete`, `-fresh`, `-final`) suggest most can go. Anything worth keeping earns a home under a config; anything else is deleted in one commit.
2. Row 2: agree the retention rule first, then sweep once. GitHub's automatic delete-on-merge setting would stop the recurrence.
3. Row 3: if the bundle is a customer deliverable, generate it from `frontend/website` at release time and stop tracking the copy. If it is not, delete it.

## Acceptance

* Every `*.spec.ts` in the repo is either reachable from a Playwright config or gone.
* Branch count is back to something a person can read, and the rule that keeps it there is written down.
* `@secuura/website` names exactly one package.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest doing row 1 together with `KS-1390` (the e2e-v2 harness is in no gate) and `KS-734` (the `tests/e2e` corpus cannot install from a clean checkout) rather than separately — all three are about which Playwright corpus is real, and the answer to "which of these three trees survives" settles all of them at once. Row 2 is independent and can go any time.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` (31 files) · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` · `secuura-website-package/source/package.json` vs `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/package.json` · `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` · related: `KS-1390`, `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-718` (Done).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — file counts and the package comparison read from the tree at that commit; the branch total came from the GitHub API because the local clone is shallow and its own count differs. Nothing was executed and nothing was deleted.

title: Suggested: move platform-k (outside systemTest + observability) to TypeScript 7.0.2 — five current tools fail on TS 7 (tested), so they would be replaced first
description:
**Owner:** Kamil; the order of work is his call. **Raised:** 2026-09-30, split from [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). **Base:** `develop` @ `4f18c59a8`.
**Companion ticket:** [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) (Peter) covers `systemTest/` + `observability/`. The two tickets reference each other and never overlap.

## 1. Summary

**Suggestion (Peter, 2026-09-30): move the rest of platform-k to TypeScript 7.0.2**, the version systemTest and observability are moving to on [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). This ticket covers the rest of platform-k: 43 `package.json` files, 38 of them on TypeScript 5.x. Whether and when to move is Kamil's decision.

**We can't just change the TypeScript version number and keep our current tools.** Five of the tools we use today **stop working** when TypeScript 7 is installed. This was tested, not assumed (§2). Those tools have to be replaced (or, for tsup, fixed) before TypeScript 7 can go in. The replacements were tested too, and they work.

## 2. Why the tools have to change

### In plain English

The `typescript` package on npm has always contained two things:

1. **The compiler** (`tsc`): you run it to check and build code.
2. **A library**: other tools load it *inside their own code* to compile or check TypeScript for you. Our test runner, our script runner, our linter and our SDK bundler all work this way.

**TypeScript 7 is a rewrite, and it ships only the compiler. The library is gone.** In the `typescript@7.0.2` package the library exports exactly **2** things: `version` and `versionMajorMinor`. In 6.0.3 it exports **2,248**. Microsoft says a new, *different* library will come with TypeScript 7.1, and gives no date. The tools that depend on the old library would then have to be rewritten against the new one.

So any tool that loads TypeScript as a library crashes when TypeScript 7 is installed. It asks for functions that no longer exist. Nothing in our config can fix that, because the code the tool needs is not in the package.

### Proof: the same test on TypeScript 6 and TypeScript 7 (2026-09-30)

**Method:**

* Two fresh projects on Node 24.18.0, identical apart from the TypeScript version.
* Each tool at the version we use today.
* The same two-file source in each: one module and one test.
* Tools installed with `--legacy-peer-deps`, because npm refuses to install ts-jest next to TypeScript 7 at all.
* **TypeScript 6.0.3 is the control:** every tool must pass there, so that a failure on 7 can only be caused by 7.

| Tool (version we use) | What we use it for | Where | Its declared TypeScript support | **TypeScript 6.0.3** | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **typescript-eslint** 8.71 (parser) | Linting TypeScript | `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root | `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`: **excludes 7** | ✅ lints | ❌ `typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.` |
| **ts-jest** 29.4 + jest 29.7 | Running unit tests | governance, originate, referral, vc-issuer | `>=4.3 <7`: **excludes 7** (npm refuses the install) | ✅ 1/1 passed | ❌ `does not expose the JavaScript compiler API required by ts-jest` |
| **ts-node** 10.9 | Running `.ts` scripts | referral, vc-issuer, staking, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `deployment/cardano` | `>=2.7`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fileExists')` |
| **ts-node-dev** 2.0 | Dev server with reload | governance | `*`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ same `fileExists` crash (it runs ts-node underneath) |
| **tsup** 8.5 (`--dts`) | Building the SDK's type declarations | `sdk/javascript` | `>=4.5.0`: claims open support | ✅ `.d.ts` written\* | ❌ `TypeError … (reading 'useCaseSensitiveFileNames')`; no `.d.ts` |

\* **tsup has a second, separate problem.** Its d.ts step injects a `baseUrl` option that TypeScript 6 already rejects as deprecated (`TS5101`) and TypeScript 7 removes entirely. The control passed only with `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"`. tsup's JS build works on both versions; only the type-declaration step fails.

**Result: 5 of 5 tools pass on TypeScript 6 and fail on TypeScript 7.** Two of them say so up front in their declared ranges. The other three *claim* support but crash when run.

### Proof: the replacements work on TypeScript 7

| Replacement | Replaces | Loads the TypeScript library? | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **oxlint 1.86 + oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003** | typescript-eslint | No. Its own parser, plus TypeScript 7's Go compiler for type-aware rules | ✅ lints ([KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) spike: 4 harnesses, 9/9 planted checks) |
| **Vitest 5.0.3** | ts-jest + jest | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ 1/1 passed |
| **tsx 4.23.15** | ts-node, ts-node-dev | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ ran |
| **tsc 7.0.2** itself | — | — | ✅ type-checks the same source clean |

## 3. Options (Kamil's call)

| Option | What it means | Trade-off |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **1. Replace the tools, then TypeScript 7.0.2** (this plan) | typescript-eslint → oxlint; ts-jest → Vitest; ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx; fix or replace tsup's d.ts step | Same TypeScript version as [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). The most work, but every replacement is proven above |
| **2. Keep the tools, run two TypeScripts side by side** | TypeScript 7 for `tsc`; TypeScript 6 installed under the name `typescript` for the tools. ts-jest's own error message recommends this | Two compilers in one tree, which can disagree. **Unproven:** the TypeScript 7 package name ts-jest suggests, `@typescript/native`, **does not exist on npm** (checked 2026-09-30); `@typescript/typescript6` does (6.0.2). Needs its own proof first |
| **3. Stay on TypeScript 6.0.3 for now** | Bump 5.x → 6.0.3, which every current tool supports; revisit when the tools support TypeScript 7.1's new library | The least work now, a second migration later. Leaves platform-k on two TypeScript versions (6.0.3 here, 7.0.2 in systemTest/observability) |

## 4. Scope

**In scope: everything in platform-k except** `systemTest/` **and** `observability/`**.** That is 43 tracked `package.json` files: the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace (services, packages, frontends, sdk, tests, connectors, deployment) and `secuura-website-package`.

**Out of scope:** `systemTest/` and `observability/` → [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint).

## 5. The work, in the proposed order (Option 1)

1. **Linting:** `Blockchain/Dev` root typescript-eslint → oxlint + tsgolint.
2. **Tests:** Jest / ts-jest → Vitest in governance, originate, referral and vc-issuer. [KS-1051](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1051/develop-is-red-on-the-servicesoriginate-jest-suite-and-nothing-catches): originate's Jest suite is already red on `develop`. Also `sdk/javascript` Vitest 1 → 5, and the rest of Vitest 4 → 5.

Review [KS-920](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-920/shared-ships-the-typescript-compiler-and-a-267-mb-dev-tree-into-all-24) alongside this: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into 24 runtime images, and TypeScript 7's compiler is a native per-platform binary.

Settle [KS-1393](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1393/repo-hygiene-31-spec-files-under-blockchaindevtests-that-no-playwright) row 1 (with [KS-1390](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1390/the-e2e-v2-harness-is-platform-ks-only-browser-portal-and) / [KS-734](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-734/the-e2e-playwright-suite-cannot-run-from-a-clean-checkout-testse2e-is)) first, because some of these test corpora may be retired.

title: 13 new advisories block every push: axios 1.18.1 ×12 (7 high — SSRF, proxy bypass, ReDoS, prototype pollution; runtime in services/kyc) and dompurify 3.4.13 — all fixed in range (axios 1.20.0, dompurify 3.4.16)
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 on** `develop`**'s own dependencies again, so no push on this repo succeeds until this lands.** Thirteen advisories published on 2026-09-30 are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`: **twelve against axios 1.18.1 (7 high)** and one against dompurify 3.4.13 (low). **No lock changed to cause this.** No `axios`/`dompurify` line in any lock moved between `377989cf3`, where both legs were rc 0 on 2026-09-30 \~02:45Z, and `4f18c59a8`.

**Every one is fixed inside the declared ranges, so this is a lock refresh, not a manifest bump.** That was checked against each advisory's `vulnerable_versions`, not inferred. `frontend/issuer` already pins axios 1.20.0 / dompurify 3.4.16 and is flagged by neither leg.

Measured at `develop` `4f18c59a8`, twice (2026-09-30 \~22:55Z and 23:11Z, identical ID sets), on Stuart's Mac: `npm run audit:gate` rc 1 (`24 distinct advisories reported, 26 baselined` → 13 NEW); `npm run audit:locks` rc 1 (`1611 distinct packages pinned — 18 advisories match, 6 already baselined` → 12 NEW).

## The thirteen, and the fix version measured for each

Each advisory's `vulnerable_versions` comes from the npm bulk-advisory endpoint, the same data the gates read, and was checked with `semver.satisfies` against both the pinned version and the candidate fix.

| `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8` | high | DoS via unhandled `error` in HTTP/2 session init | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |

| `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8` | moderate | prototype-pollution gadget in fetch adapter alters outbound requests | `>=1.7.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` | moderate | prototype pollution in default instance overrides HTTP method | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32` | moderate | header injection via inherited headers after minimal interceptor | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |

## Where, and why a lock refresh reaches it — measured

| -- | -- | -- | -- |

| `frontend/admin` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.5` | 7 |

`services/kyc` **is runtime exposure, not build-tree only.** axios is in `dependencies`, the image installs with `npm ci --omit=dev` (`services/kyc/Dockerfile:63`), and `src/providers/microsoft-entra-client.ts` imports it for outbound calls. title: Cross-tenant guard fails open for tenantless tokens (connector on /lookup and /stub; access tokens likewise)
description:
## BLUF

**The cross-tenant 404 on** `GET /api/users/lookup` **and** `POST /api/users/stub` **is skipped entirely when the caller's token carries no tenant claim.** Filed from gate54a's finding **N-1374-1** on PR #1374 (KS-1402). **Not reachable through the token exchange today** — read in the code, the exchange always issues a tenant claim — so this is a latent fail-open, not a live hole. It is filed so the guard's shape is fixed rather than left depending on a property of a different component.

## What the gate measured

* **P5: 200 at the head.** A token with no tenant claim reaches the handler and the cross-tenant branch does not fire.
* **P5b: 200 at the base too.** So this is **not a regression introduced by PR #1374** — the behaviour predates it. PR #1374 only widens which token *types* reach the route; it does not change the tenant guard.
* The guard lives at `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:759`, and it has applied to `POST /api/users/stub` since **KS 564**. `GET /api/users/lookup` joins it with PR #1374.
* **Access tokens are in scope too**, not just connector tokens: the guard keys on the presence of a tenant on the caller, not on the token type.

## Why it is not reachable today

The token exchange always issues a tenant claim. That was established **by reading the exchange code, not by exercising it** — so "unreachable" is a code reading, and a change to the exchange (or any other issuer, including a test-only or future path) could make it reachable without anything here changing.

## Fix shape

**Fail closed when the caller has no tenant**: refuse rather than fall through to the unscoped read. The route-level 404-not-200-empty convention should be preserved, so a tenantless caller gets the same 404 a cross-tenant caller gets, and the absence of a tenant is never the thing that widens a read.

## Provenance

* gate54a on PR #1374, finding N-1374-1. Report: `2026-10-05-ks1402-1374-g54a/report.md`.
* Duplicate search before filing (all 571 KS issues, title + description, searched locally): `tenantless` **0 hits**; `cross-tenant` 22; `fails open` 8; `no tenant claim` 1. Must-hit controls `connector` **86** and `tenantId` **24**, impossible-token control `zzqqxx` **0** — so the 0 is a measurement. The two closest neighbours were read and are **different mechanisms**: KS-1091 is an `x-tenant-id` header honoured on originate's direct path; KS-1119 is a `crossTenantLookup` hash fallback in verification.
* **Who builds this is not decided here.**

title: webhooks routes reject connector principals (userId connector:<id>) - 500 after KS 1345, silent 200 before
description:
**BLUF:** a caller authenticating with an API key becomes a **connector principal** whose `userId` is non-UUID (`connector:<connectorId>`), and the webhooks routes cast that value to `uuid`. `GET /api/webhooks` answered **200** `{webhooks: []}` for such a principal before KS 1345 and answers **500 INTERNAL_ERROR** after it. `POST /api/webhooks` already answered 500 for the same principals.

Filed from gate57 finding N-1381-1 (Minor) on PR 1381. Facts only; nothing here was measured live.

## The principal class, traced at source

Measured at `3ce8cd4026a6` by reading the source, with no live reach and no database read:

* the gateway sets the connector userId: `api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:301`
* it exchanges the key for an RS256 JWT minted with the same userId by `generateConnectorToken`: `auth/src/services/jwt.ts:289`
* originate's `authenticate()` accepts that token with no `type` check: `originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:82-104`
* the gateway mounts the webhooks routes behind the `webhooks:manage` scope: `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:442-446`

So a key holding `webhooks:manage` reaches a `${userId}::uuid` cast carrying `connector:...`.

## Behaviour

* before KS 1345: **200** with an empty list, which is a silent wrong answer
* after KS 1345: **500**, logged as an error on every call
* create (`POST`, the `${userId}::uuid` cast in its INSERT, no catch) already answered 500 for these principals, so the list route is now consistent with create

## UNMEASURED

* whether any **issued** API key actually holds `webhooks:manage` — this needs a database read and was not done
* whether any other path mints a non-UUID userId
* live reach: the class was traced at source only

## The open question for the owner

A 500 for a principal-class condition is arguably a mis-mapping. It could reasonably be a 4xx, or the list could be keyed on the organisation rather than the user. That decision is the owner's and was explicitly out of scope for PR 1345, which replaced a silent wrong answer with a loud one.

Related: KS 1345 (the PR that flipped the status), KS 1341 (the same file's error-body work), KS 1256 (connector allow-list failing open — a different defect in the same principal class).

title: revoke answers 400 "already revoked" where 404 belongs if the document is deleted mid-race
description:
**Pre-existing, and narrowed rather than introduced by the KS 1278 change.** Found while building PR #1393.

`updateDocument` in originate's document repository returns `null` for **two** different outcomes:

1. the document was not found — the inner `getDocument` read came back empty (the pre-existing path, `documentRepo.ts:538`);
2. the guarded write changed no row — the KS 1278 `ifStatusIsNot` guard refused it because the row was already in the target status.

The revoke route maps `null` to **400 BAD_REQUEST "Document is already revoked"**. For the ordinary case that is right, and deliberately so: the route 404s and 403s before the write, and 400s on the read, so by the time the guarded write runs the document exists and was not revoked at read time — a `null` can only mean the row became revoked in between, which is exactly the race KS 1278 closes.

**The residual:** if the document is **deleted** between the route's read and the guarded write, outcome 1 fires instead, and the caller is told **"Document is already revoked" with a 400** when the correct answer is **404 Document not found**. The window is narrow — it is a race, not a reachable sequential path — and nothing here is a security or data-integrity problem: no write happens, no provenance row is recorded and no anchor is emitted in either case. It is a response-classification defect only.

**Before KS 1278** the route did not read the write's result at all, so this particular confusion could not arise there; the same single `null` was already ambiguous for every other caller of `updateDocument`, which is why this is recorded as pre-existing in shape and merely surfaced at a new call site.

**What a fix would need.** Separate the two meanings rather than overload one `null` — for example a discriminated result (not-found vs guard-refused vs updated), or a cheap existence re-read on the `null` path before choosing the status code. Both touch every caller of `updateDocument`, which is why it was explicitly left out of KS 1278's scope rather than bolted on.

**Not measured.** No live sweep and no two-session test ran against a real PostgreSQL. The claim above is read off the control flow in `documentRepo.ts` and `routes/documents.ts` plus the mocked cells in PR #1393, not reproduced against a running stack.

Refs KS-1278

title: gate63 minors on the KS-1404 trust-anchor wiring (PR 1388): six Minors carried forward, and the image proof was never run
description:
gate63 returned **GO** on #1388 (KS-1404, the trust-anchor wiring) with six Minor findings, none
blocking and none Major. The PR has merged; this ticket carries the findings forward with the
fix-shape the gate gave for each. Report `a68b1497f421c496…`, 276 lines.

Refs KS-1404

## The six findings

**N-1388-1 — the tsc figure does not reproduce, and no host is named.** The claim "a single
pre-existing tsc error (`rfc3161-verify.ts` TS2345), its line moving 344→349" appears in the commit
message, the PR body and flow 11.4. The gate measured TypeScript 5.9.3 on standalone member
installs and got **rc 0, zero** `error TS` **lines at both** `f01c1da5717f` and `3ce575eeb63c`; the brief
expected 59. Three different counts for one figure, none with a host. The substance holds — **0 NEW**
**errors either way** — but it sits in a client-facing doc with nothing that lets a reader
re-measure it. *Fix-shape:* name the host and install recipe beside each figure, or restate as
"0 new tsc errors (base N / head N on <host>, <recipe>)". The "1937 packages" figure in the PR body
is the same class (the gate measured 349+267 standalone, 346+311 as workspace members; I measured
1,393 package directories in the worktree — three units, one number).

**N-1388-2 — the cheat sheet's corrected note points the wrong way.** The note after the KS-1404
table (`:3776-:3779`) says the wiring row is "below"; it is at `:3748`, **above**. "is now covered"
also reads as though some environment already has the anchor in effect — none does, because no
deploy has happened. *Fix-shape:* "below" → "above", and say "this change wires every
compose-launched box; in effect once deployed". This could not be fixed in the merge-in: Q-M's M1
pins the head's section byte for byte.

**N-1388-3 — cell A does not bind the default's variable name.** Tamper T-NAME
(`${OTHER_VAR:-/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt}`) stays **6/6 green**. The default still
pins D-Trust so verification is unaffected; what breaks silently is the documented override path.
*Fix-shape:* anchor the regex to `^\$\{TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM:-(.*)\}$`. *Regression test:* T-NAME
must red cell A.

**N-1388-4 — no PR cell parses the REAL per-provider file inside the verifier.** C1 hashes the PEM
with the test's own decoder; C2 uses a synthetic root. At the base C1 reds only through A's
precondition, so its own conjunct has no independent red-first. The gate's probe P1/P2 closes the
gap at runtime for this head, as does pre-existing cell 17 (the bundle's block 1 is byte-equal to
this file). *Fix-shape:* commit P1 and P2 as cells —
`parseTrustAnchors(readFileSync(<real file>)).length === 1` at the digest, and a synthetic token with
the real file by path refused "does not chain", never "no trust anchor configured".

**N-1388-5 — a missing anchor is silent until a verify, and** `/health` **carries no anchor state.**
Fail-closed is the safe direction, but a wiring failure reproduces today's "everything refused"
state behind a green `/health`. *Fix-shape:* an `anchors: {configured, count, sha256[]}` block in
`/health`, or a boot-time log line. **Operational consequence now:** the deploy sweep must use the
in-container checks in the gate's C7(a), never `/health`.

**N-1388-6 — the image also ships the two-root bundle** (DigiCert included) at
`/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors.crt`. Q-SCOPE holds and no new privilege is created.
*Fix-shape (optional):* COPY only the per-provider file, or note it in `config/README.md`.

## OWED to the kintsugi deploy round, not done here

**C6, the local image proof, is NOT RUN — the Docker daemon was unreachable (c6 rc 20).** So the
claim that the built image actually contains `/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt` is
unverified. It is owed to the deploy round, which is a separate seat on its own GO. Nothing in
#1388 has been deployed: `TSA_URL` is present-but-empty on both live boxes, which resolves to
D-Trust by code default, and `TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM` is absent on both, so every real RFC 3161
token is still refused with `no trust anchor configured` until a deploy happens.

## Also worth recording, found while merging

`merged8.py` requires nine `targets` as (blob, mode) pairs that the gate's `## MERGE ADDENDUM` line
does not publish. I sourced each by reading `ls-tree` at the head so the mode comes from git rather
than from me, but the gap between what the gate publishes and what the merge tool demands is an
invitation to guess at a value that lands on `develop` permanently.

title: pre-push: when local develop is behind, the gate's changed set comes from a stale origin/develop and refuses a push for systemTest files the author never touched
description:
## BLUF

**The pre-push hook refuses a push for** `systemTest/` **files the author never touched.** When local `develop` is behind, the hook falls back to the shared checkout's `origin/develop` ref for base selection. That ref is stale, so the computed push range includes every `systemTest/` change merged since — and the KS 989 formatting gate then selects a package the author did not touch, finds no deps in a fresh worktree, checks **0 packages** and fails closed. Measured on PR #1394.

This is **not** the same as KS 998 item 1. That item was the gate failing **OPEN** on missing deps (exit 0 when prettier is absent). It now fails **CLOSED**, which is correct and is the discipline working. The defect is upstream of it: the *changed set* names a foreign package in the first place. KS 998 anticipated exactly this tension — "hard-failing presents an environment condition as a gate failure, which is precisely KS 991's" concern — and this is that case arriving.

## Measured

| Range | Paths | of which `systemTest/akto/` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| stale `origin/develop` (`32e058975d4e`) .. head `a94ec8f6a2c6` | 38 | **21** |
| the commit alone (`d784b613c81e` .. `a94ec8f6a2c6`) | 5 | **0** |

The 21 `systemTest/akto/` paths come from KS 1411's merged commits `a964e962c` and `ffca61a3d`, already on develop.

Refs at the time, in the shared checkout:

* local `develop` = `c56dd7c32edf` (2026-10-01)
* local `origin/develop` = `32e058975d4e` (two develops behind)
* the commit's real parent = `d784b613c81e`

No local ref knows `d784b613c81e` as develop, so the fallback is taken.

## Why it had not been seen before

The previous seat's push passed this gate because **its base WAS** `32e058975d4e`, identical to the stale ref, so its range was exactly its own 6 files with 0 `systemTest/` paths and the gate selected no package at all. Every seat whose base is newer than that ref hits this, and each merge into develop widens the range further. It gets worse with time rather than being a one-off.

## The misleading line

On refusal the hook prints:

```
[pre-push] systemTest formatting gate FAILED — fix the files named above.
```

It names **no file**. The gate's own preceding output is explicit that nothing was examined — `NOTHING CHECKED — every selected package was skipped, so no file's formatting was examined. This is NOT a formatting failure: the gate could not run.` The hook line contradicts it and sends the author looking for a formatting defect that does not exist.

## The gate already has what it needs

When the gate does run and fails, it labels the offending file `(NOT in this push — inherited red)`. So the information required to avoid charging an author for a foreign package is present at the point of the message.

## Remedies, in order of narrowness

1. **Derive the gate's changed set from the push's own range** — the real parent, or develop by SHA — rather than a fallback base. Narrowest, and the gate already computes the distinction for its message.
2. **Refresh** `origin/develop` **in the shared checkout.** Fixes the symptom for all seats but is a ref write in a checkout other sessions assert byte-identical across their rounds, so it needs a window with no live seat.
3. **Have each fresh worktree install the four gated** `systemTest` **packages** before its first push. Works, but it is four installs per worktree for a gate that should not have selected them.

## Reproduce

```
git -C <worktree> diff --name-only 32e058975d4e a94ec8f6a2c6 | grep -c '^systemTest/akto/'   # 21
git -C <worktree> diff --name-only d784b613c81e a94ec8f6a2c6 | grep -c '^systemTest/'        # 0
bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh < <the first range>   # 0 checked, 1 skipped, FAIL
```

After `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in `systemTest/akto` the same command reads `1 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 0 failed`, rc 0 — and a planted formatting defect in an akto file still returns rc 1, so that green is a measurement and not an install that silenced the gate.

Four `systemTest` packages declare `format:check` (akto, api-explorer, performance, playwright) and all four have `node_modules` absent in a fresh worktree, so any of them can be the one selected.

Discovered 2026-10-05 raising PR #1394 (Refs KS 723). Host Kamil's Mac Studio (2).

nodes.body:
## Reproduced end to end, and KS-998 item 1 changes what it costs — pull request [#1532](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1532)

Facts only, from the new `ks998_pre_push_stale_base_hint.test.sh` (a real hook and the real gate against a local bare remote).

* **The shape.** A branch with no upstream whose base already contains trunk commits that the local `origin/develop` ref does not (cut from a teammate's `feature/base`; `origin/develop` still at the old commit). The hook diffs `merge-base(origin/develop, HEAD)..HEAD`, so the changed set names a package the author never touched.
* **Before item 1, on unmodified develop:** that push **lands on the remote** (the untouched package is a named SKIP and the author's own package passes).
* **After item 1:** the same push is **refused for the package the author never touched**, naming the package and the path that selected it, and saying *your origin/develop may be stale: run git fetch origin and push again*. After `git fetch origin` the same push goes through. So item 1 makes a stale base able to refuse a correct push where it only used to skip.
* **Also reproduced:** the hint is shown when the base is not the branch's own counterpart at the remote (no upstream, or an upstream that is the trunk, e.g. `git checkout -b feature/x origin/develop`), and not shown when it is.
* **This ticket is still the fix for the input.** The hint is a mitigation, not the fix. The classification reads `HEAD` and `@{upstream}` as the changed set does, so it shares KS-1483's blind spot for a push of a ref that is not checked out.

title: updateDocument: a UUID-addressed update matches 0 rows and silently writes nothing for the 12 unguarded callers
description:
A `updateDocument(id, ...)` call whose `id` is the platform UUID (the primary key) resolves the row on the READ but matches **0 rows** on the WRITE, because the UPDATE keys on `external_id`. For the one guarded caller this surfaced as a wrong 400 and is fixed under KS-1278. **For the other 12 production callers there is no guard, so the function returns the updated record and the caller reports success while the database was never written.**

Instrument for the mechanism: read of `documentRepo.ts` at `4a1620588819` (blob `e29ebcdd79c2`) plus the caller census below. The silent-success behaviour for the unguarded callers is **inferred from the same code path, not separately probed — unmeasured against a live database.**

## Why a UUID reaches these callers

`fromDbRow` returns `id: row.external_id || row.id` and `documentUuid: isValidUuid(row.external_id) ? row.external_id : row.id`. When `external_id` is not UUID-shaped, `documentUuid` IS the primary key, and the API hands clients that value. `getDocument` accepts it via its uuid fallback. The UPDATE does not.

## Caller census

Measured with `git grep -n 'updateDocument(' <sha> -- Blockchain/Dev`, read from a file. 24 lines at `4a1620588819`, 23 at the branch base `32e058975d4e`. Controls: a must-hit token returned 2 files; a nonsense token returned rc 1 with 0 lines.

Breakdown: **13 production calls**, 1 definition, 1 comment line, 9 test-file lines.

| file:line @ 4a1620588819 | id expression | where the id comes from | can carry a platform UUID | opts | base behaviour on a UUID id |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| routes/documents.ts:800 | `id` | `:639` create path, `documentUuid ?? doc-<ts>` | no in practice | none | row inserted with that external_id, so the key matches |
| routes/documents.ts:881 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | none | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:913 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:928 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | none | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:1224 | `id` | `req.params` at `:1188` | **YES** | none | **0 rows, returns the record, reports success** |
| routes/documents.ts:1408 | `id` | `req.params` at `:1327` | **YES** | none | **0 rows, returns the record, reports success** |
| routes/documents.ts:2398 | `id` | `req.params` at `:2353`, route `/:id/revoke` | **YES** | ifStatusIsNot | 0 rows, returns null, wrong 400 — FIXED under KS-1278 |
| routes/verification.ts:396 | `String(docId)` | `persistHealedAnchor` at `:389` | **YES** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:183 | `documentId` | parameter, threaded from the create path | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:258 | `documentId` | `opts.documentId` | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:295 | `documentId` | `opts.documentId` | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:376 | `document.id` | a DocumentRecord | **YES when external_id is NULL** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:414 | `document.id` | a DocumentRecord | **YES when external_id is NULL** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |

So **12 of the 13** keep `WHERE external_id` unchanged under KS-1278, and **5 of those 12** are reachable with a value that matches no row. The NULL-`external_id` case is already in gate65's own NOT TESTED list.

This census **corrects the figure of 14** used while ruling KS-1278: 14 counted the 13 production calls plus one non-call line. The measured count is 13 production callers, 1 opted in, 12 others.

## What was searched before filing

Linear team KS titles, case-insensitive: `updateDocument` 0 hits, `documentRepo.ts` 0 hits, `external_id` 0 hits. Must-hit control: `revoke` returned 18. Inverted control: a nonsense symbol returned 0. So the filter discriminates and this class was genuinely unfiled. `searchIssues` was not used as an absence instrument.

## Not fixed here

KS-1278's round 2 narrows the fix to the single opted-in revoke path on purpose, so the blast radius is one caller. Changing the other 12 needs its own decision: for an unguarded caller a 0-row update is currently indistinguishable from a successful one, so simply re-keying them would change what several callers report. Refs KS-1278.

title: unhandledRejection posture as shipped differs from KS-546's: setupGracefulShutdown has no callers, and originate survives rejections while the gateway's comment cites it as fail-fast
description:
## Summary

[KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) ruled that the api-gateway **survives** unhandled rejections and that *everything else stays fail-fast*. On `develop` `f556373b9`, two things don't match that ruling. First, the shared wrapper that would make every other service log and apply its mode, `setupGracefulShutdown`, has **no callers**, so [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify step can't be observed. Second, **originate survives** unhandled rejections: it registers its own listener, which logs and does not exit. The gateway's own comment cites originate as an example of fail-fast. Either originate is a second, undocumented `survive` service, or it's a bug. That's a ruling for you, not something to settle in systemTest.

These came up while scoping [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture), the systemTest ticket that pins the [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) posture. They're outside systemTest, so they're filed here for you.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

### 1. `setupGracefulShutdown` has no callers

* It's defined at `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts:99` and re-exported at `utils/index.ts:10`. No service imports it: `git grep setupGracefulShutdown -- Blockchain/Dev` finds only the definition, the re-export, a JSDoc example and the comment below.
* The code now says so: `packages/shared/src/index.ts:22-23` reads *"the gateway consumes these directly (the setupGracefulShutdown wrapper itself has no live consumers today)."*
* So the line [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify section says to check, `Graceful shutdown handlers registered (unhandledRejection mode: X)` (`gracefulShutdown.ts:177`), never prints. *"All other services log* `exit`*"* can't be observed on any stack.
* The only live path is the gateway, which wires `resolveUnhandledRejectionMode` + `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` itself (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1161-1171`) and logs `unhandledRejection mode: <mode>`.

### 2. originate is not fail-fast for unhandled rejections

* `services/originate/src/index.ts:72-77` calls `process.on('unhandledRejection', …)`, which logs, calls `trackError`, and **returns**. It never exits.
* Registering any listener disables Node's fatal default, so originate keeps running after an unhandled rejection. Its `uncaughtException` handler just below it *does* exit.
* The surrounding comment ([KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure)) explains why it logs: so a crash leaves a trace. It doesn't say surviving is intended.
* `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1159-1160` says *"Every other service keeps fail-fast (originate's own handler, or Node 20's fatal default)"*. That's backwards for originate. It also names Node 20, but the images are `node:24-alpine` (`services/originate/Dockerfile`).

### 3. Scope check

Only two `process.on('unhandledRejection'` registrations exist under `services/`: the gateway ([KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything), intended) and originate. Every other service has no listener, so it falls back to Node 24's fatal default and does fail fast. The `routes/verification.ts:1367` hit is a comment, not a registration.

### Not checked

Nothing was run against a stack. This is a code read only. No Platform S code is involved.

+++

## What's needed (your call)

1. **originate:** decide whether it should **survive** or be **fail-fast**.
   * If survive: say so in [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s terms. Ideally declare `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` for originate too, so the posture lives in config rather than an inline listener.
   * If fail-fast: wire originate through `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` (mode `exit`) so it still leaves the [KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure) trace before exiting.
2. `setupGracefulShutdown`**:** either have the services call it, so every service logs its mode, or delete the wrapper and amend [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify step to what can actually be observed.
3. **The gateway comment** at `api-gateway/src/index.ts:1159-1160`: correct it to match whatever (1) decides, and fix the Node version.

## How systemTest will use the answer

[KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture)'s boot-posture assertion checks that the gateway logs `survive` and a sampled non-gateway service does not. Today the only service that logs a mode at all is the gateway. [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) will assert the posture as shipped and cite this ticket. When you rule on (1) and (2), that assertion moves with your ruling, red→green.

Refs: [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) (the ruling, Done) · [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) (outage class) · [KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure) (originate's logging rationale) · [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) (systemTest pin). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.
