**Where and when**
- **Develop control:** clean develop worktree at **`5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492`**, built **2026-10-26 12:20:09 UTC**, platform-k slot 2 on Peter's Mac. Pre-merge sweep 12:23-12:40, seed 2391897950.
- **The other three runs:** platform-k slot 1, build `65ced3173`, which is develop `5f6899918` plus a systemTest-only commit from KS-1641 (no product code differs). Built 2026-10-26 11:17:45 UTC. They were the pre-merge sweep at 11:38-11:56 and the two targeted re-checks at 12:18 and 12:20.
- Every container was healthy with RestartCount 0, and image revision labels matched each build.

**Test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_status_compliance.py::TestStatusCodeServerErrors::test_no_crash_on_invalid_input`, failing with:

> `AssertionError: KS-1042: GET /documents/<'..%2F..%2Fetc'> returned 200, expected a 4xx | assert 400 <= 200`

The request is authenticated (ISSUER_ADMIN), sent to `/api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc`.

**Not measured:**
- whether the gateway or an upstream normalised the path, and which route answered (for example the document list);
- the response body.

Both are needed to tell whether this is harmless routing or a path reaching a handler it shouldn't.

*Added on Peter's instruction, 2026-10-26.*

**BLUF:** the dot-segment and `%2F` spellings this ticket measured at the api-gateway also act one layer earlier, at the nginx gateway. There, two encoded-slash dot segments take a request out of `/api/` altogether. `GET /api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc` answers **200 with the issuer portal's HTML** instead of a gateway 4xx. A KS-1042 live test found it on 2026-10-21 (slot 1, develop `280fdbcd1`).

| Authenticated `GET` (ISSUER_ADMIN) | Answer |
| -- | -- |
| `/api/documents/..%2Fetc` (one level) | **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Invalid document id in path…". The request stays in `/api/` and the gateway refuses it. |
| `/api/documents/..%2F..%2Fetc` | **200** `text/html`, the SPA's `index.html` |
| `/api/documents/..%2F..%2Fnope-ks1042` | **200** `text/html`, the same page |

**Inference, not verified in nginx's logs:** nginx decodes `%2F` and resolves the dot segments before matching a `location`. So `/api/documents/../../etc` normalises to `/etc`, misses `location /api/` (`docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:184`) and falls through to the SPA location.

**What this does not show:** any exposure. What came back is the public SPA shell. Not measured: whether a crafted spelling can reach a different `/api/` upstream than its prefix suggests (for example `/api/<a>/..%2F<b>/…`). That is the useful next probe, alongside this ticket's step 1.

**Acceptance criteria (in addition to this ticket's own)**
1. **Automated test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_status_compliance.py::TestStatusCodeServerErrors::test_no_crash_on_invalid_input` (KS-1042) drives `..%2F..%2Fetc`. It is **red today** on the 200 and goes green when the edge refuses the request with a 4xx. The front-door normaliser this ticket proposes, answering 400, would do it.
2. **Docs updated:** none expected. If the nginx config changes, update its own comments.
3. **systemTests updated:** nothing beyond the KS-1042 test above.

## Step 1 of the recommendation, measured on the real stack (2026-10-12 09:05Z, Seat K 4th, read-only)

**Result: no dot-segment or extra-segment spelling returned anything but a refusal to an unauthenticated caller on Kintsugi.** 27 unauthenticated `GET`s through the public front door (`https://secuura02-kintsugi.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com`), no credential, three bearerAuth mounts, nine spellings each (canonical, `/`, `/.`, `/./`, `/..`, `/%2e`, `/%20`, `/%2F`, and a `./` before the last segment): `/api/credentials/abc`, `/api/referrals/abc`, `/api/governance/proposals`. **All 27 answered `401 UNAUTHORIZED`**: no 2xx, no 3xx.

* **The instrument could have shown a bypass:** controls in the same run: `/health` answered `200`, and `/api/zzz-not-in-spec` and `/api/zzz-not-in-spec/.` answered `404 NOT_FOUND`.
* **What the 401s tell us.** Kintsugi does not yet run KS-1469, so the gateway's spec gate still skips the trailing-slash spelling; that spelling (`/api/credentials/abc/`) was also `401`. So the refusal comes from the layer behind the gate (the per-route `authenticateToken` and the upstream's own auth), which is the layer this ticket asked about: it held for every spelling tried. I cannot tell from the status alone which of the two answered.
* **Limits, stated:** three `GET` mounts only. Not tried: the other optional-auth mounts (`nft`, `billing`, `certifications`), any method other than `GET`, or any authenticated caller (an authenticated caller with a valid token is not a bypass of anything). Demo is unmeasured (off-limits). The stub-based reproduction in this ticket showed the gateway forwards these spellings verbatim; this shows that, on this stack, forwarding them does not yield an unauthenticated 2xx.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatK-4th/live/dotseg_probe.py` and `dotseg_probe_rows.json`.

**Re-rating.** I filed this at P3 as "a skipped layer with an unmeasured tail". With the tail measured on three mounts I am lowering it to **P4**: defence in depth, not a demonstrated bypass. The front-door normaliser recommended above is still the clean way to close the class, and the measurement should be repeated for the remaining mounts and methods before this is closed rather than kept open indefinitely. Seat K 4th changed the priority on its own ticket; Wednesday can restore it.

Another measured fact for this ticket, from the Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479), note N4: `/api/v1/v2/verification/../verification/verify` is forwarded upstream with the **literal `..`** in the path. It is the same class as the spellings above, and it is now **counted** by the verification limiter (the gate's 25 bounded spellings include `/./` and `/../` inside the tail). Whether the spec gate or nginx normalises it before the gateway is unchecked by the gate; the question this ticket already asks (does any real upstream router route a dot-segment path to a handler?) covers it. The recommended front-door normaliser would close it too.

title: pre-push gate: pushing a branch that is not checked out skips the preflight, because the hook diffs HEAD and not the pushed commits
description:
**BLUF.** `.githooks/pre-push` decides whether to run the preflight from `HEAD` (`git diff --name-only "@{upstream}" HEAD` at `:80`, `"$_b" HEAD` at `:184`), and the preflight then tests the working tree. The refs git hands the hook on stdin are read only for the force-push check (`:48-69`). So `git push origin some-other-branch`, with a clean `HEAD` on another branch, skips the preflight for a `Blockchain/Dev` change in the branch actually pushed. The push lands with no `[pre-push]` output. Pre-existing; identical in the tip's hook, `302d8d081` and the KS-884 fix. Found by the KS-884 ref matrix (scenario S15).

**Recommendation.** Make the hook judge what is pushed, not what is checked out. Read the stdin lines (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>`) and:

1. Compute the changed set per pushed ref from `<local sha>` against its base, not from `HEAD`.
2. Because the preflight tests the working tree (HEAD), also FAIL CLOSED: when a pushed `<local sha>` is not `HEAD` and it changes `Blockchain/Dev`, refuse with a clear message ("check out what you push, or push with the bypass deliberately"), rather than run the wrong tree. Running the preflight in a temporary worktree of the pushed sha is the heavier alternative.
3. Handle the shapes the stdin loop already skips: branch deletes (`<local sha>` all zeros), brand-new remote branches, tags (`refs/tags/...`), and multi-ref pushes (`--all`, several refspecs).
   Add a test cell per shape (red against today's hook for the unchecked-out branch). Not built here; this is the larger of the two KS-884 follow-ups because it changes what the hook refuses.

**Detail.**

* Measured 2026-10-12 by Seat F 17th. Scenario S15: `b-other` carries a `Blockchain/Dev` change, `HEAD` is back on a clean branch at `origin/develop`, then `git push origin b-other` to a local bare remote. Result SKIP for the tip's hook, `302d8d081`'s hook and the KS-884 fix; the saved push output is only git's two `To ...` / `* [new branch]` lines, so nothing tells the pusher the gate did not run.
* Why it is more than a corner case: `git push origin <name>` from a different checkout is an ordinary shape (a seat pushes a sibling branch, or a script pushes a ref), and the result reads like a green push.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatF-17th/ks884_ref_matrix.sh` (S15) and `ks884_matrix_full_OLD.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_CURRENT_302d8d0.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_FIXED.txt`.
* Related: KS-884 (PR #1474). Not caused or changed by it.

nodes.body:
## BLUF

**This ticket's BLUF is stale, and its own Recommendation item 2 is already in the code.** The hook no longer *skips* the preflight for a branch that is not checked out — it **REFUSES the push**, with very nearly the message this ticket asked for. Measured today at develop `ce98606212e4e0dce8212d4541ffff2484f2217b` while I was trying to land #1597's author-corrected commit. Item 1 (judge the pushed sha, not `HEAD`) and item 3 (the skipped ref shapes) are a different matter and I have **not** measured them.

## Detail — what the hook does now

`.githooks/pre-push:351-359` at `ce98606212e4`:

```sh
if [ -n "$changed" ] && [ "$_tip" != "$_head_c" ]; then
    echo "[pre-push] REFUSED — this push sends ${_lr} ($(_short "$_tip")), which changes Blockchain/Dev" >&2
    echo "           (or cannot be shown not to), but HEAD is ${_hd}." >&2
    echo "           The preflight tests the CHECKED-OUT tree, so it cannot vouch for what you are pushing." >&2
    echo "           Check out what you push (git checkout <branch>) and push again," >&2
    echo "           or push with the bypass deliberately (git push --no-verify) and say so on the PR." >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

That is this ticket's item 2 almost verbatim — *"refuse with a clear message (**check out what you push, or push with the bypass deliberately**)"*.

**Observed, not inferred.** Pushing `refs/heads/feature/ks-1634-…` while the worktree sat detached at develop, 2026-10-19T04:33:28Z: refused in **6 seconds**, before any leg ran — no `PREFLIGHT` line in the log at all. The `ALLOW_FORCE=1` non-fast-forward check *passed* first (`[pre-push] ALLOW_FORCE=1 — proceeding with a non-fast-forward push, deliberately.`), and then this guard refused. **The remote ref did not move.**

So the BLUF's *"The push lands with no `[pre-push]` output"* is no longer true for the `Blockchain/Dev`-changing case this ticket is about. Whoever picks this up should **re-measure scenario S15 before writing any code**: what remains open here is item 1 (the changed set is still computed from `HEAD`, not from the pushed `<local sha>`) and item 3 (deletes, new remote branches, tags, multi-ref pushes) — not the refusal.

## One behaviour worth a decision while this ticket is open

The guard's predicate is `[ -n "$changed" ] && [ "$_tip" != "$_head_c" ]`, and `$changed` is computed **from the push's base**, not from **the ref the push replaces**. So a force-push whose tree is **byte-identical to the ref it overwrites** — nothing new reaching `Blockchain/Dev` at all — is refused on the same footing as one that rewrites the service.

That is exactly the case I hit: `8ec96bbac643` → `8f3310c6ed85`, trees **both** `b64be7e50092c55af3d6670f065c2a75601ec584`, and `git diff` between the two commits is **0 bytes** (control: the same reader on that commit against develop returns 223,355 bytes, so it is not a broken reader). The two commits differ only in their author and committer lines. Nothing the preflight could test has changed, yet neither worktree can satisfy the hook: at the branch, leg 14 reds on the pre-fix `ALLOW_FORCE` leak (KS-1638, fixed only in `ce98606212e4` and later); at develop, this guard refuses.

**Not asking for a change here** — recording the shape, because an author-only amend is a real operation and it currently has no path through the hook that is not `--no-verify`. If item 1 lands (judge the pushed sha against the ref it replaces), this case resolves by itself.

Measured by Seat R 52nd (lane Secuura/Blockchain-R), 2026-10-19. Related: KS-1638 (merged `ce98606212e4`), KS-1643, KS-1634.

**Staying open after #1545.** Item 3 of KS-998 merged to `develop` as `0662f7213cc08d962b745fa6998fc2a3f47499a5`. Taking the three recommendation sentences in order, against what is now on develop:

1. *"Compute the changed set per pushed ref from `<local sha>` against its base, not from `HEAD`."* — **on develop**, from item 2 (#1540, `405e33a1061310662b10245c5154c3d75c49f0f4`). The hook reads the ref lines git hands it and judges each pushed sha: `remote_sha..tip` when the branch exists at the remote, else the upstream, else the merge-base with the trunk.
2. *"Also FAIL CLOSED: when a pushed `<local sha>` is not `HEAD` and it changes `Blockchain/Dev`, refuse."* — **on develop**, also from #1540, and the remedy wording is now pinned by a cell (mutant X15, killed by name: *"…remedy is 'check out what you push'"*).
3. *"Handle the shapes the stdin loop already skips: deletes, brand-new remote branches, tags, multi-ref pushes; a cell per shape."* — **on develop**. The Opus gate on #1545 re-measured these against real bare remotes: deletion lands silently (R31), a tag is judged by its commit (R4/R4c/R4d), a detached-HEAD push runs the preflight with a banner (R32), a three-ref push with one RED ref is refused (R30), and an unborn HEAD is refused with the corrected wording (R35).

**Why it does not close yet.** #1545 also added the "already on the remote" skip (`.githooks/pre-push:120`), which runs *before* the per-ref base diff. That is Minor 2 of the Opus gate on #1545, and it partially re-opens sentence 1's guarantee for shapes this ticket exists to cover — the hook does not judge every pushed ref while that skip can pre-empt it. Measured by the gate on this exact code, which is now develop:

- **R20 / R21** — fast-forwarding an existing branch onto an already-pushed RED commit: `rc 0`, the branch moves, **no gate and no preflight**. Develop before #1545 refused both, judging `remote_sha..tip`.
- **R22 / R22b / R23** — a **stale** tracking ref (the remote branch was deleted after a squash merge, or force-moved): a RED commit the remote **no longer has** lands with `rc 0` under a note saying it is already on the remote. The `fetch --prune` controls are refused, so the skip is the cause. 4 of 789 tracking refs in the project clone are already stale.

Both shapes need the RED commit to have reached the remote once (`--no-verify`, a clone without `core.hooksPath`, or a web edit), which is why the gate rated it Minor rather than Major.

**The cure is tracked on KS-1605** (item 2 there): apply the `onremote` skip only to refs the remote does not have yet (`_jr_rsha` empty or zero), *after* step 1, so existing-branch updates keep their `remote_sha..tip` judgement — plus the correction of the comment at `.githooks/pre-push:116-119`, which currently claims a stale ref can "never" lead to a pass. Cells R20 and R22.

So: sentences 1-3 are delivered, and this ticket should close when KS-1605 item 2 is on develop, not now. Nothing here deploys — developer tooling only.

BLUF: KS-1483 is folded into KS-998 item 2, pull request 1540 (head c6d103ffc4692cb075287eb8143715989abeafab). The hook now reads the ref lines git hands it and judges each pushed sha, instead of deciding from HEAD; a pushed sha that is not HEAD and changes Blockchain/Dev is refused with a message saying to check out what is pushed; a deleted ref is skipped, a tag is judged by its commit.

The pull request is not linked to this ticket automatically because the branch name carries only the KS-998 id. Ticket state unchanged; the pull request is awaiting the gate.

## Cross-reference from KS-998 item 2: the formatting gate's half of this defect will be fixed there; the PREFLIGHT half stays here

Facts only, from the KS-998 items 1+2 planning pass (Seat K 8th, 2026-10-13). This ticket already states
the defect precisely — `.githooks/pre-push:80` diffs `HEAD` and the pushed ref lines (`:48-69`) are read
only for the force-push check. I was about to file a duplicate P3 for the same thing and the board
search stopped me; recording the relationship instead.

- **KS-998 item 2** (ruled variant A′, Opus tier) makes the hook **keep `local_sha` per pushed ref** and
  archive that sha for the systemTest formatting gate. That fixes the **formatting gate's** half of
  "judges HEAD, not what is sent". It does **not** touch the preflight's changed set (`:80`, `:184`),
  which is this ticket's.
- Measured while planning: `all_changed` (`:80`) feeds **both** the Blockchain/Dev filter that decides the
  preflight **and** the systemTest filter that decides the formatting gate, so once item 2 lands the two
  would be computed from different bases (pushed shas vs `HEAD`) unless this ticket lands with or after
  it. Worth sequencing deliberately rather than discovering the divergence later.
- Related and not the same: KS-1482 (rename-out shows only the new path) and KS-1422 (a stale
  `origin/develop` makes the formatting gate select a package the author never touched).

title: Wallet login: two simultaneous first logins for one address issue a token for an id that is not in the database (4 of 5 rounds)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing on develop, found by the Opus gate on #1476 (KS-806) and filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. Two concurrent FIRST wallet logins for the same address both succeed with 200, only one row is created, and in 4 of 5 measured rounds one of the two responses carries an access token for a user id that does **not exist** in `users`. `userRepo.createUser` returns the object it was given, not the row `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` actually stored, and `getOrCreateWalletUser` trusts it.

## Recommendation

Make the wallet create path read back the stored row (or `RETURNING` it) and use THAT id, or fail and retry the lookup when the returned row's `wallet_address` does not match. Add a concurrency cell against a real Postgres (Seat J's native recipe). This is the same "fabricated object, not in the table" class KS-806 names; #1476 removes the collision between different wallets but not this race between two requests of the same wallet.

## Detail

* **Measured** (gate probe P4, real Postgres 15 built from the repo's init SQL + 49 migrations, app role `secuura_app` under RLS, the real route, real `/register`, real `userRepo`, real 039 lookup): 5 rounds of `Promise.all([login(A), login(A)])` for a fresh address A. Every round: both statuses 200, exactly 1 row. `idsInDb` per round: `[true,true]` (same id) once, then `[false,true]`, `[true,false]`, `[true,false]`, ... so in 4 of 5 rounds one returned id is not in the table. The token for that id then works until something looks the user up.
* **Where:** `services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts` `getOrCreateWalletUser` (lookup, then `userRepo.createUser(user)` with a fresh `uuidv4()`), and `userRepo.createUser`'s upsert on `email_lookup_hash` returning its input.
* **Not caused by #1476:** the same shape exists on develop; with the old 8-character email the collision made it worse (every second wallet), with the new email it only happens for a true double submit of one address.
* Evidence: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/logs/probe_head.out` (line 4) and `gateprobe1476.test.ts` (cell P4).

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1476, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `b4615b4a35be26fb`), Minor-4; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1460 (`updateUser` callers that discard the result), KS-1052.

title: api-gateway: every per-IP limiter keys on the last X-Forwarded-For hop (trust proxy 1), so a caller that reaches the gateway without nginx rotates that hop and gets a fresh bucket each request
description:
## BLUF

`index.ts:108` sets `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`, so every IP-keyed control in the gateway (the global limiter at 300 per minute, the verification limiter, the login limiters, the brute-force guard) keys on the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` hop. The Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479) **reproduced against the gateway directly** that rotating that last hop gets a fresh bucket each time, identically on base and on #1483, so the per-IP bound is only as strong as who can set the last hop. Pre-existing, not caused by KS-1479. **Whether it is reachable in practice depends on whether anything reaches the gateway without nginx appending the hop; that part is unmeasured.**

## What the repo's own configs say (READ, not measured)

* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:133`, `nginx-production.conf:296` and `nginx-demo.conf:334` all set `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, which **appends** nginx's `$remote_addr` to whatever the client sent. Through that nginx, the last hop is the address nginx saw (and on demo, `nginx-demo.conf:100-107` resolves it from `X-Forwarded-For` only for trusted source addresses with `real_ip_recursive on`). A client behind it can prepend hops but cannot choose the last one.
* The gate's reproduction sent the header **straight to the gateway**, with no nginx in front. So the exposure is any path that reaches the gateway without that nginx: a published gateway port, another container on the compose network (the comment at `nginx-demo.conf:89` already names this for nginx's own rate limit), or an ingress that passes the header through.
* The related finding on how the IP is derived at all is **KS-618** (archived, Backlog, P2): on demo every IP-keyed control saw the Docker bridge address because two proxy hops met `trust proxy 1`; its recommended fix (an explicit trusted-subnet list rather than a hop count) is also the fix shape here. Its nginx realip half appears to be in `nginx-demo.conf` now; whether it is deployed on demo and Kintsugi is not known to me.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure first, read-only, after the Kintsugi window:** through the real public front door, send several `GET /api/credentials/abc` (answered 401 by the gateway's own gate, after the global limiter) with different client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` first hops and read the `RateLimit-Remaining` header each time. If it keeps decrementing across them they share one bucket (the edge fixes the hop); if it resets, the hop is client-controlled at the real ingress. This needs no credential and writes nothing but limiter counters. Also check the compose files and VM firewalls for any published gateway port.
2. **If any path reaches the gateway without nginx:** replace the hop count with an explicit trusted-proxy list (KS-618's recommendation), so `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured only from the nginx peer.
3. Add a cell that sends a forged last hop to the real app with `trust proxy` configured as intended. Priority P2 as Wednesday ruled; it may drop to P3 if step 1 shows the edge appends the hop.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1483, 2026-10-12, note N3 and its XFF probe (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1483/verdict.md`, `evidence/`): "the key is the last hop; rotating the last hop bypasses the limit, as on develop; rotating the first hop with the last fixed does not". Edge configuration was not checked by the gate.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `X-Forwarded-For`, `trust proxy`, `last hop`, `XFF`, `x-real-ip`, `set_real_ip_from`, `spoof`: nearest is KS-618 (above); nothing covers a client-chosen last hop.

Related: KS-618, KS-1479, KS-946, KS-1469.

nodes.body: Priority changed P2 to **P3** by Seat K 4th, on Wednesday's instruction (09:05Z) and for the reason in the measurement comment above: at the real Kintsugi front door a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` hop does not move the bucket (ten requests, `RateLimit-Remaining` 1999 to 1990 with no increase), and no compose file publishes `api-gateway`. The exposure is a caller reaching the gateway without nginx, which I could not find; demo and the VMs' own firewalls remain unmeasured.

## Measured since filing (2026-10-12, Seat K 4th, read-only)

**1. The real front door, measured on Kintsugi at 09:03Z (the window had closed).** Ten unauthenticated `GET`s to `https://secuura02-kintsugi.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com/api/credentials/abc`, each answered `401` by the gateway's own gate **after** the global limiter, so `RateLimit-Remaining` shows the bucket: three with no `X-Forwarded-For`, three with a different client-supplied single hop (`203.0.113.11` to `.13`), one with two client-supplied hops, then three with no header again. **`RateLimit-Remaining` fell strictly 1999, 1998, 1997, 1996, 1995, 1994, 1993, 1992, 1991, 1990, with no increase at all.** A client-supplied hop did not move the bucket; the edge, not the client, decides the key. Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatK-4th/live/xff_probe.py` and `xff_probe_rows.json`. Writes: none beyond in-memory limiter counters; no credential was used. **Demo was not probed** (off-limits until its window closes).

**2. Published ports, from the compose files in the tree.** No compose file publishes `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml`, `.production.yml`, `.staging.yml`, `.e2e.override.yml`, `.cache.yml`, `.ci.yml`, `.isolation.yml`). Only `nginx-gateway` publishes (`${GATEWAY_PORT:-6882}:80` in `docker-compose.yml`). Positive control: the same parser sees 8 port-publishing services in `docker-compose.yml` (postgres, redis, pgbouncer, cardano-mock and others) and nginx's mapping.

**What this changes.** The gate's reproduction is real but is **direct-to-gateway only**: through the front door that the stack actually exposes, a caller cannot choose the last hop. What remains is (a) a caller that reaches the gateway without nginx: the compose network (other containers; the services call each other directly, and the #1470 gate found no service code that reads a gateway URL), a VM firewall or a port mapping added outside the repo's compose files, which I cannot see; and (b) demo, where the edge may differ and which is unmeasured. **I would rate it P3 rather than P2** and keep the explicit trusted-proxy list as hardening, but the priority is Wednesday's call and I have not changed it.

**Still unmeasured:** the VMs' own firewall and any compose override on them; demo; whether KS-618's realip half is deployed (the monotonic count above is consistent with a per-client key, but a quiet bridge address would look the same over ten seconds, so it does not prove it).

title: A real-Postgres twin of the KS-1267 transfer-custody cells: the mocked flip ignores its arguments and cannot commit or roll back (PR 1486 gate note)
description:
## BLUF

A real-Postgres twin of the two KS-1267 cells in `ks1228-a-refused-request-writes-no-provenance-row.test.ts` (`/transfer-custody`: the owner flip throws, and the custody INSERT returns no row). Found by the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1486; left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Not a regression.

## Recommendation

One small tier-2, test-only PR using the faithful local Postgres recipe (`5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`) and the existing KS-1263 route-level harness, which already drives the real `/transfer-custody` route over a real database (the KS-1310 describe there seeds a document, an owner and a holder and installs a trigger as a fault vehicle). Assert on real rows: after a flip that fails there is no `action_provenance` row for the document, no `custody_events` row and the owner is unchanged; after a flip that succeeds there is one provenance row, one custody row and the owner is the NEW holder.

## Detail

The unit cells use a mocked transaction client whose `$executeRaw` **ignores its arguments** and has **no commit or rollback model**. The gate found two mutants of `routes/documents.ts` that therefore stay GREEN (31/31):

1. **Recording after the flip but before the COMMIT** (inside the transaction): a failed commit would leave a provenance row for a transfer that did not happen, and nothing can see it.
2. **The flip writing the WRONG owner** (its `SET` pointed at `fromHolderId`): the mock never looks at the value.

A twin against a real database closes both, because it reads the rows back. Also: the title of cell 3, "the custody INSERT returns no row: 500, no row, and the owner is never flipped", over-states what it asserts. The mock cannot show the owner, so the cell asserts only the WRITE ORDER (the flip statement is never issued). The PR body and squash body say so; the title is left as merged.

Refs KS-1267, KS-1263, KS-1310.

title: Wallet login: a suspended account stored under a mixed-case address can be evaded by logging in with the lower-case form (needs a case-insensitive lookup, a migration)
description:
## BLUF

Residual declared on #1476 (KS-806) and confirmed by its Opus delta gate (round 3), filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. A wallet account whose `wallet_address` was stored before #1476 in a NON-canonical casing and has since been SUSPENDED refuses its own casing (401), but the same wallet logging in with the lower-case form gets a NEW ACTIVE account (200). Suspension can be evaded through the double-account path.

## Recommendation

A separate PR with a migration: replace `auth_find_user_by_wallet` (migration 039, exact equality) with a case-insensitive lookup (or add a functional index on `lower(wallet_address)` and look up on the lower-cased argument), and canonicalise the stored column for existing rows in the same migration. Then the lookup in `routes/wallet.ts` needs no presented-casing-first loop. Until then #1476's raw-casing-first lookup keeps a legacy row reachable by its own casing, which is the part it can fix without a migration.

## Detail

* **Why it exists:** CIP-8 verification compares the claimed and signed address case-insensitively (`utils/cip8.ts`), so one wallet can present several casings, but `auth_find_user_by_wallet` is `WHERE wallet_address = p_wallet_address` (exact). #1476 stores new rows in the canonical lower-case form and looks up the presented casing first, then the canonical form; a legacy row in a casing the wallet does not present is not found by any lookup there.
* **Effect (gate probe D5 and the residual cell):** legacy row `L` (mixed case, SUSPENDED). Login with the mixed-case form: 401 (the suspension holds). Login with the lower-case form: no row found, a new row `N` is created, ACTIVE, 200.
* **Related, declared in #1476:** `/link` stores the raw casing (`routes/wallet.ts`), so one wallet can also become two accounts there; `/status/:walletAddress` is not canonicalised. The same migration fixes the lookup side of both; the write side of `/link` should canonicalise.
* **Not caused by #1476:** before it, every casing was a separate account anyway; #1476 closes the double account for rows it creates and leaves this one for legacy rows.

Provenance: Opus delta gate on #1476 round 3, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476-r3/verdict.md`; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1486 (concurrent first logins), KS-1460.

title: GET /api/security/keys: the declared 200 body is {keys:[...]} but the handler answers {success,data}; organizationId's uuid format is declared and not enforced (KS-747 residuals)
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th on Wednesday's ruling (L11, 2026-10-12): the two residual findings on `GET /api/security/keys` that KS-747 did NOT cover, as ONE ticket, so KS-747 can close as "declare the parameter".

KS-747's fix (#1318, squash `f28cd1fbc7a5`) declared `organizationId` as a required uuid query parameter. It is on develop, deployed, and confirmed on the SERVED spec of Kintsugi (bytes equal to the yaml at the deployed commit; the parameter reads required, in query, format uuid). These two things remain:

## 1. The declared 200 body is `{keys: [...]}`; the handler answers `{success, data: [...]}`

Read at the deployed commit `65d7722f83a6`: `services/security/src/security.openapi.ts` registers `ApiKeyListResponse = z.object({ keys: z.array(ApiKeySchema) })` for the 200, and `services/security/src/index.ts` `app.get('/api/keys', ...)` ends `res.json({ success: true, data: keys })`. So the two cannot both be right. Peter measured the consequence on all four KS-1353 sweeps (slot 3, head `d9ce1403d`, seed 1353): `response_schema_conformance` **31 of 31** own-test 200s fail with `"keys" is a required property`, and one more inside a stateful chain, 32 calls in all (KS-747, comment of 2026-09-28T12:31Z). KS-908's merge note also records the `keys`-vs-`data` naming as pre-existing drift.

Decision needed: which side is the contract. The house envelope elsewhere is `{success, data}`, which argues for changing the DECLARED schema to match the handler, not the handler (consumers already read `data`). Not decided here.

## 2. `organizationId` is declared `format: uuid`, and nothing enforces it

The handler checks only `if (!organizationId)`; a value that is not a uuid is accepted and simply matches nothing. Peter's sweeps record **5** `negative_data_rejection` failures on this operation, and KS-747's own merge note flagged it as "U-1" (declaration and enforcement are separate) and left it unfiled. Decision needed: enforce the format (400 on a non-uuid) or stop declaring it.

This is one instance of the class **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

## Not established by me

I did not observe either finding LIVE: the one authed GET I was cleared to make was refused 403, because the only QA credential (role OWNER) is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`. Both are read from source at the deployed commit and from Peter's sweep data.

Related: KS-747, KS-908, KS-1022, KS-1361 (Done; the sweeps' baseline), KS-1015.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** as suggested above, both `GET /api/security/keys` baseline entries now cite **this ticket** on develop (KS-983, PR #1563, merge `fe0656b60`, 2026-10-16), with the cause measured that day and Kamil's verbatim words from this ticket (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/baseline_kamil.py["KS-1514"]`).

- They still pass the gate **only as known failures**; nothing is hidden, and the expiry is unchanged (2026-12-31).
- Re-run on 2026-10-16: `response_schema_conformance` fired and resolves here. `negative_data_rejection` did not fire on that seed, which means not sampled, not fixed.
- When this ticket's fix lands, remove both entries. The proposed acceptance criteria above still apply.

**BLUF:** both `GET /api/security/keys` pairs are still firing today, and the Schemathesis baseline still attributes them to **KS-747 (Done)** rather than to this ticket.

**Measured on 2026-10-16** (slot 2, develop `a92f46e14`, Schemathesis 4.31.1):
- `response_schema_conformance::GET /api/security/keys`: the handler answered `{"success":true,"data":[]}` where `ApiKeyListResponse` requires `keys`. This is the first half of this ticket.
- `negative_data_rejection::GET /api/security/keys`: fired again. This is the second half (the uuid format is declared but not enforced).
- KS-747's own fix is in place: `organizationId` is now declared (commit `f28cd1fbc`). So the baseline's reason for both entries, *"organizationId undeclared"*, no longer describes the cause.

**Suggestion, gently:** when convenient, re-cite both baseline entries to KS-1514 with a reason that matches the measured cause, so they have a live owner (the KS-1015 finding 2 pattern).

**Proposed acceptance criteria:**
- `GET /api/security/keys` 200 matches `ApiKeyListResponse` (or the spec changes to the envelope the handler returns).
- A non-uuid `organizationId` is rejected with 400.
- A test demonstrates the fix: Schemathesis `response_schema_conformance` and `negative_data_rejection` stop firing for this operation on a full sweep, and a targeted unit/contract test pins both behaviours.
- Both baseline entries are removed.

## Facts comment — scope of these two items, 2026-10-13

Recorded while planning **KS-1553** (Wednesday's ruling of 2026-10-13). **Nothing else on this ticket is changed**, and no code has been written for either item.

### Item 1 (the declared `{keys: […]}` body vs the handler's `{success, data}`) stays its OWN ticket

It is the only part of this ticket that changes the **spec**, and it is a contract decision — which side is right — rather than a validation fix. Folding it into KS-1553's PR would turn a small change into a published-contract change and pull in the Schemathesis pre-merge tier. Confirmed still true at develop `d19b7a70`: `ApiKeyListResponseSchema` registers `keys: z.array(ApiKeySchema)` (`services/security/src/security.openapi.ts:413-416`, used for the 200 at `:828`) while `app.get('/api/keys', …)` ends `res.json({ success: true, data: keys })`.

### Item 2 (the declared-but-unenforced `format: uuid` on `organizationId`) is DEFERRED, and here is the reason

Enforcing it — a 400 for a non-uuid — **cannot ship on its own, because it would break a page that works today, and the break would be silent.**

Measured 2026-10-13 on a scratch PostgreSQL 15 with the service connected as `secuura_app`, against the real routes, every arm with a control:

* The **Admin Dashboard** hard-codes `organizationId: 'default-org'` on both operations — the list (`frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:358-360`, called with no argument from `pages/ApiKeys.tsx:75`) and the mint (`pages/ApiKeys.tsx:92`).
* That path **works end to end today**: the mint answers **201** and stores `default-org` verbatim, and the list answers **200 and returns that key**. Controls: a different organisation id returns 0 keys (so the filter is real), and the UPPER-CASE form returns 0 (which is KS-1553 (a)).
* With the format enforced, the **list** would 400 — and `request()` (`api.ts:84-91`) turns any non-2xx into `{ok:false}`, after which `fetchApiKeys` returns `[]`. The page would show **zero keys with no error shown to the user**. The **mint** would 400 too, and the Create-Key button would stop producing a key.

**Sequencing.** Item 2 is bundled into a deferred PR together with **KS-1553 (b)** and the frontend fix (**KS-1564**), because none of the three is safe alone. That PR needs a deploy seat for the frontend surface and waits on Platform S's answer about the id form it sends (asked on KS-1553, comment `2087528f`).

**KS-1553's PR 1** is deliberately scoped to normalising the list query with no 400, so it closes KS-1553 (a) without touching this item — and it carries the Admin Dashboard's exact shape as a regression pin.

Also filed today: **KS-1564** (the frontend hard-coding, the source) and **KS-1565** (count the existing non-canonical rows, read-only, no backfill).

*Facts only; no change to this ticket's description, state or priority.*

title: Timestamping: the opentimestamps and blockchain types still report verified true, and /verify accepts a forged proof with no stored row (KS-753 gate m2)
description:
**ACTION (owner: the timestamping build lane, with a policy decision first):** decide what an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp may claim when nothing external ever checked it, then make creation and `/api/timestamps/verify` agree with that decision, the way KS-753 and KS-1404 did for `rfc3161`. Options to rule between: (a) report `verified: false` on creation and on verify for these two types until a real attestation check exists; (b) require a stored row and honour its `verified` column on verify (KS-1404's shape for rfc3161); (c) stop advertising the types in `supportedTypes` (`index.ts:185`) until they are real. Tests first, with a planted-red mutation per branch.

**Symptom (gate evidence P7, P8).**

* **P7:** creating an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp answers `verified: true` and persists `verified = true`. Both types are placeholders by design (the proof is generated locally, `generateMockOpenTimestampsProof` / blockchain at `index.ts:689` and `:705`).
* **P8:** a **forged** `opentimestamps` JSON proof (the right hash plus one attestation) with **no stored row** returns `verified: true` from `/verify` (`index.ts:616-621`; the `blockchain` case at `:625` is the same shape: hash match plus `chain` and `slot` fields). Nothing checks an attestation against anything.
* KS-1404 closed this same forgery path for `rfc3161` only.

**Why P2.** This is "a mock timestamp reported as verified" by KS-753's own wording, on an evidentiary path (Tier 1). It is **not a regression** from PR #1502 and did not block it; the PR declared these types out of scope.

**Data, handled separately.** Rows of these types already stored as `verified = true` are a data question. A backfill is approval-class (Kam), and the count must come first, read-only per environment, classified by the proof's SHAPE rather than the `(mock)` name (the name missed 1 of 5 mocks in the gate's test). Wednesday is handing the count SQL to the deploy seat.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1502 (KS-753), verdict sha256/16 `5e1fcf87edc4e8a4`, finding m2. Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (12:20Z) that this is filed as P2. PR #1502 head `5daf8830dc46`; line numbers below are at that head.

title: Decide production VC verification: no DID resolver is wired anywhere, so with NODE_ENV=production /credentials/verify refuses every Ed25519 credential
description:
**BLUF: with** `NODE_ENV=production`**,** `POST /api/credentials/verify` **answers** `verified: false` **for EVERY Ed25519 credential, including a genuine unrevoked one, because nothing in the tree supplies the verifier a** `didResolver`**. The refusal is deliberate in code; a working production verify has never been built. DECISION NEEDED: is production VC verification intentionally off until go-live (then say so, and pin it with a test), or is wiring the resolver work to schedule? The same wiring would close KS-1383.**

## Measured (2026-10-12, develop `c63cec1f6070`)

In-process, on the real `POST /api/credentials/verify` handler and the real shared verifier, with `NODE_ENV` set per call (the verifier reads it at call time). **Not** a booted production app.

| case | `NODE_ENV=development` | `NODE_ENV=production` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| genuine, never revoked | `verified: true` | `verified: false`, `No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production` |
| revoked, as issued | `false`, `Credential has been revoked` | `false`, the same resolver error plus `Credential has been revoked` |
| revoked, id never issued | `false`, `no issuer record` | `false`, the resolver error plus `no issuer record` |
| revoked, another LIVE credential's id | `true` (KS-1383) | `false`, the resolver error only |
| same, with a tampered `credentialSubject` | `true` (KS-1383) | `false`, the resolver error only |

So in production there is no bypass, and also no credential that verifies. Rows: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-4th/evidence/probe.env.txt`.

## From the code (read)

* `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts:409-411`: `// In production, this MUST fail. In dev, allow pass-through.` then `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') errors.push('No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production')`. In the file since its first commit, `e50dbde98` (2026-02-18).
* `verifier.ts:67` declares `didResolver` in the config; `:385` and `:447` use it. A search of the non-test, non-doc tree finds **no caller that supplies one**: `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:339-346` passes the revocation resolvers only.
* No test names the production message, and I found no document saying production verification is deliberately off.

## What I can and cannot establish

* **Can:** the refusal is by design (the guard and its comment), and a working production verify path does not exist.
* **Cannot:** whether leaving it unbuilt is an accepted decision for the current phase. That is the decision this ticket asks for.

## NOT measured

A booted production app (vc-issuer will not boot without `DATABASE_URL` and `PRISM_AGENT_URL`); any deployed production environment; the demo VM; `POST /api/presentations/verify` in production mode (it calls the same shared verifier, per the code, but I did not run it); behaviour with a resolver wired.

## Priority, and why P3

It fails closed, so nothing unsafe is accepted; there is no production environment today (Platform K has no public domain yet); and its fix is the same wiring as KS-1383, which is High. It becomes a go-live blocker for any use of the VC verify routes.

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included, titles, descriptions and comments, literal)

`No DID resolver configured`: 2 (KS-1375 description, as an aside "pre-existing, read, not driven"; KS-1383 only through my own comment of 2026-10-12). `verifier.ts:410`, `cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production`, `PRISM_AGENT_URL`: 1 each, all KS-1383 via that same comment. `production verif`: 2, both closed review tickets. Positive control `statusListResolver`: 4. Negative control: 0. **No open ticket tracks this as a question.** Related, not duplicates: KS-1383 (the id/proof binding), KS-1375, KS-625 (`/presentations/verify` never checks the holder signature: the opposite failure, a claim of validity with no check).

title: platform_document_registry.tenant_id has three declarations that disagree (init schema UUID, gateway CREATE TEXT, main-DB copy TEXT): decide the canonical one (UNDECIDED)
description:
## BLUF

**Nobody has decided what type** `platform_document_registry.tenant_id` **is. There are three declarations of it, and they disagree:** the platform database's init schema says `UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`; the gateway's in-code CREATE for the platform database says `TEXT`; and the MAIN database's copy of the table (created by `CORE_MIGRATIONS`) is also `TEXT`. **This is UNDECIDED.** It is the item left over when KS-1272 was closed: that ticket's defect (the de-dup `DELETE` failing `22P02` on a uuid column on every boot) is fixed by making the statement type-agnostic, and its Recommendation also asked to "decide which declaration is canonical". Nothing is broken today because both spellings now work.

## Recommendation

A decision, not a build. Pick the canonical type for the platform database's table (the init schema's `UUID` with a foreign key is the stricter reading), then decide separately whether the gateway's in-code CREATE should be aligned to it, and whether the main database should hold this table at all or hold it with the same type. Unassigned: a decision-shaped item for Wednesday or Kam.

## Detail

* **Facts at develop** `551dc9808aee` (source lines, not compiled):
  * `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:209-213`: `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`, plus `idx_doc_registry_unique` on `(content_hash, tenant_id)` at line 225.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, platform list, lines 1123-1138: `tenant_id TEXT`, then the de-dup `DELETE` at 1135-1137 using `a.tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.tenant_id` (the KS-1272 fix, PR #1104), then `uq_pdr_hash_tenant`.
  * Same file, `CORE_MIGRATIONS` (the MAIN database), lines 473-501: `tenant_id TEXT`, de-dup with `COALESCE(a.tenant_id, '') = COALESCE(b.tenant_id, '')`. That form is correct on a TEXT column and would raise `22P02` on a uuid one.
* **Why the declarations coexist:** the init script runs first on a fresh platform database, so the gateway's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op wherever that script ran. KS-1272 measured the Kintsugi platform database on 2026-09-19 (read-only): `tenant_id` is `uuid`, 0 rows, `uq_pdr_hash_tenant` present.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** a platform database built from the gateway's CREATE alone would be `TEXT` and carry no foreign key to `tenants`, while one built from the init script is `UUID` with the key; a non-UUID tenant id would then be accepted by one and refused by the other. No run was made to confirm it.
* **Related:** KS-1272 (the defect, Done), KS-598 (the registry upsert that keys on `(content_hash, tenant_id)`; the type of `tenant_id` is part of what that ticket's re-keying would have to settle).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `canonical declaration` 0; `platform_document_registry` 10 hits, of which KS-1272 and KS-598 were read; KS-590 and KS-33 are unrelated. The same instrument returned KS-1272 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: Seat handover clone recipe fails its checkout: git clone --reference of the shared 2_Project_Files stops with 'unable to parse commit 54b2a5c2' (2 seats of 2); a plain clone works
description:
**ACTION (owner: the build lane / whoever maintains the seat-handover recipe):** change the working-area recipe in the seat handovers from a `--reference ... --dissociate` clone of the shared `2_Project_Files` checkout to a plain clone from GitHub, and find out why the first one fails.

## Symptom (measured, twice)

Seat J 4th (2026-10-12) and Seat J 5th (2026-10-12T18:50Z) each ran:

```
git clone --reference "<shared 2_Project_Files>" --dissociate git@github.com:Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git <dest>
```

Both stopped with `fatal: unable to parse commit 54b2a5c26d75a28b14fdce578dd5a5aadee49039` and "Clone succeeded, but checkout failed". That commit is the tip of `main` (the PR #908 merge), the branch a clone checks out by default.

Recovery that worked both times: `git checkout -B develop origin/develop`, then `git fsck --full` (rc 0, no output) and a check that every `git ls-files -z` path exists (J 5th: 4,382 files, 0 missing).

## Control

The same clone with no `--reference` and no `--dissociate` checked out clean in 35 s (rc 0, status clean, HEAD `54b2a5c2`). One run each side, so the shared object store is implicated, not proven.

## Ruled out, read-only against the shared store

* The commit reads there: `cat-file -t` says commit, `rev-list -1` returns it.
* `git commit-graph verify` there is rc 0. Its commit-graph file is dated 30 Sep 06:16, 13 days old.
* Cause: unproven.

## Also

A clone script piped through `tee` made the harness report "completed (exit code 0)" for a clone that had failed with rc 128. The script's own printed rc was the truth. Do not pipe a step whose exit code decides what happens next.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "clone --reference dissociate", "unable to parse commit", "reference clone shared checkout", "seat handover clone recipe" and "54b2a5c2". 249 distinct issues read. Literal match for `dissociate`, `--reference`, `54b2a5c2`, "unable to parse commit", "clone recipe" and `alternates` in title or description: 0 hits. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked, so this is "0 hits in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

title: KS-1538 gate follow-ups (m1-m4): a pkey-addressed documentId passes the legacy-certify check but the UPDATE matches external_id only; check and UPDATE not in one transaction; stale provenance admits a former creator; ~0.55 ms timing difference
description:
**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane; P3, one checklist):** four Minor findings from the Opus gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), none of which blocks it. Each is quoted with the gate's measurement and its fix-shape. Decide per item whether to build, accept or close. No build is started by this ticket.

## m1. A pkey-addressed `documentId` passes the new check, but the UPDATE silently does nothing

`certifications.ts` resolves the document with `getDocument` (external_id first, then the pkey UUID), but the legacy `UPDATE documents ...` matches `external_id` only. **Measured:** the owner and a SYSTEM_ADMIN get 201 with a certification saved, while the row stays `anchored` with no `certified_at`, and nothing is logged (the new catch logs only thrown errors, not a 0-row UPDATE). **Pre-existing: identical on base.** Fix-shape: resolve to the row's `external_id` from the record the check already read before the UPDATE, or log or refuse on 0 rows.

## m2. Check and UPDATE are not in one transaction

The window spans the holder lookup and the anchoring POST, whose timeout is 10 s. **Constructed:** the owner passes the check, the owner flips to B during a 1.5 s anchoring delay (SQL simulating `transfer-custody`), and the UPDATE then lands on a document B now owns, carrying A's issuer id. Not reproduced through the real transfer route. Low severity: the caller was authorised at check time.

## m3. Stale provenance admits a former creating connector

`wasCreatedByConnector` (`provenance.ts:285-296`; the same arm `GET /api/documents/:id` uses) trusts a provenance row keyed by the document's external id. **Constructed:** connector A creates document U with `onBehalfOf`, U is deleted (superuser SQL), user B re-registers U, and connector A certifies B's document: 201, row certified. Needs a deletion plus deliberate reuse of the id. It belongs to the owner rule, not to PR #1525. Owner should consider provenance rows keyed to the pkey, or deleted with the document.

## m4. A timing oracle of about 0.55 ms (measured locally, not over a network)

The refusal bodies are byte-identical, but latency is not: for a connector, not-yours 1.474 ms (p10 1.286) vs unknown 0.923 ms (p90 1.165), so the distributions separate (A/A control 0.923 vs 0.921 ms, N=200 per series, interleaved); for humans, an unknown UUID-shaped id 1.466 ms vs not-yours 0.952 ms (the pkey fallback query). `GET /api/documents/:id` has the same shape.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "pkey UUID addressed documentId certify UPDATE external_id", "wasCreatedByConnector stale provenance former creating connector", "check and UPDATE not in one transaction certify anchoring window", "timing difference unknown not-yours refusal connector" and "legacy certify follow-ups". 315 distinct issues read. Literal matches in title or description: `wascreatedbyconnector` 0, `stale provenance` 0. The only issue matching two or more of the seven distinctive tokens was KS-1538 itself. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. Relevance-ranked: "none in the top 75 per term", not a census.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), verdict GO WITH NOTE (sha256/16 `0273b5bb14d3f036`), findings m1 to m4; Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:01Z) that they are filed as one P3 follow-up. m5 (`SUPER_ADMIN` goes 201 to 403 on this path) is stated in the PR body instead.
