title: Claude Code sessions have no secret-file guard on platform-k: add the PS-1361 hook with PS-1387's local-only exemption, covering every systemTest env and secrets file (and .env.stripe is not git-ignored)
description:
## BLUF

platform-s blocks a Claude Code session from printing a secret file ([PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule)), and is about to let through files that hold only local values ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot), [Secuura/platform-s#1199](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1387-secret-file-guard-lets-local-only-values-through-55c48feacc56), In Review). **platform-k has neither.** At `develop` `bd6697e07` the repo's tracked `.claude/` holds only `skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md`: no `settings.json` and no hook. Nothing stops a session from running `cat`, `grep` or `diff` on `Blockchain/Dev/.env` (PII keys, JWT keys, datastore passwords), `.env.local` (OAuth and IdP credentials) or any systemTest secrets file. The only protection is a rule the session has to remember. [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) exists because that failed on platform-s on 26 Oct 2026 (`terraform fmt -check -diff .` printed every dev-ps secret).

Separately, `.env.stripe`-style files, which are planned, are **not git-ignored** on platform-k today (measured below).

## Verified (28 Oct 2026, K `develop` `bd6697e07`)

**K has no guard:** `git ls-files .claude` returns only the skill file.

**systemTest env and secrets files: tracked templates, and the real file each produces (all git-ignored, checked with** `git check-ignore` **on the file path):**

| Real file (git-ignored) | Template (tracked) | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `systemTest/playwright/.env` | `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` | Playwright credentials and targets |
| `systemTest/akto/.env` | `systemTest/akto/.env.example` | Akto harness env |
| `systemTest/akto/docker.env` | `systemTest/akto/docker.env.example` | Akto container env |
| `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.example.yml` | Akto role credentials |
| `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.example.yml` | k6 credentials |
| `systemTest/schemathesis/.env-slot<N>` | written by `scripts/run.py setup` | per-slot API token |
| `.env-*` slot credential files ([KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs), root `.gitignore:14-16`) | written by tooling | slot-scoped credentials |

`systemTest/performance/config/environments.yml` is tracked. Whether it may name a secret value is not established.

**platform-k product code: env and credential files the services, frontends and deployments read.** Each was checked with `git check-ignore` on the real file path, 28 Oct 2026, `bd6697e07`.

| Real file | Template (tracked) | Ignored? | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env` | `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (canonical, [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap)); also `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | yes | PII encryption and lookup keys, JWT keypair, datastore passwords, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local` | `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` (also `env.local.example`) | yes | OAuth / IdP client secrets |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/<svc>/.env` for analytics, anchoring, api-gateway, auth, billing, governance, guardian, kyc, m365-integration, nft-certificate, originate, prism, queue, referral, security, staking, timestamping, transfer, vc-issuer, wallet-connector (20 services) | `services/<svc>/.env.example` | yes, all 20 | per-service secrets (billing: Stripe keys; m365: Microsoft app secret; kyc: provider keys) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/` real file for its second template | `services/billing/env.example` | **not established**: the real file name for this no-dot template is unknown | Stripe keys |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/.env.staging` | `deployment/azure/env.staging.example` | yes | Azure staging deployment values |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/cardano/.env` | `deployment/cardano/env.example` | yes | Cardano node / wallet configuration |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/{admin,issuer,verifier}/.env.development` | none tracked | yes | frontend local overrides |
| `Blockchain/Dev/test-wallet.env`, `Blockchain/Dev/*.wallet.env` | none | yes (`.gitignore:133-135`) | wallet seed phrases |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/ssl/*.pem`, `*.key` | none | yes (`.gitignore:70-72`) | TLS private keys |
| `.keys/`, `credentials.json`, `*-credentials.json` | none | yes (`.gitignore:93`, `:138-139`) | key material, service-account credentials |
| `USER_TESTING/Testing Harness/handoff/` | none | yes (`.gitignore:185-186`) | super-admin login handoff |
| `observability/.env`, `observability/config/alerting.env` | `observability/.env.example`, `observability/config/alerting.env.example` | yes | alerting webhooks and tokens |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/.env.stripe` (planned style) | none | **NOT ignored** | would hold Stripe keys |

Every row except the last belongs in the hook's refuse list, and none qualifies for the local-only exemption: these are product secrets, not systemTest targets. The "Holds" column is from the template names and the service's purpose, not from opening any real file.

`.env.stripe` **is not git-ignored:**

```
K  systemTest/.env.stripe          NOT-ignored
K  Blockchain/Dev/.env.stripe      NOT-ignored
```

K's root `.gitignore` names `.env`, `.env-*`, `.env.local` and a fixed list of `.env.<stage>` names, not `.env.*`. A Stripe file created today could be committed.

## Proposed scope (for the owner to decide)

1. **A PreToolUse hook for Bash, Read and Grep**, `onFailure: block`, modelled on platform-s's `.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py`:
   * it refuses any reader (cat, grep, sed, diff, jq, base64, …) pointed at the files above, plus Terraform state, plans and tfvars, and an unformatted `docker inspect` or `docker exec … env` on K containers;
   * it allows a command that only names a file (`ls`, `stat`, `test -f`, `git check-ignore`);
   * it allows a single-field `docker inspect --format`, which the K build proof uses for `org.opencontainers.image.revision`.
2. [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)**'s local-only exemption, if Kamil agrees.** A systemTest env file whose every URL / base-URL key points at `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` is readable. Anything remote, missing or unreadable stays secret. `Blockchain/Dev/.env` **and** `.env.local` **stay guarded whatever their URLs**, because they hold real PII-encryption, JWT and OAuth material.
3. **A** `.gitignore` **rule for** `.env.*` **env files** (`.env.stripe` and successors) that keeps every `*.example` template tracked.
4. **A contract test pinning what the hook refuses and allows**, as platform-s's `SecretReadHookContractTests` does. Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.

**Why it matters for running the suites.** Building K, building S and running every systemTest suite need these files created and merged from their templates. With a guard on K, the exemption in item 2 decides which K files a session can merge blind. That needs settling before the guard lands, or the env-setup step breaks the same way.

## Runs on a developer's Mac, as platform-s#1199 does

platform-s#1199 ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)) is written for a developer's own Mac running local stack slots. The platform-k guard should take the same shape:

* **Where it runs.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook on the Mac, registered in `.claude/settings.json` as `python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<name>.py"`, `onFailure: block`. `python3` ships with macOS (Xcode Command Line Tools), so no install is needed. `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the session's project folder, normally the root checkout, not a ticket worktree. A guard change therefore takes effect once the root checkout is on a `develop` that contains it.
* **What "this machine" means.** As in #1199: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `[::1]`. A systemTest env file is exempt only while every URL / base-URL key in it points there. That covers the local slots `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` 1–4, gateway `6882 + 100·(N−1)`. A file pointed at Kintsugi, demo-pk, Container Apps or any remote host stays secret, and so does a missing or unreadable file.
* **Still guarded on the Mac, as in #1199:**
  * a bare `env` / `printenv`, because the developer's shell holds real tokens;
  * the product files in the table above, which are real keys even on a laptop;
  * Terraform state, plans and tfvars.
* **K slot containers (**`secuura-s<N>-*`**, and slot 1's** `secuura-*`**).** Unlike platform-s's slot containers, they are **not** exempt. Their environment comes from `Blockchain/Dev/.env` and `.env.local` (PII and JWT keys, OAuth secrets). An unformatted `docker inspect`, or `docker exec … env` / `printenv`, is refused. A single-field `docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}'` and `--format '{{.RestartCount}}'` stay allowed, because the build proof needs them.
* **macOS tools.** The rules match on command text, so they must hold for BSD `sed`, `grep`, `stat` and `xargs` as well as GNU forms.
* **A search pattern that names a secret file is not a read** (the #1199 false-positive fix). For example, `grep -E 'tfvars|tfstate' .gitignore` is allowed. A secret file as a file operand, or as the value of `-f`, is still refused. This session's own grep of K's `.gitignore` was refused by platform-s's guard for exactly this reason.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **An automated test, offline on macOS.** A contract test, run by the K preflight and the pre-push hook with no stack up, drives the hook through `python3` on the Mac. It covers:
   * a refused and an allowed case for every file in the tables above;
   * a localhost, a remote-URL and a missing-file case for each exempt systemTest file;
   * the K-container `docker inspect` / `exec` rules;
   * a search-pattern-only grep (allowed);
   * a `.env.stripe` file that is git-ignored while its `.example` is not.

   Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.
2. **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` → security section, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, name the guard, the exemption and the file list. `Projects Documents/Stack-Slots-How-To.md` is changed only if the env-setup steps change.
3. **systemTests:** no spec, page object or fixture change. The guard's test is a contract test. Each systemTest `.env.example` should say in a comment whether its real file is exempt.

## Related

* [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) (the platform-s guard).
* [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot) / platform-s#1199 (the local-only exemption, In Review).
* [KS-1608](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1608/akto-harness-writes-credentials-to-disk-and-into-reports-reportjson) (Akto credentials written to reports, Done).
* [KS-1098](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1098/k6-runner-echo-mask-enamevalue-and-qe-namevalue-still-print-the-value) (k6 echo mask).
* [KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs) (slot credential files).
* [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap) (env template drift).

Raised from the [PS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1381/systemtest-a11y-keyboard-journey-power-user-keyboard-enter-on-the) session. **Not assigned:** the `.claude/` tooling owner on platform-k is undecided. The systemTest parts are Peter's, the rest is Kamil's.

title: tenant-provisioning: the key service still writes a tenant's key row after the caller gives up, and neither the create rollback nor tenant delete removes it
description:
**BLUF:** The tokenisation service's `POST /api/generate-key` does not notice that its caller has gone: it still inserts the tenant's wrapped key row (`tenant_keys`) and an audit row afterwards. When tenant creation gives up (its fetch bound, a client disconnect) or rolls back, nothing removes that row. The create rollback deletes only `tenant_config`, `tenant_contacts` and `tenants`; tenant delete deletes `vault_entries`, `tenant_contacts`, `tenant_config` and `platform_document_registry`; tokenisation has no delete route. The result is an ACTIVE wrapped key for a tenant whose `vault_key_hash` is NULL, or for a tenant that no longer exists. Low: nothing reachable reads it today (see the vault-key trace on KS-1240).

## Exercised

A probe against the real tokenisation entry module (`pg` replaced by a recorder and the JWT middleware stubbed; no database, no Docker): the key INSERT slowed by 400 ms and the client aborting at 150 ms. Result, verbatim:

```
{ "clientOutcome": "client aborted: AbortError",
  "tenantKeysInsertsAtTheMomentTheClientGaveUp": 0,
  "tenantKeysInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1,
  "auditInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1 }
```

So the handler does not observe a client disconnect; the key row and the audit row land after the caller has left. File in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_abort_probe.json` (the probe source is beside it as a `.txt`).

## Read (develop `2b7ef12fa564`)

* `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`: the `generate-key` route is at `:220` and the key INSERT at `:238`; no `req.on('close')` handling and no delete route (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key).
* `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: the rollback at `:322` to `:324` and the tenant delete list at `:520` name no `tenant_keys`. `tenant_keys` is written by tokenisation into the main database, tenant provisioning's `platformQuery` writes the platform database.
* `migrations/029_tokenisation_tenant_keys.sql`: `UNIQUE (tenant_id, version, status)`. A second `generate-key` for a tenant that already has an active version 1 would insert `(tenant_id, 1, 'active')` again and so answer 500 (read; not executed, it needs a real Postgres).

## Why it matters

* Tenant creation now gives up on a key service that is slower than 3 s (KS-1240 part 4). A key service that is slow but not hung still completes its insert, and the tenant ends up with a key row and a NULL `vault_key_hash`.
* The decision that keeps tenant creation answering 201 with a `keyPending` flag (KS-1240) leaves such tenants in place; a later attempt to generate their key by hand would meet the unique constraint above.
* A create that is rolled back after the key was written leaves a key (and its audit row) for a tenant that no longer exists.

## Options (not chosen here)

1. A platform-admin route on tokenisation that deletes a tenant's key rows, called by the create rollback and the tenant delete.
2. Make `generate-key` idempotent per tenant (answer with the existing active key's id and hash), so a retry or a late completion can be reconciled.
3. Have tenant creation read the hash back from the key service after a timeout instead of leaving it NULL.

## Not covered

A real Postgres (the unique-constraint rejection is read), live data (how many such rows exist on the demo or kintsugi boxes is unmeasured), and any other caller of `generate-key` (the search found tenant provisioning only).

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `tenant_keys` (KS-311, KS-288, both Done and about earlier errors in these routes), `generate-key` (KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all Done or Deployed To Prod), `rotate-key` (6 hits: KS-667, KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all closed or deployed work on these routes), `wrapped key` (0), `vault key` (0), `key row` (6 hits, none about the key service), `keyPending` (0). None records this behaviour.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: smoke-test.sh is not remote-clean: 12 localhost:60xx checks, RUNBOOK 2.2's remote full run, and URL credentials echoed in "Smoke target:"
description:
**BLUF:** `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is still not remote-clean after PR 1793 made its `GATEWAY` honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (KS-1250). One remote full run would show all three problems below at once, which is why they are one ticket. Low. Related to KS-1250. Filed on the tier-2 gate's note (gate 8, 2026-10-28), after a search of the board (quoted at the end).

**Nobody runs this script against kintsugi, demo or any live box to reproduce or check any of this.** A full run anchors a real document, and that run is held for Kam (the KS-1250 hold). Everything below was read from the script or measured with a stub `curl` on a private PATH against a `.invalid` host.

1. **12 hard-coded** `http://localhost:60xx` **service-port checks remain in the full run** (sections 7 onward): lines 259, 263, 267, 275, 283, 292, 305, 307, 317, 319, 327 and 329 of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` at PR 1793's head `29989b01ab05`. PR 1793 moves only `GATEWAY`, so with `SMOKE_BASE_URL` set to a remote gateway those 12 checks still hit localhost, and the run mixes two environments while reading as a result for one.
2. **RUNBOOK section 2.2 still tells an operator to do a remote full run.** `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md` lines 139 to 143: `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<prod-gateway-fqdn> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`, under the heading "Bash smoke against production gateway", with no `--quick`.
3. **The** `Smoke target:` **line echoes credentials embedded in the URL verbatim.** Measured with a stub `curl` and `--quick`: `SMOKE_BASE_URL='https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999'` (a fake credential) prints, as line 1 of the output, `Smoke target: https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999`. A base URL carrying a token or basic-auth would be written to the terminal and to any CI log. The stub recorded 9 requests, all to `smoke-target.invalid`.

Also on this ticket: **no test cell uses an** `https://` **base** (the new suite uses `http://smoke-target.invalid:9999`), so the gate's mutant M11 survives.

Fix shapes, not chosen here: route the 12 service-port checks through a base the way `GATEWAY` is, or skip them with a printed line when the base is not localhost; make section 2.2 say `--quick` or say what a remote full run does not cover; print the target as scheme, host and port only.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 13:4xZ): `remote-clean` 1 hit, KS-1250 itself; `smoke-test.sh` 11 hits, read: none is this follow-up (KS 1245 is the Done degraded-health fix, KS 1139 the arithmetic-under-errexit fix, KS 1101 a health-aggregation ticket); `SMOKE_BASE_URL` 2 hits, KS-1250 and a review comment on KS 1101 that repeats the same O-2 finding; `Smoke target` 1 hit, KS-1250; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6b` 0 hits.

title: Security (nit): decideMint's toUpperCase admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as a key admin; plus the role-comparison sweep
description:
**BLUF:** `decideMint` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:96-97`, the `POST /api/keys` admission test) still compares `String(caller?.role ?? '').toUpperCase()` against the key-admin set, so a role spelled with U+0131 (dotless i) or U+017F (long s), or an array role, can be read as an admin role. KS-1591 fixed the same shape in `isPlatformRole` and `requireKeyAdmin` and deliberately left this site; this ticket tracks it, and the sweep of other role comparisons that KS-1591's description asks for, so that KS-1591 can close. Reachability is not established.

## Where

`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` at develop `5dccdcb29ec20393e80cbdb1e359a49caa633165` (the build on both boxes), read with `git show`:

* line 96: `const role = String(caller?.role ?? '');`
* line 97: `if (KEY_ADMIN_ROLES.has(role.toUpperCase())) {`

## What is measured and what is not

* Measured by the tier-2 gate on 2026-10-28 (the batch covering PRs 1775, 1776 and 1780, GO WITH NOTES): `decideMint` admits a role spelled with U+0131 or U+017F, and an array role, at PR 1776's head `8b92887a6fac`. The gate's note was filed on KS-1591 as a comment (`42e97e12`).
* Read by me, not run: lines 96 and 97 are unchanged at the deployed build. I ran no test of `decideMint` with those roles.
* Not established: whether any issuer, user-management path or seed can store or sign a token with such a role. That needs a token the auth service signs. KS-1591 said the same. Until someone measures it this is a nit; if any path can, it is a privilege escalation (admission to mint API keys) and should be re-rated at once.

## Recommendation

Not built. Apply the KS-1591 remedy here: fold ASCII letters only (`replace(/[a-z]/g, ...)`, as `isPlatformRole` now does) and refuse a role that is not a string, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it. Cells: a dotless-i spelling, a long-s spelling and an array role each refused by `decideMint`; a control that every ASCII spelling admitted today is still admitted.

## Sweep candidates (not findings)

Method: `git grep -n -I "toUpperCase()"` at `5dccdcb29ec2` over `Blockchain/Dev/services` and `Blockchain/Dev/packages`, tests, `dist` and `node_modules` excluded, keeping lines that also contain "role" (case-insensitive). 14 lines. Controls: the `decideMint` line is in the result (1 line from `provisioningPolicy.ts`); a nonsense token over the same paths matches 0 files. Of the 14: 2 are comments, 2 are the sites KS-1591 fixed (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:144`, `security/src/index.ts:1104`), 1 is `decideMint`, and 9 are other candidates:

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:85` and `:102` (`ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, `SCOPED_ADMIN_ROLES`; the same file KS-1591 changed at `:144`)
* `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:288`
* `services/auth/src/routes/issuerCerts.ts:71`
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:285` and `:377`
* `services/auth/src/services/password.ts:234` (whether it is a role comparison is unread)
* `services/originate/src/middleware/rbac.ts:56` and `:58`

I read none of these beyond the matching line. The census misses a comparison split across lines or through another variable name. KS-1601 tracks the SQL counterpart (`upper(role) = $3` in the admin-scope route).

## Board search (before filing)

Issues filter with `includeArchived: true`, title or description (comments excluded), read 2026-10-29: tickets whose title contains `decideMint`: 0. Tickets naming `decideMint` together with "dotless", "0131" or "017F": 0. Controls: `isPlatformRole` finds 7 tickets (KS-1701, KS-1601, KS-1591, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-976, KS-743); a random nonsense token finds 0. The only place the gap is recorded is the gate's note on KS-1591 (a comment, which this search excludes). Tickets that mention `decideMint` for other reasons, none with this fold as its subject: KS-1594, KS-1584, KS-1570, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-1533, KS-742 and KS-486.

## Source

KS-1591 (the tier-2 gate's note, comment `42e97e12`, and its description's request for a sweep); the MERGE GO for PR 1775 recorded the narrowing: PR 1776 says `Refs KS-1591`, not `Closes`.

title: For one anchor id the anchor row reads failed while its document reads confirmed; a document read and a verify can settle it either way
description:
**BLUF:** On kintsugi, for anchor id `anchor_c09c1b1f-c639-49e3-8afc-f1fb31906732` (document `deb6d3c3-1d79-4993-82a1-7a49a75aae00`), the anchor row and the document disagree. The reconciler marked the anchor row `failed` at 2026-10-29 08:56:14Z (the 24 hour give-up). The document's stored blob reads `confirmed` against the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` (block 4801203), written at 08:56:52Z after two `POST /api/verification/verify` calls. The code has two readers that can settle the same pair in opposite directions: a document read can write `anchor_failed`, a verify wrote `confirmed`. Only the verify-first order was observed.

**Measured** (Seat T 6th, kintsugi, read-only, 09:02:43Z and 09:04:53Z):

* Anchor row: status `failed`, error "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)", `created_at` 2026-10-28T08:55:38.299Z, `updated_at` 2026-10-29T08:56:14.459Z, `retry_count` 0. Its stored transaction `e1df3f61…` is not on the preview chain; the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` is (Seat T 6th's earlier reading).
* Document (originate store, found through `documents.external_id`): row status `anchored`, `updated_at` 08:56:52.914Z; blob `blockchain.status` `confirmed`, `blockHeight` 4801203, txHash `b1cc72f9…`. originate log, 08:56:52.921Z: "KS-584: healed anchor state written back to document". audit_logs: two `verification.verify` requests answered 200 at 08:56:52.930Z and 08:56:52.951Z, and no request to the retry route `/anchor` for this document.
* Not measured: who sent the two verify calls, and why the once-a-minute document reads stopped at 05:53:39Z.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`; not exercised):

* Document read: `documents.ts:1167` calls `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` (`services/anchorStateSync.ts:353`). At `:399-400`, when the document is in flight and the anchor row's status is `failed`, it calls `markDocumentAnchorFailed`, which writes `status: 'anchor_failed'` and returns early only when the blob is already `confirmed` (`anchorStateSync.ts:173` onward). `documents.ts:1458` lets the retry route run for an `anchor_failed` blob.
* Verify: `routes/verification.ts` `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:426`) and `persistHealedAnchor` (`:496`), called at `:802-803` and `:1324-1325`; the log line above comes from `:504`.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread2_0902Z_t6.txt` (anchor row, document, logs, audit_logs, with controls)
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/evidence/reread3_trigger_t6.txt` (the two verify calls and the gateway lines)

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): the phrase "anchor row failed" 0 hits; `anchorStateSync.ts:399` 1 hit, read: KS-772, in Seat T 6th's comments of 05:50Z and 09:09Z on the stuck row. They describe this same mechanism as stream comments, not as a ticket, and the 09:09Z comment says the same shape on another document can end either way and that only one outcome was measured; `markDocumentAnchorFailed` 10 hits, `confirmStalePendingAnchor` 6 hits and `persistHealedAnchor` 7 hits, read by title: they concern threadToken erasure (KS-1058, KS-1074), block heights (KS-1509, KS-1333), unpinned guard clauses (KS-1676), the simulated flag (KS-1661) and others, and none describes a failed anchor row beside a confirmed document. KS-1384 records this kintsugi row up to 2026-10-29 00:52Z, before the row failed.

**Related:** KS-1384 (the per-event anchor design under revision), KS-772 (the review stream whose comments record the kintsugi row), KS-1676.

**From Platform S (Stuart, KS-1384 comment 50294791, 2026-10-30 01:18 UTC), recorded here because it is this ticket's defect seen from S's side. Not reproduced by us: quoted from S's report and read from code.**

- **S's report, dev-ps document `deb6d3c3-…`:** the two `POST /api/verification/verify` calls at 08:56:52 UTC on 29 Oct were S's own corroboration for rows 108 (share) and 109 (rights-assign). Verify answered with anchor id `anchor_c09c1b1f-…`, anchored, not simulated, transaction `b1cc72f9…` (block 4801203). S now shows both rows confirmed by the upload's transaction, while that anchor row reads `failed` with `e1df3f61…`.
- **S's report, demo-pk uat-ps document 18 (29 Oct, from 05:53 UTC):** the sign-cert version, certified, share and share-attach-consent all got `anchor_50fa7aab-…`, and all four S rows carry `77363baf…` (block 4804071), which on chain is the version alone. Stuart says this case came through the ordinary poll, not verify.
- **The mechanism in code** (originate `routes/verification.ts`, read at develop `40c06084919d`): `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (line 426), when anchoring's chain index attributes a confirmed transaction to the same registration (`sameDoc`, lines 463-465), returns the stored blob with `txHash` replaced by the chain's transaction and `status: 'confirmed'` (lines 467-471). The blob keeps its own `anchorId` beside a transaction that is not that anchor row's. `persistHealedAnchor` (line 496) writes it back to the document.
- **Stuart's observation, verbatim:** "verify-by-hash should not report an anchor id as confirmed when that id's own row reads failed with a different transaction."

Related: KS-1384 (the per-event anchor design; the approach outline posted there names this ticket). On S's side Stuart tracks the crediting under PS-895.

title: transfer-custody to the current holder is accepted: on kintsugi 6 of 7 custody_events for one document were from=to
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` accepts a transfer to the document's current holder and writes a full set of rows each time. On kintsugi, seven requests for one document on 2026-10-26 (03:09 to 03:15Z, 60 seconds apart) wrote seven `custody_events`. The first moved the owner to an invited recipient; events 2 to 7 have `from_holder_id` equal to `to_holder_id`. Each request also wrote an `action_provenance` row and a `documents.transfer-custody` audit row answered 201. Nothing in the route compares the current holder with the new one.

**Measured** (Seat T 6th, kintsugi, read-only, `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatT-6th/mail/04_measured_body.txt`, item B2; the API id `427c4864…` is `documents.external_id`, the internal id differs):

* `custody_events` for the document: 7 (control: another document has 1). `created_at` 03:09:24.564, 03:10:24.746, 03:11:24.832, 03:12:24.896, 03:13:25.046, 03:14:25.113, 03:15:25.262, all inside 03:09 to 03:16Z.
* Event 1 `from` none; events 2 to 7 `from` = `to` = the invited recipient (self-transfers). `transferred_by` and `anchored_tx` empty on all 7.
* `documents.owner_user_id` = the recipient; `updated_at` 03:15:25.262; status `draft`.
* `action_provenance`: 7 `transfer-custody` rows, 03:09:24 to 03:15:25. `audit_logs`: 7 `documents.transfer-custody` 201 at the same times.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`; not exercised): `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`. After the recipient-exists check (`:2088-2100`), the route inserts into `custody_events` (`:2130`) with `from_holder_id` the current owner and `to_holder_id` the resolved holder, inside `withTenant`. I read `:2088-2135` and searched the file for a same-holder or self comparison (patterns for "same holder", "already the holder", "newHolderId ===", "owner_user_id ===" and similar): 0 matches that concern this route. The only equality matches are unrelated (`:307`, `:323`, rights-holder access).

**Not decided:** whether a transfer to the current holder should be a no-op, a 4xx, or stay allowed. Nothing I read rules on it.

**Not measured:** the seven `anchors.create` 400s that followed each request in the audit trail (item B3 of the same report) and the Invalid-DID reason; both are outside this ticket.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): "self-transfer" 0 hits; "to the current holder" 0 hits; `from_holder_id` 1 hit (KS-697, archived: a non-existent holder id was accepted, a different defect); "transfer-custody" 86 hits, read by title for a same-holder case (KS-1651, KS-1654, KS-1697 and others concern other defects).

**Related:** KS-1402 (the custody transfers this was measured on).

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request returns any tenant document's content hash and a signing nonce to any authenticated caller
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1223-1265` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only. For any document in the tenant it returns the document's `contentHash` and a signing nonce, and stores a signing request, even to a caller that `GET /api/documents/:id` refuses with its ownership 404 (:1142-1160). Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role, scope, owner, recipient or creating-connector check between :1223 and :1265. `getDocument` (:1236) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response carries `hash` (the document's `contentHash`), `nonce`, `message` and `expiresAt` (:1253-1259), and `saveSigningRequest` (:1245) stores the nonce that `POST /:id/sign` accepts (filed separately).
* So a same-tenant user who is not the owner, an admin or the recipient learns a document's content hash that `GET /:id` cloaks from them, and can mint the nonce the sign route needs.
* Callers: the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1027`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it writes nothing to the document, so the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check, plus whatever the sign route's own signer policy decides.

**Priority 3:** a read gap. It mutates no document; it stores an in-memory signing request.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request` is reachable by a connector (`sk_`) key holding only `documents:read`, not just by a signed-in human, and the connector token satisfies the handler's user check. Found by QA gate 32 on pull request 1829 (KS-1807) and re-read against develop `530f09112`. Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

* **Gateway:** like `/sign` (KS-1831), the route has no mount of its own beyond `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` (`routes/verification.ts`), then falls into the `/api/documents` mount in `routes/proxy.ts`: `requireScope('documents:read', 'documents:write')` for every method except create.
* **Originate:** `getUserFromRequest` passes any principal with a `userId`; the connector token carries `connector:<id>` (`generateConnectorToken`, auth `services/jwt.ts`). The handler then reads the document by id within the caller's tenant and returns its `contentHash` and a nonce, as this ticket says.
* **Documented now:** `docs/security/AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` (operation matrix, *Request / submit a signature*) and `docs/SCOPES.md` (`documents:write` row), with an UNDECIDED line on who may request a signature that points here and to KS-1831. That is in pull request 1829, docs only, not merged.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written.

title: GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events lists any tenant document's events without the ownership 404 that GET /:id applies
description:
**BLUF:** originate `GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2885-2907` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only, then returns every lifecycle event of the document (`listLifecycleEvents`, :2900). The ownership 404 that `GET /api/documents/:id` applies (:1142-1160) is missing, so a same-tenant caller who cannot read the document can read its events. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No owner, admin, recipient or creating-connector check between :2885 and :2907. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response is `{ documentId, count, events }`: the events as stored, with their actions and payloads.

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it is a read, and the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape for it. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check (owner, admin, recipient or creating connector, else the same 404).

**Priority 3:** a read gap; it mutates nothing.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; what the stored payloads contain for real documents is not measured.

title: Scope vocabulary and enforcement drift: five scopes gate nothing or name missing routes, gateway requireScope ignores <resource>:*, mints never call validateScopes, * is mintable by every key-admin role (SCOPES.md vs code)
description:
**BLUF:** Six differences between what `SCOPES.md` (and the KS-540 inventory) say about scopes and what the code enforces. Five scopes in the vocabulary gate nothing or name routes that do not exist; the gateway's `requireScope` does not honour `<resource>:*` although the shared helper does; the key mints never call `validateScopes`; `*` can be minted by every key-admin role although the docs say super-admin only; and gates and mints use scope strings that are not in the 32-member `SCOPES` array. `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke` (minted but unenforced) are already tracked in KS-1433 and are not repeated here. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; the gateway and mint behaviour was not exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). PR-1 rewrites `SCOPES.md` to describe what is built and marks each open question `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)`; this ticket is where the code side is decided.

## Items

1. **Declared, enforced nowhere.** `certifications:share`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/share` exists in `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` with no scope or role check (and is not in the published spec). `certifications:revoke`: the route checks the caller is the certification's issuer, no scope (not in the spec). `analytics:read`: the `/api/analytics` gateway mount is authentication only. `analytics:export`: `POST /api/analytics/exports` exists (in the spec) with no scope check. `users:write`: no reference in any source file outside `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts`.
2. **Names routes that do not exist.** `certifications:sign` (no `/{id}/sign` route in originate, not in the spec), `kyc:submit` (no `/api/kyc/submit`), `kyc:read` (no `/api/kyc/status`). The vocabulary entries are pinned by `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks843-subjects-erase-scope.test.ts`, so removing them is a decision and a test edit.
3. **Gateway wildcard.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` tests `userScopes.includes(s)` (exact) plus a lone `*`; the imported shared `hasScope` is shadowed by a local `const hasScope` in the same function. A key holding only `documents:*` is refused 403 on `GET /api/documents` and every other `/api/documents` method except create (the gateway's create handler in `routes/verification.ts` does accept `documents:*`). The KS-843 comment in the same file already calls the exact match "silent". No gateway test covers a `<resource>:*` key (control: the shared tests have 8 such cells).
4. **No validation at mint.** `services/security/src/index.ts` mint schema is `scopes: z.array(z.string()).default(['read'])`; originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`) stores the list as given; the shared `validateScopes` has no caller outside its own tests. The default `read` is not a vocabulary scope.
5. `*` **is not reserved.** `decideMint` in `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` allows every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member (`SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN`) with any scope list, `*` included; only a provisioning key is refused wildcards. `SCOPES.md` says `*` is "reserved for super-admin keys".
6. **Out-of-vocabulary strings in use.** `webhooks:manage` (gates `/api/webhooks`), `users:create` (accepted by auth's `POST /api/users/stub`), `register` (legacy literal in the gateway's create handler), `metering:read` (minted onto the metering key by `services/tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts`; no gate reads it), `read`/`write` (mint defaults and the fixed set the admin portal sends), and the OAuth list (`verify:read`, `admin:read`, `admin:write` in `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts`). The KS-540 inventory raised items 3, 4 and 6 as F-3, F-4 and F-5 on 2026-07-31; none is done.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (anchors:read, documents:revoke), KS-1777 (the flat 403 body of `requireScope`), KS-1653 (`certifications:write` admits `POST /api/users/stub`), KS-839 (OAuth `*`), KS-1535 and KS-1536 (which roles may mint keys).

Searched the board before filing: `certifications:share`, `certifications:revoke`, `analytics:read`, `users:write`, `kyc:submit`, `certifications:sign`, `metering:read` and `hasScope` each 0 hits; `wildcard` 4 hits (KS-839, KS-1584, KS-1156, KS-1210, none about the gateway helper); `validateScopes` 2 hits (KS-839, KS-1156). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843 and `documents:revoke` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 (docs lead, code aligns), either make each declared scope gate its route, or take the entry out of the vocabulary and out of the docs; make `requireScope` call `hasScope`; call `validateScopes` at both mints; restrict `*` to the roles the docs name. Which of these is intended is open, and PR-1 says so in the docs.

title: Docs claim rules the code does not apply: share checks no document access, ownerless documents skip the read check, a revoked key works 60 s at the gateway, the admin dashboard reads X-Tenant-Override, metering is certification-only
description:
**BLUF:** Five statements in the platform-k security docs describe a rule the code does not apply: document share checks no per-document access, a document with no recorded owner skips the read check, a revoked API key is still accepted by the gateway for up to 60 seconds, `GET /api/admin/dashboard` reads `X-Tenant-Override` from the raw header for an `ORG_ADMIN`, and the claim that agent document operations are metered holds only for certification operations. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; none of these was exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). The docs and the code disagree on each; PR-1 describes what is built, names this ticket beside the passage, and does not write either behaviour as the intended one.

## Items

1. **Share has no per-document access check.** `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`): after the role-or-scope gate (`DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` or `documents:share`) the handler runs `getDocument(id, tenantId)` and answers 404 only when the document is absent from the tenant; it never compares the caller with the owner, a recipient or an admin. `AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` R4 says "ownership checks still apply on read/share/revoke". Same class as KS-1688 (version) and KS-1814 (anchor; fixed), and as KS-1833/KS-1834 (lifecycle events).
2. **Ownerless documents skip the read check.** `GET /api/documents/{id}`: the refusal is guarded by `userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient`. `documentRepo` maps the owner as `row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`, so a row with neither column set has `owner.id === ''` and the guard is false for every caller in the tenant. The inventory (§2.3) says reading needs owner, admin, recipient or creating connector. Not measured: how many rows have no owner.
3. **A revoked key keeps working at the gateway.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` caches a valid `sk_` key in `apiKeyCache` for 60 s (a rejection for 30 s); nothing outside tests deletes or clears the cache (zero hits for `apiKeyCache.delete` and `apiKeyCache.clear`; control: `apiKeyCache.set` has two). The security service's revoke is immediate. The rules doc R6 says keys are "revocable immediately", contract §5 says "takes effect on next validate", and the rotation grace default `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS=0` was ruled "instant revoke" (2026-08-07, KS-577).
4. `X-Tenant-Override` **is read raw by one admin route.** The inventory (§2.4) says the override is "honoured only for the super-admin list". The gateway applies that list when it sets the tenant GUC, but it also allow-lists the header through to the services (`TRUST_HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` in `services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), and `GET /api/admin/dashboard` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` reads `req.headers['x-tenant-override']` itself and, if it is a UUID, counts documents, users and verifications for that tenant under `runWithPlatformScope`; with no header it returns platform-wide totals. That router admits `ORG_ADMIN` (`requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`) and so does the gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy (`enforceAdminProxy`). By this reading an `ORG_ADMIN` can read counts for another tenant. Counts only; not exercised live.
5. **Metering covers certifications only.** The rules doc R7 says agent document operations are metered (KS-320). `charge_events` rows are inserted only by `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts`, which only `routes/certifications.ts` calls for writes; `documents.ts` and anchoring do not import it. Create, version, share, revoke, transfer-custody and anchor write none. Which operations should be metered is a product call, not a code reading.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (connectors cannot revoke; unenforced scopes), KS-1688, KS-1833, KS-1834, KS-1814.

Searched the board before filing: `x-tenant-override` 8 hits (none about the dashboard; KS-1704 is about a super-admin's override), `apiKeyCache` 0, `charge_events` 1 (KS-1401, RLS on the table, not coverage), `lifecycle-events` hits KS-1833 and KS-1834 (excluded above). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns. Items 1 and 2 are access checks in originate; item 3 is a cache invalidation or a stated TTL; item 4 is to read the override from the verified request context, not the header; item 5 needs a ruling on what is metered first.

title: api-gateway: a 401 or 403 from in front of the security service is cached as a 30 s key rejection; should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer"? (gate 31, F2)
description:
**BLUF:** A design question, not a defect found today. The gateway's `checkApiKey` treats any non-OK status from the key-validate call outside 5xx, 408 and 429 as a key rejection and negative-caches it for about 30 s (answering 401 `Invalid API key`). By the gate's reading, the real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403 (`security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path; the handler near line 1800 answers 400, 503 or 200 with `valid: false`), so a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or a WAF) and would make every key, valid ones included, answer 401 `Invalid API key` for 30 s. Pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3) now pins today's behaviour for a 403, which turns it into a tested contract. Should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer" (503, not cached) instead?

**Source.** QA gate 31 on pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F2 (Note, a design question for Kam, not that pull request's defect). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate31-1827/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1788, where the 403 cell was asked for; KS-1174, which is about forwarding a distinct code per key failure and not about this classification; KS-1240, the original timeout work. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2, lines 56 to 59 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F2 (Note, design question for Kam, not this PR's defect).** The cell freezes "any non-OK status outside {5xx, 408, 429} is a key rejection, negative-cached 30 s".
  * The real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403. `security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path, and the handler at l.1800 answers 400 (schema), 503 (KS-1370) or 200 `valid:false`.
  * So a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or WAF). Today that would answer every key, valid ones included, `401 Invalid API key` for 30 s.
  * Pinning today's behaviour is what the ticket asked for, so this is fine to merge. But this PR now makes it a pinned contract, so whether an infrastructure 401/403 should count as "could not answer" deserves a ruling.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `checkApiKey` 1 hit (KS-1788). `couldNotAnswer` 0, `infrastructure 401` 0, `negative cache` 2 (KS-1788, KS-1207: neither asks this), `keys/validate` 23 (read: KS-1174, KS-1788, KS-1240 for ingress, WAF, status or "could not answer" text: none asks whether an infrastructure 401/403 is a rejection), `WAF` 8 (none about the key-validate call).

**Not measured by this filing:** the security service's routes (the statements about them are the gate's reading, not re-read here); what any ingress or WAF in front of the service answers in practice; whether one exists on any box.

title: Spec and docs describe contracts the code does not follow: analytics export sends no Location or Retry-After and returns a data URI; kyc/submit and kyc/status are listed but absent; KYC approval never raises a verification level
description:
**BLUF:** In three areas the published spec and the docs describe a contract the code does not follow: the analytics export, the KYC steps, and the link between KYC and a user's verification level. The analytics export 202 declares `Location` and `Retry-After` headers and a poll-until-`done` flow; the code sends neither header, returns the file inline as a `data:` URI, and calls the field `downloadUrl`, not `url`. The spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`, which do not exist. And no code path raises a user's verification level when a KYC verification is approved, although `WORKFLOWS.md` says it does. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The contract is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held (findings only this round); this ticket is where it is decided which side moves.

## Analytics export (`services/analytics`)

* **Headers:** the spec's `POST /api/analytics/exports` 202 says "poll the URL in the `Location` header until state=`done`" and declares `Location` and `Retry-After` response headers. `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` sets no header (zero hits for `setHeader`, `res.set`, `location` or `retry-after`; control: `setHeader('Location'` has hits in originate's `documents.ts`).
* **Status values and fields:** `exportService.ts` sets `pending`, `processing`, `completed` and `failed`; the spec's `AnalyticsExport` schema has `completed` in its status enum but also declares `url`, `sizeBytes` and `completedAt`, which the code does not send. The code sends `downloadUrl` and `expiresAt`. `WORKFLOWS.md` says `ready` and `url` (a presigned URL with a finite TTL).
* **The download:** `downloadUrl` is `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` (`createDownloadUrl` in `exportService.ts`), so the file travels inside the status response; there is no separate download request. `pdf` and `xlsx` exports contain JSON text, and `pdf` is labelled `application/octet-stream` (a placeholder, per its own comment).
* **Request and 202 body:** the spec's request declares `from` and `to`; the code reads `period` (required) with `startDate` and `endDate`, and also accepts `xlsx`. The 202 body is `{ success, data: { id, status, type, format, createdAt } }`, not the bare object.

## KYC (`services/kyc`)

* **Steps:** the spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`. `services/kyc/src/index.ts` registers `initiate`, `/:id`, `/user/:userId`, `/:id/document`, `/:id/selfie`, `/:id/complete`, `/:id/review`, `/:id/result` and `DELETE /user/:userId/data`. `GET /api/kyc/status` is read as `/:id` with id `status` and answers 404; `POST /api/kyc/submit` matches no service route (by reading the gateway's method map it would answer 405, because the path matches the spec's `/api/kyc/{id}`, which allows only GET; not executed). `initiate` answers 201 (not 202) with `verificationId`; statuses are lowercase `pending`, `in_progress`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`.
* **The level never moves:** `WORKFLOWS.md` says `GET /api/users/me` shows the new `verificationLevel` after KYC and that a raised level unlocks higher-tier document types. A search of service source (tests excluded) finds `users.verification_level` written only by the gateway admin route, the social-login path in auth and originate's admin route; the kyc service has no access to the users table (0 hits for `FROM users`, `UPDATE users`, `INTO users` in `services/kyc/src`; control: `verification_level` has 5 hits in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`). So an approved KYC verification does not change a token's level by this reading. The seeded `PROPERTY_DEED` document type also needs no level (`creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`), though the gate itself exists.

## Not repeated here

The create-document response shape (flat, not `DocumentDetail`), the `/anchor` 202 body, the verify `source` values and the error messages are recorded in the PR-2 pull request body as doc corrections, because there the code is plainly the intended behaviour; if you want them in the contract-corrections batch, say so.

Searched the board before filing: `kyc/submit`, `analytics exports`, `Retry-After` returned no ticket about these contract differences (KS-1327 is about KYC write races, KS-1372 about the login lockout). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. For the export, either send the headers and a real download, or change the spec and docs to the inline `data:` form; for KYC, remove the two steps from `x-workflows` and decide whether approval should raise the level.

**BLUF:** Four more differences between the published spec and the code, found by two read-only verifiers during the KS-1807 PR-2 pass; I re-read each against the spec and the handler at develop `85cd24d81`. Read, not probed on a running stack. Correcting the spec is a product-source change (it is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`) and is held this round, so this is findings only. This adds to the three items in my earlier comment on this ticket.

**1. `FlatAnchorRequest.contentHash` is stricter in the spec than in the code.** The spec pattern is `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` (lowercase only). The handler's schema (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts`) is `/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/i`, which accepts upper case. A spec that is stricter than its server is the shape the code's own comment on `ACCEPTED_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` says it wants to avoid.

**2. `FlatAnchorRequest.documentId` has the length bounds but no `pattern` in the spec.** The spec gives `minLength: 1` and `maxLength: 128` and a description that says "doc-… external id or a UUID (anchorSchema.ts documentId pattern)", in prose. The code adds a regex on top of the same length bounds (`anchorSchema.ts`, `documentId`), so a value the spec accepts can still be refused 400.

**3. `DocumentCreateRequest` does not list `contentHash`.** The spec's properties are `title`, `documentType`, `data`, `onBehalfOf`, `documentUuid`, `userUuid` and `organizationUuid`. The create handler (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `POST /`) reads `contentHash` from the body, and its own 400 for the unsupported `content` field says "send 'contentHash' (sha256 hex) or 'data' instead". A caller working from the spec is told to send a field it cannot find.

**4. Live routes the spec does not declare.** Searching the spec's path keys (control: `/api/documents` is declared): `POST /api/documents/{id}/sign`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/sign/request` (KS-1831, KS-1832 cover their behaviour, not their absence from the spec) and `/api/certifications/{id}/lineage` have no entry. `/api/certifications/{id}/verify`, `/api/admin/verification-queue` and `/api/admin/audit-logs` are also undeclared, and are covered by KS-1855.

**Also noted, code comment only (no contract difference):** the comment above `TRANSITIONAL_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` in `anchorSchema.ts` says "docs and the spec describe the vocabulary K advertises, and `certify` is no longer part of it". The spec's verb enum is generated from `ACCEPTED_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (in `anchoring.openapi.ts`), which includes the transitional `certify`, so the published enum does list it. `docs/VOCABULARY.md` in the PR-2 pull request states this correctly.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; whether Schemathesis flags item 1 (an upper-case hash the spec says is invalid) was not checked.

**BLUF:** Three more places where the published spec describes something the code does not do, found while re-checking the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The worst is billing `POST /api/billing/admin/credits`: the spec's request body is refused 400 by the handler. Read from code and spec at develop `85cd24d81`; not probed on a running stack. The spec is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held this round (findings only).

**1. `POST /api/billing/admin/credits`: the spec's request and the handler's do not match**

* Spec (`BillingAdminAdjustCreditsRequest`): `{ customerId, delta (integer), reason }`, `customerId` and `delta` required. The description says "Positive delta to grant; negative to deduct. Audit-logged." The 200 response is `BillingSuccess`, `{ success, message }`.
* Handler (`services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts`, `POST /admin/credits`): the Zod schema is `{ customerId: string, credits: positive integer }`. A request that follows the spec carries `delta` and no `credits`, so it fails validation and the handler answers 400. The handler only ever adds credits (`addCertificationCredits`); nothing deducts. It answers `{ customerId, creditsAdded, newBalance }`.
* "Audit-logged": the call writes an application log line (`[Stripe] Added credits`) and no audit record. Searching the billing service's non-test source for `audit` finds only the spec description (`billing.openapi.ts`) and text in the webhook handler (control: `logger.info` is found in 6 files of the same tree).
* Related, already tracked: KS-1850 (the handler admits `OWNER`, `ORG_ADMIN` and `SYSTEM_ADMIN`).

**2. The spec's second server is a deleted environment.** `servers[1]` is `https://secuura02-demo-api.kindtree-935b2ded.southeastasia.azurecontainerapps.io/api`, described as "Demo environment (Founders Hub, Azure Container Apps, southeastasia)". The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31 (the project record says those URLs are dead); the live demo is the VM stack. Anyone using the spec's server picker for the demo calls a dead host.

**3. Seven gateway operations under `/api/admin/document-types` are not in the spec.** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` registers GET (list, by id, an id's documents), POST, PUT, PATCH `/:id/status` and DELETE on `/api/admin/document-types`, all behind `requireAdmin`.
