title: The Schemathesis KS 1042 isolation fixture fails every run once an isolation tenant is archived: it re-activates with archived → active, which KS-1860 refuses with 409
description:
## BLUF

**The Schemathesis isolation fixture (**`systemTest/schemathesis/tests/isolation_tenant_fixtures.py`**) brings a found isolation tenant back to** `active` **with one** `PATCH …/status {"status": "active"}`**, and fails the requesting test on any answer but 200. Once KS-1860's PR (#1876) merges,** `archived → active` **answers 409. On any slot where isolation tenant A or B is archived, every run that requests the fixture then fails its KS 1042 precondition, and nothing through the API brings that tenant back. #1876 does not change the fixture.**

Filed by Seat S 9th on Wednesday's word of 2026-10-31 17:47:36Z, from QA gate 64 finding G64-F2 (found by code reading; not run live). Read from develop `32e8fe25cb24`.

## What the fixture does

* `_ensure_tenant` (`isolation_tenant_fixtures.py:17-44`) lists `/platform/tenants` and finds the row by slug.
  * If there is none, it creates the tenant (`:30-35`).
  * If `needs_reactivation(row)` (`tests/support/isolation_tenants.py:48-57`, true for any status other than `active`), it sends `PATCH /platform/tenants/{id}/status` with `{"status": "active"}` (`:37-39`).
  * Any answer but 200 is a `pytest.fail` whose message says it could not re-activate the isolation tenant, prefixed with KS 1042's key (`:40-43`).
* The comment at `:38` reads: "A sweep can suspend or archive any tenant; the test needs this one live."

## What changes underneath it

* **KS-1860, PR #1876 (gated, not merged).** The status route allows only `provisioning → active`, `active → suspended`, `suspended → active` and `suspended → archived`. So:
  * a suspended or provisioning isolation tenant is still re-activated (200);
  * an archived one answers 409, so the fixture fails, on every run.
* **How an isolation tenant becomes archived:**
  * On develop, one `active → archived` call archives it.
  * With #1876 it takes two calls (`active → suspended → archived`). A sweep can still make both.
* **KS-1861 (PR not yet raised).** `DELETE /platform/tenants/{id}` with `{"confirm": true}` archives the tenant instead of deleting its row.
  * On develop, a sweep that reached that call removed the row, and the fixture re-created the tenant by slug.
  * Afterwards it leaves an archived row with the same slug, so that path ends in the same failure.
* **No way back through the API:** an archived tenant is terminal, unless Kam's open card on KS-1861 (`secuura-ks1861-archive-from-which-status-1101`) allows `archived → suspended`. If he does, the fixture would need two moves, `archived → suspended → active`.

## Expected

The fixture handles an archived isolation tenant, so a slot that ever archived one does not fail every later run. How is systemTest's call (work-stream G, KS 492). For example:

* take the two-step route if Kam allows it;
* otherwise fail with a message that names the archived tenant and what to do;
* or stop sweeps from archiving the isolation tenants.

## Board search before filing

Searched titles and descriptions on the KS team for `isolation_tenant_fixtures`, `needs_reactivation`, `_ensure_tenant`, the fixture's "precondition: could not re-activate" message, `isolation tenant` and `re-activate` (0 each). Positive controls: `isolation` (55 hits) and `cross-tenant` (52 hits) find tickets. None covers this: KS 1740 and KS 1741 concern cross-tenant peers, and KS 1042 is Done.

Not done here: the fixture is not changed (Wednesday: "Do not change the fixture in this PR"); nothing run against a stack.

title: KS-1384 R1 re-anchor unknown-outcome residuals: a holder dying before the mark, a non-2xx after anchoring persisted, and the marker trusting anchoring's fail-open 404 can still pay a second fee
description:
## What this is

QA gate 65 (GO WITH NOTES on KS-1384 R1 round 3, pull request 1868, head `7ed460cc4258`) measured three ways the re-anchor retry route can still pay a second anchoring fee. Its finding is G65-F2. Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-31 at 19:11Z: one ticket for all three.

**None is a regression.** Each cell pays the same at round 2 (`a46c251e1419`) as at the head. They were measured on real Postgres under the app role, against a loopback anchoring fake that counts POST /api/anchors (the fee point) on arrival.

## The three residuals (the gate's wording)

**(i) A holder that dies between its POST and the mark.**

* A deploy, an OOM or a container restart in that window leaves no marker. So does a mark that throws: a DB error gives a 500 before the 503.
* The window is at most about 20 s. It needs no 10-minute freeze, because the kept claim simply lapses.
* After the lease, a confirmed row reads as absent (G58-F2), and the retry POSTs.
* Cell `R3-crash` (claim kept, no marker, row confirmed): **1 extra POST at the head and at the base.**
* Who closes it: R2a's landed-anchor answer (G58-F2 Q3a), for a row that has confirmed. R2a's gate re-runs this cell; it must pay once.

**(ii) A non-2xx from an intermediary after anchoring persisted.**

* Any non-2xx answered after anchoring persisted takes the same path:
  * a 502, 503 or 504 from an ingress;
  * anchoring crashing after `dbPersistAnchor` behind a proxy.
* `postReanchor` calls it `answered`, and the route sends it down R1's failure path. The re-check has already removed any marker.
* Cell `R4-502`: **2 POSTs at the head and at the base.**
* R2a's landed-anchor answer covers it only if the row has confirmed. A row still `failed` reads as absent, as before. R2a's gate re-runs this cell; it must pay once.

**(iii) The marker trusts anchoring's fail-open 404 (G58-F3).**

* The only way a maybe-landed marker clears is anchoring answering 404 "no row". Anchoring answers exactly that 404 when its DB read fails (G58-F3, gate 58, by reading).
* Cell `R2-f3` (marked, row confirmed, the read answers the swallowed 404): **1 POST at the head**, a second fee where the design intends 0. It is 1 at the base too.
* Wednesday ruled that **G58-F3 joins the KS-1384 train's deploy hold**, beside F0, F-b, R2a and R2b.
* **G58-F3 itself is fixed in R2a** (pull request 1874): anchoring's `GET /api/anchors/document/{documentId}` answers 503 for a read that throws and for a database that is down, with no error text (R2a's cells f3a, f3b and f3g). originate turns that 503 into its own 503, with nothing posted. So (iii) is closed when R2a merges, and the hold guarantees R1 never deploys without it. Gate 65's R2-f3 cell keeps the OLD 404 in its fake on purpose, so it stays red by construction; R2a's anchoring cells are the proof.

## What would close each

* (i) and (ii), for a confirmed row: R2a (KS-1384, pull request 1874), proven by gate 65's two cells at R2a's gate.
* (iii): R2a, as above. One related read is NOT covered: the by-id route's document-id fallback still reads a failed database read as no rows. That is outside G58-F3, and the retry route does not use it.
* (i) and (ii), for a row that is still `failed`: nothing in the train today. This ticket holds them.
  * (ii) for a failed row needs the route to treat a non-2xx after a sent POST as unknown, not as a failure, or anchoring to tell the two apart.

## Not measured (from the gate)

* The real anchoring service: the swallowed 404 is by reading.
* Real POST latencies.
* Which intermediary answers what, and after how long.
* Real crash windows: the gate seeded the post-crash state.
* Node 24 LTS: the gate ran Node v26.8.1.

## References

* Ticket: KS-1384. Pull requests: 1868 (R1) and 1874 (R2a).
* Corrected the same evening: the first version of this ticket said nothing in the train closes (iii). R2a's G58-F3 fix does.
* Gate 65's verdict and probe are held in Wednesday's gate record for 2026-11-01 (`gate65-r1r3-probe.integration.test.ts`, cells R2-f3, R3-crash and R4-502).
* Filed by Seat W 14th on Wednesday's ruling. Board search first: 17 terms, none matched these residuals (`markReanchorPostUnknown`, `retryPostUnknown`, `postReanchor`, G58-F3, G65-F2, "fail-open 404", "maybe-landed", "intermediary", `confirmReanchorClaim`, `claimDocumentForReanchor` and others).

title: social adapters: decide error-field parity with github.ts per provider
description:
## BLUF

After KS 1858 (pull request 1879, merged as `9bc1cf3b538b`), the Google, Facebook, LinkedIn and Microsoft (personal) adapters refuse a 200 token answer with no usable `access_token`, but unlike `github.ts` (KS 1792) they do not also refuse one that carries an `error` field. Gate 67 measured the split through the real adapter classes with a stubbed `fetch` (8 answer shapes by 4 adapters, the same probe on develop for comparison): a 200 with only `{error: 'invalid_grant'}` is refused on all four, by the `access_token` check (the profile endpoint is never called); a 200 with `{access_token: 'tok', error: 'invalid_grant'}` resolves on all four, exactly as before the change, where `github.ts` would refuse it. Whether any of the four providers ever answers a token request that way is not known: nothing was measured against a provider. Low. The decision belongs to whoever owns auth; the instrument that closes it is named below.

## Item 1: decide error-field parity, per provider

* **What differs.** `github.ts` refuses on `typeof access_token !== 'string' || access_token === '' || tokenBody.error !== undefined` (line 89 at develop `9bc1cf3b538b`, with a comment saying GitHub answers a bad or expired code with HTTP 200 and an error body). The four adapters refuse on the first two conditions only: `google.ts` line 88, `facebook.ts` line 83, `linkedin.ts` line 86, `microsoft-personal.ts` line 88.
* **Closing instrument.** Each provider's own token-endpoint error documentation, or a live probe of a bad code. Then either add the `error` clause to that adapter, or add a cell that pins the token-plus-error shape as accepted, so the choice is on record per provider.
* **Why it may not matter.** The ticket that raised the sibling guard (KS 1858) records that these providers answer errors with a non-2xx status as RFC 6749 section 5.2 requires; that is a statement from the source gate, not tested here.

## Item 2 (second item, not its own ticket): the refusal's log line

* **Unpinned.** The mutant "the `logger.warn` line removed" survives on all four adapters (28 mutants, 24 killed, these 4 survived; all five cells of each file still pass). No cell asserts the log.
* **Thinner than the GitHub adapter's.** `github.ts` logs a bounded `error` value (`error.slice(0, 80)`) with its refusal (line 90); the four new lines log only the provider name (`google.ts` line 89, `facebook.ts` line 84, `linkedin.ts` line 87, `microsoft-personal.ts` line 89), so an operator sees "answered 200 without an access token" and no reason. The flow fragment of pull request 1879 declares this ("the provider name only, no body"), so it is a deliberate choice; the gate called it a diagnosability gap, not a security problem (nothing from the body is logged).

## Source and related (different tickets, named in plain text)

QA gate 67 on pull request 1879, findings G67-F1 and G67-F2 (verdict file local to the coordinator). KS 1858 (the ticket whose change this follows; stays open), KS 1792 (the GitHub guard), KS 1885 (a different class: the callback echoes an exchange error whole, so a token with a newline reaches the 400), KS 1617 (the social sign-in umbrella; Apple's `id_token` is its item 8).

## Board search before filing (team KS: issue title and description through `searchableContent`, comment bodies through the `comments` filter, because `searchableContent` does not reach comments)

* 'token exchange failed (no access token)': issue title/description 0 hit(s):  | comment bodies 1 issue(s): KS 1792
* 'answered 200 without an access token': issue title/description 0 hit(s):  | comment bodies 0 issue(s):
* 'refuses a token answer': issue title/description 0 hit(s):  | comment bodies 0 issue(s):
* 'safeReason': issue title/description 5 hit(s): KS 1915 \[Backlog\]; KS 1904 \[Backlog\]; KS 1895 \[Backlog\]; KS 1893 \[Backlog\]; KS 1868 \[In Progress\] | comment bodies 1 issue(s): KS 1868
* 'a random token that exists nowhere': issue title/description 0 hit(s):  | comment bodies 0 issue(s): 
  Positive control `safeReason` hit in both and the fresh random token hit 0 in both. The hits for the terms that name this topic are KS 1792 and KS 1858 only, both named above; none records the `error`-field question or the unpinned log line. KS 1885 and KS 1617 were read and are different.

title: KS-1384 R2b follow-up: a bound bearer-less verify heal, so a v2 or anonymous v1 verify can heal a stale-pending blob from verify-by-hash's answer
description:
## What this is

A follow-up to KS-1384 R2b, filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-10-31 19:55:30Z. It gets its own tier-1 gate instead of riding inside R2b's money-path pull request.

**Before R2b,** both verify heals could heal a stale-pending blob from verify-by-hash's pre-auth chain answer:

* v1 used `confirmStalePendingAnchor`, and v2 used `healBlobWithChainFact`;
* each healed on the same transaction OR "sameDoc" (the chain index naming the document id);
* each wrote through `persistHealedAnchor`.

**R2b replaces both** with one shared path, `anchorStateSync` `healAnchorForVerify`, which:

* reads the blob's OWN anchor row (`GET /api/anchors/:anchorId`) with the caller's bearer;
* lets the one resolver decide;
* writes a `confirmed` decision through the conditional blob write.

**The cost:** anchoring's anchor read and own-create sit behind its JWT gate (`app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`). So the heal cannot run without a bearer:

* a **v2 verify** (caller-independent by design: it forwards no bearer) heals nothing;
* an **anonymous v1 verify** heals nothing.

Both present the STORED state, fail closed, until the document's GET reconcile or the poller heals it. That costs staleness, never a fee.

## The variant to build and gate

For a verify with no usable row read (v2, an anonymous v1, or a 401 or 404), give the resolver verify-by-hash's own answer AS the row, and do NOT ask own-create:

* the row is built from that answer's `metadata.documentId` or `certId`, its transaction, its block, and its payload timestamp;
* only a confirmed chain fact that names this document AND binds to one of its recorded create attempts heals (the resolver's binding rule, to the millisecond);
* "sameDoc" alone, and an unbound chain answer, stay refused.

## Why a separate gate

It is a NEW write path driven by an unauthenticated request. Binding to the create attempts may well make it safe, but that is a claim a gate must test (Wednesday's words): "safe because the binding is tight" is exactly a claim a gate must test, not one to ship inside a money-path PR that is already large.

## Cells it would need (at least)

* A bound chain answer heals on v2 and on an anonymous v1, and is written once.
* A chain answer naming the document but NOT bound (another create attempt's timestamp, or an event's) heals nothing.
* A chain answer naming another document heals nothing.
* A simulated or non-64-hex answer heals nothing (KS-1661, KS-1676).
* No caller bearer is ever forwarded on v2 (the KS-584 QA-High rule).
* A mutant per rule.

## References

* KS-1384 (R2b part 5, the pull request after 1874).
* KS-584 (the caller-independent v2 contract).
* KS-1661 and KS-1676 (the heal guards, kept in the shared path).
* KS-1809 (a document read and a verify can settle the same anchor differently; related, not the same).
* Board searched first: `healAnchorForVerify`, `healBlobWithChainFact`, `confirmStalePendingAnchor`, `persistHealedAnchor`, `fetchChainFact`, "caller-independent", "bearer-less", "verify heal", "stale-pending heal", "verify-by-hash". None covers this variant.
* Filed by Seat W 14th on Wednesday's ruling.

title: KS-1384 R2a residual: anchoring's upsert never refreshes content_hash, so a confirmed row with a different hash is paid again on every retry (reachability first)
description:
## What this is

QA gate 68 (GO WITH NOTES on KS-1384 R2a, pull request 1874, head `31d146678`) recorded this as G68-F3, a NOTE. It is a residual, not a regression: it pays the same at R1 round 3's head `7ed460cc4258` as at R2a's. Filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-10-31 20:51Z: one ticket.

## The residual

* R2a's "already anchored" rule treats a confirmed anchor row whose stored hash DIFFERS from the document's as "not this content's anchor". So the retry route POSTs (R2a's own cell f2e pins that branch).
* Anchoring's upsert (`index.ts` `dbPersistAnchor`, `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)`) **never updates** `content_hash` in its update list.
* So the row keeps its old hash. It never matches the document again, and each later pass through an `anchor_failed` blob POSTs again.
* Gate 68's cell H-diff-repeat: **2 POSTs, at the head and at the base.**

## First question: is it reachable?

Can a document's `content_hash` change IN PLACE after it was anchored, with its blob later back at `anchor_failed`?

* `POST /api/documents/:id/version` records a NEW document by its own description (KS 86), which would make this unreachable in-product. Gate 68 did not trace the handler, and neither has this ticket.
* If no in-place path exists, the severity stays a NOTE and the fix is a documented invariant plus a test.
* If one exists, the fix is in anchoring's upsert (refresh `content_hash`, or refuse a hash change on a confirmed row) and in R2a's rule.

## Not measured

* The `/version` trace.
* A real anchoring service; gate 68 used a loopback fake.
* Real chain state.

## References

* KS-1384 (R2a, pull request 1874; QA gate 68's verdict record).
* Related, not the same: KS 1650 (originate's own already-anchored check is not network-bound) and KS 1200 (where the `(document_id, network)` unique is declared).
* Board searched first: `isLandedForThisContent`, G68-F3, `content_hash`, "ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)", "upsert never updates", H-diff-repeat, "hash can change", `documents/:id/version`. None covers this residual.
* Filed by Seat W 14th on Wednesday's ruling.

title: KS 1384 R2b follow-up (G70-F1): an own-create confirmed blob takes originate's network, so a confirmed document can name the wrong network for good
description:
**BLUF:** When the retry route's own-create lookup finds a document's create on chain, it confirms the document with ORIGINATE's `CARDANO_NETWORK` (default `preprod`), not the network the transaction is on. Since KS 1384 R2b made `confirmed` terminal in SQL, nothing can correct that label afterwards. Where originate and anchoring are configured with different networks, a confirmed document names the wrong network permanently. It is not a money issue.

**Where** (at R2b's head `ecfe4f07fdce`, PR 1884; line numbers move with merges):

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` \~1582: the own-create `found` branch builds the confirmed blob with `network: process.env.CARDANO_NETWORK || 'preprod'`.
* It writes through `writeReanchorOutcome`. The terminal predicates are `documentRepo.ts` \~939 (the outcome write) and \~994 (`writeAnchorBlobIf('confirmed')` requires `status IS DISTINCT FROM 'confirmed'`). So the poller, the GET reconcile and the verify heal can never rewrite the label.
* Those readers' own confirmed blob takes `row.network` (`anchorStateSync.ts` `confirmedBlobOf`), which is right. Only the own-create `found` write is wrong.

**Mechanism:** anchoring scans ITS wallet on ITS network (anchoring's `CARDANO_NETWORK`). The route then writes the transaction under originate's network label.

**Measured by QA gate 70** (probe70 cell N-ocnet, anchoring on preview, originate's network unset): `409 This document is already anchored on chain (9b0a9d…) blob network preprod row network preview posts 0`. Red-before: at `31d146678` the same document POSTs (`N-ocnet 202 … posts 1`). The wrong-label write is new with R2b's step 3.

**Not traced:** which clients present `blockchain.network` (an explorer link, say).

**Fix shapes** (QA gate 70):

* (a) Return the network in own-create's answer (anchoring knows it) and write that.
* (b) Or make the train's deploy-hold check (originate's and anchoring's `CARDANO_NETWORK` equal on each box) a boot check.

**Folded in (gate 70's G70-F5 i and ii, text and dead field, ruled to this ticket):**

* `services/originate/src/services/reanchorInFlight.ts` :13 (module header) and :160 (the `anchored` reason string, logged) still say "on this network". The rule above :118 still states the network leg before the R2b paragraph that drops it.
* `InFlightContext.network` (:87) is still required and still passed (`documents.ts` \~1631), but nothing reads it. It is harmless; a future reader may think it is compared.

**Until this is closed:** the KS 1384 train's deploy hold keeps its check that both services' `CARDANO_NETWORK` are equal on every box (QA gate 70 condition (a)).

Source: QA gate 70 verdict (G70-F1, G70-F5), Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-01 00:44:35Z. Board-searched first by symbol and path (own-create, ownCreate, confirmedBlob, writeReanchorOutcome, InFlightContext, "network: process.env.CARDANO_NETWORK", "on this network", "wrong network", [blockchain.network](<http://blockchain.network>), documents.ts:1582, G70-F1): no existing ticket covers it.

title: The tenant status route writes its audit row outside the status change: a failed audit write answers 500 after the move has committed, with no audit row
description:
## BLUF

`PATCH /api/tenants/:id/status` **(**`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`**) commits the status change and then writes its** `tenant_status_changed` **audit row as a second, separate statement. If the audit write fails, the route answers the constant 500, yet the move has already committed and nothing records it. QA gate 71 measured this on real Postgres for** `archived → suspended`**, the archive reversal. A retry then answers 409. Refs KS 1860 / KS 1861.**

Filed by Seat S 9th on Wednesday's word of 2026-11-01 01:30:50Z, from QA gate 71 findings G71-F1 and G71-F2. Read at source on #1885's head `48d05f02` and on develop `3d036184`.

## What the code does

* The route runs the conditional update through `platformQuery`, which is `platformPool.query`, so it autocommits on its own (`index.ts:453-456` at `48d05f02`; `:451-454` on develop):
  `UPDATE tenants SET status = $1, updated_at = now() WHERE id = $2 AND status = ANY($3::text[])`.
* After a successful update, it writes the audit row with a second `platformQuery` (`:474-478` at `48d05f02`; `:472-476` on develop):
  `INSERT INTO platform_audit_log (action, …) VALUES ('tenant_status_changed', 'tenant', $1, $2)`.
* If that INSERT throws, the `catch` answers `500 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR",…}}`. The UPDATE is not undone.

## Measured (QA gate 71, real Postgres 15, the real entry module)

* Gate cell S1: `archived → suspended`, with the audit INSERT made to fail by a gate-only trigger. Result: `{"code":500, …, "status":"suspended", "audit":[]}`.
  * The client is told the move failed.
  * The tenant has left `archived`.
  * No audit row exists.
  * A retry answers 409 "Cannot change tenant status from suspended to suspended".
  * Evidence is in Wednesday's gate 71 folder (`evidence/s1_status_route_audit_fail.json`).
* The same shape applies to every allowed move on this route.

## Scope

* **Not introduced by KS 1861's PR (#1885).** The shape has been on develop since KS 1860's PR (#1876); gate 64 did not flag it.
* #1885 routes the archive reversal (`archived → suspended`, Kam's ruling b) through these lines, so the gap now covers reversing an archive too.
* **Contrast:** the Delete route (#1885) already wraps its status change and its `tenant_archived` row in one transaction on a pool client: BEGIN, UPDATE, INSERT, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK, then release (`index.ts:585-608` at `48d05f02`). The fix is the same pattern on the status route.

## Expected

* The status change and its `tenant_status_changed` row commit together, or neither does.
* A failed audit write answers 500 and leaves the status as it was.
* A failure is recorded at least as well as Delete records one.

## Test strength to carry into the fix (G71-F2)

Two of gate 71's mutants of the Delete transaction pass all 30 cells of #1885's own tests, because their fake `pg` cannot see them:

* **G71-M2:** the `tenant_archived` row is written on the pool (`platformQuery`) instead of the transaction client. The fake's BEGIN snapshot includes the audit array, so a ROLLBACK also reverts an out-of-transaction row. Only a COMMIT failure on real Postgres (gate cell E8) shows a `tenant_archived` row surviving a rolled-back archive.
* **G71-M4:** `client.release()` is dropped. The fake's `release` is a no-op. On the real pool (max 5) the connections run out, and 42 gate cells time out.

The fix's red-proof should kill both, as well as the status route's own gap. Either use a real-Postgres cell for the transactions, or a fake whose `pool.query` path sits outside the transaction snapshot and whose `release` calls are counted.

## Board search before filing

Searched titles and descriptions on the KS team for:

* `tenant_status_changed`: 1 hit, KS 1913, the audit-log colour;
* `tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: 12 hits, none on audit atomicity;
* `status route`: 2 hits, KS 1914 and an unrelated credential ticket;
* `audit row outside`: 0;
* `outside the transaction`: 2 hits, both other services;
* `client.release`: 0.

No ticket covers this.

Not done here: no code change; nothing run by me against a database (the measurement is gate 71's).

title: analytics: a failed export stores the thrown error's message, and GET /api/analytics/exports/:id returns it to the caller
description:
**BLUF:** `ExportService.processExport` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/analytics/src/services/exportService.ts`, line 160) stores the thrown error's message on the export record, and the analytics export routes return that record to the caller. A failed export therefore puts internal error text (a database, filesystem or library message) into the API answer. This is the KS 1410 class (an error message landing in a client-visible body). It is not covered by KS 1853 or KS 1856 (dedupe below). Filed on Wednesday's word; found while raising the KS 1868 analytics loaders, which do not touch this line.

**Where (read at source, develop** `a71479b49bf3`**):**

* Line 160, in the catch of the private `processExport` (starts at line 106): `exportResult.error = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error';`
* The record type `ExportResult` has `error?: string` (`src/types/analytics.types.ts:419`).
* `GET /api/analytics/exports/:id` answers `res.json({ success: true, data: exportResult })` (`src/routes/analytics.ts:334-346`), so the stored message is in the body. The list route (`GET /api/analytics/exports`, lines 362-365) and the create route's answer (lines 305-308) return the same record type; those two were read, not traced to the field.

**Measured and not measured:** read with sed and grep at the paths above. NOT reproduced against a running service, and what a given failure message contains was not measured.

**Same file or neighbour, check during the fix:** `dbSaveExport` (`exportService.ts:30`), `dbSaveAlertRule` (`scheduledJobs.ts:30`), `dbSaveAlert` (`scheduledJobs.ts:63`).

**Dedupe (board search by symbol and path, issues and comment bodies; positive control** `gracefulShutdown` **hit, random token 0):** `exportService.ts` hits KS 1853 (spec and docs contracts the code does not follow) and KS 1856 (the list route returns every caller's exports; no role, tenant or user), and neither is this. `dbSaveExport`, `dbSaveAlertRule`, `dbSaveAlert` and `loadScheduledJobsFromDb` return 0.

**Found by:** Seat R 69th, 2026-11-01.

title: AuditLogger.flush: an event can still be lost when logging the failure throws; multi-failure retry order breaks the hash chain; the buffer is unbounded on persistent failure
description:
**BLUF:** In `AuditLogger.flush` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/security/audit-logger.ts`) an audit event can still be lost when the failure log itself throws; with several failures in one flush the events are retried in reverse order, so the hash chain does not verify in delivery order; and nothing bounds the buffer when `onEvent` keeps failing. QA gate 73 found these on pull request 1888 (KS 1868, tier 1, GO WITH NOTES), where they are recorded as limits of that change, not defects of it. Filed on Wednesday's word. The module is a published subpath of the shared package with no importer at this base, so none of this is reachable from a service today.

**G73-F1 (medium, pre-existing):** in the catch of `flush`, `logger.error(...)` (line 328 at the head of pull request 1888) runs before `this.eventBuffer.unshift(event)` (line 330). If the logger throws (the gate names winston given a non-string message), the `unshift` is skipped and the event is dropped. Read at source by this seat.

**G73-F3 (pre-existing):** `flush` copies the buffer, empties it, then loops; each failed event is put at the FRONT with `unshift`, so two failures A then B leave the buffer as B, A. They are retried in reverse order and the audit hash chain does not verify in delivery order. Read at source by this seat.

**G73-F4 (pre-existing):** nothing caps the buffer. `maxBatchSize` (line 272) only triggers a flush; it does not bound `eventBuffer`. When `onEvent` keeps failing, every flush re-adds every failed event and new events keep arriving, so the buffer grows and the retries pile up. Pull request 1888 routes the unreadable-thrown-value case onto this same path. Read at source by this seat; growth was not measured.

**Required for this ticket's red-proof (G73-F2):** the cells in pull request 1888 log one event each, so two gate mutants survive them: `unshift` replaced by `push`, and stopping after the first failure. The red-proof here must include multi-event cells (at least two failing events in one flush, asserting that none is lost and the retry order) that kill both mutants.

**Measured and not measured:** the findings are the gate's; the verdict is at `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-01_gate73-ks1868-auditlogger-1888/verdict.md`. This seat re-read F1, F3 and F4 at source (instrument: sed and grep of the file above) and did NOT reproduce any of them against a running service.

**Dedupe (board search over** `AuditLogger`**,** `audit-logger`**,** `eventBuffer`**,** `hashIntegrity`**; issues and comment bodies; positive control** `gracefulShutdown` **hit, random token 0):** `audit-logger` hits KS 1595 (a `gdpr.ts` and JWT-claim follow-up, not this); `AuditLogger` and `eventBuffer` hit only comments on KS 1868; `hashIntegrity` returns 0.

**Found by:** Seat R 69th, 2026-11-01.

title: nft-certificate: ensureFreshParams reuses cached protocol parameters with no maximum age, so after a long Blockfrost outage the mint TTL is stale and the chain rejects the transaction
description:
**BLUF:** In nft-certificate, `ensureFreshParams()` puts no maximum age on the cached protocol parameters, and the mint transaction's TTL is built from the cached `slot`. After a Blockfrost outage longer than about two hours, a mint is built with a TTL behind the chain's current slot, which the chain rejects: a failed mint, not a wrong one. Found by QA gate 76 on pull request 1891 (KS 1868) as a pre-existing item at develop `85c56a3d1eb9`; it is not caused by that change. Priority Low.

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/cardano/index.ts:75-84`, `ensureFreshParams()`. It refreshes when the cache is older than `PARAMS_CACHE_TTL_MS` (5 minutes), but when `fetchProtocolParams()` returns `null` it keeps and returns the old `cachedParams` with no age limit; it throws `Protocol parameters unavailable` (line 83) only when nothing is cached. `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/cardano/mintTransaction.ts:115` sets the TTL to `params.slot + 7200` from those cached parameters.
* **Effect (read from the code, not reproduced):** `slot` is the chain tip at the last successful fetch, and 7200 slots is about two hours. If every refresh fails for longer than that, the TTL is already in the past when the transaction is built.
* **Related:** pull request 1891 makes an unreadable thrown value take the same path as an ordinary Error (`null`, then the cached parameters). It does not create this behaviour; it now reaches it for one more kind of value.
* **Not measured:** a real outage, the chain's exact rejection, or how often this occurs. A direction for whoever picks it up, which the owner decides: give the cached parameters a maximum age and throw `Protocol parameters unavailable` past it.

title: analytics: createExport answers 202 for an export the database never saved, because dbSaveExport swallows every database error
description:
**BLUF:** In the analytics service, `POST /api/analytics/exports` answers `202` for an export the database never saved. `ExportService.dbSaveExport` catches every database error and only logs it, so `createExport` carries on and the route reports success. This holds for ANY error, an ordinary one included. Found by QA gate 78 on pull request 1893 (KS 1868) as a pre-existing item at develop `85c56a3d1eb9`; that change does not cause it. Priority Low.

* **Where (develop** `85c56a3d1eb9`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/analytics/src/services/exportService.ts`. `dbSaveExport` puts the export in the in-memory map first (line 31); when a database is configured it then runs the INSERT in a try whose catch, at line 56, only logs `DB save export failed` and returns. `createExport` awaits it at line 75, starts `processExport` without an await, and returns the record. `Blockchain/Dev/services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts:308-310` awaits `createExport` and answers `res.status(202)`.
* **Effect (read from the code, not reproduced):** when the database write fails (an outage, a constraint, a bad value), the caller still gets `202` and an export id, and the record exists only in that process's memory map. It would be lost on a restart and would not be visible to another instance, while the database never holds it. `processExport` swallows its own saves the same way (lines 113, 157 and 161 at the base).
* **Not caused by pull request 1893:** that change reads the thrown value safely inside this same catch. Before it, an unreadable value rejected `createExport` (a route 500) or left an unhandled rejection from `processExport` (gate 78); after it, that case behaves like an ordinary Error, which already answered `202`.
* **Not the same as:** KS 1922 (the stored error message that the export routes return) and KS 1856 (the list route's missing role and tenant checks). Both touch `exportService.ts`; neither covers a failed save.
* **Not measured:** a real database failure, whether anything depends on the `202`, or how often a save fails. A direction for the owner to decide: let `dbSaveExport` report the failure to `createExport` and answer a non-2xx, or document the memory-only behaviour.

title: persona switch: if anything throws after the refresh-token cookie is set, the generic 500 still carries the Set-Cookie (pre-existing, no real trigger found)
description:
**BLUF:** in demo-service `POST /demo-api/persona/switch` (`src/routes/persona.ts`), if anything throws after the upstream refresh-token cookie has been copied onto the response (lines 61-63), the catch (lines 76-80 at develop `d7691f35312e`) answers the generic 500 and the 500 still carries that `Set-Cookie`. This is pre-existing (not introduced by pull request 1894), no real trigger was found, and the gate that found it probed it on the real router. Priority Medium because it is a session cookie on an error response.

## Where

* `persona.ts:61-63`: `res.setHeader('Set-Cookie', authResult.setCookieHeader)` runs before `res.json(...)` builds the success answer.
* `persona.ts:76-80`: the catch logs and answers `res.status(500).json(...)` without clearing headers already set.

## Evidence (QA gate 79, 2026-11-01)

A probe on the real router with a user object carrying a BigInt made `res.json` throw at line 65. The answer was HTTP 500 with a `set-cookie` header holding the probe's stand-in `refresh_token` value and `HttpOnly` (probe log: `logs/probe_setcookie_on_500.out` in the verdict folder). Verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-01_gate79-ks1868-persona-1894/verdict.md` (finding G79-F2).

## Not known

No real source of an exception between the cookie and the response was found in the code read (the success answer is a plain object of values taken from the auth result). Whether the cookie reaches a browser on a 500 (the demo overlay may ignore it) was not tested.

## Fix shape (not made)

Set the cookie only after the last step that can throw, or clear it in the catch (`res.removeHeader('Set-Cookie')` before the 500).

## Related

KS 1868 (the unreadable-thrown-value umbrella) is where this was found; pull request 1894 (open when this was filed) does not touch lines 61-63 or the 500 answer.

title: nft-certificate: if the DB save after a successful on-chain mint fails, the client gets success and the record stays at status minting, with nothing to reconcile it
description:
**BLUF:** in nft-certificate `mintNFT` (`src/services/minting.service.ts`), the save that records status `minted` runs after the on-chain mint has returned (line 350 at develop `d7691f35312e`). `dbSaveNFTCertificate` swallows a database error (its catch only logs), so if that one save fails the client is told the mint succeeded (it gets a txHash) and memory says `minted`, but the database keeps the previous status `minting`, and nothing in the service reads or reconciles that status. This is pre-existing (it is what an ordinary Error does today); it was measured by QA gate 84 on pull request 1899, which does not change it. Priority Medium: a stuck record for a mint that really happened on chain.

## Where

* `minting.service.ts:350` (at `d7691f35312e`): `await dbSaveNFTCertificate(nftRecord)` with status MINTED, after `mintOnCardano` returned.
* `minting.service.ts:40-91`: the helper sets the in-memory record first, then `await query(...)` in a try whose catch only logs `DB save certificate failed`; no rethrow, no retry.
* `NFTStatus.MINTING` (`types/index.ts:295`) is written at `minting.service.ts:315` and read nowhere else under `services/nft-certificate/src` outside tests (`git grep -w MINTING`), so no code looks for a record left at that status. The in-memory map is lost on a restart and `loadFromDb` fills it from the database, which says `minting` (read, not probed).

## Measured (QA gate 84, 2026-11-01)

A probe called `mintNFT` with a stand-in `query` that rejects only the final save. The certification data and the chain step are stubs, so no real mint ran. At the unmodified base, with an ordinary `Error('db down')`: the client gets `success: true` with a txHash, the in-memory status is `minted`, the database statuses written are `pending`, `processing`, `minting` (the `minted` write is the one that failed), and the log shows `DB save certificate failed {"error":"db down"}`. Probe and logs: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-02_gate84-ks1868-minting-1899/` (`scripts/probe.test.ts`, `logs/probe_base.jsonl`, `logs/probe_base_vitest.log`).

## Not known

* What a client or the UI shows for a record at `minting`; not read.
* Whether a real database failure can hit only that one write (a short outage between the chain step and the save is the case); the probe forces it.
* Whether the chain step is real in a given deployment (preview testnet when configured); not probed here.

## Fix shape (not made)

The contract comes first: retry the final save, or tell the client the NFT exists but is not recorded (not as a mint failure, since it minted), or a reconcile pass over records left at `minting` that carry a txHash. That is a design decision for the owner.

## Related

KS 1868 (the unreadable-thrown-value umbrella): pull request 1899 changes how an unreadable database error reaches this path, and after it the result equals the ordinary-Error result described above.

title: kyc: dbGetVerificationsByUser returns [] on any read error, so the GDPR erasure cascade (dbDeleteUserData) continues with an incomplete list, against its own comment
description:
**BLUF:** `dbGetVerificationsByUser` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/src/index.ts` (`:207-221`) catches every ordinary database or decrypt error, logs it and returns `[]`. `dbDeleteUserData` (`:332`), the GDPR erasure cascade, calls it at `:350` to collect legacy image ids and then deletes by `user_id` regardless, so on a read failure the cascade continues with an incomplete list. The comment at `:340-345` says the opposite: failures THROW so the event bus retries and dead-letters. After pull request 1900 an unreadable thrown value takes the same path. **Read, not run.**

## What I read (develop `8126b22bd5aa`, line numbers at that sha)

* `dbGetVerificationsByUser` (`index.ts:207-221`): `try { query(...); return await Promise.all(rows.map(rowToVerification)) } catch (err) { logger.error(...); return []; }`.
* `dbDeleteUserData` (`:332-368`): `:350` `const verifications = await dbGetVerificationsByUser(userId)`; `:351-357` collects `frontImageId` / `backImageId` from the decrypted documents; `:359-361` deletes those images by id; `:362-364` then deletes images, consents and verifications by `user_id`; `:367` evicts the cached DEK. The comment at `:340-345` says failures THROW "so the event bus retries and dead-letters instead of reporting a successful cascade that deleted nothing".
* Entry points: `DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data` (`:1176-1186`, no `try`, answers 200 `All KYC data for user has been deleted.`) and the `user.erased` subscriber (`userErasedSubscriber.ts`, started at `:1274`, which logs and rethrows a rejection so the bus retries).

## Effect, by reading

When the read in `dbGetVerificationsByUser` fails for an ordinary reason (a database error, or a row that cannot be decrypted and throws), the helper returns `[]`. The cascade then skips the legacy image ids found through the verification documents and deletes the verification rows by `user_id`. Legacy images that carry no `user_id` can be found only through those documents, so they are not deleted, and the rows that pointed to them are. The route still answers that all data was deleted, and the subscriber logs `user.erased handled`.

## Not measured

No database failure was injected and the cascade was not run. I did not look for legacy `svc_kyc_images` rows without a `user_id` in any environment, so how many images this could leave behind is unknown. I did not read the migration that stamped `user_id` (035) for what it leaves out.

## Context

Found while raising the KS 1868 kyc passes (pull request 1900), which make an unreadable thrown value in this helper log a constant reason and return `[]`, so the cascade now continues for that value too instead of aborting. The change is deliberate and described in that pull request; this ticket is about the existing behaviour for ordinary errors. Filed on the coordinator's word after a board search by symbol and path (`dbGetVerificationsByUser`, `dbDeleteUserData`, "erasure cascade", "failures THROW": no hits).

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** gate 85 on pull request 1900 found two more points in the same erasure path, which belong with this ticket. Both come from a probe with a stand-in database through the `DELETE` route and the real `user.erased` subscriber, not from PostgreSQL. Verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-02_gate85-ks1868-kyc-1900/verdict.md`. Line numbers are at the pull request head `a06c3441c237`; at the base they are 30 lower for `index.ts`, and `userErasedSubscriber.ts` is unchanged.

* **G85-F1 (LOW), the subscriber's failure log line is lost in a double fault.** `userErasedSubscriber.ts:42` logs `err?.message` unguarded. When the verification `SELECT` and the `DELETE`s all reject with an unreadable thrown value (a revoked Proxy, or an Error whose `message` getter throws), the handler still rejects, so the bus's three attempts and the dead-letter are unchanged, but reading `err?.message` throws and the `[cascade] user.erased handler failed` line with the user id and request id is not written. With an ordinary Error the line is written.
* **G85-F3 (INFO, pre-existing), the `DELETE` route has no `try`.** `index.ts:1206` (`app.delete('/api/kyc/user/:userId/data', ...)`) awaits `dbDeleteUserData` with no `try`. An ordinary database error on any `DELETE` inside it rejects out of the handler: an unhandled rejection, which exits the kyc process (no `unhandledRejection` listener; Express 4.22.3 does not catch a rejected async handler). The probe showed the same at base and at head.
* **Open question the gate raised for this ticket:** whether `dbDeleteUserData` should fail closed when the `SELECT` fails (for example by using a `SELECT` that throws, instead of the helper that swallows the error and returns `[]`), as its own comment at `index.ts:372-373` says it should.
* The gate also notes, for the record: migration 045 records 0 `svc_kyc_images` rows in local and demo (2026-09-05); production was not measured.
* Read and probed, not run against a real database.

title: check-no-sql-injection.sh misses a *RawUnsafe call when a comment sits between the "(" and the template, and for five other call shapes
description:
**BLUF:** The SQL-injection guard (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-sql-injection.sh`, pre-push leg 15) reads a `*RawUnsafe` call only when its first argument is a template literal written directly after the `(`, with nothing but whitespace between. Two groups of call shapes that the guard means to read are missed (exit 0, "OK"): a comment between the `(` and the template (G87-F1), and five edge shapes (G87-F2). Found by QA gate 87 on PR 1903 (KS 1867 and KS 1865), which is GO WITH NOTES with no fix before merge. Neither group occurs in the tree today: the guard is green on develop.

## The shapes (measured by the gate on the PR head `12bafc96c912`, develop `8afcf256ed5f`, BSD awk 20200816)

**G87-F1, a comment between** `(` **and the template** (the awk skips whitespace only):

* `db.$queryRawUnsafe(/* c */ \`SELECT ${t}\`)\` is missed (exit 0).
* `db.$queryRawUnsafe( // c` then a new line `\`SELECT ${t}\`)\` is missed (exit 0).

**G87-F2, edge shapes**, all missed:

* a parenthesised template: `$queryRawUnsafe((\`..${t}\`))\`;
* an optional call: `$queryRawUnsafe?.(`;
* bracket access: `db["$queryRawUnsafe"](`;
* `.call(db, ...)` and a `.bind(db)` alias;
* a generic that contains a `(`, such as `<(a:number)=>void>` (the guard's pattern for the generic is `<[^(]*>`, which cannot span a parenthesis).

## Out of scope here, named so it is not lost (G87-F3)

A template built in a variable and then passed (`const q = \`..${t}\`; $queryRawUnsafe(q)`), `String.raw`, concatenation (`'..' + x`), and `buildSql(t)\` are also missed. The guard's header says "first argument is a template literal", and the PR 1903 cheat-sheet fragment discloses variable and concatenation as not covered. That is a data-flow question and a different ticket; this one is only about calls the guard already means to read.

## Acceptance

* Each G87-F1 and G87-F2 shape above is reported when it carries a `${` in its SQL template, and the matching harmless shape (no `${`, or a positional-parameter call) stays clean, in cells that are red against the guard as merged and green after.
* The guard's header lists what it does not read.

## Not part of this ticket (notes on PR 1903 only)

* G87-F4: under a UTF-8 locale, BSD awk fails with a multibyte conversion error on a source file that holds invalid UTF-8; the guard then exits 2 (fails closed); under `LC_ALL=C` the file is scanned. No tracked file triggers it.
* G87-F5: the allow-list key pins the sink (path, opener, interpolated expressions), not what feeds the interpolated arrays; re-trace an entry when its function changes.

## Where

* Gate verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-02_gate87-ks1867-sqlguard-1903/verdict.md`.
* Board search before filing (2026-11-02): `check-no-sql-injection.sh` finds KS 1857, KS 1865, KS 1866, KS 1867 and KS 1929, none about these shapes (KS 1866 is five other guards; KS 1857 is the guard's speed and reporting); "comment between" 0; positive control `parseScopeString` 18; random token 0.

title: Billing: checkout.session.completed credits a purchase without checking that payment_status is 'paid'
description:
**BLUF:** The billing webhook adds certification credits on every `checkout.session.completed` that carries a customer and a `certifications` count, without checking the session's `payment_status`. A Checkout Session paid by a delayed payment method completes with `payment_status: 'unpaid'`, so its credits would be granted before the money arrives, and granted even if the payment later fails. Read in code, not run. Whether it is live depends on whether delayed payment methods are enabled on the Stripe account and which events the live endpoint receives: that is Kam's own check under his 2026-11-02 ruling on KS-1933.

**Where** (`services/billing/src/routes/webhooks.ts` at PR 1913's head `5d6bd74daa3e`)

* `handleCheckoutComplete` (:466-502) credits at :483 when `customerId` is set and `certifications > 0`. `session.payment_status` is only logged, at :498, after the credit.
* `handleWebhookEvent` (:365-453) has no case for `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` or `checkout.session.async_payment_failed` (no `async_payment` anywhere in billing).
* Stripe's own type (stripe 14.25.0, `types/Checkout/Sessions.d.ts:208-212`): "The payment status of the Checkout Session, one of `paid`, `unpaid`, or `no_payment_required`. You can use this value to decide when to fulfill your customer's order."

**With KS-1933's fix:** the per-payment ledger keys a purchase on its PaymentIntent id, so if the checkout handler stopped crediting an unpaid session, a later `payment_intent.succeeded` for the same purchase would credit it exactly once.

**Not in scope here:** no fix is designed or built in KS-1933's pull request; this ticket records the reading. Found by Seat F 22nd while tracing KS-1933 (Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-11-02 commissioned this filing).

**Related:** KS-1933.

title: Billing: addCertificationCredits' optimistic lock is not a compare-and-set, so one call can credit twice under a concurrent write
description:
**BLUF:** `StripeService.addCertificationCredits` keeps the credit balance in Stripe customer metadata and calls its read-update-verify loop "optimistic locking", but Stripe's customer update is unconditional, so the loop is not a compare-and-set. When a concurrent writer changes the balance between this call's update and its verify read, the loop re-reads and adds the credits AGAIN, so one call can credit twice; a write can also be lost. Read in code, not run. It is the same money class as KS-1933 (one purchase credited more than once), through a different door.

**Where** (`services/billing/src/services/stripeService.ts` at PR 1913's head `5d6bd74daa3e`)

* `addCertificationCredits` (:226-247): up to 3 attempts of retrieve (:229), compute `currentBalance + credits` (:231-232), `customers.update` with the new `certificationCredits` (:234-236), retrieve again (:239); if the read-back is not the value it wrote, it logs a conflict (:244) and goes round again from a fresh read.
* `useCertificationCredits` (:252-278) has the same loop for debits.

**A sequence that credits twice (worked from the code):** the balance is 10. Call A (+5) and call B (+3) both read 10. A writes 15, B writes 13 (A's write is lost). A's verify reads 13, not 15: A retries, reads 13, writes 18, verify passes. B's verify reads 18, not 13: B retries, reads 18, writes 21, verify passes. The final 21 is 10 + 5 + 3 + 3: B's credit landed twice.

**Not in scope here:** no fix is designed or built in KS-1933's pull request (KS-1933 adds a per-payment ledger in PostgreSQL that stops a second CALL for the same purchase; it does not change what one call does). Found by Seat F 22nd while tracing KS-1933 (Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-11-02 commissioned this filing).

**Related:** KS-1933.

title: api-gateway: ORG_ADMIN and ISSUER_ADMIN can set any user's verification level (tenant bound unmeasured)
description:
**BLUF:** In the api-gateway, `PATCH /api/admin/identity/users/:id/level` sits behind `requireAdmin`, and `requireAdmin` admits `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN` (and the lower-case `issuer_admin`). A probe with a stub database showed both roles reach the handler and issue `UPDATE users SET verification_level = $1 ... WHERE id = $2::uuid` for ANY user id. The SQL has no tenant or organisation predicate. **Whether row-level security (or anything else) stops those two roles from changing a user in another tenant was NOT run**, so this is an open question, not a confirmed cross-tenant write. A real-PostgreSQL probe with a cross-tenant id settles it.

## What is read in the code (develop `d9acf71a3fcc`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`)

* `:600` `const ADMIN_ROLES = ['SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'system_admin', 'super_admin', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'platform_admin', 'ORG_ADMIN', 'ISSUER_ADMIN', 'issuer_admin'];`
* `:602-:605` a comment (KS 458) says platform-level admins read across tenants and that "ORG_ADMIN / ISSUER_ADMIN keep the tenant-scoped view the policy now enforces (their request ALS context applies)". `PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES` (`:606`) lists only the five platform roles, and `adminScope` (`:607-:610`) runs a query under the platform scope for those five only.
* `:612-:651` `requireAdmin` checks the token and then only `ADMIN_ROLES.includes(role)`; a role outside the list gets 403. It does not look at the target user, the caller's organisation or the caller's tenant.
* `:1313` `router.patch('/api/admin/identity/users/:id/level', requireAdmin, mockBodyParser, ...)`. The body's `verificationLevel` must be one of NONE, BASIC, SOCIAL, STANDARD, ENHANCED, HIGH, GOVERNMENT (anything else answers 400 with no query).
* `:1322-:1325` `adminScope(req, () => query('UPDATE users SET verification_level = $1, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $2::uuid RETURNING id, verification_level', [verificationLevel, id]))`. The only predicate is the user id. `rowCount === 0` answers 404.

## Source and its limit

Found by gate 98 (the QA gate on pull request 1916, the KS 1868 `admin.ts` catch-read change), finding G98-F4, 2026-11-02. It ran the real admin router (real `createAdminRoutes`, real `requireAdmin`, real `ADMIN_ROLES`) on a loopback listener with only the token verifier, the database, the logger and redis replaced. Its auth matrix: no token 401, a plain USER 403, and ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN and SYSTEM_ADMIN each 200 with exactly one query, `UPDATE users SET verification_level = $1`, parameters the level and the id. **The database was a stub, so row-level security was not run.** The behaviour is pre-existing and unchanged by pull request 1916 (that change only guards how a thrown value is read for a log line). Filed on Wednesday's commission from that note; I read the code lines above at `d9acf71a3fcc`, and I did not run anything against a database.

## What is not known, and what would settle it

1. **Cross-tenant.** Does the tenant row-level security on `users` reject the UPDATE when an `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` of tenant A names a user of tenant B? Settle with a real PostgreSQL carrying the project's RLS policies and migrations: two tenants, a user in B, a token for an `ORG_ADMIN` of A, `PATCH` the level for B's user. 404 (zero rows) means RLS bounds the call; 200 and a changed row means it does not.
2. **Same tenant, other organisation.** Tenant row-level security does not know organisations, so an `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` may be able to change the level of a user in a different organisation of the SAME tenant. Not measured either way. The policy question of which roles may cross an organisation boundary is KS 1535 and the role-list drift is KS 1536; neither covers this route.
3. **What a changed level buys.** The board's KS 1176 and KS 1190 describe the gateway's `meetsVerificationLevel` checks on this value. Which routes read the stored level for an access decision was not traced here.

## Board search (so nobody files this twice)

Run 2026-11-02 over this team's issues and comment bodies for `admin/identity`, `identity/users`, `/level`, `verification_level`, `requireAdmin`, `ADMIN_ROLES`, `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`; positive control KS 1865 found. The route terms hit only the KS 1868 umbrella's own comments; the symbol terms hit tickets about other routes. Closest, and not covering this route: KS 1536 (role vocabularies), KS 1584 (an organisation-bound escape through a provisioning key), KS 1855 (gateway admin stand-ins).

## Not in scope

No change to `admin.ts` is proposed or made here. Severity is not asserted: priority High is the commissioning call, pending the probe above.

title: governance: createProposal's best-effort DELETE swallows a failure; the re-save then fails on the unique wallet address (500) and leaves an orphan participant row
description:
**BLUF:** In `services/governance`, `createProposal` auto-registers an unknown proposer, then deletes the auto-generated row and re-saves it under the proposer's id. A failed DELETE is swallowed (`governanceService.ts:512-514`, `catch { /* best effort */ }`), so the re-save at `:516` runs with the auto-generated row still present. Both rows carry `wallet_address = proposerId` (the auto-register passes the proposer id as the wallet address, `:505`), so on a table with `wallet_address ... UNIQUE` the re-save fails with a unique violation, `dbSaveParticipant` rethrows (`:186-189`), and the request answers 500 with the orphan auto-generated row left behind. On a table without the constraint the result is a second row for the same wallet.

## Where (develop `c234c2388a16`; read from source, NOT run)

* `services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts:503-517`: the auto-register block; `:512-514` the swallowed DELETE; `:516` the re-save; `:186-189` the save helper's rethrow.
* DDL `wallet_address TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`: `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:1108`, `docker/init/04-sprint2-service-tables.sql:189`, `migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql:366`.

## What the next request does (read only, not measured)

The next `createProposal` by the same user finds no row by id; the auto-register's by-address read finds the orphan (wallet = proposerId) and reuses its id; the DELETE and re-save run again. If the DELETE succeeds that time, the state heals.

## Scope

A failed WRITE (the DELETE), not a failed lookup, so it is outside KS 1940, whose fix stops the lookups and leaves this block unchanged. Fix shape not chosen here: for example the auto-register, delete and re-save in one transaction, or a single insert under the proposer id instead of insert, delete, re-insert.

## Searched first

Board search over issue content and comment bodies: "auto-generated record" 0 hits; "DELETE FROM svc_governance_participants" 0; "best effort" finds KS 1779 only (originate, unrelated). Control: "minProposalStake" finds KS 1940.

## Found by

Seat F 23rd while designing KS 1940; filed on the coordinator's ruling. Not measured against a database.

nodes.body:

When a proposer's user id equals ANOTHER participant's `wallet_address`, that participant's row is upserted at minProposalStake, deleted, and re-inserted under the proposer's id, so the other participant's row is lost. Read from source, not run. PR 1939 does not change it; the gate places it with this ticket.

Gate 121's finding, verbatim (from its `verdict.md`, sha256 `f82c0e71131d1d71`...):

The other participant's row is lost. This PR does not change it; it belongs with KS-1941.
