title: POST /api/gdpr/retention/enforce answers 200 "Retention enforcement complete" when the policy read or a policy failed, and its count is not a policy count (routes/gdpr.ts lines 625-636)
description:
**BLUF:** the SYSTEM_ADMIN route `POST /api/gdpr/retention/enforce` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts` :625-636, read at develop `91ccb1553f02`) answers `200 {"success":true,"message":"Retention enforcement complete. N data types processed.",...}` even when the policy SELECT failed or a policy failed in the middle of the sweep, and `N` cannot tell "nothing had expired" from "the sweep could not read its policies". Pre-existing; an ordinary Error reaches it, not only an unreadable thrown value.

## What the source does (read, develop `91ccb1553f02`)

* The route awaits `gdpr.enforceRetention()` and answers `` res.json({ success: true, message: `Retention enforcement complete. ${logs.length} data types processed.`, deletionLog: logs }) `` (:627-632). Only a throw reaches `fail500` (:633-635).
* `enforceRetentionImpl` (`services/gdprService.ts` :438-507) never throws for a database failure: the per-policy catch (:498-500) and the outer catch (:502-504) only log, and the function returns `logs` (:506).
* So when the policy SELECT (:442-444) fails, the outer catch logs and returns an empty list: the route answers 200, "0 data types processed". When one policy fails mid-sweep, that policy is missing from `logs`, the others carry on, and the route still answers 200 "complete".
* `logs.length` counts only policies whose `affected > 0` and whose deletion-log INSERT returned a row (:484-490). It is not a count of policies, nor of policies that failed.
* The other caller, `services/retentionScheduler.ts` :40-58 (`runEnforcement`), reads the same resolved list and logs `Enforcement complete` or `Enforcement complete — no records required processing`; its own catch is reached only if `enforceRetention` throws.

## Reported by QA gate 117 (PR 1935), not re-run here

Measured with the real route handler on a loopback listener and a statement recorder: for an ordinary Error and a string the SELECT failure answers 200 "0 data types processed" at the base and at the head, and an Error on `DELETE user_sessions` answers "2 data types processed". PR 1935 moves the unreadable-value cases onto this existing answer; it does not change it.

## Not known

* Not run against a real PostgreSQL or a booted originate.
* Whether any client or operator procedure reads the message or `success` as proof the sweep ran is not checked.
* No fix is proposed here (the route could report failed policies, or answer a non-200 status; not decided).

nodes.body: **BLUF:** related, not addressed: PR 1945 (KS 1943) makes each retention policy's DELETE, deletion-log row and stamp one transaction, and it changes neither the `POST /api/gdpr/retention/enforce` status contract nor its wording. After it, `deletionLog` never lists a policy that rolled back, but the message still says "complete" when a policy failed, so this ticket stands as filed.

title: third-party verifier approve: a throw after the UPDATE leaves the verifier active with a stored key hash and answers 500 without the one-time key; re-approve answers 404 (thirdPartyVerifiers.ts lines 172-201)
description:
**BLUF:** in the approve handler (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` :158-203, read at develop `c70f339063ee`) the UPDATE that sets `status = 'active'` and writes `api_key_hash` (:172-181) runs before the one-time key is returned (:192-197). If anything after the UPDATE throws, the catch (:198-201) answers 500 with no key, and the verifier is left active with a stored key hash that nobody holds. Approving again cannot recover it: the UPDATE only matches `status = 'pending'` (:180) and a zero-row result answers 404 (:183-188). Pre-existing, and it holds for an ordinary Error as well.

## What I read (develop `c70f339063ee`)

* `generateApiKey()` and `hashApiKey()` run first (:168-169); the UPDATE follows (:172-181, `WHERE id = ... AND status = 'pending'`); then `logger.info` (:190); then `res.json({ success: true, message: 'Verifier approved', apiKey, note: 'Store this API key securely. It will not be shown again.' })` (:192-197).
* The key exists only in that response body; only its hash is stored.
* The catch (:198-201) logs and answers the constant 500 `Failed to approve verifier`. Nothing undoes the UPDATE.
* Within `services/originate/src`, the only write of `api_key_hash` is that UPDATE (:175) and the only read is the `/verify` lookup by key hash (:328). The router's routes are register, list, approve, suspend, reinstate, verify and records; none issues a new key. I did not check outside `services/originate/src` (admin tooling, other services, manual SQL).

## Reported by QA gate 118 (PR 1936), not re-run here

With the real handler on a loopback listener and a statement recorder: in the cell that throws after the write (`approve | after`) the UPDATE is issued once (status `'active'` and `api_key_hash` written) and the answer is 500 with no key, for an ordinary Error at the base and at the head; the success cell returns the key, and the sha256 of that key equals the hash in the recorded UPDATE. Pull request 1936 does not change which paths return the key. The earlier gate that raised this as candidate G104-F3 read it from the source.

## Not known

* Nothing was run against a real PostgreSQL.
* No trigger for a throw at that point is identified in the code (a logger call, building the response); how likely it is in production is not measured.
* Whether another path can give an active verifier a new key.
* No fix is proposed here.

title: staking: POST /api/stake takes address and amount from the caller, so any signed-in user can create or grow a stake position for any address
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/stake` (`services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts:189-245`) takes `address` and `amount` from the request body and saves a stake position for that address with no ownership or chain check. By the same shape, the unstake routes (`POST /api/stake/unstake` `:263`, `POST /api/stake/complete-unstake` `:317`) also take the address from the body; they were not read line by line. So any signed-in caller can create or grow a stake position for any address. `txHash` is optional and is logged but never verified. KS 1942's design treats `svc_stake_positions` as NOT a trusted stake source for this reason.

## Where (develop `0e3a9b65cdd6`; read from source, NOT run)

* Mount: `services/staking/src/index.ts:80` applies `jwtAuthenticate()` to `/api`, and `:82` mounts the stake routes at `/api/stake`. Any signed-in caller reaches them.
* `routes/stake.ts:189-245`: the handler parses `StakeSchema` from `req.body` (`:191`), takes `{ address, amount, txHash }` (`:196`), loads the position for that address (`:199`), adds `amount` to it or creates it (`:213-228`), and saves it (`:230`). It also adds to the in-process pool stats (`:233-236`).
* `req.user` is not read anywhere in `routes/stake.ts`. `txHash` is optional in the schema (`:33`), and its only other use is the log line (`:243`).

## Why it matters

KS 1942 (the governance register route takes stake from the caller) is being fixed by making stake and roles admin-set only. Its design rejected `svc_stake_positions` as a stake source because this route lets any caller assert any position.

## Not checked

The unstake and complete-unstake handlers line by line. Whether the gateway restricts `/api/stake` to a role. Whether any client other than the tests calls these routes. Whether the Aiken staking validator is meant to be the source of truth (no service reads it).

## Related

KS 1942 (governance register route, same class). KS 1845 (covers only the admin listing `GET /api/stake/all`, not these routes).

## Searched first

Board search over issue content and comment bodies:

* "svc_stake_positions" and "routes/stake.ts" find KS 1845 (an issue covering only `GET /api/stake/all`) and a KS 1544 comment.
* "POST /api/stake" finds comments on KS 188, KS 256 and KS 492, about business-rule refusals and OpenAPI examples on `/unstake` and `/complete-unstake`, not ownership.
* "StakeSchema" and "staking service" find 0.
* Control: "minProposalStake" finds KS 1940.

## Found by

Seat F 23rd while designing KS 1942; filed on the coordinator's ruling (D4). Not measured against a running service.

title: originate retention sweep: give each policy's unit a real per-statement bound in both modes (SET LOCAL statement_timeout and lock_timeout right after BEGIN)
description:
**BLUF:** the originate retention sweep has no real per-statement time bound. In single-tenant mode each policy's unit (PR 1945, KS 1943) runs under Prisma's default interactive-transaction timeout of 5000 ms, and that timeout does not cancel a blocked statement; in multi-tenant mode there is no bound at all (QA gate 127 verdict on PR 1945, G127-F1). Candidate: `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` and `lock_timeout` right after BEGIN, in both branches of `withPlatformScopeTransaction` (originate `src/db.ts`). Filed on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER 2026-11-02 12:51:19Z). The values and the multi-tenant change are decided when this is worked, not now.

**Evidence** (QA gate 127 verdict on PR 1945: FINDINGS G127-F1 and G127-F2, and section Q3; measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 15 with all 58 repo migrations, as the non-superuser app role):

* Prisma checks the timeout only when the next query or the COMMIT is issued, so it does not cancel an in-flight statement (G127-F1).
* With a superuser holding `FOR UPDATE` on the expired user_sessions rows, the single-tenant DELETE sat `active / Lock:transactionid` for 7.5 s and more, holding RowExclusive and tuple locks. The sweep settled only after the lock was released, at about 9.06 s. Then the unit rolled back: 3 rows remaining, no log row, no stamp, the other 4 policies stamped, and afterwards 0 idle-in-transaction backends and 0 app locks (G127-F1, Q3).
* Multi-tenant mode has no timeout: the unit waited, then committed after the release (G127-F1).
* Base (develop `0e3a9b65cdd6`) behaves the same in both modes, so PR 1945 makes nothing worse (G127-F1).
* In single-tenant mode a policy whose unit exceeds the timeout does all its work and then rolls back on every run, so it never progresses. Base already had this for the DELETE alone (G127-F2).

**Unmeasured:** live table sizes, so whether any live policy's unit comes near 5 s is unknown; pgbouncer in the path; the right values.

**To decide when worked:** the two values; the multi-tenant behaviour change (multi-tenant has no bound today, so adding one changes its behaviour and needs a ruling, per G127-F1).

**Board search before filing** (read-only, 2026-11-02, Seat E 29th): the control term `withPlatformScopeTransaction` found KS 1943. `statement_timeout`: 3 hits, KS 1582 and KS 1587 (a transaction-local timeout on the auth users read, the nearest precedent) and KS 1585 (another gate's follow-up); none covers the retention units. `SET LOCAL`: KS 1582, KS 1587. `enforceRetention`: KS 1938, KS 1943, KS 1944, none of them a bound. `lock_timeout`, `retention timeout`, `retention sweep timeout`, `interactive-transaction timeout` and `transaction timeout`: 0 hits.

**Related:** PR 1945, [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1945](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1945>) (KS 1943), open and not merged when this was filed.

title: api-gateway: with Redis unavailable, enforceDocumentTypeRules passes every document (catalogue reads empty), so MFA-required types are allowed
description:
**BLUF:** When `isRedisAvailable()` is false (every Redis outage: an ordinary error on the client, a socket `close`, or the 4th retry), `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`, called at `routes/verification.ts` line 856) reads an EMPTY document-type catalogue on every replica (`documentTypesStore` is only written while the flag is false), `resolveDocumentType` returns null, and the "catalogue empty" branch returns `{ ok: true, docType: {} }`. A document type registered with `requireMFA: true` is then allowed.

**Measured by QA gate 144** (real `redis.ts`, `enforcement.ts` and winston; only `ioredis` replaced; two replicas sharing one store): a type registered with `requireMFA: true` is REFUSED with 403 `MFA_REQUIRED` while the flag is true, and ALLOWED on both replicas while the flag is false, with Redis up or down, at develop's base AND at PR 1960's head after an ordinary Error. Evidence: `logs/probe_site3_table.log`, enforce block, rows `base trigger=ordinary` and `head trigger=ordinary`: `ALLOWED ok:true docType={}` on replica A and B, with `down=0` and `down=1`.

**By reading, not run:** the same pass-through skips the `isActive` check, the verification-level check (`creatorVerificationLevel`), the auth-provider check (`allowedAuthProviders`), the metadata-schema check (`metadataSchema`) and the approval-workflow gate (`createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` sees no `requiresApproval`).

**Where it sits at develop** `4d1ab2cb6574`**, read by the filer:** `resolveDocumentType` calls `redisService.getAllDocumentTypes()` at `enforcement.ts` line 72; `enforceDocumentTypeRules` reads the catalogue again at line 126 and returns `{ ok: true, docType: {} }` at lines 117 and 137, where the code comment says an empty catalogue means "never seeded, or Redis TTL expiry". The gate cites `enforcement.ts` lines 78 and 128; the statements I read are at lines 72 and 126, so cite them by function name.

**Reach:** every Redis blip in production puts the gateway in this state (an ordinary error, `close`, or retry 4). PR 1960 (the `redis.ts` error listener and `initRedis` catch) does not cause it and does not change it; it makes the unreadable-value path land in the same state an ordinary Error already reaches.

**Not tested:** a real Redis or `ioredis` client (a stand-in was used; the `ioredis` emit, close and retry path was read in `node_modules` 5.11.1, not run); a booted gateway over HTTP (the middleware and `enforceDocumentTypeRules` were called directly); `createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` and the `isActive`, verification-level, provider and schema skips under fallback (read, only the MFA rule was run); admin routes in fallback; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Suggested fix shape (the gate's, not a decision):** in fallback mode `enforceDocumentTypeRules` should refuse with 503 instead of treating an unreadable catalogue as an empty one, as the connector-create and connector-info readers already do (`routes/verification.ts` line 795 and `services/health.ts` line 54, which gate 144 read as answering 503 when the flag is false).

**Related:** KS-1256, KS-1540, KS-1532, KS-1627 (readers of the same flag); KS-1466 (untyped creates never meet the catalogue's document rules: a different defect); KS-1868 (PR 1960, unrelated cause).

**Found by:** QA gate 144 on PR 1960, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G144-F1: recommended follow-up, HIGH, pre-existing, measured).

title: originate GDPR erasure: a lifecycle event row skipped by the erasure sweep stays decryptable under the platform keyring after the erasure reports completed
description:
**BLUF:** In originate's GDPR erasure, a lifecycle event row that the sweep skips keeps the subject's email recoverable by anyone holding the platform keyring, in live data and in backups, after an erasure that reports `success: true` with the data-subject request marked completed. Step 11 destroys only the subject's own data key (the DEK); lifecycle payloads are encrypted under the platform-wide `v<N>:` keyring (`encodeLifecyclePayload` calls `encryptField`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/utils/lifecyclePayloadCodec.ts` lines 34 to 38), not under it. Step 5d skips a row when `decodeLifecyclePayload` reports `payloadUnavailable` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts` lines 688 to 690). The deletion log and the DSR record say nothing about the skipped row; the only trace is one error line carrying the event id.

**Not new (measured):** an ORDINARY decrypt error at develop's base already leaves the same row in the same state (a key version that is not loaded). PR 1961 (the thrown-value guard) does not cause this. It routes the unreadable-value case into that same ordinary state; before it, a hostile throw aborted the whole erasure loudly (`success: false`, DSR left open), and that abort was not atomic: the earlier steps and rows had already been written. The old state was also not a real remedy, because a retry hits the same row and aborts again (read, not run).

**Measured by QA gate 145** (the real `executeErasure`, the real lifecycle codec, the real `SubjectDekProvider`, real AES-GCM `encryptField` / `decryptField` / `encryptFieldWithDek` with keys generated in-process, the real winston logger; only the database replaced by an in-memory SQL stand-in). E2 is a lifecycle row holding the subject's email whose decrypt fails; after the erasure the whole platform keyring (v1 + v2) is loaded and E2 is tried.

| version | failure on row E2 | erasure result | DSR completed | subject DEK destroyed | row E2 rewritten | E2 decrypts with the platform keyring | E2 still holds the subject email |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| base | none (control) | success | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| base | ordinary decrypt error | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |
| base | unreadable thrown value | `success: false` ("Erasure failed") | no | no (DEK still live) | no | yes | YES |
| head (PR 1961) | none (control) | success | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| head (PR 1961) | ordinary decrypt error | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |
| head (PR 1961) | unreadable thrown value | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |

Head with an unreadable value equals base with an ordinary error in every column. In the success rows the log says `Erasure completed`; the deletion log does not mention E2.

**Why step 11 cannot shred it:** `executeErasureImpl` step 11 (`gdprService.ts` lines 893 to 894) calls `subjectDeks.destroyDek(userId)`, which sets the wrapped DEK to NULL in `pii_subject_keys` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/subjectDek.ts`). No lifecycle payload depends on that key. The shared module's own comment in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/encryptedField.ts` says the `v<N>:` format "makes single-subject erasure impossible to guarantee in backups (there is no per-subject key to destroy)". After a completed erasure the skipped row can still be decrypted by `listLifecycleEvents` (`lifecycleEventRepo.ts` line 138, tenant-scoped document listing), which would show the email to whoever can list that document's events (read, not run).

**Retry does not reach it (read, not run):** `payloadUnavailable` is read only at line 690. A second erasure looks up the subject email at step 5c from a users row that step 10 already set to a placeholder of the form `deleted_<id>` at the `anonymized.local` domain, so it cannot match the address inside E2, and nothing else revisits the row.

**Suggested fix shapes (the gate's, not a decision):**

* (a) count skipped rows, and do not mark the DSR plainly `completed` while any remain; record them in the deletion log as `skipped` with the event ids; and/or
* (b) move lifecycle payloads to the subject-DEK (`d1:`) envelope so that step 11 shreds them, as the KS-291 design does for users, consents and DSRs.

**Not tested:** the live PR body; a real Postgres or Prisma client (the SQL stand-in answers by statement prefix, so the real SQL semantics of the other steps are not exercised); a real Key Vault or production keyring (keys were generated in-process); whether a real decrypt ever throws an unreadable value (none is known; Node crypto throws Errors); the HTTP routes (`POST /api/gdpr/erasure/:userId`, `executeErasureByExternalRef`) and a booted service; a second erasure run against the same subject; `listLifecycleEvents`; backups; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Related:** KS-537 (lifecycle payload encryption and erasure), KS-291 (the subject-DEK design for users, consents and DSRs), KS-1868 (PR 1961, unrelated cause).

**Found by:** QA gate 145 on PR 1961, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G145-F1: recommended follow-up, HIGH priority for data protection, pre-existing, measured).

title: transfer approval sweep: when the workflow reads fail, every overdue step is marked timed_out (terminal), including steps set to escalate, so escalations are silently lost
description:
**BLUF:** In the transfer service's escalation sweep (`processEscalations` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/approvalWorkflowService.ts`), when the reads that look up a step's workflow fail, every overdue pending step is marked `timed_out`, including steps configured to auto-escalate. `timed_out` is terminal: a later sweep does not select it again and `processApproval` refuses a step that is not pending, so the escalation is silently lost and running the sweep again cannot repair it.

**Cause:** `findWorkflowByStepId` (line 670) reads the workflows through `dbGetActiveWorkflows` (line 238, with a bare `catch { return []; }` at line 243) and then a second `SELECT * FROM svc_approval_workflows` whose failure is swallowed by a bare `catch { /* fall back to active-only */ }`. If both reads fail the workflow is `undefined`, so `stepDef` is `undefined`, the test `stepDef?.autoEscalate && stepDef.escalateTo && !instance.escalatedAt` (line 611) is false, and the `else` branch (lines 622 to 625) sets `status = 'timed_out'`. (The gate cites lines 235 to 243 and 695 to 698 at the PR head; the lines above are at develop `4d1ab2cb6574`, so cite by function name.)

**Measured by QA gate 146** (the REAL transfer service booted as its own Node process for every cell, the real routes and authentication; only the `pg` module replaced, by an in-memory model of the two workflow tables with a unique-id upsert). Setup: 4 overdue pending steps; I1 and I3 on a custom step with `autoEscalate`, `escalateTo: boss-user` and `timeoutHours: 1`; I2 and I4 on the default `step-1`, which times out; `POST /api/workflows/escalate` as a platform administrator. Cell `sweep_wfread`, with the workflow reads failing: the answer is 200 with `{ escalatedCount: 0, timedOutCount: 4 }`. I1 and I3, which should escalate to boss-user, are marked `timed_out`, and a second POST cannot repair them. The result is the same at develop's base and at PR 1962's head, for every kind of failure value including an ordinary Error.

**Effect on approval:** the state refuses rather than grants. The transfer's own execute path gates on the transfer record, not on step instances (`index.ts` lines 802 to 814, read, not run), so nothing this sweep writes can let a transfer proceed. What is lost is the escalation to the named escalation user.

**Suggested fix shape (the gate's, not a decision):** when the step's workflow cannot be found, skip the row and leave it `pending` instead of marking it `timed_out`.

**Related:** a sweep that fails part-way answers `200 success: true` with partial counts and no error indicator (gate finding G146-F4; pre-existing, true at base for an ordinary Error and now for an unreadable value too). The admin caller cannot tell the sweep was incomplete; only a log line says so. Also KS-1881 (the route's platform-admin check, Done) and KS-1868 (PR 1962, unrelated cause).

**Not tested:** a real PostgreSQL (the store is a model; the real WHERE and ON CONFLICT semantics are emulated, not executed); pgbouncer or a mid-statement connection loss; the api-gateway hop to the escalate route (whether and how it is proxied is not traced); a production-mode boot; multi-tenancy pools; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Found by:** QA gate 146 on PR 1962, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G146-F3: recommended follow-up, pre-existing, measured, base = head for every value including an ordinary Error). PR 1962 does not cause it.

title: GDPR erasure: a failed kyc or wallet-connector user.erased step leaves the subject's data in place and nothing reports it (dead-letter unread; request already marked completed)
description:
**BLUF:** When the kyc or wallet-connector `user.erased` handler fails, the erasure is left silently incomplete and nobody is told. The shared event bus tries the handler 3 times back to back, then writes one dead-letter entry with the constant text `Failed after 3 attempts` and acknowledges the message. Nothing reads the dead-letter stream and no retry job exists. The data-subject request was already marked completed: originate's erasure marks it completed at step 12, before it publishes `user.erased` at step 13. What stays behind is the subject's data in that service, as measured below.

**What survives, measured by QA gate 147** (the real kyc `index.ts` and wallet-connector `server.ts` handlers through the real shared `EventBus` subscribe loop, with only the database and the bus's Redis client replaced; the subject has one verification, three document images, one consent with IP address and user agent; a second user's rows are never touched). kyc's four deletes run in this order with no transaction: select verifications, delete images by id, delete images by user id, delete consents, delete verifications, then evict the subject key. Each attempt re-runs the whole sequence.

| failure point (fails on every attempt) | attempts | dead-letter entries | left after the dead-letter (images / consents / verifications) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| kyc: delete images by id | 3 | 1 | 3 / 1 / 1 (everything) |
| kyc: delete consents | 3 | 1 | 0 / 1 / 1 |
| kyc: delete verifications | 3 | 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 |
| wallet-connector: delete sessions | 3 | 1 | every session row for the address |

A failure on the first attempt only (consents once, or the wallet delete once) completes on the second attempt and leaves nothing. By schema (`migrations/002_*.sql` lines 474 to 533 and 813 to 820): the surviving kyc verification holds `provider_application_id`, `provider_check_id`, `liveness_score`, `overall_score`, `risk_level`, `status`, `review_notes` and `documents`; the consent holds the IP address, user agent and timestamps; wallet-connector rows hold the address, wallet type and connected time, all plaintext. Columns written under the subject key (`d1:` envelopes such as `documents` and `review_notes`) are crypto-shredded by originate's step 11. Legacy `v<N>:` kyc rows are under the platform keyring and stay decryptable; that is the same class as `KS-1953`, a different erasure gap (originate lifecycle rows).

**Not new (measured):** an ORDINARY Error at develop's base already leaves exactly this state. PR 1963 (the thrown-value guard on both handlers) does not cause it; it only makes the unreadable-value case behave like the ordinary one (same attempts, same rows erased and left, same dead-letter entry).

**Suggested fix shapes (the gate's, not a decision):**

* a dead-letter consumer or alarm that reopens or flags the data-subject request per service;
* a backoff between attempts, or a re-delivery schedule, instead of three immediate tries;
* wrap kyc's deletes in `transaction()` (the service's `db.ts` already has one) so a failure leaves all or nothing;
* record per-service cascade completion against the request.

**Related (pre-existing, read from source, not run):**

* kyc `dbDeleteUserData` returns 0 when `isDbAvailable()` is false (`index.ts` line 373). The handler then logs `handled` and the bus acknowledges: an erasure silently skipped with no dead-letter. wallet-connector's handler never clears `memConnectedWallets`, so in-memory sessions for the address persist until a restart (gate finding G147-F3).
* The `user.erased` stream entry (user id, request id, `performedBy`, wallet address) is acknowledged but never deleted: `publish` has no XDEL or MAXLEN. A dead-letter copies the raw event into `secuura:events:dead-letter`. So the subject's wallet address stays in Redis after an erasure, whether it succeeded or not (gate finding G147-F4).

**Not tested:** a real Redis (the stream, consumer group, pending list, redelivery after a crash between attempts and the acknowledgement, recovery from a missing group); a real Postgres (the real SQL semantics and the foreign-key cascade are modelled; the timing of the three attempts); a booted service, and the admin HTTP delete path at kyc `index.ts` line 1224, which calls `dbDeleteUserData` directly; originate's publish side end to end; the auth, m365 and other `user.erased` subscribers; backups; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Found by:** QA gate 147 on PR 1963, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G147-F1: HIGH, pre-existing, measured; not caused by `KS-1868`'s PR 1963, not a merge block).

title: originate document signing: a sign, sign-cert or sign-wallet request can answer 500 after the signature or signed document is saved, and a retry duplicates it
description:
**BLUF:** In originate, `POST /api/documents/:id/sign`, `/:id/sign-cert` and `/:id/sign-wallet` can answer 500 after the signature, or the signed derived document, is already saved. A retry then saves a second one. This is pre-existing: it happens the same way for an ordinary Error at base, and pull request 1964 does not cause it. Found by QA gate 149 on PR 1964 (findings G149-F1 and G149-F2).

**What happens** (measured by gate 149: the six real document routes in their own Node process, with an in-memory documents model that rejects AFTER it has applied the write; the identical request is then retried with no fault):

* `POST /:id/sign` (`updateDocument` is the write): the signature is persisted and the status is `signed`, the caller gets 500, and the signing nonce is NOT consumed. A retry with the same body inside the 5-minute nonce window answers 200 and appends a SECOND signature entry (1 signature, then 2).
* `POST /:id/sign-cert` and `POST /:id/sign-wallet` (`saveDocument` is the write): a derived document with status `signed` is persisted, carrying the sigJson or sigWallet envelope. The caller gets 500 and no `document.versioned` event is published. A retry mints a second derived signed document (derived 1, then 2, one event). For sign-cert the orphaned envelope can be fetched from the public `GET /:id/sig-json` route.
* `POST /:id/sign/request`: not affected. Its only write is synchronous and nothing is awaited after it; an orphan nonce expires after 5 minutes.

**Same at base:** with an ordinary `Error('Connection terminated unexpectedly')` at base, and with each of six unreadable thrown values at the head of PR 1964, the persisted state and the retry result were identical in all 288 compared cells. At base an unreadable value was worse: the caller got no answer, and so was just as likely to retry.

**Suggested shapes (from the gate, not chosen here):**

* sign: consume the nonce before the write (delete it, write, restore it on a definite pre-commit failure), or make the append idempotent on (signerId, nonce).
* sign-cert and sign-wallet: an idempotency key, or a deterministic derived id with `conflictMode: 'skip'` keyed on (parent, signature).

**Not tested:** a real PostgreSQL or Prisma client (the documents and lifecycle tables were an in-memory model); a real ambiguous commit (modelled as "write applied, then reject"); the real `authenticate()` and the gateway hop; a real Redis event bus; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

Related: `KS-1831` (the sign route: authorization, revoked status and no signature verified), `KS-1693` (the same sign-cert and sign-wallet routes: no provenance recorded for the derived document).

title: referral: duplicate milestone reward rows the re-award bug already stored stay stored and still count as pending rewards
description:
**BLUF:** The referral re-award bug (KS 1956) stored duplicate CLAIMABLE milestone reward rows in `svc_referral_milestones_rewards`: the same user and milestone, more than once. The repair in pull request 1979 stops NEW duplicates; it removes none. The rows already stored stay stored, and `GET /api/rewards/user` still counts every one of them as a pending reward that can be claimed. Any cleanup is a DATA change and Kam's decision later; this ticket proposes nothing destructive. Pre-existing, High (QA gate 162).

## What is measured

* **QA gate 162** (2026-11-03, real PostgreSQL 15, the real referral service over HTTP, on pull request 1979): before the repair the same user and milestone reached 2 to 4 rows across its cells. After the repair, new checks add none, and the progress row records each milestone once. Every duplicate row stored earlier is still there and is still a pending reward.
* **QA gate 153** (2026-11-03): `GET /api/rewards/user` shows these rows as pending with `canClaim: true`, which inflates the balance a user sees.

## What is not measured

* Whether production has `svc_referral_milestones_rewards` at all (the repo has no DDL for it, KS 1956), and if so how many duplicate rows it holds. Nothing in the repo shows production's schema or data.
* Claiming: `POST /api/rewards/claim` reads `svc_referral_rewards` only, so milestone rewards cannot be claimed through it (read, not run). No money moves inside the referral service.

## A first step that changes nothing

Size it, read-only: count rows per (`user_id`, `source_id`) where `source_type = 'MILESTONE'` and the count is above 1, on whichever database holds the table. What to do with any duplicates found is for Kam to decide; it is not proposed here.

## Related

KS 1956 (the re-award bug and its repair, pull request 1979), KS 1957 (the owner and role check on the award routes, pull request 1980).

title: auth email.ts writes the recipient's email address in clear to the console on send, failure and refusal (seven lines)
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/email.ts` writes the recipient's email address (`options.to`) in clear to the console at seven places: the ACS sent line, the ACS send-failed and send-threw lines, the allow-list refusal, the no-provider line, and the SMTP sent and failed lines. This is pre-existing, unchanged by pull request 1978, and not a thrown-object leak. It was disclosed by the author of pull request 1978 and raised by QA gate 161 (G161-F8). It conflicts with Kam's card `secuura-ks1346-logging-thrown-objects-leaks-secrets` = a ("Log what kind of thing was thrown and the NAMES of its fields, never their values"). Related to KS-1937, the same pattern in originate's notificationClient (the recipient address at INFO). A separate fix in a separate service, so a separate ticket (Kam, 2026-09-07). Nothing here is a fix; no code change is proposed or made.

## What is read (develop `32921f7921c2`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/email.ts`, 331 lines)

* `:161` `console.log` of `[Email/ACS] Sent to ${options.to}: ${options.subject}` (ACS sent)
* `:164` `console.error` of `[Email/ACS] Send failed for ${options.to}` (ACS failed status)
* `:167` `console.error` of `[Email/ACS] Send threw for ${options.to}: ${err?.message}` (ACS catch)
* `:180` `console.warn` of `Recipient not in EMAIL_RECIPIENT_ALLOWLIST — refusing to send: ${options.to}`
* `:192` `console.log` of `No provider configured — would send to ${options.to}: ${options.subject}`
* `:204` `console.log` of `[Email/SMTP] Sent to ${options.to}: ${options.subject}`
* `:207` `console.error` of `[Email/SMTP] Failed to send to ${options.to}: ${error.message}` (SMTP catch)

Three of the seven are failure paths (`:164`, `:167`, `:207`); the other four are the sent, refused and no-provider lines. The gate's finding names the catches; this ticket lists every line that carries the address.

## What is not measured

Whether this console output reaches a persisted log file or a log collector in any deployment; the same lines on the head of pull request 1978 (not re-read here); whether the address is ever a user's personal address rather than a system one in a given flow.

## Board search (duplicate check, `tools/file_ticket_r78.py`)

Terms: `services/email.ts`, `recipient's email address`, `recipient address`, `email address in clear`, `console line`. Positive control: the phrase "recipient's email address" returns KS-1937. Negative control: a random token returns 0. Candidates read by title and named as reviewed: KS-485 (the security review umbrella), KS-1937 (originate, the related ticket), KS-1526 (api-gateway file logs), KS-1313 (suite counts). None covers auth `email.ts`.

## Priority

Medium, as KS-1937 reads on the board (priority 3, state Todo, at filing).

Source: gate 161's verdict, `0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate161-ks1868-pr1978/verdict.md`, finding G161-F8.

title: auth: if Redis is down when the service boots, the session availability flag never returns to true, because the ready listener is only attached after the first successful connect
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/session.ts`, `initRedisSession` attaches its `error`, `reconnecting` and `ready` listeners only AFTER `await redis.connect()` and `await redis.ping()` have succeeded. If Redis is down when auth boots, the connect rejects, the catch sets the availability flag false and returns, and no listener is ever attached. ioredis keeps reconnecting in the background (the retry strategy from KS-617 never gives up), and when Redis comes back the client reaches `ready`, but nothing sets the flag true again. The flag stays false until the process is restarted, so every authenticated request is refused and no login can mint a session, while the container keeps running. This is the boot-time sibling of KS-617 (which addressed the same symptom after a blip, when the listeners already exist). Found by QA gate 160 (G160-F8, read only); MEASURED here.

**Relation to KS-617:** KS-617's fix (the retry strategy never returns null) covers a client that was established and then lost Redis, not this boot path.

## Measurement (read-only, loopback only; no real Redis, no box)

Real `session.ts` at develop `32921f7921c2`, real ioredis 5.11.1 (wrapped only to capture the client), a minimal RESP stub server on 127.0.0.1; recorder `5_Project_History/2026-11-03_seatR-78th/drafts/ks617/rec_redis_boot.test.ts`, recording `evidence/ks617/rec.json`.

* **Scenario A (the claim): Redis down at boot, then up.** `initRedisSession` returned after 1066 ms with the flag false. The client existed with status `reconnecting` and had 0 listeners for `error`, `ready` and `reconnecting`. After the stub came up the client reached status `ready` (the stub saw a connection and the commands `client`, `client`, `info`), yet the flag was still false after 12 s and `getRedisClient()` still returned null.
* **Control B (the listeners ARE attached): Redis up at boot.** Flag true, 1 listener each. A simulated `error` set the flag false; after an outage (connections reset, server closed) the client was `reconnecting`; after the stub restarted it reached `ready` and the flag returned to true within 12 s. So the instrument can see the flag returning to true.

## What the flag false does (read from the callers, per gate 160)

`getSession` returns null, so `authenticate` answers 401 to every authenticated request; `createSession` throws "Redis is not available", so no login mints a session; password change and reset answer 503; the refresh denylist fails closed; the login lockout fails open (already tracked as a decision for Kam). The service's own log line says "using in-memory session fallback", which is false (there is no in-memory store).

## Not measured

A real Redis server (the stub speaks only enough RESP for ioredis to reach `ready`); a booted auth service or any HTTP request; the same boot-order case in api-gateway, originate and governance, which KS-617 also names; whether a deployment's orchestration (depends_on, health checks, restart policy) makes the boot-time case reachable in practice; any fix. No fix is proposed here; the fix shapes are open (for example attaching the listeners before the first connect).

## Compose ordering and priority (read, not run)

Read at develop `32921f7921c2`, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, service `auth` (starts at line 729):

* `:836-842` `depends_on` lists `pgbouncer` (`condition: service_healthy`), `redis` (`:839-840`, `condition: service_healthy`) and `migrations` (`condition: service_completed_successfully`). So a `docker compose up` starts auth only after Redis reports healthy; the redis service has a healthcheck (`:227-231`, `redis-cli ... ping`, retries 5).
* `:738` `restart: unless-stopped`. `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.production.yml` is an override used with the base file (`-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml`, its own header and `Makefile:9`) and sets `restart: always` for auth (`:149`); it does not remove the base file's `depends_on`.
* Priority is **Medium**, because `service_healthy` guarantees the order on a cold `up`: the boot-time case then needs Redis to be down when auth (re)starts. What the file does not show, and what is NOT measured here, is whether a restart policy brings auth back before Redis is healthy (for example after a host or Docker daemon restart), since `depends_on` is applied by `docker compose up` and not by a restart policy. The Container Apps deploy template (a different deployment form) was not read.

## Board search

KS-617 (Deployed to UAT) describes the latch after a blip and corrects the retry strategy; its description and six comments have 0 mentions of `initRedisSession`, `lazyConnect`, a listener, or the boot-time connect failure. The terms `initRedisSession`, `lazyConnect`, `ready listener`, `after a failed connect`, `availability flag` and `session availability` each return 0 issues (`tools/file_ticket_r78.py`; positive control: the phrase "recipient's email address" returns KS-1937; negative control: a random token returns 0). No candidate to review.

title: api-gateway register-connector answers rotated: true and drops priorKeysRevoked when the prior key's retire failed, so a re-keyed leaked credential can stay valid unannounced
description:
**BLUF:** When the security service's rotate mints the new key but the retire of the prior key fails, it answers 201 with `priorKeysRevoked: null` and the prior credential stays valid (the deliberate KS-577 design: mint first, then revoke). The one production caller that rotates, the api-gateway's register-connector route (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`), drops that field: it only writes a `console.error`, records its audit entry `connector.key-rotate` without the failure, and answers its own caller `rotated: true` with no `priorKeysRevoked`. A Platform S admin re-keying a leaked credential is told it rotated while the old key still works. Pre-existing, and not caused by pull request 1981; found by QA gate 164 (G164-F3, MEDIUM). The same behaviour is already recorded as item R-880-1 on KS-1152 (the omnibus gate-records ticket, classed "design choice, pre-existing"); this ticket is the standalone with the measurement and the two remedies. Related to KS-577.

## What is read (develop `32921f7921c2`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`)

* `:877-879` the gateway types the mint body with `priorKeysRevoked?: number | null`.
* `:884-889` when `rotate && mintBody?.data?.priorKeysRevoked === null`, the only action is `console.error('[KS-577] rotate minted a new key but the prior-key revoke FAILED — prior credential STILL VALID', { externalRef, organizationId })`.
* `:895-907` the best-effort audit POST records the action `connector.key-rotate` with details `{ externalRef, keyId, keyPrefix, tenantId }`: there is no field for a failed retire.
* `:909-921` the response (200 for an existing connector, 201 for a new one) carries `rotated: rotate && existing.rows.length > 0` and no `priorKeysRevoked`.
* Callers of the security service's `POST /api/keys` that send `rotate` (gate 164, whole repository, with a positive control): only this route (`platform.ts:847`). `tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts:52` never sends `rotate`.

## What gate 164 measured (G164-F3)

With a real Postgres lock timeout on the retire (a superuser holding `FOR UPDATE` on the prior row, the app role at `lock_timeout=500ms`, nothing injected), the security service answers 201 with the new key valid, the prior key valid and 2 active rows, and logs "canceling statement due to lock timeout"; the same before and after pull request 1981. Likelihood is low: only a statement-level failure of the retire UPDATE alone fails open (a lock or statement timeout, a cancel, a deadlock), and the security service sets no `statement_timeout` or `lock_timeout` in code, so server defaults wait on a lock. Impact is high: the rotate exists to cut off a lost or leaked credential. The gate read, and did not drive, the gateway route, and read no retry or sweep that retires the key later.

## Two remedies, named neutrally (nothing is built, and neither is chosen here)

* (a) The gateway passes `priorKeysRevoked` through in its response and records the failure in its audit entry, so the caller is told the truth. The old key stays valid until it is retired some other way.
* (b) The rotate fails closed when the retire fails: no new key is issued unless the prior key is retired. The failure then becomes a failed rotate, which KS-577's ruling weighed as the worse failure.

Wednesday will bring (b) to Kam with the other fail-closed rulings.

## Not measured

The gateway route over HTTP; `statement_timeout`, a cancel or a deadlock as the real trigger (only `lock_timeout` was driven); a non-zero `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`; concurrent rotates.

## Board search (duplicate check, `tools/file_ticket_r78.py`)

Terms: `priorKeysRevoked`, `rotated: true`, `connector.key-rotate`, `prior credential`, `STILL VALID`. Positive control: the phrase "recipient's email address" returns KS-1937; negative control: a random token returns 0. Candidates read by title and named as reviewed: KS-1152 (R-880-1 and the gate 90 note record the behaviour from source, with no measurement, no audit finding and no remedies), KS-1370 (validate reads keys from a boot-only memory map), KS-583 (a DR rehearsal that expects the old key dead) and KS-869 (connectorId persistence); none reports the gateway's `rotated: true` after a failed retire. KS-577 was also read (the original rotate ruling and its comments).

Source: gate 164's verdict, `0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate164-ks1868-pr1981/verdict.md`, finding G164-F3.

title: vc verifier: with no DID resolver configured, a credential signed with the source's default development key verifies, also under NODE_ENV=production
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts`, when no DID resolver is configured (as the vc-issuer routes configure it) and `VC_SIGNING_KEY` is unset, a proof starting `zDEV_` is checked against an HMAC made with the literal default key in the source (line 356), so a credential "signed" with that known key verifies, including with `NODE_ENV=production`. Pre-existing: base = head; these are not the lines KS-1868 pull request 1993 changes. LOW (the gate's severity). **Measurement limit: measured on the module; the route was not driven; whether any deployed vc-issuer runs with the key unset is UNMEASURED.**

## Measured (gate 177, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate177-ks1868-pr1993/verdict.md`, finding G177-F7 (LOW, PRE-EXISTING).

* `verify()` with an empty config and `VC_SIGNING_KEY` unset: a `zDEV_` proof made with the default key gives `verified: true`, `signature: true` under `NODE_ENV=test` AND under `NODE_ENV=production`.

Whether vc-issuer runs with `VC_SIGNING_KEY` set (the production compose passes it through; when it is set, the `zDEV_` key is that value, not the default) and with `NODE_ENV=production`; and the routes' revocation resolvers, which fail closed on an unknown credential id, so a forgery would also need an id with a stored, unrevoked record. The gate did not check whether this is already ticketed; the board was searched for the default key, `zDEV_` and the `secuura-dev` literal (no ticket found; related reading only: KS-1352, KS-624, KS-625). It does not bear on any merge.

title: restore-local-secrets.sh: a .env line that closes stderr hides the PATH refusal (G180-F1); compose config has no time limit; census pin misses 4 of 8 keys
description:
**BLUF:** Four follow-ups on `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/restore-local-secrets.sh` (KS-915, PR 1989, merged 2026-11-04 as squash `26d8314e4f77`). QA gates 174 and 180 named them, and KS-915 comment 820f9aff lists them "for tickets, not in this round". They are one fix to the script and its suite, proven by one suite run, so they are one ticket (Kam, 2026-09-07: the unit of a ticket is the test pass). Item 1 is the one Kam ruled to ticket (live board 2026-11-04 12:51 AEDT, card `secuura-pr1989-round3-go-hold-demo-accounts-1104` = a: "Merge it, and ticket G180-F1"). All are LOW or INFO; none was ruled blocking.

The code was read at develop `5c1ca287ed74` with `git show`. The script blob is the same at the merge squash: `7eef8a0e47e6` at both.

1. **G180-F1 (LOW): a** `.env` **line that closes stderr hides the readonly-PATH refusal.**
   * The bash reader (`restore-local-secrets.sh:306-307`) sources the file under `readonly PATH; set -r; set -a`. It counts refusals by piping the reader's stderr into `grep -c ': PATH: '`.
   * A line that runs `exec 2<&-` before the PATH assignment closes stderr. The refusal is then never counted, while bash still skips the rest of that line.
   * Gate 180 measured a crafted two-line `.env`. At head: rc 0, ADMIN written, mode 600. At round 2: rc 3.
   * Independent readers: dotenv and both compose entries read the local host; a plain `set -a` read a remote POSTGRES_HOST. No command executed (the gate's r3 cell: the PATH lock holds).
   * Measured on macOS bash 3.2.57 only, NOT on bash 4/5 or Linux.
   * Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate180-ks915-pr1989-r3/verdict.md`, section G180-F1.
   * Fix direction (the gate's, direction only): a sentinel the reader must print after the source, whose absence counts as a refusal; or a stderr-liveness check after the source.
2. **G174-F4 (LOW):** `docker compose config` **has no time limit.**
   * The three compose reads (`:326`, `:329`, `:479`) run with no timeout.
   * Gate 174 made `docker compose config` hang. In 3 of 3 runs the script hung until the gate's 45 s alarm (rc 142). The `.env` stayed byte-identical and nothing was written, so it fails closed.
   * In 3 of 3 runs the compose child was still running after the script ended.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 35-36 (`/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate174-ks915-pr1989-r2/verdict.md`).
3. **G174-F3 (LOW, test strength): the census pin catches 4 of 8 planted address keys.**
   * `CENSUS_JS` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/restore_local_secrets.test.sh:623`) is name-based.
   * The gate planted one key per run through a compose override. The pin caught DB_READ_HOST, PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_HOST, READ_REPLICA_URL and SQLALCHEMY_HOST. It missed REPLICA_HOST, TYPEORM_HOST, AUDIT_STORE_ADDR and PRISMA_URL.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 31-33.
4. **G174-F5 (INFO): the repo-root note is asymmetric.**
   * When ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD is kept (`:537`) and the repo-root entry passes a different value, no note prints. For a kept ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS the note does print (`:482-490`).
   * Gate 174 called this truthful under the note's own rule, "an asymmetry, not a defect". To decide: make the two cases symmetric or leave them.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 38-39.

**Not measured for this ticket:** none of the four was re-run; every result above is the gate's. Whether item 1 reproduces on bash 4/5 or on Linux is also not measured.

**Related, not filed here:**

* The wider class of a hostile `.env` forging the bash reader (G173-F2), and the looping `.env`. Both are named in KS-915 comment 820f9aff.
* The pgbouncer `entrypoint.sh` userlist echo from the same comment, filed as its own ticket (a different file, fix and test).

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

* `G180-F1`: 0 hits. `exec 2<&-`: 0. `CENSUS_JS`: 0.
* `G174-F3`, `G174-F4`, `G174-F5`: 1 hit each, all in KS-915 comment 820f9aff, which names them for tickets.
* `restore-local-secrets`: 2 hits (KS-915; KS-600, closed). No ticket covers these items.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Two more items for this ticket. They are in the same script and are proven by the same suite run, so they belong here rather than in tickets of their own (Kam, 2026-09-07: the unit of a ticket is the test pass). KS-915 comment 820f9aff names both "for tickets, not in this round". Reading the code at develop `5c1ca287ed74` shows both are still there. Neither was re-run for this comment.

5. **G173-F2 (MEDIUM): a crafted `.env` can forge the bash reader's verdict.**
   * The reader (`restore-local-secrets.sh:306`) sources the file, then prints its result record with `printf` behind a fixed marker.
   * Gate 173 measured two forms at round 1:
     * A `printf()` function defined by the file: rc 0, ADMIN written, while an independent `set -a` read NODE_ENV=production, or a DATABASE_URL naming the gate's remote marker.
     * A file that prints its own record and then exits: rc 0. The gate did not count this one as a slip, because the exit also ends a consumer shell.
   * At develop, by reading: the record is still printed with `printf` after the source, behind the same fixed marker. The script has 0 hits each for `unset -f`, `set -o posix`, `builtin printf` and a per-run marker (`RANDOM`, `urandom`, `nonce`); the control `readonly PATH` has 2 hits.
   * Item 1 (G180-F1) is one form of this class: it shuts the reader's stderr first.
   * Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate173-ks915-pr1989/verdict.md:44-56`.
   * Fix direction (the gate's, direction only): print through something the file cannot redefine (`set -o posix` with `export -p`, or `builtin` after `unset -f printf builtin`). Use a per-run random marker, and refuse when a second marker appears.
6. **The looping `.env` (LOW): the bash reader has no time limit.**
   * Gate 173 (G173-F3, "Hang"): a `.env` holding `while :; do :; done` kept the script running until the gate's 60 s alarm (rc 142). Nothing was written. The looping reader outlived its parent, and one sandbox directory was left in TMPDIR.
   * At develop, by reading: the reader (`:306-307`) runs with no time limit. The script has 0 hits each for `timeout`, `alarm`, `watchdog`, `kill ` and `sleep `.
   * Item 2 (G174-F4) is the same gap in the compose reader. One reader time limit that fails closed and reaps its child would cover both.
   * The other half of G173-F3 is closed: `history -w` writing a file under `set -r`. `:306` now runs `enable -n history kill; HISTFILE=/dev/null`, and gate 174 measured 0 of 7 history routes writing.
   * Source: gate 173 `verdict.md:57-69`.

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):
* `G173-F2`: 2 hits, KS-915 comment 820f9aff and this ticket.
* `G173-F3`: 0. `while :; do :; done`: 0. `RLS-KS915`: 0.

This supersedes the "Related, not filed here" line in the description for these two.

title: e2e fixtures register with breached passwords: since KS-1968 B1 seven register call sites get 422 instead of an account
description:
**BLUF:** Since KS-1968 B1 (PR 1988, squash `1cbf260548e7`, deployed to kintsugi at `ee1e1b832115`), `POST /api/auth/register` and `POST /api/auth/reset-password` answer 422 to a password that the HaveIBeenPwned range check finds. Seven e2e call sites send such a password to register on the success path, so on a stack with the check on they get 422 instead of an account. Fix: give those fixtures generated, non-breached passwords (or run them with `HIBP_ENABLED=false`, if that is the ruled choice). Medium priority, because a merged and deployed change breaks known test sites. This was measured by reading the code, not by a run.

**Source:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatD-50th/evidence/hibp_corpus_ee1e1b832115.txt`, Seat D 50th's corpus at target `ee1e1b832115`.

* The file tags 16 rows `[reg/reset]` (the header's 21 counts occurrences; the rows are what it tagged).
* No literal is copied into this ticket.

  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/tests/tier1-api/email-notifications.api.spec.ts:48`. Asserts a status below 500, so a 422 passes silently and no account is made.

* **Weak-password cells (2 sites, 3 rows): not changed by KS-1968 if the literal fails the strength rules.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:651-652` and `auth.api.spec.ts:56`. Register checks strength before the breach list (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:205`, then `:214`, at `ee1e1b832115`).
* **Duplicate-email cell (1): not changed.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/sysadmin-exhaustive.admin.spec.ts:998` registers an existing email. The conflict answer at `auth.ts:198-201` comes before both checks.

**Not measured:**

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

title: pgbouncer entrypoint.sh writes the four userlist credentials unescaped: a newline in a value adds a userlist entry
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/docker/pgbouncer/entrypoint.sh:27-30` writes four user/password pairs into `/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt` with one `echo` per pair and no escaping. A value that contains a newline therefore adds a userlist line of its own: an extra auth entry, not an upstream. Seat E 33rd found this during KS-915 round 3, and it was ruled out of that PR. KS-915 comment 820f9aff names it for a ticket. Low: the values come from the operator's own `.env` or compose environment.

**Read at develop** `5c1ca287ed74` **with** `git show` (the same blob is at `ee1e1b832115`):

* `:13-24` map eight environment keys to four pairs:
  * POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD
  * PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_USER / PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_PASSWORD
  * PGBOUNCER_STATS_USER / PGBOUNCER_STATS_PASSWORD

**Fix direction only:** refuse a newline or a double quote in these eight values at start-up, or double each quote and refuse newlines before writing. Also correct the header comment, or write md5 entries as it says.

**Not measured:**

* Nothing was run.
* Whether pgbouncer accepts the extra line as a working entry.
* What a double quote inside a value does to its line (pgbouncer's userlist format escapes a quote by doubling it).
* Whether any deployed environment holds such a value.

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

title: api-gateway image crash-loops under NODE_ENV=production: EACCES mkdir 'logs' (the production File transports write to relative logs/, and /app is not writable by USER nodejs)
description:
## BLUF

* **The api-gateway image does not boot in production mode.** With `NODE_ENV=production` it exits at import with `Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir 'logs'` and restarts in a loop.
* **Cause (code at** `ee1e1b832115`**, byte-identical at develop** `d92b849ece73`**):** in production the logger adds two winston File transports at the relative path `logs/`. The image runs as `USER nodejs` in `/app`, a directory that user cannot write to.
* **Measured on a disposable local stack at** `ee1e1b832115`**, not on kintsugi.** `NODE_ENV=production` was set by an override on the base compose; the production compose file itself was not run. A writable tmpfs at `/app/logs` (a stack mount, no code change) let the same image boot and serve.
* **Priority Medium (3).** It is a hard boot failure, but no deployed environment is shown to run this image in production mode. Raise it if one is.

## What ran

Seat W 25th ran this on stack `w25`, 2026-11-04 \~08:34Z, with throwaway data. The api-gateway container was recreated with `NODE_ENV: production` set by a compose override. It crash-looped. Container output, verbatim (lines 1-5 and 11-16 of the saved file):

```
Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir 'logs'
    at Object.mkdirSync (node:fs:1410:26)
    at File._createLogDirIfNotExist (/app/node_modules/winston/lib/winston/transports/file.js:791:10)
    at new File (/app/node_modules/winston/lib/winston/transports/file.js:94:28)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/app/dist/utils/logger.js:32:21)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1674:12) {
  errno: -13,
  code: 'EACCES',
  syscall: 'mkdir',
  path: 'logs'
}
```

The container was then recreated with a tmpfs at `/app/logs` (mode 1777) added to that override. The production-mode gateway booted and answered 155 requests in the KS-1469/KS-1479 run (307 x31, 404 x122, 429 x2).

## Code (`Blockchain/Dev/`, at `ee1e1b832115`)

* `services/api-gateway/src/utils/logger.ts:30-35`: when `isProduction`, the logger pushes `new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/error.log', ... })` and `new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/combined.log', ... })`. Winston creates the directory at construction time, relative to the cwd.
* `services/api-gateway/Dockerfile` (99 lines, read whole):
  * the runtime stage sets `WORKDIR /app` (line 45);
  * `RUN chmod -R a+rX /app /shared` (line 84) grants read and execute only;
  * the user `nodejs` (uid 1001) is created at lines 87-88, and `USER nodejs` is set at line 89;
  * no line makes a `logs` directory or chowns anything to `nodejs`.
* `docker-compose.production.yml`: the `api-gateway:` block (lines 79-117) sets `NODE_ENV=production` (line 81) and mounts nothing. The whole file has 0 hits for `tmpfs`, `/logs`, `logs:` and `read_only`. The control `NODE_ENV=production` has 22 hits.
* `docker-compose.yml` (the base the production file overlays): the `api-gateway:` block has one volume, the OpenAPI spec mounted read-only. Its comment says Container Apps production deploys do not use this compose file.
* Develop: these four files are byte-identical at `d92b849ece73` and `ee1e1b832115`, read in a kept seat clone.

## Why Medium

* The failure is total for anyone who runs the image in production mode without a writable `/app/logs`.
* No current deployment is shown to do that. Seat U 11th's live check on kintsugi (2026-11-04, at `ee1e1b832115`) read the api-gateway `NODE_ENV=development`; that reading is carried, not re-measured here. The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31 (project CLAUDE.md).
* `docker-compose.production.yml` exists to run the stack in production mode. Whoever first uses it will hit this.

## Related

* **KS-1526** (Done) fixed the *format* of these same File transports (a column of `undefined`). Its description listed as unmeasured whether winston's default `mkdir('logs')` throws EACCES for a non-root user, and whether the File transports write anywhere in the deployed containers. This ticket measures the first: it does throw, and the gateway does not boot.
* KS-1348 (Done) is the originate half of the format defect. Whether originate's image has the same boot failure was not measured here.

## Board search before filing (team KS, includeArchived)

* Searched title or description, plus comment bodies, for: `EACCES`, `mkdir('logs')`, `/app/logs`, `tmpfs`, `USER nodejs`, `crash-loop`, `crashloop`, `logger.ts`, `not writable`, `read-only file`, `combined.log`.
* No open ticket covers this.
* The six open `EACCES` hits (KS-1025, 1152, 1402, 1571, 1686, 1776) are false positives: a case-insensitive `EACCES` matches inside `generateAccessToken` and `authenticateAccessOrConnector`.
* The only mentions of the boot failure are Seat W 25th's closing comments on KS-1469 and KS-1479 (both Done), which used the tmpfs as a stack workaround.

## Options (not decided here)

1. Create `/app/logs` owned by `nodejs` in the Dockerfile's runtime stage, before `USER nodejs`.
